Cardinals' Interest in Daniel Jones is Real
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals fell to 3-8 in Week 11 , marking their third straight loss while starting their fourth different quarterback on offense.
Jacoby Brissett's out of the picture. Gardner Minshew is done for the season. Carson Beck is dealing with a back injury with no clear timetable for return while Josh Johnson isn't an ideal starter to end the 2026 season.
A new option emerged for the Cardinals to potentially entertain over the weekend when the Indianapolis Colts released veteran quarterback Daniel Jones, and it appears Arizona's interest in the former first-round pick is legitimate.
From ESPN's Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter:
The Cardinals, per reports, also were interested in signing Jones before he inked a deal with Indianapolis in free agency a few offseasons ago.
Jones does have to make it through waivers, though he's unlikely to be claimed by an NFL team prior to Monday at 2:00 pm MST.
A team who claims him would take on Jones' $2 million salary for the rest of 2026, a $4 million roster bonus for next season and the $10.51 million injury guarantee per ESPN. The Cardinals are seventh in waiver priority, which is based on the inverse order of NFL standings.
ESPN is also reporting Jones is unlikely to sign somewhere immediately if he does clear waivers, as the quarterback wants to take his time and assess what the next best step is for him moving forward.
Jones' next team will be an interesting decision, as there's only six weeks left in the regular season. Will he opt to choose for a team he could immediately start for? Or does he join a Super Bowl-caliber team in hopes of providing a quarterback room some veteran experience as a backup?
As for the Cardinals and their interest, it could very well be tied to the overall health of Beck — who was suddenly ruled out for Sunday's Week 11 contest due to a back injury.
Arizona needs to see all that they can of the third-round pick, though if Beck can't go, the Cardinals may feel the need to pivot to Jones — who could likely be had for the veteran minimum if he does indeed clear waivers.

title: 4 Big Instant Reactions After Cardinals' Ugly Loss vs Chiefs
full_text:
That is what a game looks like when a Super Bowl Contender goes against a three-win team.
The Kansas City Chiefs handed the Arizona Cardinals one of their ugliest losses in recent years, winning 34-7 at Arrowhead. The Cardinals drop to 3-8 on the season and have plenty of questions with few answers.
After a brutal road game, what are the main takeaways for the Cardinals?
Unfortunately, a theme of first-year head coach Mike LaFleur's tenure in Arizona has been opposing teams out-coaching him. This game was a prime example, as Kansas City head coach Andy Reid had the perfect game plan for Arizona. The Kansas City offense diced up the Cardinals' defense, drive in and drive out throughout the day.
Meanwhile, LaFleur struggled to get any consistency going.
For the second straight week, tight end Trey McBride was not as involved as he should have been in the offensive game plan. While his final box score stats look good (nine catches for 54 yards) he only had one catch by the time the Chiefs were up 21-7.
Arizona tried to run the ball early, even though that wasn't a good idea. Kansas City's run defense is one of the league's better units, while the Cardinals' running game has been poor.
An overall poor day for the Cardinals offense, which first starts with its play-caller.
While Baker is still a quality player, he isn't the same elite defensive back he was a couple of years ago. This was shown when Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes laced a touchdown pass to tight end Travis Kelce that went over Baker's head, one of many slip-ups Baker had in pass coverage.
Many Cardinal fans thought that Baker could have been traded to a Super Bowl contender at the trade deadline a couple of weeks ago. Instead of trading Baker to a team like the Buffalo Bills or Jacksonville Jaguars and getting draft picks, Arizona kept him.
Baker is 30, and keeping him on a team in a rebuilding phase like the Cardinals continues to show it was not the best idea.
Mahomes has accomplished a lot in his NFL career. From winning three Super Bowls, two MVPs, and breaking passing records, he is one of the best quarterbacks ever to throw a football. However, Mahomes's kryptonite has been facing a very good pass rush. This was a key reason why Mahomes lost both of his Super Bowls.
With a proven game plan for beating a superstar like Mahomes, Arizona could hardly get any pressure on him. The Cardinals only had one sack in the game with five hits on the quarterback all afternoon.
For what felt like most of the game, Mahomes had all day in the pocket to thread passes to wideout Josh Downs, running back Emmett Johnson, and of course Kelce. Now, that one sack was a very nice play by second-year defensive tackle Walter Nolen III. However, Arizona should have had way more sacks in Arrowhead.
One reason Mahomes got to where he is today is that he sat behind veteran Alex Smith before taking over full-time duties. 2017 was Mahomes' rookie year, and the future Hall of Famer has said how much sitting and learning behind Smith has helped him in his NFL journey. There is a chance the Cardinals take a quarterback in next year's draft, and Johnson, who is 40 and has played for many teams, could be an excellent mentor for a rookie signal caller.
In terms of the game itself, Johnson was solid. He wasn't terrible and was far from the reason Arizona lost. Johnson's best play was a nice touchdown throw to Simi Fehoko in the first half. Hopefully rookie quarterback Carson Beck gets healthier, but if he misses another game due to injury, Johnson has proven that he could be serviceable at quarterback under LaFleur.

title: 10 Winners and Losers From Cardinals' Blowout Loss to Chiefs
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals' Week 11 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs was practically predictable before the two sides even met at Arrowhead.
The Cardinals, on their fourth starting quarterback in as many weeks, were easily handled by Patrick Mahomes and co. to the tune of a 34-7 scoreline. Arizona drops to 3-8 on the season after a forgettable but expected performance from both sides of the ball.
Ten winners and losers from Arizona's Week 11 loss:
Johnson, signed 12 days ago, deserves credit for the performance he was able to put on display today. Don't let the box score fool you: Johnson looked about as good as a 40-year-old who was signed 12 days ago could with a severely undermanned Cardinals offense. His passes had zip and accuracy wasn't an issue — his day was also plagued by three drops from his pass catchers.
Perfect? Not even close, and it wasn't good enough to win. Though Johnson's sudden jump to starting duties on the road against Kansas City went about as good as he or the Cardinals could have hoped from an individual standpoint.
Baker wasn't traded at the deadline to the Buffalo Bills, and as the Cardinals again sink further into the depth of the NFL standings, Josh Allen and co. are surging with Super Bowl hopes very much in the realm of realism.
Meanwhile, Baker's performance in Kansas City was forgettable. With Andrew Wingard on injured reserve, the Cardinals are forced to keep Baker — their best safety — out of the box and more in coverage. Baker was picked on numerous times by Patrick Mahomes in the passing attack, one being a touchdown pass.
The Cardinals' receiving corps has been a constant game of musical chairs due to trades and injuries, which essentially now has Arizona featuring a practice squad receiving corps at this point in the season.
Yet absence creates opportunity, and Wallace emerged out of Kansas City leading the Cardinals with 57 receiving yards on four receptions for a 14.3 yard-per-catch average. Wallace made some noise in training camp thanks to his speed, and now that he's getting more looks, it's good to see him parlay that success into the regular season.
One of the best things about LaFleur is his creativity in terms of play-design and play-calling. Arizona hasn't quite had the parts to make those two work at the same time, so that can't quite lean all on LaFleur.
However, there is something to be said about the timing of when LaFleur wants to get tricky. Opportunities with wide receiver reverses (twice) went nowhere while a fourth-down jet sweep was stopped short by the Chiefs, forcing a turnover on downs.
The first-year head coach is still learning how and where to pick and choose his spots, though today in Kansas City the play-caller found himself getting too cute too often.
The Cardinals just need Nolen to stay healthy.
That was evident on Sunday, where he was one of very few bright spots for Arizona's defense that again allowed 30+ points in a game. Nolen brought down Patrick Mahomes for a sack and made an incredible effort on a run-stuffing play that ended up in a tackle for loss.
The Chiefs' offense felt like it could do whatever it wanted in Week 11, though Nolen did his part.
This isn't calling McBride a loser personally, but more so McBride's an unfortunate byproduct of how things have gotten in Arizona.
With virtually nobody else to provide a legitimate threat in the passing game, teams are able to allocate more attention on McBride while daring Arizona's cast of receivers to step up. That was the case last week against the Rams, and again was reality this week against Kansas City.
He was held to just six yards per reception today, an eye-openingly low figure for a player of his status.

title: Cardinals Make Surprise Starting Lineup Change vs. Chiefs
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals , down and depleted, keep trying to find ways to shift their lineup in hopes of finding the best way to win.
That includes making their fifth starting lineup change along the offensive line in their last seven games.
Hoping to pull off a massive upset at Arrowhead, the Cardinals are replacing starting right tackle Elijah Wilkinson with Jayden Williams against the Kansas City Chiefs . Josh Fryar remains at left tackle.
Wilkinson has been fairly disappointing as Arizona's starting right tackle after signing with the Cardinals in free agency this past offseason. His Pro Football Focus grade of 59.1 ranks 58th out of 72 eligible NFL tackles.
Wilkinson has allowed 22 pressures, ten quarterback hits and four sacks in pass protection while his run-blocking grade is just outside of the bottom ten of NFL offensive tackles.
Meanwhile, left tackle has been something of a turnstile with starting left tackle Paris Johnson Jr. going down with a season-ending injury. Both Williams and Fryar have spent time at the position.
Yet with Arizona just 3-7, the Cardinals are hoping to find some sort of success upfront. Williams, a seventh-round pick that was a pleasant training camp surprise, has earned the respect of Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur.
“We got a lot of confidence in this young man. He’s wise beyond his years. He’s going to get a start a little quicker than we were anticipating but here we are," LaFleur said of Williams back in October.
Williams hasn't flashed much better stats in his small sample size, though his youth and upside just might make him a better option.
"We've talked about this but football is not too big for him," former Cardinals starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett told reporters earlier this season on Williams.
"The NFL is not too big for him. His ability to just go out there- he doesn’t say much, but he gives you those looks of he’s going to take care of business. I remember when he was first starting, I kind of said, ‘Hey, if you need anything from me, whether that’s step up or change the cadence or whatever, just tell me.’
"His response was, ‘If I’m talking to you, I’m doing something wrong.’ That held a lot of weight for me and he gave me a lot of comfort. So, he is perfect to me."

title: Who is Josh Johnson? Cardinals QB Will Make History vs Chiefs
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals are set to roll out Josh Johnson against the Kansas City Chiefs today, which will mark their fourth starting quarterback of 2026 after the team was forced to rule out Carson Beck.
If you're asking yourself, "who is Josh Johnson?" — you're not alone. Arizona just signed him just two weeks ago from Cincinnati's practice squad as a last-resort thanks to injuries piling up in the team's quarterback room.
The Cardinals have now exercised the "break glass in case of emergency" option.
Meet your new starting quarterback:
Johnson, now 40, initially entered the league as a fifth-round pick in 2008 by the Tampa Buccaneers. Since then, he has played for:
This does not include stints in the UFL, AAF and XFL.
In total, Johnson has 50 games played in his career with 11 starts. As a starter, he has a 2-9 record with a 58.7% completion rate with 14 touchdowns to 18 interceptions.
Johnson is Arizona's fourth starting quarterback in as many weeks, as it's been a chaotic game of musical chairs:
Johnson, due to his age, will join Jim Thorpe as one of the oldest non-specialist players to suit up for Arizona.
From Cardinals VP of media relations Mark Dalton:
"Tomorrow at KC, QB Josh Johnson (40 years, 191 days) will be the 2nd-oldest non-specialist to appear in a game for the Cardinals behind only Jim Thorpe, who was 41 years, 185 days old when he played his lone game with the Cardinals on Thanksgiving (11/29) in 1928 vs. the Bears."
Johnson spent some brief time with Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur in 2020, where the two were both in San Francisco (LaFleur was the team's passing game coordinator). That was also the case in 2021, where LaFleur was the New York Jets' offensive coordinator.
Johnson's prior experience with LaFleur — on top of his overall experience in the league — made him a coveted addition to Arizona's quarterback room at this point in the season.
"You got to have a baseline talent level, which clearly half the league has felt like he has, and I'm sure all 32 teams [feel the same]. It's just who needs one and who doesn't," LaFleur said of Johnson this week.
"He is incredible in the quarterback room. He's incredible for the starters. He's incredible for young quarterbacks in terms of just the way he sees the game, his energy, his positivity, how he keeps it real. He's mature and he can still sling it. Obviously he's been in this league. It's not like he was just on the street."
Kickoff is at 11:00 AM MST at Arrowhead.

title: Bold Predictions: Chiefs Offense Erupts vs Cardinals
full_text:
Welcome to game day, as the Arizona Cardinals and the Kansas City Chiefs meet for Week 11 action at Arrowhead.
The Cardinals enter today as underwhelming underdogs to Patrick Mahomes and co., with doubt only growing after Arizona was forced to rule out rookie quarterback Carson Beck.
Things could get funky in Kansas City — let's make some bold predictions:
This is by no means saying Mahomes will have a worse game than Johnson — this is actually more of a compliment to Kansas City's rushing attack and how that will shift the dynamic of the game.
In spite of Kenneth Walker's injury, Kansas City is slated to run the ball fairly well with Emmett Johnson in the backfield. The Chiefs are highly expected to be up early in this contest, which will eventually lean towards Kansas City's rushing attack taking over.
That, like practically every other Cardinals game this season, could push Johnson and the Cardinals' offense more towards a pass-heavy approach in the second half. More opportunities plus a softened Kansas City defense not wanting to give up big plays quickly does work in this favor.
This could very well be a game where the Chiefs win 35-17, though Mahomes has just one passing touchdown while Johnson somehow finishes the game with two.
The Cardinals' rush defense is nowhere close to threatening, and despite Walker's injury, Kansas City can still run the football at high rates.
That's partly thanks to Johnson, who totaled 171 scrimmage yards last week against the Atlanta Falcons. It's incredibly hard for anybody to repeat a performance like that, but if there's any defensive front who could allow it... It'd be the Cardinals.
The Rams ran 15 consecutive rushing plays in the fourth quarter to bleed out the clock after obtaining possession with 12:15 left in the game. The Cardinals couldn't stop the run then, and it's tough to imagine they've magically fixed their approach — especially with Mahomes at the helm.
The Chiefs will be ahead early and often, which paves the path for Johnson to hit the big play.
Perhaps this isn't quite a bold prediction given the Chiefs hit 461 yards and five touchdowns last week, though doing so two consecutive weeks would be downright eye-opening... for both sides.
The Cardinals' defense is by far the healthier of the two sides. While Arizona's unit does rank near the bottom of the league, they've proven capable of stepping up in recent weeks.
Yet they're about to run into a buzzsaw with Mahomes another week healthier and Andy Reid orchestrating the offense. The Cardinals' defense has faced some of the league's best teams, though Nick Rallis hasn't faced a talented and red-hot attack like what awaits in Kansas City.
This could be ugly. Very ugly for the Cardinals.

title: 3 Chiefs vs Cardinals Prop Bets Experts Love in Week 11
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs and Arizona Cardinals are set to clash at Arrowhead for an early slate Week 11 matchup.
The Chiefs are massive favorites over the Cardinals, who will be starting their fourth quarterback in as many weeks in 40-year-old Josh Johnson.
Moneyline is out of the picture — but what about prop bets?
Three of the best we could find across the web:
Josh Inglis, Covers.com : "In his first game with the Chiefs after being acquired at the trade deadline, the former Colt put up 51 yards and a touchdown on five targets while running just eight routes. That's an impressive TPRR that should only increase as he becomes more familiar with the offense.
"Kenneth Walker is still trying to get healthy, and Patrick Mahomes is coming off a five-touchdown performance. The Chiefs also get an Arizona team that has struggled to move the ball. Even with a lead, KC can get creative in the red zone, which should lead to a less conservative play-calling approach. If Downs sees a snap-share jump, gets another 6+ targets, and scores this week, his TD price is falling from 3.2x to 2.6x. I'd play it this week to 3x."
Josh Shepardson, Sharp Football : "With some running back uncertainty, leaning into Rice to score the game's first touchdown in a likely one-sided affair favoring the host Chiefs is appealing. Rice has 2 receiving touchdowns and 5 red-zone targets this year. He should also benefit from Arizona's coverage tendencies.
"The Cardinals rank sixth in zone coverage (81.8%) this year, and their 23.9% Cover 6 rate is the second-highest mark, well above the league average (12.0%). Rice has a 27% target rate per route and 2.75 Y/RR on 105 routes against zone coverage this year, and he has a 29% target rate per route and 3.24 Y/RR on 59 routes against Cover 6 since last season. The Cardinals have also been flamed for 12 receiving touchdowns by wideouts in 10 games this season."
Ryan Gilbert, SI : "Harrison Butker’s field goal failures have been widely publicized this season. He’s made just 12 of 19 attempts, with multiple field goals made in just two of the Chiefs’ nine games.
"The Cardinals don’t always allow too many field goals, mainly because offenses can find the end zone against them. I think that will be the case for Kansas City this week, so I’ll happily fade Butker at home against Arizona.
"The Chiefs should be up big in this one, so it’s easy to envision Cook getting plenty of looks in the second half."

title: Cardinals Make Final Carson Beck Decision vs Chiefs
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals are officially ruling out Carson Beck for their Week 11 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs.
Beck, initially questionable with back spasms, now has the door shut on his availability as the Cardinals prepare for their road test at Arrowhead.
This officially places Josh Johnson as the Cardinals' starter, which will be Arizona's fourth different quarterback in as many games.
Johnson, 40, was just signed from Cincinnati's practice squad weeks ago. Now, he's on his 15th NFL team after being drafted in 2008.
"You've got to have a baseline talent level, which clearly half the league has felt like [Johnson] has," LaFleur said.
"He is incredible in the quarterback room. He's incredible for the starter. He's incredible for young quarterbacks in terms of just the way he sees the game, his energy, his positivity, how he keeps it real. He's mature, and he can still sling it. He's been in this league. It's not like he was just on the street."
Johnson previously played under LaFleur during their short stint together with the New York Jets.
Meanwhile, Beck is fresh off his first NFL start — though this is the second time he's dealt with back spasms this season.
"I can't answer that because you just treat it. You go with the people that know what they're doing to treat it, and it's not like it's the first time he's dealt with it," LaFleur said when asked if there was any preventative measures the Cardinals could take.
"So he's going about his business. He's going to handle it just like he does preparing for a football game, just like he does playing a football game. So we'll see. We'll see more tomorrow."
Tomorrow has arrived, and as the team boards their plane for Kansas City, Beck will not be on it.

title: Insider: Cardinals Are Potential Team for Blockbuster No. 1 Pick Trade
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals , as it sits right now, are far removed from the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft.
Arizona clings to the seventh pick in the order entering Week 11, where a loss to the Kansas City Chiefs feels all but likely as the team is down to their fourth starting quarterback in as many weeks.
According to ESPN's analytics, the Cardinals have a 66% chance to finish with a top ten pick and a 19% chance to finish with a top-five pick. As for the No. 1 pick itself, there's less than a 1% chance.
Finishing with the top pick isn't realistic, but trading up for it certainly is according to NFL insider Adam Schefter.
Schefter looped the Cardinals in with several other teams who could make a push for the No. 1 overall pick next offseason.
Discussing a world in which the Tennessee Titans land the No. 1 overall pick in April’s NFL Draft, as they currently have. Cc: @tyschmit 🎧 https://t.co/zy1jY5Gg8R pic.twitter.com/CHM6ke7LmP
"There is going to be an auction, I believe for the number one pick, for the right to draft Drew Mestemaker, the Oklahoma State quarterback. Whether that's the Jets trading up. Whether that's the Cardinals trading up. Whether that's any of these other teams trading up ... Dolphins, Jets, Cardinals, Browns, whoever — somebody is going to want to trade up to No. 1 if it's Tennessee or the Chargers," he said.
The Cardinals haven't had the No. 1 pick since 2019, where they drafted Kyler Murray. Arizona did use a third-round pick on Carson Beck last offseason, though his future is very much unclear .
If Arizona did indeed make a move for that pick, the Cardinals would be making a massive gamble on Mestemaker while emptying their stockpile of draft ammo. Arizona has six picks in the first four rounds for 2027 while owning original picks in the first five rounds of 2028's draft.
The problem? Arizona's very unlikely to outbid some other teams who may be looking to make the climb up to No. 1. The Jets have three first-round picks while the Browns (2x), Eagles (2x) and Titans (2x) are other teams with multiple firsts in 2027.
It also depends on who is around to make the picks, as a new general manager could have a massively different vision for the Cardinals than current placeholder Monti Ossenfort, who is facing pressure as his fourth season running the team begins to come to a close.

title: Grand Theft Contract: 5 Worst Cardinals Free-Agent Signings Under Monti Ossenfort
full_text:
Grand Theft Auto VI has taken world by storm, delivering on the hype of making it one of the most popular video games of all time.
That got us thinking about some of the worst contracts under current Arizona Cardinals general manager, who has been with the team since 2023. We omitted his 2026 class since they've barely played half of a season.
The five worst deals Ossenfort's made:
Year : 2024 Contract : 2-YR, $30M
This probably takes the cake for the worst contract Ossenfort has ever awarded. Williams was awarded $15 million annually to anchor the team's right tackle spot but was placed on injured reserve after just one game in 2024 and also landed on the list in Week 10 of 2025 – playing just 17 games across two seasons.
Year : 2024 Contract : 3-YR, $30.1M
Jones was awarded $10 million annually to help bolster the Cardinals' defensive line. The results? He tore his triceps in Week 3 of his first season before a knee injury in 2025's training camp placed him on IR again. He was paid $19.75M guaranteed for just three games across two years.
Year : 2024 Contract : 3-YR, $25.5M
There was plenty of hype around Murphy-Bunting and his prior Super Bowl experience. However, he did miss two games with a neck injury and graded poorly for his first year in Arizona. Next offseason, he landed on the reserve/NFI list with a torn ACL/MCL, which kept him out for all of 2025. He didn't make it past final roster cuts this past season.
Year : 2024 Contract : 3-YR, $21M
Nichols, a prior teammate of Jones in Chicago, also struggled in the health department once he landed in Arizona. He played in six games his first season before suffering a neck injury (which landed him on injured reserve) before he also landed on injured reserve after four games due to a knee injury.
Year : 2025 Contract : 2-YR, $29M
Tomlinson signed with Arizona last offseason in hopes of making a bigger impact than he did. While he did play all 17 games in 2025, he statistically had the worst year of his career with just 26 tackles and one sack — which was a massive letdown considering his price tag, and the Cardinals agreed when they cut him last offseason.

title: Falcons Manage to Lose During Their Bye Week
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons spent Week 11 watching from home, but Sunday’s NFL action still had significant implications for their season. With Atlanta sitting at 3-7, the results around the league impacted both its position in the NFC South and its projected spot in the 2027 NFL Draft.
The good news for Atlanta is that it moved ahead of the New Orleans Saints in the division standings. The bad news is that the Carolina Panthers continued to create separation at the top, making the Falcons’ path back into playoff contention increasingly difficult.
The NFC South standings received another shakeup Sunday, with Carolina being the only division team to pick up a victory.
The Panthers defeated the Baltimore Ravens, improving to 5-5 and extending their division lead to two games. Meanwhile, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers fell 31-21 to the Detroit Lions, and the Saints lost 21-13 to the Chicago Bears.
Those results leave three teams tied at 3-7 behind Carolina.
NFC South standings after Week 11:
Atlanta holds the tiebreaker over New Orleans following its earlier head-to-head victory. That moves the Falcons out of the division’s last-place position despite their three-game losing streak.
While the division remains within reach mathematically, Atlanta has little room for error. The Falcons have seven games remaining and need to find a way to put together a consistent stretch of football if they hope to make a late-season push.
The other significant development involves the 2027 NFL Draft.
Entering Week 11, Atlanta was projected to own the eighth overall selection. They are now projected to hold the No. 10 overall pick after today’s outcomes. With the Falcons remaining idle during their bye week, their position continues to reflect their 3-7 record and strength-of-schedule tiebreakers.
The Saints and Buccaneers moved ahead of the Falcons. The first tie-breaker in the NFL Draft is strength of schedule, and only the Miami Dolphins (.595) have a stronger strength of schedule than the Falcons (.559).
Unlike in years past, when the Falcons were bad against an easy schedule, they won't win many tie-breakers this year. Atlanta got that benefit in 2022 when they picked first among six 7-10 teams and first again among four 7-10 teams in 2023.
The projected draft position gives Atlanta an opportunity to add another significant piece to its roster, particularly if the team cannot turn its season around over the final seven games.
Offensive tackle, quarterback, wide receiver, and cornerback are among the premium positions that could receive attention during the offseason.
The offensive line is particularly interesting. Jake Matthews is approaching the latter stages of his career, and finding a long-term successor at left tackle could become an important priority for the organization.
Atlanta also has questions surrounding its quarterback situation , making the remainder of the season important for evaluating the roster and determining its direction heading into 2027.
Picking inside the top 10 would give general manager Ian Cunningham an opportunity to addresss these moves and evaluate the franchise moving forward.
Ultimately, the Falcons are entering an important evaluation period. Winning games would give the organization momentum heading into the offseason and potentially keep its playoff hopes alive.
However, if the losing continues, the focus will increasingly shift toward the 2027 NFL Draft, evaluating young players and determining which veterans belong in the team's long-term plans .

title: Falcons' Slow Starts Have Created a Problem They Can't Escape
full_text:
FLOWERY BRANCH – The Atlanta Falcons are constantly playing from behind, and, more often than not, it's buried them.
They struggle to find consistency and have trailed by at least 10 points on 35.9% of their offensive snaps through 10 weeks (the league's highest rate). The results have been three consecutive double-digit losses, with slow starts repeatedly forcing the offense to play catch-up.
“When you're down, it's hard for the coaches, because the playbook gets limited and you have to get some points and stuff like that, get big chunk plays,” left guard Matthew Bergeron said. “It's hard to get the offense rolling when you're trying to get back (in games). We call it G-Bot when you're trying to get back on track. It's not easy. Those guys (the defense), they want to rush the passer, and it makes their life easier. So we just gotta keep working on it.”
Self-inflicted errors have crushed the Falcons through their first 10 games , but Bergeron was adamant that the bye week's priority would be to “clean up” the offensive operation ahead of the season's final stretch. He said that the “leadership” on the roster gives him confidence that they can get there.
“The guys we have in the locker room, I think we have some great guys, some great leaders, on our team,” the left guard said. “I feel like we're going to fight until the end, and we proved that (against the Chiefs). We were down, and we just kept fighting. That's just who we are, and if we hadn't made those mistakes early in the game, we would have been in it.”
But nothing will matter unless this offense can find its legs.
The Falcons' offense looked dramatically different after Michael Penix Jr. returned from injury. Atlanta averaged 31.0 points per game from Weeks 3 through 7, leading the NFL during that stretch. Opposing defenses have since adjusted, and the Falcons have averaged just 10 points over their last three games, all losses.
The rushing attack, in particular, has taken a hit. Despite rostering one of the league’s premier skill players in Bijan Robinson, the Falcons have been outrushed in five of their last six games. The star back has reached the 100-yard rushing mark only once in that stretch and has had at least 20 carries in only one game (their only win).
The slow starts have a lot to do with that, but so does not getting the ball to their star player earlier in games – Robinson only had one carry over the first four possessions against the Chiefs (all three-and-outs).
This inability to establish the offense has drawn scrutiny on the coaching staff. Stefanski confirmed this week that offensive coordinator Tommy Rees will continue calling plays, but the head coach acknowledged that the execution hasn't been good enough.
For an offense that has so much invested in it, this is particularly worrying.
They feature several first-rounders and big-contract players – the five largest contracts are offensive players – but that investment hasn't produced the return the Falcons need so far. That group is averaging just 20.1 points per game and -0.16 EPA per play.
Since Week 5, the numbers are particularly concerning.
According to NextGenStats , the Falcons are 30th in third-down conversion rate and have produced -0.12 EPA per rush. Penix has posted -0.13 EPA per dropback with six interceptions during that stretch, while the offense has averaged just 2.2 points in the first quarter.
Rees was moved from the box to the sideline to improve communication and produce better results, but that change didn’t move the needle against the Chiefs. It remains to be seen whether that move will be permanent.
“The responsibility falls on me,” head coach Kevin Stefanski said about the poor offensive play. “Everything falls on me. We all have to be better. That’s the truth. We are all going to learn from it. We’re not going to hide from it; we’re going to learn from it.”
Stefanski will pull everything apart during the week off to “get under the hood” to see how this team can get back on track, but it starts with these players.
“It’s definitely a mentality, and it’s habits,” Jahan Dotson said. “It’s what you do every day in practice. It doesn’t just happen on game day. It’s what you do every single day. If you are going to say you want to be (a good offense), then you have to be about it every day, and you have to create those habits.”
Frustration is high in the locker room over how the games have gone, but the Falcons still have time to get back on track. Atlanta is still within striking distance in a struggling NFC South and still has games against all three division opponents before the end of the year.
The key now is to keep the team together, despite the 3-7 start. Players have maintained that they still have the right guys in the locker room and the right mindset heading into the final seven games.
“I think the way our team is wired, and the way we were brought on this year – it's not pretty, but we're gonna keep fighting,” Bergeron said. “You just gotta turn that frustration into motivation. And listen, we have a week to fix the bumps and bruises and get back to work.”
“We have a lot of guys that care,” Dotson added. “We have a lot of guys that love this game, a lot of guys that love winning. Obviously, we have not been on that path, so the guys want to fix that.”
Center Corey Levin said the offense is “one guy away” from finding explosive plays. But after 10 games of inconsistent execution, the Falcons need to find out how to turn that optimism into points during this week off.
Otherwise, this season will keep spiraling.
Garrett Chapman is a sports broadcaster, writer, and content creator based in Atlanta. He has several years of experience covering the Atlanta sports scene, college football, Georgia high school football, recruiting for 24/7 Sports, and the NFL. You can also hear him on Sports Radio 92.9 The Game.

title: What Falcons Fans Should Be Watching Around the NFL This Sunday
full_text:
With the Atlanta Falcons on their bye week, Sunday gives fans an opportunity to step back and monitor the rest of the NFL. Although Atlanta cannot improve its 3-7 record this weekend, several matchups could have significant implications for the NFC South standings and the team’s postseason hopes.
The Falcons have struggled to find consistency this season, but the division race remains something worth monitoring. With several weeks remaining, Atlanta needs some help from its divisional opponents while preparing for an important stretch of games after the bye.
Here are four things Falcons fans should be watching this Sunday.
The first matchup Falcons fans should have their eyes on is Carolina against Baltimore.
The Panthers enter Sunday sitting atop the NFC South with a 4-5 record. With Atlanta at 3-7, every Carolina loss could help the Falcons’ chances of making a late-season push.
A Baltimore victory would give Carolina another divisional setback and potentially open the door for the rest of the NFC South to close the gap.
Atlanta needs Carolina to struggle down the stretch if it hopes to make the division race interesting.
The Buccaneers are another team Falcons fans should monitor closely.
Tampa Bay enters Week 11 with a 3-6 record, remaining within reach of Carolina in the division standings. A loss against Detroit would make the Buccaneers’ path toward the division title even more difficult.
Detroit also presents an opportunity for Atlanta fans to evaluate an upcoming opponent. The Falcons are scheduled to face the Lions on December 6, making this matchup particularly interesting.
Watching how Detroit attacks Tampa Bay defensively could provide some insight into what Atlanta will need to prepare for in two weeks.
New Orleans enters Sunday with a 3-6 record, tied with Tampa Bay and ahead of Atlanta.
The Saints are coming off a loss to Carolina and now face a difficult challenge against Chicago. A Bears victory would give New Orleans another setback and help Atlanta’s position in the NFC South.
The Falcons still have a January 3 matchup against the Saints, meaning the division race could come down to the final weeks of the season.
Atlanta needs New Orleans to continue dropping games while finding a way to turn its own season around.
Sunday night’s matchup might be the most important game for Falcons fans looking ahead.
Atlanta returns from its bye week on November 29 against Minnesota, giving fans an opportunity to get an early look at their next opponent.

The Falcons cannot control what happens around the NFL, but Sunday’s will shape their postseason and draft outlook.
Ideally, Atlanta fans want to see Carolina, Tampa Bay and New Orleans all lose. Those results would give the Falcons an opportunity to gain ground without playing a game.
However, the bigger challenge remains within Atlanta’s locker room. At 3-7, the Falcons need to find answers quickly.

title: Falcons Fans Aren't Going to Like NFL Network's Re-Ranking of 2024 QBs
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons surprised the NFL landscape when they called Michael Penix Jr.'s name at No. 8 overall in the 2024 NFL Draft.
He was the fourth quarterback taken, with Caleb Williams, Jayden Daniels, and Drake Maye going with the first three picks. J.J. McCarthy and Bo Nix would both go in the next four picks, giving the Class of 2024 six quarterbacks in the first 12 picks.
Two and a half seasons have gone by, and each of the quarterbacks has seen their share of ups and downs. Penix's journey in Atlanta is well documented, so we won't rehash the Kirk Cousins debacle and subsequent knee injury in 2025 that helped limit Penix to just 20 starts thus far.
NFL Network's Bucky Brooks recently took a look back at the Class of 2024 and ranked the quarterbacks and rendered a verdict on whether or not each quarterback should have his fifth-year option picked up this spring. The decision on the fifth year of first-round picks must be made before they begin their fourth season.
Brooks kept the first three in draft order before shaking up the next three.
Brooks points to Penix's injury history and lack of development because of missed time as reasons he would not exercise his fifth-year option. Though, he has massive praise for Penix's overall ability.
"In an offense that allows him to throw to multiple blue-chip playmakers, Penix could post ridiculous numbers while operating like a point guard leading a fast break. Although he is still finding his way in navigating Kevin Stefanski's system, the impressive flashes from the left-handed gunslinger could still allow one to envision him as a long-term solution in Atlanta," Brooks wrote on NFL.com.
What he liked didn't overcome what he didn't like about Penix, though. Penix is one of the worst quarterbacks in the NFL when pressured, and Brooks acknowledges a new system and missed time as possible causes. However, he worries about Penix's ability to be on the field enough to gain the needed experience.
That said, it still feels like a bit of recency bias to put Penix behind McCarthy. They entered the league under similar circumstances, with a veteran taking the snaps during the first season. They both had season-ending injuries. The Vikings dumped McCarthy for a lowly fifth-round pick from the Giants.
McCarthy is 2-1 for the 5-3-1 Giants, but his numbers are nothing to write home about. He's thrown for 915 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions.
We can give Brooks the benefit of the doubt that he gave the nod to McCarthy based on recurring injury history and age. Yes, McCarthy (23) missed last season with an injury as well, but Penix (26) has had five season-ending injuries in seven seasons as a starter, dating back to college.
Still, this feels like a typical "Falcons Tax": When players are pushed down in individual rankings based on the collective failure of the team and franchise. Penix hasn't played better than McCarthy in the last two weeks, and he's playing for a worse team. But, he's been objectively better in nearly every meaningful quarterback category.
Heck, Spencer Rattler has played more games, has a better TD-to-INT ratio and passer rating than McCarthy to date.
At the end of the day though, Penix's competition isn't McCarthy; it's himself. He has seven games to prove to the general manager Ian Cunningham and the Falcons that he can take the reins of the team in 2027 to push them towards a playoff push.
If he doesn't, the Falcons will be investing in the quarterback position this offseason .
Scott is an Atlanta-based sports media professional with stints as Director of Scouting of Scout.com, VP of Content Production at Sports Illustrated, and Managing Editor at CBS Interactive / 247 Sports, among others.

title: Falcons’ Young Defensive Core Gives Atlanta Reason for Hope
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons have fallen short of expectations during the 2026 season, but the development of several young defensive players has provided reasons for optimism about the future.
Atlanta is in the middle of its bye week at 3-7, sitting at the bottom of the NFC South.
While the team’s postseason hopes have taken a significant hit, the final games present an opportunity to evaluate the young talent that could become the foundation of the defense moving forward.
Daniels has arguably been one of Atlanta’s biggest surprises this season.
Selected 134th overall out of Oklahoma, Daniels entered the season expected to provide linebacker depth. Instead, he has worked his way into a significant defensive role.
Through 10 games, Daniels leads the Falcons with 69 total tackles, including 43 solo stops. He has also recorded one sack, one interception and a fumble recovery.
His performance against the San Francisco 49ers was a defining moment in his rookie campaign. Daniels finished with 11 tackles, nine solo stops, an interception, and a fumble recovery.
His versatility has become increasingly valuable, particularly with Divine Deablo dealing with injuries. Daniels has also taken on additional leadership responsibilities, including wearing the green dot and communicating defensive adjustments.
Perkins has also emerged as an important piece of Atlanta’s defense.
The sixth-round selection out of LSU has recorded 49 tackles, four tackles for loss and 1.5 sacks through 10 games.
His ability to contribute in coverage has been particularly encouraging. According to Pro Football Focus, Perkins owns a 79.6 coverage grade, ranking third among 82 qualifying linebackers.
His athleticism and versatility give Atlanta another option against both the run and pass. With Deablo’s injury history and the emergence of two young linebackers, Perkins could have an opportunity to establish himself as a long-term starter.
Atlanta’s defensive future is not limited to Daniels and Perkins.
Second-round rookie Avieon Terrell has recorded 12 tackles through eight games while adjusting to the speed of the NFL. The Clemson product finished his final college season with 48 tackles, three sacks, and nine pass breakups. He's battled a hamstring injury most of the season; the same injury that contributed to him falling out of the first round in the first place.
Meanwhile, second-year safety Xavier Watts continues to develop into an important contributor. Through 10 games, Watts has recorded 62 tackles, one interception, and two forced fumbles.
The Falcons also have young defensive linemen Maason Smith and Brandon Dorlus contributing. Smith has recorded 17 tackles and one sack, while Dorlus has produced 17 tackles, 1.5 sacks and six quarterback hits.
Anchoring the defensive line is Gervon Dexter Sr. General manager Ian Cunningham acquired him in a trade just before roster cutdowns, and he has arguably been the Falcons' best defensive player this season.
Dexter is the highest-graded defensive player on the team at 79.4, placing him No. 9 in the NFL, according to PFF. He leads the team with 23 quarterback hurries. The Falcons locked him down to a four-year, $78 million extension in September, a week before his 25th birthday
There are also reasons to monitor James Pearce Jr. and Jalon Walker. Pearce missed the first eight games due to suspension, while Walker suffered a season-ending ACL injury during training camp. Both are expected to contribute heavily in 2027.
Atlanta’s 3-7 record tells one story about its season. The development of its young defenders tells another.
The remaining seven games should provide valuable opportunities for Daniels, Perkins and Terrell to establish themselves while the coaching staff evaluates its long-term defensive personnel.
The Falcons still need improvements in their pass rush and overall consistency, but the emergence of two late-round linebackers is an encouraging development.
If Atlanta can continue developing its young talent, the organization could enter the 2027 offseason with a stronger defensive foundation than its record suggests.

title: 5 Falcons Veterans Who Need a Strong Finish to the 2026 Season
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons have seven games remaining in the 2026 season, and the bye week provides an opportunity for several players to reset before the final stretch.
At 3-7, Atlanta has fallen well short of its preseason expectations . With the team’s playoff hopes fading, the remaining schedule is about more than wins and losses. It is also an opportunity for important pieces of the roster to prove they belong in the franchise’s long-term plans.
Here are five Falcons players who need a strong finish to the 2026 season.
Few players have more riding on the final seven games than Michael Penix Jr.
The young quarterback entered the season with expectations of taking another step forward and establishing himself as Atlanta’s franchise quarterback. Instead, his development has become one of the biggest concerns surrounding the team’s disappointing season.
Through eight games, Penix has completed 147 of 242 passes for 1,730 yards, 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions. He has completed 60.7% of his attempts while posting an 84.2 passer rating (23rd in the NFL among 31 qualifying QBs). He has also taken 12 sacks and lost one of his five fumbles.
His recent performances have been particularly concerning. Against Kansas City, Penix completed 23 of 43 passes for 286 yards, zero touchdowns, and one interception in a 35-13 loss. He has thrown six interceptions over his last three games.
The Falcons need to see improved decision-making, better accuracy, and more consistency in the passing game. Atlanta cannot afford continued offensive struggles, especially with the quarterback position being one of the most important pieces of its long-term future.
Is Penix still the unquestioned starting quarterback heading into 2027, or will Atlanta need to consider bringing in legitimate competition ? The final seven games could go a long way toward answering that question.
A.J. Terrell is another player who needs a strong finish after a disappointing 2026 campaign.
The veteran cornerback has been an important part of Atlanta’s secondary for years, but his performance this season has raised concerns about whether he can return to his previous level of play.
Through six games, Terrell has recorded 21 combined tackles and three passes defended without an interception. According to Pro Football Focus, his 37.4 overall defensive grade ranks 99th among 103 qualified cornerbacks. His coverage grade of 38.5 ranks 97th.
He has also allowed a 148.5 passer rating when targeted, according to PFF.
Those numbers are concerning for a player expected to be a difference-maker in the secondary. Atlanta needs Terrell to become more consistent in coverage, limit explosive plays, and provide the type of veteran leadership that can help stabilize the defense.
Can Terrell return to being a top-level cornerback, or is Atlanta approaching a point where it needs to reconsider his role as a foundational piece of the defense? His remaining performances will be important in determining how the organization evaluates its secondary heading into the offseason.
Kyle Pitts might have one of the most interesting situations of any Falcons player entering the final seven games.
Atlanta made a significant commitment to Pitts this offseason, signing him to a three-year, $54 million contract extension that includes $36 million in guaranteed money. The agreement keeps him under contract through the 2028 season.
However, his production has not consistently matched the expectations that come with that investment.
Through 10 games, Pitts has recorded 29 receptions for 270 yards and four touchdowns on 42 targets. He is averaging just 9.3 yards per reception.
Although his four receiving touchdowns are a positive, his overall production has been underwhelming. His 270 receiving yards rank 22nd among 38 qualified tight ends, while his 60.2 PFF grade ranks 33rd.
The former first-round selection has the physical tools to become one of the NFL’s most dangerous tight ends. However, Atlanta needs more consistent production from him, particularly as the offense continues searching for answers.
With seven games remaining, Pitts needs to establish himself as a dependable part of the passing game. Creating mismatches, making contested catches and becoming a bigger factor in the red zone should all be priorities.
Can Pitts become the consistent offensive weapon Atlanta envisioned when it invested $54 million in him? His contract suggests the organization believes in his future, but the Falcons need to see that investment translate into production.
Veteran offensive tackle Jake Matthews also has something to prove during the final stretch of the season.
Matthews has been one of Atlanta’s most experienced offensive linemen, providing stability at left tackle since being selected in the first round of the 2014 NFL Draft.
However, his performance this season has not been without concerns.
According to Pro Football Focus, Matthews has allowed 14 pressures, including three sacks and two quarterback hits through 10 games. His overall PFF grade of 62.2 ranks 49th among 71 qualified offensive tackles.
His pass-blocking grade of 72.5 has been more encouraging, but his run-blocking grade of 51.7 ranks 65th at the position.
Protecting Penix has to remain a priority. Atlanta’s offense cannot find consistency if its quarterback is constantly dealing with pressure and struggling to establish himself in the pocket.
At 34 years old, Matthews is also approaching the latter stages of his NFL career. The Falcons must begin evaluating their long-term plans at offensive tackle, especially as they consider how to build a more consistent offensive line.
How much longer can Matthews remain Atlanta’s starting left tackle, and should the organization begin preparing for his eventual replacement? A strong finish would provide some reassurance that he can continue serving as a reliable starter.
Divine Deablo could be facing an important stretch of games as the Falcons evaluate the future of their linebacker room.
Atlanta brought Deablo in to provide experience and stability at linebacker, but injuries have made it difficult for him to consistently remain on the field. His 2026 season has already included a forearm injury suffered against the Chicago Bears in Week 6, forcing him to miss two consecutive games. Although he returned against Cincinnati in Week 9, the injury continued to be an issue heading into the Kansas City matchup, where he was listed as doubtful.
Deablo’s availability has become an important storyline, especially with two rookies taking advantage of their opportunities in his absence.
Kendal Daniels and Harold Perkins Jr. have emerged as two of Atlanta’s most promising young defensive players. Daniels has taken over the defensive play-calling responsibilities and has shown impressive instincts, athleticism, and playmaking ability.
Against San Francisco, Daniels recorded 11 tackles, nine solo tackles, an interception, and a fumble recovery. His emergence has been particularly impressive, considering he entered the season expected to develop behind Atlanta’s veteran linebackers.
Perkins has also made a strong impression. The sixth-round selection has recorded 30 solo tackles, two sacks, and a 79.6 PFF coverage grade through the bye week. His ability to contribute against the run, rush the passer, and defend in coverage has given Atlanta another intriguing young option.
With both rookies continuing to develop, Deablo’s place in the linebacker rotation is becoming an increasingly interesting question. With his contract set to expire at the end of the year, he’s not doing himself any favors with free agency approaching.
The Falcons need dependable production and availability from their linebackers. While Deablo brings valuable NFL experience, the organization must consider whether his injury concerns and the emergence of its young talent could change how the position is handled moving forward.

title: ESPN Analyst Delivers Blunt Verdict on Falcons' Quarterback Future
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons are into the bye week at 3-7, but still have plenty of questions to answer over the final seven games of the season. The playoffs are still (theoretically) in play for this team , so they still have plenty to play for. However, finding these solutions should be top of mind , with none bigger than who plays quarterback in 2027.
The conversation over whether Michael Penix Jr. can be the long-term answer has dominated the conversation all season. But with seven games remaining, the Falcons appear no closer to finding a definitive answer. At this point, that uncertainty is becoming a problem in itself.
ESPN ’s Ben Solak attempted to tackle this question in his weekly evaluations of the league. His take aligns with what many now believe as we hit the second half of the NFL season: “I think ... the Falcons need a new starting QB in 2027,” Solak wrote.
Solak pointed to injury concerns surrounding Penix, who has only 20 starts. He has delivered impressive performances this season, including against the Packers, Saints, and 49ers, but has struggled to maintain that level consistently.
His arm strength is undeniable, but that alone is not enough to justify a fourth year to see if he can figure it out.
Solak correctly points out the timeline the Falcons have set for themselves after paying Bijan Robinson, Drake London, and Kyle Pitts Sr. This talented offensive core is entering its prime, but those investments mean little if the team cannot find a quarterback who can consistently get them the football.
The Falcons don't necessarily need to have their long-term answer figured out this season, but they cannot afford to let too many more pass without meaningful progress at the position.
Penix has started eight games this season, and the Falcons are 3-5. He has an NFC Offensive Player of the Week to his credit, but the recent struggles have been central to the team's three-game losing streak . Overthrows, interceptions, slow starts, and struggles against pressure have hurt his consistency and cost the Falcons games.
Head coach Kevin Stefanski made it clear that the organization evaluates its players weekly.
“Big picture, just our evaluations of our players are weekly and season-long, of course. But in terms of anything past that, I'm not really thinking about that,” Kevin Stefanski said. “But anytime you're evaluating any player, you're taking everything into consideration, circumstances and whatnot.”
But the numbers have not been in Penix’s favor. Down-to-down accuracy was a top priority coming into the year, and it hasn't improved as much as many hoped. He has an 18.4% off-target rate on quick passes this season, the second-worst mark in the NFL. His QBR (63.6) is also well below the league average (76.0) on those throws.
Solak called Penix “a bit robotic mechanically” and lacking a “particularly fluid build.” As a result, he telegraphs those quick throws, giving defenders time to respond. Solak also sees a quarterback who struggles to throw to the right side of the field, citing an off-target rate of 25.3% when throwing to the right compared to 18.8% to the left.
“So quick-game throws are tough, and half the field is cut off,” he wrote.
More concerning, his biggest strength has recently exposed another weakness.
Penix’s big arm helps mitigate those issues, but those routes take time and require a quarterback who can hold onto the ball a bit longer. With his issues standing tall in the pocket against looming pressure (he is 22nd out of 37 QBs in the league in EPA per unpressured dropback compared to 36th in EPA per pressured dropback), these plays are almost impossible to call consistently.
Teams have recognized this and have dialed up blitzes. Even though they aren’t hitting him (his 4.7 contacts per game is the league low and his QB pressure rate is second-lowest), Penix rushes through his progressions because of the looming defenders and misses his targets.
When defenders do get to him, Penix has a 39.1 passer rating and 35% completion percentage (63 attempts), both NFL-worst.
His teammates backed him up on Sunday after the loss, but that doesn't mean the front office will this spring. Penix has seven games to change that perception, but barring a turnaround after the bye week, the Falcons could start over at quarterback in 2027.
Garrett Chapman is a sports broadcaster, writer, and content creator based in Atlanta. He has several years of experience covering the Atlanta sports scene, college football, Georgia high school football, recruiting for 24/7 Sports, and the NFL. You can also hear him on Sports Radio 92.9 The Game.

title: Atlanta Falcons Face Defining Moment Entering Bye Week at 3-7
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons enter their bye week at 3-7 following three consecutive losses, including a disappointing 35-13 defeat against the Kansas City Chiefs . With seven games remaining, Atlanta is running out of time to turn its season around.
After entering the year with expectations of competing for the NFC South title, the Falcons have struggled to find consistency on both sides of the football. Their 201 points scored rank 24th in the NFL, while their 258 points allowed rank 23rd. Head coach Kevin Stefanski and his coaching staff have an important opportunity to evaluate the team’s shortcomings and find solutions.
Atlanta’s biggest issue has been establishing an offensive identity . The Falcons have scored just 20.1 points per game and converted 34.4% of their third downs, ranking 27th in the league.
Michael Penix Jr. has completed 60.7% of his passes for 1,730 yards, 10 touchdowns, and seven interceptions through eight games. His inconsistency has contributed to Atlanta’s offensive struggles , particularly against defenses that force the Falcons to rely on the passing game.
Bijan Robinson remains one of Atlanta’s biggest strengths, totaling 951 rushing yards and six touchdowns on 185 carries. He is averaging 5.1 yards per carry, but the team’s rushing production has declined significantly. Atlanta averaged 181 rushing yards per game through its first four games but has averaged just 101.8 over its last six.
Drake London has also been productive, recording 50 receptions for 801 yards and one touchdown. Jahan Dotson has added 416 receiving yards, while Kyle Pitts leads the team with four receiving touchdowns. Finding ways to maximize those weapons needs to be a priority coming out of the bye.
The defense has struggled to provide consistent support, allowing 25.8 points and 358.2 total yards per game. Opponents have also scored touchdowns on 67.6% of their red zone trips against Atlanta.
There have been individual bright spots. Za’Darius Smith leads the Falcons with 4.5 sacks, while Kendal Daniels leads the team with 43 tackles. Harold Perkins Jr. has contributed 31 tackles, giving Atlanta another young defender to develop during the second half of the season.
Stefanski accepted responsibility following the loss to Kansas City, saying, “The responsibility falls on me.” However, accountability must eventually translate into better results.
The bye week gives Atlanta time to evaluate its personnel, playcalling and overall approach before returning to action.
Despite its 3-7 record, Atlanta still has an opportunity to compete in the NFC South. The Falcons face Minnesota, Detroit, Cleveland, and Washington before closing the season with three consecutive divisional matchups against Tampa Bay, New Orleans, and Carolina.
Those final games could determine whether Atlanta has a chance to salvage its season.
The talent is there, but the numbers show how much improvement is needed. The bye week provides an opportunity to reset, get healthy, and establish a new direction. With seven games remaining, Atlanta has one final opportunity to show that its season is not over.
Darius has a Master's in Communications from Georgia State and has previous experience covering the Atlanta Falcons with 3 Point Conversion and covering the NFL with On SI.

title: What's Gone Right and Wrong for Tommy Rees, Atlanta Falcons Offense
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons entered 2026 as a transition year. The team had a new general manager, new head coach, and new offensive coordinator. But with limited draft picks and very little salary cap room, the personnel, especially on offense, looked pretty much the same.
Tommy Rees took over as offensive coordinator and play caller for the Falcons and Jahan Dotson came in as a starting wide receiver. But those were the only real changes made on that side of the ball.
The big question coming into the year was whether the Atlanta Falcons could find their franchise quarterback in Michael Penix Jr. or not.
Penix has had his ups and downs this season, not totally surprising for a player coming into the season on a repaired ACL and 12 starts to his name. But with seven games left in the season, the jury is still out on him.
ESPN asked its legion of beat writers what has gone right and what has gone wrong for each team, and Marc Ramondi epitomized the Jekyll and Hyde nature of this team by naming running back Bijan Robinson and Penix in both categories. He points out that Robinson is third in the NFL in rushing yards and has the most runs of 20 or more yards of anyone in the NFL.
"The Falcons staff has also successfully made Michael Penix Jr. into an under-center quarterback after he spent almost all of the past two seasons and college working mostly out of the pistol," Ramondi wrote on ESPN .
Penix has thrown for 1,730 yards and 10 touchdowns, while throwing seven interceptions in eight starts (4 of which came in the Tampa monsoon). However, teams have figured out that if they blitz Penix, crash the pocket, they can not only limit Robinson by stopping him before he gets started, but Penix isn't going to make them pay for bringing extra defenders.
"Penix has been poor under pressure, and Rees and company have not yet figured out a way to mitigate the problem. Penix has the worst completion percentage in the league while under pressure (34.9%) and the second-worst success rate (21.5%)," Ramondi continued.
Kill two birds (no pun intended) with one stone. Defenses have one target. If they aim about five yards behind center, they'll either find Penix trying to pass or Penix handing off to Robinson. The pre-snap and post-snap reads aren't punishing defensive coordinators for taking a risk sending six defenders into the offensive backfield.
The Falcons have a bye week to try and figure it out. The Chiefs blitzed the Falcons on nearly every play, and their bllitz percentage on the season is just 28.7%.
Atlanta faces the Minnesota Vikings next week, who blitz on 67.3% of defensive plays, nearly double the New York Giants, who come in second at 37.5% (the Falcons are 28th at 19.8%).
Questions about Penix's ability to handle pressure have already led some national pundits to predict the Falcons will be in the quarterback market in April's NFL Draft . If he's going to stop that from happening, he and Rees need to figure out how to have some success against pressure.
The Vikings present the ultimate test on Sunday, November 29th.
Scott is an Atlanta-based sports media professional with stints as Director of Scouting of Scout.com, VP of Content Production at Sports Illustrated, and Managing Editor at CBS Interactive / 247 Sports, among others.

title: Atlanta Falcons Move On from Michael Penix Jr. in ESPN's Latest Mock Draft
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons came into the season with their biggest question being at quarterback. Could Michael Penix Jr. or Tua Tagovailoa show enough this season to solidify himself as the quarterback of the future for this team?
We have a definitive answer on the Tagovailoa part of that question, but after 10 weeks of the 2026 season and a 3-7 record, the jury is still out on Penix. Maybe it shouldn't be all that surprising that a quarterback with 12 career starts, coming off a season-ending knee injury, would have ups and downs this season.
But three years is a lifetime in the NFL, and Penix is running out of time to lock down the Falcons starting quarterback job in 2027.
ESPN's Jordan Reid has already seen enough, and has the Falcons taking Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr with the No. 8 overall pick, a spot in the draft order made popular by former head coach Arthur Smith.
Reid's reasoning for selecting Carr almost sounds like he's course-correcting for the Falcons and choosing the anti-Penix option.
"Carr is an instinctive passer who consistently has answers and has already been given considerable autonomy in Notre Dame's offense," Reid wrote on ESPN . "He doesn't have the high-end traits of some passers in the class (picture a more mobile Kirk Cousins), but he is polished in many of the skills that are essential to playing the position."
Reid may have hurt his case with Falcons fans by mentioning Cousins, but I've also heard Carr described as a more toolsy Brock Purdy. Purdy didn't have the traits to get drafted in the first round (or almost drafted at all), but he's loaded with all of the "skills essential to playing the position."
At 3-7 with the Minnesota Vikings and Detroit Lions on deck, the Falcons are facing 3-9 in the face and could end up with a higher selection than No. 8. Drew Mestemaker is the only quarterback Reid has taken higher than Carr, going to the Jets at No. 2 overall after a trade with the Chargers.
The Dolphins (No. 3), Eagles (No. 5), and Cardinals (No. 7) will also be threats to take a quarterback, and the Chargers (No. 4) could be a trade-down candidate for a team behind the Falcons looking for a quarterback.
If the Falcons stay put, but don't like the quarterback options available when they're on the clock, offensive tackle, wide receiver, and cornerback are glaring needs. Indiana wide receiver Charlie Becker goes No. 4 to the Chargers. Notre Dame cornerback Leonard Moore is selected by the Jets (ironically, with a pick they got from the Colts for Sauce Gardner) at No. 6. Offensive tackle Jordan Seaton of LSU is taken by the Cardinals at No. 7.
Utah offensive tackle Zereoue Williams is an intriguing prospect still on the board when the Falcons pick and goes to the Texans at No. 9.
General manager Ian Cunningham took the job in January when the Falcons were light on draft picks and low on available salary cap. That won't be a problem this offseason.
However, he's got a lot of holes to fill on a team that is headed towards its ninth consecutive losing season.
