title: By Ravens' Standards, Jesse Minter's Defense Is Historically Bad. Bottom 3 And Sinking
full_text:
Part of what made Jesse Minter such an irresistible choice for Ravens general manager and team president Sashi Brown, besides him being a newbie and incredibly malleable and willing to work cheap, was his deep ties to this organization.
He had worked here as a very young assistant on defense, under Wink Martindale (who isn’t shy about detailing DeCosta’s role in this franchise’s collapse ), and understood the loftiest of standards set for Baltimore on defense. Minter had mastered the fabric and schemes of the past that would allow him to erase the many mistakes of former coordinator Zach Orr (who, what do you know, was a superior coach of this defense than Minter has proven to be).
DeCosta and Brown and owner Steve Bisciotti bathed themselves in their past and claimed Minter as one of their own and anointed him capable of leading the franchise to the Super Bowl in his first year here – despite a staff of relatives, neophytes and college buddies – because it was potential Hall of Fame head coach John Harbaugh and his expensive staff there holding this roster and this franchise back. That's the parable they pushed.
So, one can assume, nothing laid out in this article could surprise Minter, an expert on the Ravens’ defensive history who already has a uniquely bleak place in it and is making a strong case to be fired after one year on the job, with Sunday’s debacle to the Panthers the latest example of how ill-equipped he appears to run an NFL defense at this point, let alone an entire team. He can’t manage personnel on special teams, he can’t manage timeouts and he is commanding one of the most embarrassing defenses in the history of this franchise.
The Panthers created explosive plays against Minter like everyone else does, and when they needed a late drive for a field goal to take a 35-33 lead, of course they got it. It's time for Anthony Weaver, or someone else, to call plays.
"I'm the head coach, and I'm calling the plays on defense," Minter said in asking for blame (though also deflected plenty to the offense and special teams when his D is the culprit. Here’s who bad this defense, through its first 11 games, ranks with every other in Ravens history.
Minter has already allowed 294 points. Only two teams in franchise history have allowed more in 11 games; the 1996 team that had just relocated from Cleveland, was scrambling and had most of the resources in the offensive side of the ball. The other was 2007, a team that totally fell apart, looked a lot like this one, and got Brian Billick, the first Super Bowl winning coach in franchise history, fired.
That 2007 team also lost six straight games, with Minter’s team becoming just the third in franchise history to do so a mere 11 games in. That 2007 team – a coach killer, forcing Bisciotti into action for the first time – lost nine in a row, a franchise low. Minter’s outfit, overseen by a front office that is becoming a laughingstock (the Daniel Jones pursuit is a chef’s kiss ), seems quite capable of that and might not win again.
Minter’s Ravens have the third-worst point differential (-52) through 11 games in franchise history.
Minter’s defense is truly horrific and broken in the second half, where the lack of adjustments and tactical shifts have utterly undermined any chance to win and led them to blow a double-digit lead for the fifth time this season (they lost four of those games, continuing the nastiest of trades that dates back to DeCosta taking over for legendary GM Ozzie Newsome). But in its totality, this pass defense has been a joke.
Minter is supposed to have the secret sauce like former Ravens coordinator Mike Macdonald to win up front with light boxes and flood the quadrants of the field where the QB is most likely to pass with willing defenders. Worked with the Chargers; been a disaster here. he has a team-record $160M defensive payroll and none of his big-money players is having a strong season.
The Ravens, despite facing pedestrian-or-worse QBs (like Bryce Young Sunday), have allowed an opposing QB rating of 96.6 – that’s third worst through 11 games in franchise history. They not only do not get any plays on the ball – TJ Tampa registered their first interception by a corner all season on Sunday – but they can’t even prevent big plays despite teams pushing the ball downfield on them.
Opposing QBs are completing 66% of their passes (third worst through 11 games). They have just 22 sacks – a grand total of two from alleged season-changing “closer” Trey Hendrickson HYPR EX – which is fifth lowest in Ravens history through this point in the season. Ten total takeaways for a mastermind coordinator who was going to put players in pristine position is damning.
Sunday was the same typical garbage – middle of field wide open, no one defending the slot – and Minter had no answers for it. He tried putting Kyle Hamilton back deeper in coverage and he gave up a 35-yard pass and did nothing on the football.
Young was 14/18 for 143 yds with a TD (118.3 rating) throwing to the middle of the field and 12/14 for 146 yds (110.1 rating) throwing to the slot. It’s no coincidence that Minter’s operation has so much in common with the 1996 edition that was just trying to get through the relocation and the one that cost Billick his job.
It merits a similar outcome.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Jesse Minter Exposed Again In Ravens' Sixth-Straight Loss: Key Takeaways From Another Debacle
full_text:
The Ravens season was summed up in one stretch of the first half of this game.
Their inability to seize the moment, their predilection for undermining their own success, and the utter cluelessness of this novice coaching staff far too often (in this case not making obvious adjustments on defense and special teams) dooms them week after week, and their failure to take a commanding lead caught up to them again.
The Ravens lost their sixth straight game – something that’s happened in one season only twice prior in franchise history – despite a fast start in a 35-33 defeat to the Panthers in Carolina. Rookie head coach Jesse Minter is making a compelling case for his staff being fired after one season on the job , general manager Eric DeCosta is getting ridiculed around the NFL (with a failed attempt to land broken QB Daniel Jones the latest head scratcher - and this team (4-7) might not win another game.
Lamar Jackson is not coming back to save them, this season or maybe ever again , and one sequence in this game summed up the Jesse Minter Experience (he's allowed 33 points or more in four of the last five games):
In the span of around three minutes of play, with the Ravens holding an early 12-7 lead after getting a safety early and an explosive touchdown off a flea flicker, things got weird, the Panthers were able to keep this a close game, and that did not bode well for the worst second-half team in the NFL.
Justice Hill was about to finish a long run for a touchdown when the ball was punched out of his hands at the two and rolled out of the endzone for a touchback and a turnover. The defense forced a rare three-and-out, and then struggling return man LaJohntay Wester muffed the punt for another turnover. Carolina scored almost immediately, then Devontez Walker returned the ensuing kickoff for a TD, and a 19-14 lead, but the defense would get rolled the rest of the way in another embarrassing outing for that horrible unit.
Back-up quarterback Jacoby Brissett (276 passing yards with a TD) was once again better than anyone could have expected, but it wasn’t enough to buck this season collapsing, with another Derrick Henry fourth-down fumble contributing to this latest debacle (he scored a late TD and hit the back of his head hard, checked for a concussion).
When Minter needed a stop late, his unit gave up a field goal, same as it ever was. He should be running out of time for a team that billed itself as a top Lombardi Trophy contender.
"At the end of the day we're on the field with the lead and we didn't hold it," Minter said. "So I take responsibility for that."
Minter sells out to take away big plays yet still gets exposed and unmask every week – mostly be pedestrian offenses – despite all his efforts. The Panthers' attack was fueled by big plays. Their first scoring drive featured consecutive big plays, Carolina had 10 plays of 10 yards or more through three quarters and four of 25 yards or more – it’s been obvious for weeks Minter needs to relinquish defensive play calling duties and perhaps this will cement it.
Receiver Jalen Coker beat Kyle Hamilton in coverage on an underthrown ball for 35 yards and flea flicker for 25 yards on the next play produced a TD and cut Baltimore’s lead to 12-7. Bryce Young came out firing in the second half with big shots to Tet McMillan and Darren Waller and only an interception by TJ Tampa (first by a Ravens corner all season) in the endzone, with excellent job trailing McMillan, kept this from getting out of hand sooner. It was bad on the ground too (more on that below).
"I'm the head coach and I'm calling the plays on defense," Minter said, repeatedly putting the onus on himself in his post-game remarks.
"I really don't know what to say at this point, honestly," said linebacker/safety Hamilton, who played more coverage in this game with little positive impact.
On the bright side, Mike Green continues to flash breakout pass-rush impact.
Every unit has been bad for long stretches of this season and special teams was brutal Sunday, even with Devontez Walker taking a kick return back for a touchdown.
If this coaching staff had a clue, Wester would have been benched after muffing a punt early in the game. He had made no impact since being drafted and doesn’t field the ball cleanly often enough and even after swinging the game in that regard, with a turnover, he wasn’t done. Wester totally misplayed another punt at the end of the first half; it bounced off his helmet and was nearly a scoop-and-score for Carolina.
Baltimore recovered at the 2, but it cost precious field position and the Ravens ended up stalling at midfield.
But the rot went beyond that. The Ravens kept giving up big returns on kick coverage units. Rookie Ethan Burke had a bad penalty on teams late in the first half. And their specialists have been an issue on and off all season.
The one thing this defense clung to was that it looked okay against the run. Of course, they haven’t faced many teams all season that can run the ball. And they entered Week 10 having been among the least run on defenses in the NFL. OF course, that changed with the Chargers churning them up and down the field for 160 yards and the Panthers picked up where LA left off.
Without top defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike, and with $60M “closer” Trey Hendrickson (two sacks all season; just three pressures Sunday) bad against the run the Panthers believed they could run the ball off the edge and up the middle and they were correct, especially as they shifted in not more 12 personnel (multiple tight ends) in the second quarter. They were able to key both Chuba Hubbard and Travis Etienne sprung for big runs in critical spots, and this is yet another hole Minter – totally overmatched to this point – is going to have to try to fix on the fly.
Hubbard came out of the half with a seven-yard burst and then again gutted Baltimore up the middle for 26 yards and he finished the drive with an easy, two-yard touchdown to cap the drive and five the Panthers a 29-26 lead.
Teams will absolutely be attacking Baltimore on the ground as weather becomes a factor and the Ravens do not have any more dome games or warm-weather road games, so buckle up. Carolina’s backs ran 14 times for 79 yards in the first half; Hubbard had a 19-yard TD blast off left tackle and Etienne took a carry inside the tackles for 18.
Carolina finished with 149 rushing yards and Hubbard had 120 himself.
The Ravens offensive line was embarrassed Monday night in every aspect of play. And no rushing yards in the first half and 15 carries for 16 yards in that game led to quite the inquiry leading up to this game.
The run blocking was much improved, the Ravens got Henry going on outside for the first time in weeks and struggling offensive coordinator Declan Doyle leaned into many of the tweaks we suggested – more Zay Flowers deception behind the line of scrimmage, more inside sprint plays for Hill, and more screens all around.
The Ravens had 12 carries for 116 yards in the first half, Brissett was able to crank up the play-action passing off of those looks and this was a truly balanced offense for the first time since Jackson was injured at the end of the first half in Week 4.
Henry finished with 94 rushing yards (7.2 yards/carry) and Hill added 90 scrimmage yards.
Doyle has no answers in the second half of games, once he gets beyond his early scripts.
The razzle-dazzle that worked early in the game fell flat after the half, he didn’t lean into the run game enough that had established itself in the early going and this team didn’t register a first down in the third quarter until just before it expired.
Baltimore hadn’t led at all in three games entering this, and the lack of adjustments in-game have been staggering. The Ravens entered this game having scored the second fewest points in the NFL after the half (64) and during the five-game slide their second-half scoring amounted to: 10, 7, 3, 0, 0. They managed seven points Sunday after…

title: Four Pivotal Ravens Matchups to Watch vs. Panthers
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens' Week 11 bout against the Carolina Panthers could ultimately be decided by battles between specific position groups or individual players outperforming their counterparts on the other side of the ball.
In the team's second game with journeyman veteran Jacoby Brissett at center after he nearly led them to a comeback win in his first, they're entering this matchup as understandable underdogs following last week's inexcusable loss to the previously winless Los Angeles Chargers .
If the Ravens prevail, they will improve to 5-6 and will still be in last place in the AFC North standings since they're the only team without a division win. Here are the four matchups that can either make or break this game:
With four-time Pro Bowler Marlon Humphrey deactivated for this game , the Ravens will be going up against the talented wideout tandem of Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker without one of their top playmaking corners. They still have their No. 1 player at the position in third-year pro Nate Wiggins, and playing opposite him on the perimeter will be a two-man rotation of 10-year veteran Chidobe Awuzie and third-year pro T.J. Tampa , a young player who fans and pundits have been clamoring to see more of for weeks.
The Ravens' third-year pro and starting right tackle will go up against the reigning NFC Defensive Player of the Week, who primarily lines up at SAM. In his first game back from injury since Week 6, Phillips was an absolute menace off the edge for the Panthers, recording five total tackles, including four solos and three for a loss, a strip-sack, and a fumble recovery. Rosengarten is coming off a rough game in pass protection in which he allowed a team-high six pressures, according to Pro Football Focus , so he'll have his hands full again and will need to step his game up to help keep Brissett upright more often than not.
While the Ravens aren't going up against one of the top overall rushing attacks in the league in this game, they are tasked with trying to limit one of its best and most dynamic running backs. Hubbard leads the Panthers and ranks eighth in the NFL with 711 rushing yards and ranks ninth among all players in both scrimmage yards (958) and touchdowns (nine). This means the Ravens' off-ball linebacker trio of Roquan Smith, Trenton Simpson and Teddye Buchanan could find themselves matched up with the six-year veteran in the hole at the line of scrimmage, in coverage out in space, or in the backfield on a blitz pickup, and will need to make plays in all three instances to excel in this game.
Carolina has been Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde when it comes to defending the opposing team's rushing attacks this year. Against poor running games, they are stout and have held five of their nine opponents to under 100 rushing yards, but in the other four games when they've faced more potent rushing offenses, they've allowed over 250 yards on the ground twice and an average of 209.5.
The Ravens' ground game without Lamar Jackson has been anything but prolific in all but one of the six games he's missed, especially during this current skid, when they've averaged just 86.8 rushing yards a game. However, if offensive coordinator Declan Doyle and his much-maligned offensive line can find a way to establish the run with any sort of consistency, five-time Pro Bowl running back Derrick Henry could do some serious damage and take a lot of the onus from Brissett to have to put the entire offense on his back again in just his second start for the team.

title: Ravens Reported Pursuit Of Daniel Jones Latest Example Of A Desperate And Reaching Front Office
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens have been exposed as a desperate, panicked front office for months now.
That’s not a new revelation – from bailing on the Maxx Crosby trade in March to making a ridiculous deal for struggling-and-concussed offensive lineman Cam Jurgens on Oct. 7 – and with their season spiraling into the abyss Ravens fans got a double dose of these realities on Sunday.
According to ESPN, Ravens failing general manager Eric DeCosta  – bizarrely lauded for “batting .800” in his personnel moves by increasingly-checked out owner Steve Bisciotti in January - offered a fourth round pick that could also end up a fifth-round selection to the Colts for quarterback Daniel Jones, one of the worst starters in the NFL on a bloated contract who is clearly still hobbled by an Achilles tear a year ago. Meantime, the struggling team facing an arduous rebuild with one of the worst rosters, payrolls and salary caps in the NFL, refuses to play many of its rookie and young players, seemingly hoping a few meaningless wins down the stretch keep people employed in Owings Mills.
This franchise isn’t fooling anyone, anymore , previously sympathetic landing spots in the media have been forced to report and comment on the gross inadequacies of this organization. Just this week the Ravens opted to bench one of their highest-paid players (only after Mayor Brandon Scott publicly chastised him), a social media account tied to Lamar Jackson, at least to some degree, posted video of all the QB injuries suffered behind DeCosta’s tragic offensive line this season, and around the league there is a growing sense that Jackson would like to be elsewhere in 2027 .
Amid all of that, after Jackson and back-up Snoop Huntley headed to Injured Reserve with long-term injuries, DeCosta thought Jones would make his team better in the immediate future. He ended up landing journeyman Jacoby Brissett – who got demoted in Arizona just like Jones would in Indianapolis – but at a time when trusted evaluators and general managers around the league were telling me how shattered and bad Jones was, Baltimore’s reported push to land him begs even more questions of a front office that seems to be losing touch with reality.
The Ravens are short of draft capital in the next two drafts already, have short-and-long-term holes at premium positions throughout the roster, and Jones carries a nasty contract that alone should have been a non-starter. And this coaching staff is looking overwhelmed and naive.
The fact that Jones has $6.5M in 2027 fully guaranteed, and the oft-injured player had $10M in injury guarantees for next season, is part of why many believe he may clear waivers. Then there is the fact that his legs – a massive part of his game – have been rendered mute by his Achilles – and he is a woefully inaccurate passer who has been largely terrible in his career outside of one half season with the Giants and the start of the 2025 season.
Jones ranks bottom three in every critical QB metric this season and the Ravens saw firsthand how washed he was in Week 1. He cannot complete 58% of his passes despite never pushing the ball downfield, he has 7 TDs to 13 INTs and a 65.4 rating which ranks worst among every qualified QB in the NFL.
Execs around the NFL were shocked the Colts have Jones a ridiculous, multi-year contract early in 2026, when interested around the league was muted at best, and they are even more stupefied the Colts didn’t dump this contract for anything they could. What no one is surprised about is that Jones landed on waivers with Anthony Richardson getting a shot with the Colts; it would have made more sense for DeCosta to pursue that young, athletic, recent first-round pick than Jones.
NFL analysts who have joined us on “The Daily Flock” have been bemoaning the descent of this front office since its peak under legendary GM Ozzie Newsome – Amy Trask, Marty Hurney, Phil Simms, Brian Baldinger, Bucky Brooks, Marvin Lewis, among others – and the Ravens clearly should have made some changes to their personnel department when they fired potential Hall of Fame head coach John Harbaugh, leaving Bisciotti to ponder overarching questions this offseason.
“That’s a bad football team,” one NFL exec who has advanced the Ravens told me before a recent game. “Bad roster. We watched them film, now, that team doesn’t play with a full effort all the time. There’s some quitting going on there. Bad front office. Panic moves … They are going to keep losing football games.”
Jones would have only made it worse. It took one of a very few front offices worse than Baltimore’s – the Colts have an interim GM – to save them from themselves.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Free-Falling Ravens Refuse To Embrace Youth Again In Their Week 11 Inactives
full_text:
The Ravens refuse to lean into many of their young players despite a five-game losing streak that has relegated their playoff odds to some of the worst in football.
Baltimore (4-6) is in Carolina Sunday trying to right its season with a compromised roster and a coaching staff that some believe could be one-and-done , yet still they are benching rookies who could offer something at positions of need. The Ravens traveled to this game already without two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson, almost certain not to play again this season if ever for the Ravens again, while $19M corner Marlon Humphrey was left at home for making disparaging remarks about Baltimore on his podcast last week amid a season where he has been a bottom-five starting corner in the NFL, again .
Top defensive lineman Nnamdi Madubuike (hamstring) was also ruled out and seems unlikely to play until after the Week 13 bye. Supposed $60M “closer” Trey Hendrickson , who was overpaid by general manager Eric DeCosta to elevate this defense by a failing front office, has been far less effective since having finger surgery than he was while playing through the painful injury. Premier defensive weapon Kyle Hamilton has been bemoaning his own play recently and 2026 first-round pick Malaki Starks, a free safety, has been one of the worst players in coverage in the NFL regardless of position.
You might think with all of that going on, and with the least-experienced coaching staff in the NFL , and after keeping 10 rookies on their season-opening roster, that that the Ravens would be doing all they could to look at as many youngsters as possible, but like most things regarding this franchise, they refuse to embrace that reality.
The Ravens, on Friday, also ruled out starting safety Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) who has made no impact after being one of their offseason signings who was supposed to provide value. Their other inactive players were surprising for anyone who has watched them closely now and is interested in their immediate future.
Rookie “Joker” Adam Randall (fifth round), who should provide versatility and some new wrinkles at multiple positions, is back off Injured Reserve, but was scratched from what could have been his NFL debut. Baltimore is averaging just 3.7 yards/carry during its slump with rookie coordinator Declan Doyle under fire .  Receiver Elijah Sarratt (fourth round) continues to see no action and young offensive lineman Emery Jones was also scratched.
The Ravens drafted 11 players and kept 10 of them in the organization, including the practice squad, and also had two undrafted players make the team – edge Ethan Burke and quarterback Joe Fagnano. They have received virtually no real contributions from the entire class in a lost season (the Ravens and Orioles are tragically similar).
Despite having a suspect defensive line and being without Madubuike, the did not elevate seventh-round pick Rayshaun Benny from the practice squad. Sarratt, a on a desperate offense, has run just 11 routes all season and has one catch. Even after their season began to spiral after blowing a double-digit lead in the second half to lose to the Browns and former offensive coordinator Todd Monken in week 5, the Ravens continue to operate like they can win now (reports of their trade offer for Daniel Jones are shameful).
Monken will garner NFL Coach of the Year consideration and has the Browns on a playoff path despite being given virtually no chance to reach the postseason, while rookie head coach Jesse Minter’s Ravens had the best odds in the AFC of going to the Super Bowl and might not win another game.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Four Ravens X-Factors For Clash vs. Panthers
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens will continue the 2026 regular season with a road game in Week 11 against the Carolina Panthers . Going up against a fellow sub- .500 team, the difference in the game could come down to how an individual player performs when it matters most or over the course of the game, by capitalizing on opportunities when presented with them.
With a win, the Ravens would improve to 5-6 and would still be last in the AFC North division standings, but would stay in the hunt for a wildcard playoff berth. A loss would tie for their longest losing streak since they lost six straight to close out the 2021 season after losing Lamar Jackson due to an ankle injury.
Here are four players who could wind up tilting the scales in favor of the Ravens and first-year head coach Jesse Minter.
While five-time Pro Bowl starter Derrick Henry is far from the reason the Ravens' ground game hasn't been able to get going, an influx of new blood into the backfield rotation and a break from the predictability of their norm could be the kind of spark they've been looking for and are desperately in need of . The fifth-round rookie, who was handpicked by team owner Steve Bisciotti himself , has spent the first 10 weeks of the regular season on injured reserve and was finally activated before his window closed earlier in the week. Randall is a former converted college receiver who could bring some of the best of both worlds that Henry and fellow veteran Justice Hill provide, rolled into one. He could also add some juice to the return game, an aspect of the Ravens' special teams that they've sorely needed more production from all year.
Even before the Ravens decided to deactivate four-time Pro Bowl starter Marlon Humphrey and leave him back in Baltimore for this game for disciplinary reasons , his fellow 10th-year veteran was cutting into his playing time as part of a regular rotation with third-year pro T.J. Tampa. Now it will be the Awuzie and Tampa show for a full game, lining up across from top outside corner Nate Wiggins against the Panthers as they face a formidable wide receiver tandem with Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker. As the more experienced of the two, Awuzie might get the starting nod and a slight edge in total defensive snaps played by the end of the game. He's been targeted 12 times in coverage and has allowed eight catches for 120 yards and a completion percentage of 66.7%.
Coming off his best game of the season, in which he showed a strong connection with new starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett and was a reliable possession target, the three-time Pro Bowler will likely be looked to do more of the same in this must-win game. He's another week removed from being fully recovered from a broken hand that hampered him early in the year and probably contributed to him being among the league leaders in drops through nine weeks. Andrews caught eight of his targets against the Chargers and finished as the team's leader in catches and with a season-high 82 receiving yards. The Ravens are going to need a repeat performance from the franchise legend and all-time leader in catches, receiving yards and touchdowns and maybe even more if they want to come out on top in this game.
With two-time Pro Bowler Nnamdi Madubuike out due to a hamstring injury , the Ravens are going to need their hulk of a nose tackle to be more than an upper-echelon run-stuffer in this game. While slowing down Panthers' standout running back Chuba Hubbard, who ranks eighth in the league in rushing yards, is a top priority, Jones is going to have to step up and be more of a penetrating presence as an interior pass rusher to keep undersized quarterback Bryce Young from climbing the pocket with quick pressures. After leading the team with a career-high five sacks last year, the fifth-year veteran has yet to log one through 10 games and only has four pressures and two hurries.

title: Four Storylines For Ravens' Matchup vs. Panthers
full_text:
Coming off their worst defeat of the season, in which they allowed the downtrodden Los Angeles Chargers to come into M&T Bank Stadium and leave with their first win , the Baltimore Ravens will be back on the road and looking to snap a five-game losing streak in Week 11 when they travel to take on the Carolina Panthers on Sunday.
Going up against a second straight team with a losing record, the Ravens currently have the worst record in the AFC North at 4-6 but have a chance to get back to a game of being .500 with a win.
There are several intriguing storylines surrounding this matchup between these two teams fighting to keep their fleeting playoff hopes alive. Here are the top four.
Ever since former Pro Bowl backup quarterback Tyler Huntley led the Ravens to an impressive win over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 5, the Ravens not only haven't won a game, but they've looked like one of the worst teams in the league over their last five games. During this incredibly rough stretch, they've averaged just under 13 points per game, allowed 28 points per game, and been shut out twice in the second half. Even the 20 points they managed to scrounge up against the Chargers in Jacoby Brissett's debut as the fourth Ravens starting quarterback looked like it was a chore.
This team has yet to play a complete game in which they executed at a high level and played complementary football this season. The defense has allowed opposing teams to start hot in each of their last three games; the offense has struggled to move the ball with any consistency or balance and special teams has seen three different kickers and poor performances from their kick/punt return and coverage units. In order for this team to start turning its fortunes around and give themselves a chance to win a game for the first time in over a month, they have to play off each other instead of holding each other back.
The most disappointing aspect of the Ravens' current skid, almost as much as the mounting losses themselves, has been their inability to move the ball on the ground with any efficiency or physicality. After averaging 164.4 rushing yards in their first five games, they've been held to under 100 yards in four of the last five, with a measly average of 86.8 yards per game. Their woeful performance against the Chargers was absolute rock bottom for this team's rushing attack, as they had zero net yards on the ground at halftime for the first time in franchise history and finished with 16 yards in 15 carries.
"Anytime you rush for 16 yards, and it's November, that's not going to win the game for you," offensive coordinator Declan Doyle said. "I felt like they beat us up physically. That was just the bottom line. There's no sugarcoating that; that's what showed up on tape. The tape is the truth. We have to play better."
As impressive as Brissett was operating the passing game after being on the team for less than two weeks since being acquired via trade, expecting him to drop back 50-plus times is not a recipe for success. It's clear that the Ravens don't have continuity or requisite skill sets along the offensive line to deploy a primary outside zone running scheme. Doyle should mix in some other concepts and be less predictable in his play-calling when it comes to the ground game going up against a Panthers' defense that is tied for the seventh-most rushing yards per attempt in the league.
The Ravens will be without three defenders they were counting on to play major roles in their success on that side of the ball this season when they take on Carolina. While two-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike and veteran safety Jaylinn Hawkins were ruled out due to knee and hamstring injuries, respectively, four-time Pro Bowl cornerback Marlon Humphrey was deactivated and left behind in Baltimore for comments on his podcast.
Although none of them have been playing up to their potential this year, Madubuike and Humphrey are two of the most experienced and well-compensated players at their respective positions on the team and the Panthers will certainly look to take advantage of their absences. In the trenches, the Ravens are going to need more from stud nose tackle Travis Jones and six-time Pro Bowl defensive end, Calais Campbell.
Humphrey had already been losing snaps to third-year pro T.J. Tampa and fellow 10-year veteran Chidobe Awuzie, and now they'll see even more action. This will mark Hawkins' fifth straight game missed, which means more action for the likes of second-year pro Keondre Jackson and veteran K'Von Wallace.
This matchup will pit two of the most penalized teams in the league against each other. The Panthers are ranked first with 87 penalties, are on pace to set the NFL single-season record and are coming off getting called for a franchise-record 17 flags for 152 yards in last week's overtime win over the New Orleans Saints.
The Ravens aren't too far behind them, with 80 penalties being the fourth-most in the league, and they lead the NFL in offensive infractions ranging from false starts to illegal shifts and delay of games, and encompassing ineligible man downfield and holds. Whichever team exercises the most discipline and isn't actively being its own worst enemy might ultimately have the edge in this game, and hopefully they don't combine for a flag-fest.

title: Top Three Reasons The Panthers Will Send The Ravens To A Sixth-Straight Defeat
full_text:
John Harbaugh spent 18 years as head coach of the Baltimore Ravens and lost six straight games in a season just once, at the end of 2021, with Lamar Jackson injured.
Jesse Minter is threatening to do that within his first 11 games on the job. Minter picked up Harbaugh’s nasty predilection for blowing double-digit leads in the second half of games and quickly made it his hallmark. He has failing units on offense, defense and special teams and it may stand to reason that Monday night, hosting the winless Chargers, was the last time Minter will be a favorite in his maiden campaign in the NFL; and that was a disaster.
The chatter around the league about Minter looking like a potential one-and-done head coach is only going to grow louder the deeper this rot goes, and Jackson is not going to throw another pass for him this season, or maybe, ever again (and Lamar Jackson Entertainment on social media is having a field day carving up this coaching staff and front office without mentioning them). This is a mentally soft football team, with a low football IQ and an overmatched general manager and coaching staff. They might not win another game the rest of the year.
It’s not just who you play, it’s when you play them. And the Panthers are catching these Ravens at the right time:
Carolina is right in the thick of the lowly NFC South “race” while the Ravens are going to finish last in the AFC North, they play like a team that is resigned to that fact, and the only question is how many games do they fall off the pace (they are the Orioles of the NFL, folks). If ever the Ravens were going to bow up and fight and show something, it would have been at home Monday and instead they immediately fell behind by two scores against a team that hasn’t had a lead all season.
If you watched anything Minter said or did this week – including finally disciplining bottom-five NFL starting corner Marlon Humphrey for inane comments on his podcast (and even then, only after Mayor Brandon Scott excoriated him) – and detect any signs of life or hope, you are a true believer. Way more than this locker room believes.
The Ravens are a heartless, directionless bunch until proven otherwise, and the Panthers are a winning team the last two years when Bryce Young starts at home (66% completions, 19 TDs to 9 INTS, 64.5 rating).
Neither of these coaching staffs are any good, though Dave Canales did get the Panthers to the playoffs last year. But the best friend of a novice head coach is the ability to grind the game down, shorten it on your terms, dominate time of possession and exert physical will on an opponent.
Yeah, that’s not the Ravens, not without Jackson being a genius on the field. Rookie offensive play caller Declan Doyle, way out of his depth without Jackson , told you just how physically weak his offensive line was this week, and if you think they’re going to respond by running through walls for this guy you haven’t been paying attention.
“I felt like they beat us up physically,” Doyle said of the Chargers, “and that was just the bottom line. There's no sugarcoating that. That's what showed up on tape, and the tape is the truth. So, we have to play better.”
Doubt this bodes well for him being able to run the ball well Sunday, it’s at 3.7 yards/carry the last six weeks and 2.7 trying to run under center and there is no reason to think Doyle will make the necessary adjustments in personnel and scheme to key the run.
Carolina, meantime is getting 100 scrimmage yards and touchdown per game out of Chuba Hubbard, and while teams up until the Chargers haven’t really tried to run on Baltimore much, that’s going to change as the weather changes and this front is now without its top tackle by a mile in Nnamdi Madubuike and its best edge-setting lineman by far (Tavius Robinson). Good luck.
Baltimore’s staff is at its worst once Doyle gets past his early script and when Minter’s unit gets a lead (but we don’t have to worry much about that anymore). This second-half operation is terrible, they couldn’t get enough done against the Chargers – the worst team in the NFL entering Week 10 by some margin – and the Panthers play well at home.
The Ravens have many new parts on offense, which shows up in giveaways, and their -6 turnover differential in the second half is tied for worst in the NFL. They have scored just 64 points in the second half, second-fewest in the NFL, while allowing 156 (the second most, just one fewer than Dallas). They are a disaster and as the game goes on, they shrink.
Carolina is a solid-enough second-half operation, with a +13 scoring margin and Young needs time to settle into the game sometimes. He’s going to enjoy throwing to Tet McMillan and his tight ends against this woeful secondary and they will find holes downfield. Maybe not quite as many as they would if Humphrey was still starting on the outside, but more than enough.

title: What To Expect From Jacoby Brissett In His Second Ravens Start Sunday
full_text:
The Ravens nearly got Jacoby Brissett knocked from the football game in his second series playing quarterback for them last week.
The journeyman starter, who will finish the season at QB if able to stay healthy with Lamar Jackson essentially done for the season , quickly showed he can provide a modicum of hope in the passing game but it also comes with serious limitations. And without time to throw, any chance rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle has of salvaging this campaign is down the drain .
There are also things Doyle can do to make life easier for him, and after getting blown up with multiple offensive linemen spun around and beat and pushed back into him , Brissett will surely lean into those options now having grasped from field level (and not just film) how desperate of a situation this is. Brissett will hang in there and try to create plays for others downfield, but Doyle must recalibrate himself and if they drop Brissett back 50 times again this game is not going to go well on the scoreboard or on next week’s injury report.
Here’s what to expect from Brissett in his second game with the Ravens:
We chronicled from the moment it was clear Baltimore was interested in Brissett who stood to gain the most from his arrival. He throws to TEs more than anyone else and has far and away his best success with those big targets … yet Matthew Hibner and Josh Cuevas, rookie TEs, combined for just 33 offensive snaps in his debut with all that passing.
That was silly, since Brissett was 11/11 on passes to TEs and he raised Mark Andrews’s career from the dead with his best game in over season-and-a-half. Rookie receiver Ja’Kobi Lane has size too, but he is raw and missed a ton of time and I would recommend getting into 12 and 13 personnel HYPER and letting Hibner and Cuevas run those seam routes from the slot.
Teams haven’t really tried to push the ball downfield with TEs against the Panthers. Brissett should. Getting an explosive play out of Hibner and Cuevas absolutely needs to be an objective in Week 11.
Running back Justice Hill carved out an immediate role in the pass game, and when he is your third-down back and best pass protector and your line stinks this bad, he’d better be on the field and available a bunch . Screens for Derrick Henry – not as adroit in space – went nowhere but Hill and rookie Adam Randall need to show up with targets.
If they don’t trust Randall is pass pro, get him in pony packages with Hill but use him more as a pass catcher while manning an internal stance in the offense. The screens to Zay Flowers behind the line of scrimmage can be pretty devastating too. Doyle was yammering about “five-man routes” this week; that’s silly. Make the most of 3-4 potential targets with misdirection and multiplicity in the pass game and help the OL while you are at it.
If Joe Fagnano (in the preseason, but still) can run to a spot and throw a screen back across his body to the far side, Brissett can do it better. Those concepts better get some run on Sunday.
The Ravens don’t have the weapons or the offensive line to sustain that much volume in the pass game. They need to stick with the run to keep the game close given their failing defense . Brissett needs to check into runs, they need to commit to heavy personnel to help the run and be willing to take play-action shots out of that.
If there is not a completion to a tight end for 25+ yards – or a few – out of heavy personnel looks in play action, something ain’t right. Sadly, lately, a lot ain’t been right about this crew, but Brissett is a gamer and he more than did his part on Monday. What he was asked to do was, in so many ways, misguided.
The overarching emphasis from this staff must be on finding ways to fight for 30 rushes in this game as a team, if not more, against a Panthers defense that is in the bottom six in the NFL in run defense Expected Points Added.

title: It's Time For These 5 Young Ravens Players To Get A More Meaningful Look
full_text:
The Ravens insisted on keeping 10 of the 11 players they drafted around into Thanksgiving.
It’s time to start playing them. Some, just getting active on game day and into some semblance of a rotation, and others need to be given a wide ramp to more meaningful playing time. Frankly, in a lost season amid a five-game losing streak with rampant issues on all sides of the ball, it’s time for a bunch of players on rookie contracts to be more empowered.
Rookie head coach Jesse Minter has been tasked with pretending this was a Super Bowl contender, and, if weighed against those expectations, is being questioned around the league as a potential one-and-done . His defense stinks and the offense, without Lamar Jackson, can’t run or throw the ball, and the bloated and overpaid roster is loaded with veterans who Minter cannot reach or get to perform anything close to the level at which they are being compensated .
Enough of all the BS about “accountability” and “telling the truth.” With $19M corner Marlon Humphrey embarrassing the franchise this week, getting called out by Mayor Brandon Scott , and then finally benched, it’s the perfect time for Minter to lean into youth. It better be about building a future and finding pieces for the future, because the present is as bad as it can get losing on Monday night at home to a winless team. A lot needs to change in Owings Mills and the obvious rebuild should be getting a jumpstart Sunday in Carolina with Jackson out for the season (trust me) and Humphrey suspended by the team and top defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike already ruled out with a hamstring injury.
These kids need to start getting a look, or a longer look:
Yeah, the Chargers were the rare team this season that invested any volume in their run game at all. I get that. But getting him on the field for just four snaps and not seeing him as someone with the potential to play regularly in this defense seems silly. Roquan Smith shouldn’t be playing every snap, maybe more Kyle Hamilton in coverage – with safety Jaylinn Hawkins still hurt – helps create a spot, too.
It’s not impossible for Buchanan and Trenton Simpson – who has made the case for a new contract with a breakout season – to be on the field more together. Slashing this kid’s role as he works back from ACL surgery, unless mandated by physical condition, would be foolish. Was one of very few youngsters to standout in 2025 and did so as a rookie.
Fellow-rookie Josh Cuevas has passed him by and is getting a chance to do more in the slot and run seam routes. Hibner should be faster and more explosive and play faster and more explosive and this offense should be living in 12 and 13 personnel. The fact that overpaid veteran Mark Andrews had his best game in two years shouldn’t deter from an effort to get the kid TEs on the field more with a quarterback in Jacoby Brissett who loves throwing to that position group.
The fact Hibner and Cuevas combined for 33 snaps on offense is fairly ridiculous and rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle is struggling mightily right now with concepts and formations .
We’ve been calling for him to start phasing Humphrey out on the boundary all year. Humphrey should have never been on this team in the first place. The Ravens love to create whisper campaigns about how great their mid-round picks are going to be, but then when they have to play, if general manager Eric DeCosta picked them, it’s usually bleak.
He should be a fit with Minter’s scheme but whatever he was showing in practice had to be ugly since it took Humphrey getting international scorn for his juvenile podcast in order to finally get Tampa on the field more.
Could be an interesting jack-of-all-trades piece at a time when the offensive roster is flat. Can he create for himself in space? Let’s find out, because this broken offensive line can’t do anything for anyone in the run game or the pass game. Catch balls out of the backfield, get him involved in pony packages . Let’s go.
Remember him? Took him near the end of the draft. Been on the practice squad. With Madubuike out, let’s start taking a look. Madubuike is only signed for one more year, anyway, and that neck injury was a big deal. Travis Jones is a guy who can help out, but he’s not special and playing 40-year-old Calais Campbell in a lost season ahead of this kid is silly.
Evaluators I trust thought he was a potential steal and this franchise is brutal evaluating tackles and abstained from leaning into loaded recent drafts at the DT spot. He might surprise them if they let him play.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Bills' Week 12 Injury Outlook: DJ Moore, Dalton Kincaid Updates With Chiefs Looming
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills ' medical staff had somewhat of a quiet day during the November 22 home win over the Miami Dolphins.
When it comes to new injuries, it appears that the Bills escaped almost entirely unscathed as they prepare to host the Kansas City Chiefs for a Thanksgiving night special on a short week.
Wide receiver DJ Moore was lone Bills' player to officially leave the Week 11 victory due to injury. He was ruled questionable to return, and did not miss a single offensive possession while being examined.
"Obviously, we had the DJ [issue] a little bit to end half. Then, he came back," said Bills' head coach Joe Brady after the 26-9 win.
Even though Moore played, and played effectively, the rest of the way, how his knee responds with only three days in between games is worth watching.
Including Moore, there are currently four Bills' starters with injuries to monitor on the short week. Cornerback Christian Benford, tight end Dalton Kincaid and inside linebacker Dorian Williams were all scratched from the Week 11 lineup.
Moore, who finished with eight receptions for 91 yards and one touchdown, hyperextended his left knee when targeted on what wound up as an interception late during the first half.
With the pass fluttering due to Josh Allen's arm being hit upon the release, Moore leaped and came down somewhat awkwardly as the left leg stuck in the ground . There was 1:33 remaining on the second-quarter clock as Moore went straight into the locker room .
Evaluated during the change of possession, Moore returned after only 19 seconds of game time elapsed as Miami settled for a field goal following a quick three-and-out.
"I battle through everything," said Moore on Monday morning during a WGR radio appearance . "With that play, the hyperextension, I was just like alright, let's check all the boxes and make sure everything is in the right spot, and it was."
Brady, who knows Moore well from their shared time with the Carolina Panthers, sounds as if he expects his top wide receiver to be fully available when the Chiefs visit on Thursday.
"He's as tough as they come. He's as competitive as it gets," said Brady.
Ruled out for the November 22 game on Friday, along with Williams, Benford did not log any practice participation in Week 11 after injuring his groin against the New York Jets on November 15.
After playing 53 snaps, Benford left the win over the Jets during the second half, and he did not return. The Bills started Maxwell Hairston in his place in Week 11, also rotating practice squad call-up Tre'Davious White into the mix.
"Hope we get Christian back, but we feel confident. That's why Tre White's here," said Brady postgame.
Since an average groin injury can take multiple weeks to heal, expecting Benford to return against the Chiefs may be a bit too ambitious.
Playing through a Week 9 ankle injury against the Jets in Week 10, Kincaid's thumb became a problem.
During a third-quarter red zone play, the tight end can be seen briefly engaging with Jets' linebacker Demario Davis about nine yards past the line of scrimmage, and immediately looking at his left hand in apparent discomfort. Kincaid returned to play two more snaps before being sidelined for the remainder of the second half.
Kincaid remained a non-participant throughout the practice week leading up to the Dolphins game, earning a doubtful tag on the final injury report. Kincaid was seen on the field prior to kickoff, seemingly making a point to keep his left hand down at his side .
Afterwards, Brady was asked directly, "was Kincaid close at all to going in this one?"
"Yeah," said the rookie head coach as he left the podium .
The Bills ruled Williams questionable to return due to a calf problem early in fourth quarter against the Jets, but fourth-round rookie Kaleb Elarms-Orr took over for him the rest of the way. His last snap came with 2:07 remaining in the third quarter.
Williams was one of three Bills' players to miss all three Week 11 practices. Although the severity of the calf injury is unknown publicly, it is reportedly not expected to keep the linebacker out long-term.
While it's strictly speculation, it's possible that Buffalo held Williams out of practice completely to give him uninterrupted recovery time with the hope that he'll be available to face Kansas City.

title: Three Bills' Game Balls for Each Phase in Week 11 Victory over Dolphins
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills posted another victory, defeating the Miami Dolphins , 26-9, in Orchard Park, and, as a result, game balls are in order.
In the Bills' locker room, first-year head coach Joe Brady awarded game balls to running back James Cook and outside linebacker Greg Rousseau. Both men reached individual milestones while contributing to the team's ninth win.
Rousseau, a 2021 first-round draft pick, reached 10.0 sacks in a season for the first time in his career.
Cook, a 2022 second-round selection, surpassed Hall-of-Famers LaDanian Tomlinson and John Riggins to become the only player in NFL history to record 75+ rush yards and 1+ touchdown in nine consecutive games.
As for Bills On SI , we chose three other worthy game ball recipients to highlight in Week 11.
Thus far, he's been a heckuva seventh-round draft pick .
Doman would crack the NFL Top 10 in net punting average (43.6) if he had enough attempts to qualify. While Buffalo did not punt once on Sunday against the Dolphins, the rookie punter made his presence felt as a passer and kickoff specialist.
In punt formation for the only time during the game, the Bills successfully executed a fake with Doman passing to tight end Keleki Latu for a 30-yard gain on 4th-and-8 from their own 34 midway through the first quarter. The punter admitted it was the first time he's ever thrown a pass in game action during his lifetime.
"It was awesome. I didn't know what was going on," said quarterback Josh Allen. "To be honest, I was a little ticked off. I got to the sideline. I got the iPad. I was trying to figure out how to progress on the next drive. All of a sudden I see the ball floating, and Leki catching it. That was pretty cool. It gave us points. Kudos to our guys for calling it, and kudos to him for making the play."
Doman also laid the lumber on a subsequent kickoff, and he was credited with a tackle.
The ultra-reliable Shakir did whatever was needed from him against the Dolphins. He logged 81 percent of offensive snaps, tying Keon Coleman for the most playing time amongst skill players in Sunday.
As a pass-catcher, Shakir made five receptions for a game-high 101 yards. He was also credited with two rush yards on two attempts. Each of his first three catches moved the chains for Buffalo.
Additionally, Shakir, who perfected "Joe Brady routes" long ago, was a noticeable force blocking downfield for other receivers. He nearly helped spring Ty Johnson for a touchdown on a 17-yard gain down to the Miami 7.
"Khalil is as selfless as they come. [He] does an outstanding job in the run game, does a lot of dirty work in the slot, and just when he's out there, he just makes plays," said Brady.
The longtime fan favorite was on the field for the first time in the new Highmark Stadium, and it just felt proper .
"Great to get back in the stadium, in front of the fans. It's been a long time. It's been about 10 months since I played a football game," said the 31-year-old White.
Appearing as a practice squad game day elevation with starting cornerback Christian Benford unavailable , White saw 42 percent of Bills' defensive snaps in his first live action since last year's divisional round road loss to the Denver Broncos. He was credited with one pass break-up.
"Excited for the win. Excited for my teammates. Just to get another opportunity to put on that Bills' gear, it's something I don't take lightly," said White.

title: Oscar-Winner Explains Josh Allen’s Purpose Behind Bills-Related HBO Documentary
full_text:
Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills are handling business on the field, heading to 9-1 on Sunday . Off the field, he's set to join his wife in the world of media.
Allen, the head of his new production company — Out-of-Pocket Studios — is set to release its first major title, the Buffalo Miracle. In production with Breakwater Studios, Skydance Studios, and HBO Sports, the documentary about the 2022 Buffalo blizzard is premiering just ahead of Thanksgiving, when the Bills play the Kansas City Chiefs .
Ben Proudfoot — the two-time Oscar-winning director — had already heard of the situation in the deadly snowstorm. But as Allen was beginning his new studio, he wanted to be a part of bringing this story together.
#Bills quarterback Josh Allen says the HBO documentary he executive produced, "The Buffalo Miracle," which tells the story of the 2022 Christmas blizzard, shows the resiliency of Western New York, adding people will be brought to tears. #BillsMafia pic.twitter.com/LkOMf5vY50
"This is a story about the community and the people that have been so generous and supportive of him. And I think he sees this as a way to celebrate his fans, his city, the people that show up for him. it's a very Buffalo story. This is a good neighbor's story."
As devastating of a holiday season as that was, Allen and Buffalo were able to bring cheer with a comeback-win over the Bears on Christmas Eve.
That moment is captured in the Buffalo Miracle, as several Buffalo natives found respite in a local McDonald's in the midst of the storm.
As Allen serves as executive producer of the documentary, Proudfoot shared how "it meant so much" being able to work with the MVP quarterback.
"Of all the stories he could tell, I think this felt like an obvious forray," said Proudfoot. "None of them expected this would turn into a movie, or connect them with their hero. It's a very special thing, we're very honored to work with him. And he's a collaborative and creative guy, I think you're going to see a lot more of coming [from] Out-of-Pocket in the future.
The Buffalo Miracle debuts at 9 pm on HBO Max on November 24.
I was lucky enough to watch an advanced screening of The Buffalo Miracle. Ben Proudfoot, Josh Allen and everyone involved did an outstanding job on this documentary. It’s a perfect representation of Buffalo and the city of good neighbors. #TheBuffaloMiracle #BillsMafia https://t.co/nMcWF05x5b
In his first game since the exclusive premiere, Allen quarterbacked the Bills to a 26-9 victory over the rival Miami Dolphins on November 22 in Orchard Park. The five-time NFL MVP finalist passed for 304 yards and one touchdown.
It's another busy week for Allen as "The Buffalo Miracle" hits HBO Max on November 24. Two days later, the Bills will host the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving night.

title: Bills CB Tre'Davious White Professes Love For Buffalo Following Return Game
full_text:
Tre'Davious White was a first-round pick for the Buffalo Bills in 2017. He was their top cornerback for seven seasons before leaving in 2024. He split time with the Baltimore Ravens and Los Angeles Rams that year, but was thrilled to return to Buffalo in 2025 .
White started 16 games for the Bills and had 40 tackles, 10 pass breakups, and one interception during the regular season. He added another six tackles and three pass breakups in two postseason games, but was not re-signed to begin the 2026 season.
General manager Brandon Beane said they would keep an eye on White and he was eventually added back to the practice squad . This week, he was elevated to the game day roster to help fill in for Christian Benford, who was out with a groin injury .
White was on the field against Miami and while he didn't record a tackle, he did have one pass breakup. After the game, he said he felt energized by the crowd after they went "crazy" seeing him back on the field.
"I heard the crowd start going crazy, I was like, I gotta kind of reciprocate this energy, you know? It was great. It was a great moment. A lot of guys was talking about it. A guy in the locker room was like, it was louder than you for Josh Allen today. You know, but really appreciate it. It just shows the love that the fans have for the team and have for me. The love is reciprocated. I love, love, love Buffalo," White said via Matt Bove .
He was then asked about his pass breakup, and how there was a loud pop from the crowd once they realized it was him. White said that meant a lot to him and showed that the city loves him as well.
"It just shows, like, man, Buffalo loves me. I love Buffalo. And, I mean, it's my ninth season here, 10th year in the league. So, I mean, I pretty much, you know, grown here, became a man here. And, obviously, I would always want to be here. And, you know, just to receive that love, like, it means so much to me because, you know, because I battled a lot. And then coming back here to be able to play with my brothers, like, that's what it's all about," White said.
Buffalo has seen rookie Davison Igbinosun quickly develop into a solid starter and Maxwell Hairston had a solid outing this week after being benched earlier in the year . If they can get White playing at a high level as well, the cornerback position could wind up being a strength as the playoffs approach.

title: Four Winners & One Loser From Bills Week 11 Win vs. Dolphins
full_text:
It wasn't pretty, but the Buffalo Bills defeated the Miami Dolphins 26-9 in Week 11 . That improved their record to 9-1 as they maintained their firm lead in the AFC East .
While the Bills had to be happy with holding Miami to just nine points, there was some meat left on the bone offensively. Josh Allen also had two interceptions and nearly had a third (which was negated by a penalty).
Still, they did enough to win, and that's what really matters. With this one in the books, let's take a look back at the victory and identify who stood out as both winners and losers in Week 11.
It appeared as though Buffalo was going to end its second drive of the game without points when an incompletion from Josh Allen left them with a fourth-and-eight. That wasn't the case thanks to punter Tommy Doman Jr. The Bills dialed up a fake punt, and Doman delivered with a 30-yard pass to backup tight end Keleki Latu.
Fake punt works to perfection for the Bills! MIAvsBUF on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/bztDNhTMDz
Doman was the first Bills punter to complete a pass since Chris Mohr in 2000. He's also just one of five punters in franchise history to complete a pass. The Bills were unable to capitalize on Doman's play with a touchdown, but they still ended with points as Tyler Bass connected on a 54-yard field goal to make it 6-0.
During the first half, Greg Rousseau recorded two sacks on Kyle McCord, his ninth and 10th of the season. That's significant for Rousseau, since he entered the game tied with his career high of eight. The new personal record is indicative of how well Rousseau has responded to the scheme change under new defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard. He's been vocal about his love for playing from a two-point stance, and he continues to impress.
DJ Moore had an injury scare in the first half when he seemed to bang up his knee. Fortunately, he returned to the field without missing a snap and finished the first half with seven receptions for 79 yards and one touchdown. Moore continued to deliver, finishing with eight receptions for 91 yards.
The Bills had 405 yards on the day, but they struggled once they got inside the 20. They had five trips inside the red zone, but managed to score just two touchdowns. A 40 percent success rate isn't anything to get excited about, and with the Chiefs up in a few days, they must find a way to improve this.
The often undervalued Khalil Shakir had another great game for the Bills. Shakir caught five passes on Sunday for 101 yards, with a long of 38 yards. Shakir is an elite slot receiver and often lines up in the backfield. Because of that, he doesn't typically rack up a ton of yards per reception, but that wasn't the case on Sunday as he averaged 20.2 yards per catch in the win, making him one of the Bills' biggest winners in Week 11.

title: Biggest Takeaways From Bills' Ugly Week 11 Win vs. Dolphins
full_text:
This weekend was supposed to be easy for the Buffalo Bills . They entered Week 11 as the No. 1 seed in the AFC and were hosting a one-win Miami Dolphins team. Not only was Buffalo favored due to their record, but Miami was starting Kyle McCord for just the second time in his career.
In the end, the Bills won this by a multi-score margin (26-9), but it was anything but easy. The Bills left a lot of points on the board, as too many of their drives ended with field goals rather than touchdowns. There were also multiple turnovers, which allowed the Dolphins to hang around for far too long.
What matters most, however, is the fact that the Bills got the win. They need to be better in Week 12 to defeat the Kansas City Chiefs , as head coach Joe Brady will surely say. Beyond that, here are some of the biggest takeaways from the ugly win for Buffalo.
There were questions about Ty Johnson's status with the Bills this offseason. He was dealing with injuries during camp and had a much higher cap hit than any other backup running back. Even so, Josh Allen and Joe Brady were always quick to sing his praises, and Sunday was another reminder of how important a player he is.
Johnson had a 13-yard reception on third-and-eight, helping set up a rushing touchdown from James Cook. He also had a seven-yard reception on third-and-five in the third quarter. Buffalo missed a field goal on that drive, but Johnson kept it alive, giving them a shot to score.
In all, Johnson had seven receptions for 55 yards. He's a reliable weapon who never gets the credit he deserves.
He's not the only underrated player, however. Khalil Shakir is another player who doesn't get the love he deserves. At least not outside of Buffalo. Bills fans understand how vital he is to their success, and that was also on display in Week 11.
Shakir finished with five receptions for 101 yards. He's also been utilized in the backfield often. Shakir is far from flashy, which is why he's overlooked, but this offense wouldn't be the same without him.
Head coach Joe Brady was clearly trying to be more aggressive this week, with Josh Allen taking several shots downfield early in the game. More often than not, those passes fell incomplete. That was better, however, than the frustrating end of the first half.
Allen threw an interception, which wasn't completely his fault. The pass was tipped by Chop Robinson, allowing Jacob Rodriguez to catch the interception. On the next drive, Allen tried to go deep again, this time being picked off by Zayne Anderson. He was bailed out by Damar Hamlin, who picked off Kyle McCord, but Allen nearly had another huge mistake.
In the closing seconds of the half, he again threw a deep ball that was intercepted, this time by Julius Wood. Thankfully, that play was wiped out by a defensive holding, but it was a reminder that Allen needs to take better care of the football. They can get away with turnovers against the Dolphins, but not when the postseason rolls around.
Greg Rousseau entered this game with eight sacks, which tied his career high. He surpassed that with two sacks in the first half, giving him double digits for the first time in his career. Rousseau nearly had a third in the first half as well, but McCord somehow escaped the pressure from Rousseau on that one.
After three games, Rousseau had six sacks and was being discussed as a potential Defensive Player of the Year candidate . He went three games without a sack , which cooled that talk off, but it has been reignited, as he has at least one sack in three of their past four games and 10 in 10 games.
It took a long time for the Bills to decide who would be their new defensive coordinator, and they ultimately decided to hire Jim Leonhard. He had some big shoes to fill after Sean McDermott ran an efficient defense for years, and he started the season slowly. In recent weeks, that hasn't been the case.
Buffalo has been an elite defense and has hit 40 straight possessions without a touchdown in the third quarter of this game.
That's 40 straight possessions without allowing a touchdown for the #Bills defense. Say what you want about the competition, but yeesh that's a long time in the NFL.
They ended this without a touchdown, making it three games in a row. Even against subpar competition, that's a major accomplishment. It should also help build confidence for this unit, which will carry over to games against more impressive offenses.
I mentioned earlier that far too many drives ended in field goals. Buffalo had five trips inside the red zone on Sunday and scored touchdowns just twice. One was a four-yard catch from DJ Moore and the other was an 11-yard touchdown from James Cook.
The Bills will host the Chiefs on Thanksgiving in Week 12. They have the talent to beat them, especially since they're at home, but they need to be more efficient in the red zone for that to happen.

title: DJ Moore Injury Update: Bills WR Heads to Locker Room in First Half
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills have been playing well against the Miami Dolphins , running out to a 20-3 lead in the first half. As the first half closed, however, Miami made a huge play to give them some life.
Chop Robinson tipped a pass from Josh Allen at the line of scrimmage, and the ball floated into the air. Rookie linebacker Jacob Rodriguez ended up making the catch, giving the Dolphins a short field. Even more notable, however, was what happened after the play.
Buffalo wide receiver DJ Moore appeared to have injured his knee and was slow to get off the ground.  He walked slowly to the sideline with trainers before heading into the locker room for further evaluation.
Allen's pass tipped and intercepted by the Dolphins. DJ Moore is down hurt.
Buffalo confirmed that it is a knee injury for Moore, saying that his return is questionable . Moore has been the top receiver on the day for the Bills. He has five receptions for 41 yards and a touchdown before entering the locker room.
UPDATE: DJ Moore back on the field
While it seemed as though Moore could miss time, the veteran wideout didn't miss a snap. After Buffalo's defense held Miami to a field goal, the offense took the field with Moore once again. He quickly made a big play, hauling in an 18-yard pass on third down as the Bills looked for more points before the half.
Buffalo was unable to score on that drive as Allen threw an interception, ending the second consecutive drive with a turnover. The Bills took the ball right back when Damar Hamlin recorded an interception of his own.
Moore had not missed a game since the 2020 season, meaning the Bills felt they were getting an incredibly durable player in their trade with the Chicago Bears.
That hasn't been the case this season. Moore suffered a shoulder injury in Week 2 and it seemed as though he could miss extensive time. He was fortunate enough to miss minimal time, playing in seven games this season. The offense missed him when he wasn't on the field, which is why there was a collective intake of breath in Buffalo when Moore limped off the field on Sunday.
While he might not be on pace for elite numbers, Moore has been a solid wide receiver, helping to open up the offense this year.

title: Should Bills Bring Back Accomplished WR for Stretch Run?
full_text:
A familiar name hit the waiver wire this weekend when the San Francisco 49ers moved on from veteran wide receiver Brandin Cooks . That name will sound familiar to Buffalo Bills fans since Cooks played in five games for the Bills during the 2025 regular season as well as both playoff games.
Cooks began the season with the New Orleans Saints, but was released in November. He joined the receiver-needy Bills and had five receptions for 114 yards. While he did have some unfortunate drops , his average of 22.8 yards per reception made him a player to keep an eye on.
This year, the Bills are much better in the receiver department with the addition of DJ Moore . Still, there are some times when the passing game could use a spark, which is why it's fair to ask if Cooks should be brought back.
Due to the 49ers submitting a waiver claim, he is subject to waiver rules and can be claimed. If no one claims him by Monday, he is free to sign with any team. It's unlikely anyone will claim Cooks, but will general manager Brandon Beane kick the tires?
We all know Beane loves a good reunion story. This week, for example, the Bills elevated cornerback Tre'Davious White and linebacker Shaq Thompson to the game day roster. Both players seemed to be gone this offseason, but Beane decided they could be helpful.
For White, this is the second time he returned to the Bills. He was signed in 2025 after spending 2024 with the Baltimore Ravens and Los Angeles Rams. That same year, Beane reunited with multiple players, including safety Jordan Poyer , wide receiver Gabe Davis, defensive tackle Jordan Phillips, and defensive end Shaq Lawson (among others). He's also had backup quarterbacks with multiple stints including Kyle Allen, Mitchell Trubisky, and Shane Buechele.
As for Cooks, he not only made some splash plays in the regular season, but was nearly a hero in the playoffs. He had five receptions for 78 yards, and nearly hauled in a potential game-winner in overtime against the Denver Broncos.
Facing a third-and-11, Josh Allen targeted Cooks deep and he had both hands on the ball. Unfortunately, Denver cornerback Ja'Quan McMillian wrestled it away as they hit the ground. It was controversially ruled an interception and instead of setting Buffalo up for the game-winning kick, it allowed the Broncos to win 33-30. That said, the current receiving corps offers more than Cooks and if they get desperate, they should turn to someone such as rookie Skyler Bell first.
Verdict : Bills don't need a reunion with Cooks

title: How Rare Would Bills' Loss to Underdog Dolphins Be Considering Massive Point Spread?
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills stepped on a rake, so to speak, when they faced the Miami Dolphins last season in November.
Miami, which was 2-7 at the time, posted a 30-13 home victory over the Bills , who entered with a 6-2 record. Buffalo was a 7.5-point road favorite entering the game.
This time, however, the situation is less conducive to a potential upset by the Dolphins.
Not only is Miami (1-8) the road team for the Week 11 matchup against Buffalo (8-1), running back De'Von Achane and quarterback Malik Willis are unavailable for the visitors. Ollie Gordon and former Syracuse starter Kyle McCord will start in place of the aforementioned duo.
"I never focus on the records. It's all about what the tape shows. You watch a lot of the [Miami] games, you watch in the fourth quarter and it's seven-point games. It's them having leads," said Bills' head coach Joe Brady.
Although they lost all four games, the Dolphins covered the point spread in recent outings against the Minnesota Vikings, New England Patriots and Indianapolis Colts while pushing against the Cincinnati Bengals.
The Bills are the largest favorite they've been thus far this season for the November 22 home game against the Dolphins. Buffalo is favored by a 16.5-point margin ( per DraftKings ) for the 1 p.m. ET kickoff at Highmark Stadium.
Buffalo has only lost thrice outright in its history when favored by at least 14.5 points (h/t WGR's Joe Dibiase). The last time it happened was during November 2021 when the Bills lost, 9-6, to the Jacksonville Jaguars as a 14.5-point road favorite.
The other two instances occurred in back-to-back weeks during the 1992 season. The Bills lost, 16-13, to the Colts in overtime as a 16.5-point road favorite one week before losing, 24-17, to the Jets as a 17-point home favorite.
The Bills are a 16.5 point favorite against the Dolphins. They have lost as a two touchdown or more favorite only three times in their history. 1992: NYJ 24 - BUF 17 (-17) 1992: IND 16 - BUF 13 (-16.5) 2021: JAX 9 - BUF 6 (-14.5) The two 1992 games were in BACK TO BACK WEEKS.
While no one will be surprised if the Dolphins were to keep the final outcome within a 16.5-point margin on Sunday, the likelihood of them escaping Orchard Park with an outright upset victory is slim.
According to OptaStats, in games "between a team with one loss or fewer and a team with one win or fewer in Week 11 or later, the team with the better record has won in all eight previous matchups by an average of 22.6 points since the AFL-NFL merger in 1970."

title: Dalton Kincaid Headlines Bills Week 11 Inactive List vs. Dolphins
full_text:
