title: Versatility the Hallmark of New-Look Panthers Offense This Season
full_text:
In April of 2025, Carolina Panthers’ president of football operations Dan Morgan used the eighth overall pick in the draft on University of Arizona wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan. It proved to be a wise selection as the 6’4”, 220-pound performer lead the team in catches (70), receiving yards (1,014) and touchdown receptions (7). He earned NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year honors.
The former Wildcat was complimented by emerging wideout Jalen Coker, who totaled 33 grabs for 394 yards and three scores in just 11 regular-season games. The former undrafted free agent from Holy Cross came up huge down the stretch and had a big game in the team’s playoff loss to the Rams. Coker snared nine passes for 134 yards and one touchdown in the 34-31 wild card loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
Last season, Dave Canales’s team totaled 33 offensive touchdowns in 17 regular-season contests in 2025, the vast majority of those through the air (24). And more than half of those TD receptions (15) came via wide receivers. The other nine scoring catches came from tight ends (5) and running backs (4).
Now 10 games into 2026 and an offensive attack led by play-caller Brad Idzik has already reached the end zone 29 times. There have been 11 rushing touchdowns while fourth-year signal-caller Bryce Young has thrown for 18 scores. Wide receivers and tight ends have each accounted for eight of those aerial scores, while running back Chuba Hubbard has hauled in a pair of TD tosses via Young.
Bryce Young to Tetairoa McMillan for a Panthers TD! BALvsCAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/DrvaI7l2dE
On Sunday vs. the Ravens, McMillan caught six passes for 71 yards and a seven-yard score. Young hit on 22-of-30 throws for 254 yards and two touchdowns (1 interception), with wide receivers totaling 12 of those receptions for 143 yards and the aforementioned score.
Meanwhile, tight end Mitchell Evans finished with five catches for 44 yards and his first TD catch of the season. Tight ends totaled nine grabs for 104 and that Evans’ TD grab in the team’s 35-33 victory over the visiting Baltimore Ravens.
CHUBA HUBBARD CAN'T STOP SCORING 🍁 pic.twitter.com/fSgi04M6dE
Running back Trevor Etienne (7 yards) accounted for the other Young completion. Meanwhile, Hubbard added 27 carries for 120 yards and two touchdowns and a two-point conversion run in the two-point win.
Mitchell Evans. Would totally trade for whichever of he or Tremble the Panthers are willing to give up this offseason pic.twitter.com/qYdr9gacf6
Led by veteran newcomer Darren Waller, six-year pro Tommy Tremble and Evans, Carolina tight ends have combined for 71 receptions, good for 801 yards (11.3 average) and eight touchdowns. That’s as many trips to the end zone by Panthers’ tight ends as the position managed the previous two seasons combined.
It’s safe to say that Idzik’s offense is certainly evolving. And Canales’s team spotted Baltimore a 12-0 first-quarter lead before outscoring the Ravens 35-21 the rest of the way. Next Monday night, they need to prove that this attack is headed in the right direction as they look to avenge that ugly 43-13 home loss to the Buccaneers in Week 7.

title: Panthers Rise Again in Power Rankings After Clutch Win vs. Ravens
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers secured a much-needed victory over the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday . It wasn't pretty, but a win is a win. Moving to two games in front of the rest of the NFC South is significant.
The Panthers should've blown out the listless Ravens, but they came out flat and let Baltimore take a 12-0 lead. Miscues continued throughout, particularly on special teams, but the end result is another comeback win for Bryce Young and company.
Ryan Fitzgerald won it with a chip-shot field goal after the two-minute warning, aided by an interception from Tyrel Dodson on the ensuing possession.
The result is another bump in the weekly NFL Power Rankings, and the Panthers are beginning to separate from the rest of the NFC South.
The NFL Power Rankings do not mean very much. A team being ranked 20th is not indicative of much because it's one analyst's opinion on how the team stacks up against another, and there's usually rampant disagreement.
What does matter is whether a team is going up or down. The comparison from last week to this week in placement is the important part. Last week, the Panthers broke a three-game losing streak (which had sent them spiraling down the rankings ) and moved up.
This week, they're rising again, even if they didn't exactly inspire ultimate confidence in how they handled the Jacoby Brissett-led Ravens.
Last week, Vinnie Iyer of Sporting News ranked the Panthers 19th. This week, they're 18th. It may not be much of a rise, but they are higher than last week.
"The Panthers, after beating the Ravens, are 3-0 this season when Bryce Young passes for 250 or more yards and Chuba Hubbard rushes for 120 or more yards in the same game. Their offense can be inconsistent with its balance and production, but it's a necessary ball-control approach to help a bad run defense," Iyer wrote.
We can quibble about them being ranked lower than the Dallas Cowboys or New England Patriots, but that's not too bad. The Panthers are higher than their NFC South rivals: Buccaneers at 23, Falcons at 24, and Saints at 25.
Next week, they'll have a chance to continue their winning streak, put more distance between the Panthers and the rest of the NFC South, move up in the Power Rankings even further, and get revenge. They're facing the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the team that started that aforementioned slide with a 43-13 dismantling of Carolina.

title: Dave Canales May Not Be the Coach of the Future for the Carolina Panthers
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers have a coaching problem. Dave Canales has helped this team make strides from being the worst in the NFL before his hiring, but that growth has been stymied by things that are in his control. The Panthers just can't make the leap under Canales.
Three years isn't exactly enough for a first-time head coach (with one coordinating year under his belt) to be perfect, but many of these issues have persisted throughout his three seasons. The things he struggled with in 2024 are still present. There's been little growth.
Canales gave away play-calling duties to help open things up, and the offense took a step forward (that's telling in and of itself). But it didn't allow Canales to take a step forward as a coach with less on his plate.
This Panthers team is painfully undisciplined . That's a coaching issue. They commit the most penalties in the NFL, and they give up a lot of bad ones (pass interference and unnecessary roughness, for example). Canales doesn't have his players playing clean, disciplined football.
They also come out flat in every scenario where they shouldn't. Momentum from week-to-week? Nonexistent. The joke that the Panthers could win one week and would absolutely lose the next week didn't come out of nowhere.
This year was the first year that the Panthers, under Canales, came out of the preseason with any semblance of a grasp on the offense and were ready to play. The defense wasn't remotely ready, but that may have been an Ejiro Evero problem.
During Canales' tenure, the bye week hasn't been kind to the Panthers. They come out of it flat, sluggish, and unprepared. This year, they're lucky they had Tanner McKee and the injured Philadelphia Eagles coming back from an international trip this time.
When the Panthers have an opportunity to make a statement, they don't. Well, they do, but not the kind of statement anyone wants to see. They had the one-win Tampa Bay Buccaneers at home with a chance to secure a firm grip on the NFC South. They lost by 30, and that barely illustrates how ugly it was.
They had a chance against the listless Baltimore Ravens, again at home, who were coming off a loss to the previously winless Los Angeles Chargers, and Canales' team came out flat and couldn't get anything going for almost a full quarter. By a single second, they broke a long first-quarter touchdown drought.
How long are these issues going to persist? Canales does some things well, but it's clear that his shortcomings are going to hold the Panthers back from ever making the leap from pesky NFC South contender to legitimate good team.
Sometimes, a coach is in the intermediate. Sometimes, that coach needs to bring the team up a level, but he's not the one to take them to the next level. Canales may just be that for the Panthers.

title: Panthers May Have Made the Right Call Letting Rico Dowdle Walk in Free Agency
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers had a big decision to make regarding Rico Dowdle in free agency this offseason. Dowdle had been a productive running back for Carolina during his lone season with the team, rushing for over 1,000 yards. The Panthers had Chuba Hubbard under contract for the upcoming season as well and had to determine if both would be a good fit for the team’s backfield.
The Panthers chose to go in a different direction, with Hubbard as the team’s starting running back, and thus far, the decision has been the correct one for the organization.
Hubbard is putting up another solid season on the ground for the Panthers. He has rushed for 831 yards and scored nine touchdowns through 10 games in 2026. This is exactly what the Panthers were looking for from their running back after Dowdle left in free agency.
While Rico Dowdle was productive for the Panthers during his time in Carolina, that production also created a big decision for the organization as it went into the offseason. Hubbard, the Panthers’ other running back, had already proven to be a productive player for the team’s offense.
Hubbard had a solid season in 2024 as well, rushing for 1,195 yards and 10 touchdowns. However, because of injuries and a decrease in playing time, Hubbard’s numbers dropped last season. Carolina’s offense still needed a solid running back, and that’s what Hubbard has provided this season.
Hubbard has rushed for 831 yards through 10 games this season, averaging 4.4 yards per carry. He has also scored nine touchdowns so far this season for the Panthers. That is exactly what the Panthers needed after Dowdle's departure.
The Panthers have been able to keep their running game productive without Dowdle because of what Hubbard has done this season. Dowdle deserves credit for the season he had in Carolina, but the team had to move on to help it succeed in the future.
In addition to the on-field decision, the financial commitment required to re-sign Dowdle to a similar contract to the one he received from Pittsburgh was significant. Dowdle signed a two-year, $12.25 million contract with the Steelers. Hubbard is already under contract with the Panthers, which creates a very solid situation for the team at running back.

title: Grading Bryce Young in Panthers Clutch Win vs Ravens
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers secure a 35-33 victory over the Baltimore Ravens in what was maybe the wildest game of the season. This game was drunk from the start: muffed punts by Baltimore, a safety to open the game, and trickery on both teams' first touchdowns.
There were seven lead changes, and the game came down to a tipped pass by Will Lee III , leading to a Tyrel Dodson interception to clinch the win. Chuba Hubbard was once again outstanding, rushing for 120 yards and scoring two touchdowns.
The quarterback play looked bleak at the beginning of the game. Carolina's first possession ended in a safety when Bryce Young tried to get the ball out, but his knee went down in the end zone. The next possession ended in a punt. After that, Young and the Carolina offense found their rhythm.
Young is back to playing with poise and conviction. Against the Ravens, Young completed 22 of 30 passes for 254 yards, 2 touchdowns, and 1 interception. In two of Carolina's last three games, Young completed over 70% of his passes and now has three games this season doing so, completing 73% on Sunday.
For the most part, Carolina's offensive line was solid today, giving Young time to make subtle movements in the pocket and launch the ball downfield. Young also spread the wealth, finding eight different receivers, with four receivers having at least three catches.
Entering Sunday, the Panthers were 0-5 when Young threw an interception, which changed today, finally ending a season-long trend.
Young threw a bad interception in the third quarter, his first real mistake of the game. Young rolled to his right and tried to force a throw to Tetairoa McMillan at the back of the end zone, but T.J. Tampa picked it off.
Carolina was in the red zone and up by three points; a touchdown likely would've clinched the game, and even a field goal would've put them in a great position. Instead, the Ravens scored in the fourth quarter to take the lead, leaving the Panthers needing a go-ahead drive.
Despite the third-quarter interception in the endzone, Young was dialed in all game, and in the fourth quarter, down 33-32, Young made the plays needed for Carolina to score.
Young made three big-time throws in Carolina's game-winning drive. The first was a 13-yard strike to McMillan that put the Panthers in Baltimore territory; the next was an 18-yard pass to Tommy Tremble in the middle of the field. Lastly, Young found Jalen Coker on a 6-yard pass to the Baltimore 19-yard line, setting up Ryan Fitzgerald's game-winning field goal by Ryan Fitzgerald.
Carolina couldn't punch it in the end zone, but Young made the biggest plays of the game.
Young was great against Baltimore, Carolina's QB1 certainly had help from Hubbard and the defense making timely plays, but Young did enough to secure the win and made elite plays when elite plays were needed.
Even on a day with a safety and a bad interception, it's encouraging to see Young stay on an even keel and be confident in the biggest moments. That's what a franchise QB does.
Preston is an experienced sports writer focusing on NFL, College Football, NBA, and MMA topics. He is a passionate Charlotte and Oklahoma sports fan and graduated from the University of Science and Arts Oklahoma in 2025 with a Bachelor of Arts in Communications degree with a focus in journalism.

title: Panthers Beat Ravens, But These 3 Concerns Still Loom Large
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers were looking to clean up their act with the number of penalties they had committed throughout the season. They entered Week 11 among the NFL's most-penalized teams, making Sunday's matchup with the Baltimore Ravens another opportunity to show some progress in that department. Carolina's penalty problems were also a major concern in its previous win over the Saints.
The Panthers finished with six penalties for 54 yards against Baltimore, while the Ravens were flagged five times for 41 yards. Although the difference between the two teams was small, Carolina still has work to do when it comes to avoiding costly mistakes. In its Week 10 win over New Orleans, Carolina committed 17 penalties for 152 yards.
Defensive pass interference was called on Panthers cornerback Will Lee III on a third-down play during Baltimore's opening drive. That penalty extended the possession, and the Ravens took advantage on the very next play with a 52-yard touchdown pass from Jacoby Brissett to Rashod Bateman.
While the Panthers had six penalties for 54 yards in this game, it is the nature of the penalties that has been a problem for Carolina in recent weeks. The flags have come at some of the worst possible times, giving opposing teams opportunities to extend drives and put points on the board.
The Panthers still have work to do when it comes to cleaning up their penalties. Getting those numbers down would help them move away from being among the league leaders in penalty yardage. More importantly, Carolina needs to show that those mistakes won't continue to give opponents extra chances to score in key situations.
Bryce Young had some good moments against Baltimore, throwing for 254 yards and two touchdowns while completing 22 of 30 passes. He also threw an interception, but the Panthers got enough from their quarterback to help put themselves in position to win.
Chuba Hubbard added 120 rushing yards and two touchdowns, giving the Panthers another productive performance on the ground. His performance helped Carolina keep the pressure on Baltimore and provided an important boost to the offense.
Carolina will need to find a way to keep getting this kind of production from Young and Hubbard. If the two can continue making plays, the offense will have a better chance of helping the Panthers win games down the stretch.
The Panthers have had their share of strong moments on defense, but they haven't always been able to sustain that level of play. Special teams also had a costly moment against Baltimore that nearly changed the outcome of the game.
One of the biggest plays came when Baltimore's Devontez Walker returned a kickoff 86 yards for a touchdown. The return gave the Ravens another answer after Carolina had taken the lead and put additional pressure on the Panthers.
Carolina cannot afford to give opponents those kinds of opportunities. The Panthers managed to overcome the mistakes against Baltimore, but they won't always be able to count on the offense to bail them out.
The Panthers have several areas to improve upon for the rest of the season. The coaching staff will have to address the number of penalties Carolina continues to commit, especially with the team entering games already carrying a reputation for struggling in that department.
There were positives to take away from Young and Hubbard's performances, and Carolina showed some fight by overcoming an early deficit to get the win. Still, the defense and special teams will need to become more consistent.
The Panthers found a way to beat Baltimore, but they cannot continue making the same mistakes and expect things to work out in their favor every week.

title: 7 Winners and 5 Losers from Panthers' Tightly Contested Win Over Ravens
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers were favored at home against the Baltimore Ravens, but you'd never know it by what transpired. One of the weirdest games of the NFL season was strangely very accurate to the Panthers experience. But a win is a win.
Insane punch out by Will Lee to punch the ball out before Hill crosses the plane pic.twitter.com/HEXeV6Roon
Will Lee's physical play continued to lead to some unfortunate penalties, but he had arguably the biggest play of the entire day. Turned around on a long run to the goal line, he punched the ball out of Justice Hill's hands before he scored, forcing a touchback to keep momentum back with the Panthers.
He then forced a second turnover in the fourth quarter by stripping Derrick Henry. Lee also broke up what ended up being the game-ending interception.
It's so unclear why the Panthers won't move on from Luke Fortner. Is Sam Hecht really that bad? Fortner struggled to open run lanes and was little more than a traffic cone in pass protection. Several times, he ruined passing plays by falling into Bryce Young's lap.
PANTHERS HISTORY! 🚨 The ONLY players in Carolina Panthers history to record the following through the team's first 10 games of a season: 1,000+ Scrimmage Yards 10+ Touchdowns Christian McCaffrey Chuba Hubbard pic.twitter.com/sNIs4ngGA4
Just pencil Chuba Hubbard in as a winner every week. He is playing about as well as any running back in the entire NFL. He is scoring, getting tough yards, and playing through contact behind an offensive line that certainly isn't the best. Today, more of the same.
if the closest player to Zay Flowers is a LB, it's going to be a long day for the Panthers defense
Declan Doyle had Todd Wash's number on Sunday. The interim defensive coordinator did not have his best day, as Doyle did whatever he wanted with a backup quarterback. The screens that Doyle turned to so many times worked almost every single time, but Wash was helpless to stop them. The poor tackling from Ejiro Evero's tenure returned, too. He had a much better second half, but that's likely more down to talent and the fact that he was facing Jacoby Brissett.
No Jonathon Brooks, no problem. Trevor Etienne had a huge miscue letting a punt roll to the five, but he made up for it on offense when his number was called. It is possible that he's never looked as good as he did today as a running back.
We keep mentioning Tracy Smith, but that's because the Panthers have inexplicably poor special teams. Today, they allowed a kickoff return for a touchdown after taking the lead and had other special teams miscues. Again.
We mentioned how bad the special teams was again, but that was mostly on coverages and other miscues. On kickoff returns, the Panthers routinely did well. Tre Tyus had a few really nice returns to give the Panthers good field position.
Zakee Wheatley has had a terrible game. A true "welcome to the NFL" game for the rookie safety.
Zakee Wheatley has been one of the NFL's best rookies. Today, he struggled. He got beat in coverage, missed tackles, and showed some real growing pains. It was out of character for him, but it really hurt the Panthers.
For good reason, we've been critical of Robert Hunt all year. He has made bad penalties, been blown up by defenders, and just not his usual Pro Bowl self. Today, though, even while exiting with an injury and returning later, he looked a whole lot better. They ran behind him to great success today.
Malcolm DeWalt fumbles a walk-in TD after another LaJohntay Wester muffed punt. It's the second time DeWalt has failed to recover a muff today.
The Panthers had a golden chance before the half to take the lead. A second muffed punt dropped right into Malcolm DeWalt's hands, but he tried to pick it up and run (which isn't even allowed) instead of falling on it. That is a monstrous miscue that cost the Panthers a pristine scoring chance.
this DeWalt guy might be the worst special teams player I've ever seen
He's lucky his first miscue didn't hurt the Panthers, but this one really did. DeWalt also made a huge mistake on the kickoff return touchdown.  To make matters worse, he downed a punt at the one... while his foot was on the line. That is an enormous mistake.
Princely Umanmielen had his breakout game today. He's been solid all year, but the Panthers didn't get as much from Jaelan Phillips as last week, so Umanmielen had to pick up the load. He did well, recording a couple of enormous sacks.
We mentioned Will Lee making the game-sealing tip, but it was Tyrel Dodson who came down with the actual interception. He was also all over the place making tackles, and he was only starting because Bobby Okereke is hurt again.

title: Fantasy Start or Sit: Tetairoa McMillan, Panthers D/ST, Darren Waller
full_text:
Carolina wants to keep its winning streak alive when the Ravens visit Bank of America Stadium this week. There are several fantasy decisions to consider ahead of Sunday's game, including three Panthers players who could factor into your lineup.
Tetairoa McMillan , Carolina's defense and Darren Waller each bring something different to the fantasy conversation heading into Week 11.
McMillan hasn't been producing on the same level as he was earlier in the season, but he is still a key target for rookie quarterback Bryce Young.
As of late, defenses have started to lock on to the rookie receiver more and more, making it difficult for him to create space downfield. Carolina knows how important it is to get McMillan involved in the passing game and will look to do so on Sunday against the Ravens.
Marlon Humphrey will be out for the Ravens in Week 11, which should open up more opportunities for McMillan in this game. The Ravens have been struggling on defense in recent weeks during their five-game losing streak.
McMillan remains a player who can make a difference with just a few opportunities.
Fantasy call: Start McMillan.
The Panthers' defense has shown some life at times this season, but in a tough matchup, it is hard to rely on them for fantasy purposes.
The Ravens still have Derrick Henry in the backfield, and he will pose a huge threat to the Panthers' front seven. The Ravens also have enough weapons on offense to get the Panthers' defense off the field, which has been a struggle for them at times this season.
The Panthers average 1.6 sacks per game, which ranks 31st in the league.
Fantasy verdict: Sit Carolina's defense.
Waller gives the Panthers another receiving option, particularly when they need a target in the middle of the field. Bryce Young can benefit from having him available.
The Panthers tight end is dealing with a knee injury and was listed as questionable for Sunday's game after practicing in a limited capacity on Thursday and Friday.
The Ravens have given up some opportunities to opposing tight ends this season, and Waller is more than capable of taking advantage of them if he can stay on the field.
If Waller is active for Sunday's game, then fantasy owners can look to start him as a TE1 or TE2 in most leagues. However, if he is inactive for the game, then owners will have to look for alternatives.
Fantasy call: Start Waller if active.

title: Fantasy Football Start or Sit Week 11: Bryce Young, Jalen Coker, Chuba Hubbard
full_text:
With the Carolina Panthers set to take on the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday, it's time to make decisions on quarterback Bryce Young, wide receiver Jalen Coker and running back Chuba Hubbard in fantasy football for Week 11.
Young came back down to Earth last week versus the New Orleans Saints after barely reaching the 200-yard mark and not scoring a touchdown in the 20-17 victory over the Saints .
Coker had his worst game of the 2026 season in the same contest after he was completely blanked on four targets in the win.
Hubbard's yardage output was nothing special after he finished with 87 yards from scrimmage, but Hubbard found pay dirt twice, including once on the the ground to break his two-game rushing score drought.
Now, a look at what we're doing with Young, Hubbard and Coker for the Week 11 game against the Ravens.
After performing like one of the elite fantasy quarterbacks earlier in the campaign, Young is no longer a set-and-forget option after ranking as QB20 overall in fantasy points per game the last four weeks, according to Fantasy Pros .
So, we're focused on matchups with Young, who squares off versus a Ravens defense surrendering the 15th-most fantasy points per game to quarterbacks, per CBS Sports .
That's good enough to justify putting Young in lineups, especially when there are six teams on bye.
Coker has not surpassed 36 yards and has scored once over his last four games, ranking as WR72 overall in that span, which is a far cry from what he did over his first four games.
The Ravens are giving up the 14th-most fantasy points per game to wideouts this season, and not having Marlon Humphrey, who is serving a punishment for controversial comments he made on his podcast, should benefit Coker.
However, after posting a bagel last week and doing almost nothing for four games in a row, we simply can't trust Coker in lineups this week.
While everyone else on the Panthers' roster has let us down lately, the same cannot be said for Hubbard, who continues chugging right along toward an elite fantasy season.
Through 10 games, Hubbard ranks as RB5 overall, making him one of the very best running backs in fantasy football in 2026. You never sit a player like that.
There was some concern that maybe Jonathon Brooks could eat into Hubbard's workload upon his return from injury, but head coach Dave Canales sent a clear message that won't be happening.
"I'm not comparing him to Jahmyr Gibbs. I'm just saying the Lions really give Jahmyr a lot of touches. In the pass game, in the run game. That's their guy. And we have our guy," Canales said of Hubbard.
The Ravens are giving up the 12th-fewest fantasy points per game to the position this season, but are also permitting the sixth-most touchdowns per game and finding pay dirt has been Hubbard's specialty.

title: Will the Panthers Beat the Ravens? Here Are Our Staff Predictions
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers finally got back to winning last weekend, and today, they can get back to .500. If they can beat the struggling Baltimore Ravens , who are without some key contributors, they will do that and remain in first place.
But as is often the case with this Panthers team, nothing is as simple as it seems. The Panthers have won games they had no business winning and lost games they had no business losing. It's difficult to pin down, even in a very winnable contest.
So, will the Panthers make it two in a row? Here's what the Panthers On SI staff believes.
Dave Canales’s team can get back to the .500 mark with a win, but it may not be easy against a plummeting Ravens team in the midst of a five-game skid. The Panthers could have Mike Jackson back, while the Ravens won’t have cornerback Marlon Humphrey.
Baltimore ran for a total of 16 yards on Monday night, but that should change. But Carolina’s defense will come up with a few takeaways as Canales’s club wins at home for just the second time.
The Panthers are getting healthier, while the Ravens are losing players. Jacoby Brissett is starting, and the Ravens benched starting cornerback Marlon Humphrey. Both things give Carolina an edge they otherwise wouldn't have had.
Backup quarterbacks have been this defense's bread and butter (Tanner McKee and Cooper Rush are half the victories), and the defense is in better shape with Mike Jackson potentially back and Todd Wash running things.
The Ravens struggle to run the ball, and the Panthers have defended the run better of late. The Ravens' secondary has been porous, and the Panthers can thrive aerially if there isn't rampant pressure. Baltimore is eighth-lowest in pressure rate. The Panthers could coast, but it will be closer than it should be.
I like Carolina in this one. The Panthers are coming off a big win, and I think they have a real chance to keep things rolling at home. I’m taking Bryce Young and the offense to make enough plays, while the defense comes up with a big stop late. Give me the Panthers!
Carolina needs to take care of business Sunday. A win here would give this team some much-needed momentum and keep things interesting in the NFC South. I think the Panthers get it done.
Coming off a slugfest win against New Orleans, Carolina has to take advantage of a depleted Baltimore team that's without Lamar Jackson. Derrick Henry is the focal point; Todd Wash and the defense will key in on him.
Carolina has to win the time of possession battle here, Baltimore will crush the Panthers if they sustain long drives or get gifted first downs with penalties. The Panthers should be able to score here, not 30+ or anything, but enough to beat a mediocre Ravens offense. This game is going to be ugly like last week's was.

title: Clark Phillips Starting to Give Bears Return on Investment From Gervon Dexter Trade
full_text:
When the Chicago Bears traded Gervon Dexter , I was totally against it, and for a few reasons.
Dexter was a bad fit in Dennis Allen's defense and he was a terrible run defender, but he was also the team's best interior pass-rusher and the options to replace him were shaky , at best, and that was proven true after Jordan van den Berg and Kentavius Street weren't very good (van berg was especially bad) in his stead.
The other issue I had with the trade was the return. The Bears only received a fifth-round pick and defensive back Clark Phillips, who was coming off an injury-plagued 2025 campaign and was a career backup.
But things have begun to change the last few weeks and Phillips is starting to give the Bears some return on investment from the trade.
Phillips played a season-high 23 snaps in Week 9 thanks to injuries to Malik Muhammad and Tyrique Stevenson and he responded by giving up zero completions on two targets on the boundary and added one tackle for good measure.
Then, in Week 11 when the Bears were missing slot cornerback Kyler Gordon due to injury , it was Phillips who was called into action in the slot and he once again made the most of his opportunity.
Phillips had four tackles, including one for loss, one sack, one QB hit, two pressures and one pass defensed. He did give up three completions on four of the targets thrown his way, but those catches only gained seven yards and Phillips' passer rating against was an impressive 77.1.
One of those targets came against Saints No. 1 wideout Chris Olave and the pass fell incomplete.
But that wasn't even the entire extent of Phillips' contribution on Sunday. The veteran defensive back also forced a fumble that the Bears recovered and ultimately turned into points.
"You're watching every position out there. Obviously, you're seeing how other teams play them. This week, for instance, you're looking at Chris Olave, you're looking at Devaugh Vele, you're looking at Juwan Johnson, you're looking at everybody that could possibly be in that spot that you're going to be in," Phillips said , per NBC Chicago's Natalie Spala. "For me, I'm just grateful for the opportunity and we gotta keep it going."
Ahead of the deadline, the Bears were reportedly in the market for a cornerback trade to bolster their room .
But it appears the cornerback they needed was on the roster the whole time. Phillips' versatility and ability to step up when called upon is a huge development for Chicago's ascending defense.
Now, this doesn't mean the Dexter trade is fully justified, but it is certainly looking better than it did just a few weeks ago.

title: Chicago Bears Report Card for 21-13 Win Over Saints: Cleanup Required
full_text:
Ben Johnson on Sunday was only too willing after a win to look ahead to trying to ruin turkey day for the people who used to pay his salary.
Who could blame him? Sunday's 21-13 victory over New Orleans was about as glamorous as carrying out the garbage and a much less tidy duty.
In only four days the Bears will play again on Thanksgiving at Detroit, where Johnson is cursed at, and against a team he failed to beat last year. First place in the NFC North will be at stake.
“Every game counts as one, but this one (with Detroit), because it's a divisional one, you could say it's one and a half," Johnson said. "It's a big one, but we keep saying it every week. It's the next one, the next one's the biggest one.
“The @ChicagoBears are the team to beat in the NFC North.” @TheSamAcho answers who is the bigger NFC threat between the Bears and Lions 👀 pic.twitter.com/qNTq61vlEL
"So that's really our sole focus. These guys will go home tonight. They'll enjoy the night, and then it'll be a quick turnaround. We'll be able to catch up on rest after Thursday. But for the next little bit, it's going to be a race to get ready for this next one.”
Caleb Williams looked back at Sunday's 181-yard winning passing effort and became a bit philosophical.
“We win in multiple ways and that's good for us as a team to know that when we get in these situations throughout the year and late in this year, we’ve got each other's back," Williams said. "And we know that we can win in a multitude of ways.”
Sunday's multitude of ways was a lot like the game they had just played before the bye.  It made you wonder where they'd all be without Jeffery Simmons.
What a catch by Zavion Thomas. Check out the route too. So quick in and out of the break after the wiggle. 👀 #DaBears #Bears pic.twitter.com/E0fX0Bog72
They have played five straight games without trailing for the first time since 1959, but they still can't afford to play the same way on Thanksgiving as they did in their last two games or they won't make it six straight wins at Ford Field.
Here is the report card for a game showing the Bears really have established a trend for winning ugly — get ahead early, play sloppy and then finish the right way.
Well that sucks. Swift gets stripped after the safety and Bears starting their possession on the 50 pic.twitter.com/BA3T4LQess
Sure, it was more team rushing yardage than they had against any of their previous five opponents but the consistent longer, physical yards from backs were missing and D'Andre Swift's third fumble of the year left a bad aftertaste. Kyle Monangai's 2.3-yard average suggests maybe he's not 100% yet, or at least has a little confidence to regain in his injured toe. Give practice squad player Salvon Ahmed credit for a second straight effective game when they needed a third back to produce because of Roschon Johnson's ankle injury. The run blocking isn't getting to the second level as it did much of last year and it's easy to feel they miss Cole Kmet on the edge of the line sealing or leading the way downfield with run blocks.
BIG TIME BLOCK BY CALEB ON THE LONG RUN BY ZAVION THOMAS 👀 pic.twitter.com/UrS0GG1uW3
Averaging 7.9 yards per pass attempt isn't easy when you have only one completion longer than 19 yards, but Caleb Williams did this. The 181 passing yards didn't say much for their catch-and-run abilities. Luther Burden was virtually invisible much of the day and it's easy to wonder if he was fully ready after his concussion two weeks ago. Williams' one interception thrown was off a deflected pass but he seemed ill at ease in the pocket much of the day against a strong Saints rush. The pass blocking allowed too much penetration to a group of good pass rushers.
Caleb Williams throw to Zavion Thomas. pic.twitter.com/OYJWUWna5i
Their 5.5-yard average against looks horrifying but it's deceiving. One 30-yard run came on a Tyler Shough scramble straight up the middle, so that yardage came on an intended pass play. Travis Etienne broke one 46-yard run early and ran for only 30 yards on his other 13 carries. Take away the one early breakaway run and the Saints' running backs gained only 36 yards on 15 carries. All told, the Bears made 10 tackles for loss.
The rookie Dillon Thieneman gets his 2nd career INT! NOvsCHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/xNaPZIWEoN
Third down coverage leaked a bit compared to recent efforts, at 8-for-17 allowed, after they'd been giving up 22% on the year. However, the pass rush made up for it with three Simmons sacks and two QB hits, and a sack, a safety, and three QB hits for Montez Sweat. Six total sacks were their most in five years, and Pro Football Focus gave them a season-high 24 pressures. Chris Olave's nine receptions made that 8-for-17 possible for New Orleans but the pass rush was strong enough and the pass defense produced two takeaways -- one on Dillon Thieneman's interception and the other on a fumble forced by Clark Phillips.
Montez Sweat gets to Shough to force the safety! 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/jSkcquzudc
Cairo Santos did miss an extra point, which could have been costly had it not been for their defense. They kept the Saints' return game bottled up after a 40-yard kick returned allowed in the first quarter. Bears special teams didn't necessarily do the spectacular, as Santos made two short field goals. At least they didn't do the really stupid things the Saints' did with a missed field goal and two kickoffs out of bounds. One of the kickoffs was on a free kick after a safety, so it meant the Bears got the ball at the 50. Punter Tory Taylor put down two punts inside the 20 and only one with a touchback, while the Saints had three touchbacks with none inside the 20.
Oh boy the Saints kicked the free punt out of bounds. #Bears offense will get the ball at the 50(!) to start here.
Johnson and the offense talked all week about getting the running game goin again. Next time they should leave the talk about running until after the game because they struggled as they fought for every inch. Dennis Allen's scheme again came with a nice blend of blitz and four-man pressure and he found ways to make up for the loss of injured Kyler Gordon through strong play from Malik Muhammad, Phillips and Cam Lewis. At least Bears coaches didn't make the same mistake Saints coach Kellen Moore did with 8:51 left. He decided to go for it on fourth-and-2 from the 10 down 11 points. The field goal there would have given them the chance at the tie on their final drive. Instead, they had to make up the field goal then and then resort to a complete prayer with an onside kick.
#Bears DC Dennis Allen after defeating his former #Saints team today: pic.twitter.com/xfsN5oSIW1
The way the Bears' offense played with their food for much of the second half gave the Saints an opportunity to get back within striking distance.  This wasn't an effort anyone will long remember but they don't have long to think about it anyway. The next one is huge and arrives quickly on Thursday.
I have no evidence to back up this claim, but this has to be the most difficult stretch of games a team has ever had in the NFL. If they make it through this stretch 4-3 I will be happy. That may be good enough to win the division. More than likely they'll need to be 5-2. #Bears https://t.co/HtQH6Um8Cc

title: Chicago Bears Assistant Coach Goes Viral During Saints Game for Jacked Physique
full_text:
You just never know what the internet is going to get a hold of and run with during an NFL game and we saw an example of that in the Chicago Bears' Week 11 victory over the New Orleans Saints.
It was quite a boring game overall , as neither offense did much with the Bears' unit struggling, and Chicago's defense put the clamps on the Saints' offense all game long.
So, the internet needed to find ways to entertain itself during the game and it found a way, and more specifically, with Bears assistant strength and conditioning coach, Mark Philippi.
When cameras cut to the Bears' sideline at one point, there was Philippi, looking like an absolute unit.
Philippi, who is 63 years young and in his second season with the Bears, is in better shape than most people can hope to be in at any stage of their life.
What made the shot of Philippi on the sideline even better was running back D'Andre Swift giving him a quick massage.
Kyle Monangai and D'Andre Swift on the sideline pic.twitter.com/ZmUTuJksgB
You could probably combine Swift and fellow back Kyle Monangai into one person and it still wouldn't create a bigger human than Philppi.
As you'd expect, the internet had plenty of fun with just one look at the Bears' coach.
"The Bears' asst strength coach is a seven-time World's Strongest Man qualifier and, thus, the final boss all other strength coaches must strive to defeat," Christian D'Andrea of For The Win said.
"I think the Bears have their solve for the O line issues.  Suit up Mark Philippi, their assistant strength and conditioning coach," one Bears fan said .
"Bears strength coach or bouncer at Richard’s Bar? Nobody knows for sure," another Bears fan said .
After seeing what he looks like, you won't be surprised to find out that Philippi was a world champion powerlifter and strongman competitor.
He competed in the World's Strongest Man competition seven times, finishing as high as seventh. Philippi also competed in the America's Strongest Man Competition and finished first in 1997.
In 1996, Philippi won the WDFPF World Powerlifting Championship and won the Beauty and the Beast (excellent name) strongman competition in 1998.
Despite his age, Philippi looks like he could give the Bears a few snaps along the offensive line. In fact, he was an offensive lineman during his college days at Montana Tech.
Prior to joining the Bears' coaching staff in 2025, Philippi owned and directed performance training at Philippi Sports Institute in Las Vegas that trained Olympic gold medal competitors.
Before that, Philippi was the director of strength and conditioning for UNLV Athletics for 15 years, with his role involving overseeing the sports performance programs for over 400 athletes per year.
Safe to say, the Bears' strength and conditioning program is in good hands with Philippi around.

title: D'Andre Swift Could be Headed for Punishment After Ben Johnson's Response to Latest Fumble
full_text:
When the Chicago Bears struggle on offense the way they did in Week 11, the last thing the team can afford is a turnover.
The Bears had not one, but two on Sunday in the 21-13 win over the New Orleans Saints, with Caleb Williams throwing a pick on a tipped pass and D'Andre Swift losing a fumble .
Swift's fumble came in the fourth quarter, when the Bears were holding a 21-10 lead. Thankfully, it didn't prove to be costly, as Chicago's defense got a stop on the next series.
That said, just because the fumble didn't impact the Bears doesn't mean head coach Ben Johnson won't punish him for it.
After the game, head coach Ben Johnson had a one-word response when asked if he had anything else to say to Swift following his latest fumble.
"With Swift, when he puts the ball on the ground (against the Saints), I know you've talked to him about it already. Is there anything more to say to him or no?" a reporter asked .
The fact that Johnson had no desire to give a longer response like he did the last time Swift fumbled tells you everything you need to know about how frustrated the Bears head coach is.
There is no doubt Swift is in the dog house, but will that be enough for him to get benched?
This isn't the first time Swift has fumbled away the ball this season. Swift also lost a fumble in Week 2 against the Minnesota Vikings, and in Week 4 versus the New York Jets.
The latter fumble got Swift benched in the second half , which led to a more detailed response from Johnson than the one he gave after the Week 11 turnover. That's why Johnson's one-word answer on Sunday was very telling.
"Yeah, it's very uncharacteristic," he said of Swift's fumbling issue after Week 4. "I think the (fumble against the Jets) was egregious, though. That's one that we can't have.
"There's too many times where the ball is getting away from our body and he knows that. And he takes a lot of pride in it, hence why it's never been an issue over the course of his career."
We would definitely put the possibility of a Swift benching on the table or, at the very least, a reduced workload in Week 12.
The Bears have the option to take one of those two approaches thanks to the presence of Kyle Monangai, who returned in Week 11 after missing the last five games. Monangai has actually been the Bears' best running back when on the field this season.
That said, the Bears are also slated to play a massively important game against the Detroit Lions in Week 12 on Thanksgiving, so that could deter Johnson from punishing his veteran back.

title: Bears Rookie Zavion Thomas Sure to Get More Touches After Big Day
full_text:
CHICAGO — Considering how little opportunity there can be for younger wide receivers in the Bears offense , rookie Zavion Thomas has simply had to make do with just 10 targets over the first nine games.
The speedy third-rounder from LSU finally made a statement on offense Sunday to end a week when no one could have even been sure he would play because of an ankle injury suffered during practice.
Thomas made the only Bears plays 20 yards or longer during their 21-13 win and provided hope he could be the speed factor they need to open up bigger throws downfield in the season's second half.
“He's a player that continues to learn, and we get more trust in every week," coach Ben Johnson said. "I know he's working hard behind the scenes. (Receivers) Coach (Antwaan) Randle El, (offensive quality control) coach Isaiah Ford, they're spending a lot of extra time with him. So, you see over the course of a week of practice that he's more on it. As a result, the coaches and his teammates have more trust in him."
What a catch by Zavion Thomas. Check out the route too. So quick in and out of the break after the wiggle. 👀 #DaBears #Bears pic.twitter.com/E0fX0Bog72
Thomas caught a 40-yard pass downfield near the sideline on third-and-17 to ignite a drive to a field goal for a 19-10 Bears lead in the third quarter. His 30-yard run on a reverse in the second quarter came two plays before Caleb Williams threw a 15-yard TD pass to Colston Loveland.
"Each and every opportunity I get a chance to make a play that's what I'm going to do," Thomas said.
He more or less has to with Rome Odunze, Luther Burden, Colston Loveland and Kalif Raymond all ranking ahead of him in receiver pecking order. The ledger Sunday read two catches for 56 yards on three targets, a 30-yard run and a 29-yard kick return.
Another Bears rookie making an impact! Zavion Thomas with a big pickup on the trick play NOvsCHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/aY4TjGV5pB
As impressive as both the big plays were, the catch he made in the fourth quarter on third-and-1 for 16 yards might have been the biggest. He came back after his route to the sidelines and caught a pass Williams threw on the run under pressure to his left for a 16-yard gain, getting the Bears out of a hole when they led 21-10. Replay verified the catch.
The reception let the Bears chew more clock and the Saints simply didn't have time to do anything at the end but try a failed onside kick.
“He made a hell of a catch right there," Williams said. "Couldn't get all of it behind the throw because of, I think it was (Saints LB Danny) Stutsman, right there, right next to me, running with me. And so he made an aggressive movement. We locked eyes, and he came back and made a play for us.”
If Zavion gets outside to the hashes instead of trying to split two defenders here he scores. Never ran that fast in my life maybe it’s hard to make that cut, but he had a lineman with leverage. Use it. https://t.co/OkyBKxPWui pic.twitter.com/pNUogYajTZ
Thomas is still a rookie, so he's coming into games with a specific set of plays designed to take advantage of his 4.28-second 40-yard speed.
"His package of plays that he goes into a game with, it's going to continue to grow," Johnson said. "We know how much of a playmaker he can be when the ball gets in his hands.
Caleb with a 40-yard dime to Zavion 🔥 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/IrHylu2dhR
"Elite speed; I think for a guy that fast, it's really impressive how well he can track the ball and has natural hands when it comes to that. I think we'll continue to see where it goes. He's got a really bright future.”
Expect that package of plays to continue expanding as long as Thomas is going to produce results like Sunday, when he made three of their six longest plays.

title: Jeffery Simmons Wins the Race to the Quarterback in Bears' Victory
full_text:
CHICAGO — Jeffery Simmons' romp through opposing backfields to quarterbacks continues. It apparently needs to because the Bears' offense suddenly needs all the help it can get.
Caleb Williams and the Bears' offense has to be especially grateful because without Simmons, Montez Sweat and blitzing defensive backs, there might have been some explaining to do Sunday. As it was, the Bears had a 21-13 ho-hum win over a 3-7 Saints team that plays most teams tough but manages to lose.
Simmons' three sacks brought his three-game Chicago total to five and obviously has opponents scrambling to do anything they can to slow him.
Good luck with that. He played with a brace on his left knee Sunday after a minor knee injury and still ravaged New Orleans' passing game.
"He's a momentum changer, swings the momentum in our favor a lot of times," Williams said.  "So having him on the team, having him making plays for us, having him bringing the energy, having him lead, it's been awesome, it's been fun. It's been fun to be able to watch myself."
Jeffery Simmons grabbing Montez Sweat on the sideline after the Sweat sack pic.twitter.com/Q8TCDRZZQK
Simmons had two sacks by halftime, then the last one for a 13-yard loss came when he basically threw Tyler Shough to the ground. It came a play after the two-minute warning and left the Saints in such poor down and distance they had to settle for a 51-yard field goal before trying an onside kick , one that went straight into Luther Burden's hands for the Bears win.
Simmons had flipped with defensive end Austin Booker and came from outside on the rush.
"At that point in the game to be on the same page with the rest of the front, coming off the edge, that moment it's always about for me to embrace it," Simmons said. "In my mind it's 'Let's go win this game.' You know, get our offense back the ball so they can go kneel it and call game.
Another look at the Jeffery Simmons move on the 3rd sack. pic.twitter.com/njolPyUmcc
"It's not so much what I'm thinking about outside that moment. In that particular moment it was all right, go win this game for the team."
Booker moved inside to the 3-technique for that play after Simmons suggested it.
"That's what it is for us up front, where we don't have a selfish room and everyone wants to win a football game," Simmons said. "With us being on the same page, with us not having selfish guys in the room, that's what made that sack."
For all of last year and part of this season the Bears had the look of an explosive offense and an inconsistent defense. Simmons had brought a new dynamic. They're starting to look like Bears teams of old that could control opposing offenses with their rush. Their six sacks was a season high and brought the team total to 32.
They had an interception by Dillon Thieneman and a fumble recovery by Booker after a hit by Clark Phillips, who also had a sack. Cam Lewis also added a sack off a blitz.
The key sack without doubt was from Sweat for his first career safety. Shough held the ball too long near the end of the third quarter and the two points put the Bears up 21-10, making it a two-score game throughout the fourth quarter.
Sweat said he feels a bit rejuvenated with his college friend and All-Pro on the defensive front now taking up double teams, taking names and kicking QB rear.
"It's a race," Sweat said. "Who's going to get there first?
"Obviously he (Simmons) was getting a little faster than a couple of the other people."
Not on the safety, though Sweat's big tackle in the end zone let the Bears play comfortably ahead and continue to tee off.
Dennis Allen uh stanky leg attempt? pic.twitter.com/MlCmHh8djG
"The game is won in all three phases," Simmons said. "We know it don't matter where they get the ball at, as a defense we've got to draw the line.
"Especially when it really matters guys have got to make plays and that's what we did, across the field, across the board."
It's always a good thing to know someone besides Caleb Williams and the offense can take matters into their hands and win. However, they're going to need the offense to activate to a higher level on Thanksgiving at Detroit.
Jeffery Simmons said on his final sack he asked Austin Booker to switch so he could get a 1-on-1 with the RT. "When you don't have a selfish room, everyone wants to win a football game. I said 'Book let's switch on this one,' and he said let's do it." #Bears pic.twitter.com/sJKyGzQSas

title: NFC North Standings: Where Bears Sit Entering Week 12 After Vikings, Lions Games on Sunday
full_text:
With the Chicago Bears, Detroit Lions and Minnesota Vikings all having completed their Week 11 games , it's time to take a look at the updated NFC North standings going into Week 12.
The only NFC North squad that didn't play in Week 11 was the Green Bay Packers, who were on a bye.
During the early slate on Sunday, the Bears emerged victorious over the New Orleans Saints , 21-13, and the Lions defeated the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, 31-21.
Then, on Sunday night, the Vikings' vaunted defense had its worst showing of the 2026 campaign after getting blown out by the San Francisco 49ers.
Now, here's where things stand in the NFC North going into Week 12.
1. Detroit Lions (8-2) 2. Chicago Bears (8-2) 3. Minnesota Vikings (7-3) 4. Green Bay Packers (6-4)
The Lions own first place over the Bears going into Week 12 because of their superior divisional record.
Detroit is a perfect 2-0 in the NFC North thanks to wins over the Packers and Vikings, and Chicago is 0-2 because of losses to Minnesota and Green Bay .
With how close things are in the division right now, the Bears have got to secure some NFC North wins moving forward or else they could fall victim to tie-breakers.
With both teams sitting at 8-2, the Lions and Bears will be playing for sole possession of first place in the NFC North on Thanksgiving Day.
With a loss in that game, the Bears would either remain in second place if the Vikings lose, or they would fall to third if Minnesota wins because the Vikings own the head-to-head tie-breaker thanks to the Week 2 win over Chicago .
The Lions can't go any lower than second place with a loss even if the Vikings win because Detroit beat Minnesota earlier in the season.
The Vikings can move up to second place with a win and a Bears loss, but they would remain in third place if the Bears beat Detroit. Green Bay will remain in the cellar for another week no matter what.
As we already noted, the Lions and Bears will square off at Ford Field in Week 12 on Thanksgiving and the winner will sit in first place going into Week 13.
Before that, the Packers will travel to SoFi Stadium to take on the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday, and the Vikings will host the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday afternoon.

title: Kyle Monangai's Return Fails to Activate Bears Running Game in Rough Win
full_text:
CHICAGO — There are real questions at this point about the Bears offense in more than one regard.
Caleb Williams normally gets his share of scrutiny when things are as rugged for the Bears passing game, and after Sunday's 21-13 win over New Orleans he was anything but elated with the point production.
However, the Bears running game continues to struggle along even after Kyle Monangai came back to the lineup. The bottom line looks fine at 4.4 yards a carry and 33 rushes for 146 yards but coach Ben Johnson had another view of it afterward.
“We weren't as consistent running the ball as we had wanted to be coming off the bye, that was a point of emphasis for us," Johnson said. "When I looked at our runners, they were under 4 yards a carry. That (rushing) efficiency stat that we talked about, we weren't hitting that.
"We'll see why that was the case, and we'll go from there.”
Caleb Williams asked about Kyle Monangai being back. pic.twitter.com/wOGk5u6bLp
The 146-yard total was their most since they beat the Jets in Week 4, but it included 30 from wide receiver Zavion Thomas on a reverse, and 11 from Williams on scrambles, as well as another 3 by Luther Burden on an end-around. The backs had 27 runs for 102 yards and D'Andre Swift led the way with 51 yards on 13 attempts. He did add a TD on a 3-yard shovel-type flip from Williams, but added his third lost fumble.
The disappointing aspect was just 18 on eight carries by Monangai after he missed five games due to turf toe and a thumb injury.
Also, the passing game in the second half went down the same path the running game seemed to take all day. They had only 68 passing yards in the second half, as Williams finished 15 of 23 for 181 yards
"I think it was sloppy as far as like turnovers, penalties and kind of, not loafing, but we didn't start as fast as we should have," tight end Colston Loveland said. "But we ended up winning time of possession at the end, which was pretty good. There was some good to take out of it."
Shovel pass to D'Andre Swift for 6 🐻 NOvsCHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/jq89cXduQK
There was good directly from Loveland in the first half, as well. He did his best Edwin Moses imitation and hurdled over on-coming safety Julian Blackmon when he caught a short pass and turned it into a 15-yard TD for a 16-0 Bears lead.
Loveland said he never ran the hurdles in high school but maybe he missed his calling. Afterward Loveland had a brief conversation with Blackmon.
"After the game he said, 'Man why'd you have to do me like that?' "
It was one of the few times the Bears offense able to embarrass the Saints, who have lost only twice by more than a TD and conversion.
"I think we can be a lot better," Williams said in a classic understatement. "I think there was  opportunity for a lot of points out there, whether it's us being on the same page, us being efficient running and efficient passing.
"I think there was a lot more we left out there and a lot more we can be better at this week coming up."
Colston Loveland hurdle and TD! NOvsCHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/F1Ivvb3Pas

title: Bears Survive Uneven, Potentially Costly Win Over Saints at Soldier Field
full_text:
The Chicago Bears picked up a 21-13 win over the New Orleans Saints at Soldier Field that left plenty to be desired.
First and foremost to be desired: good health. Chicago lost running back Roschon Johnson to an ankle injury in kickoff coverage that saw him carted off the field . The Bears also lost Theo Benedet with under eight minutes remaining in the fourth quarter to go to the injury tent .
Johnson's injury comes as Ben Johnson is unimpressed with his running back room. While Salvon Ahmed took advantage of the opportunity, Kyle Monangai struggled in his return from toe and thumb injuries and D'Andre Swift underwhelmed in the passing game and on his 13 carries.
Meanwhile, Benedet's injury reshuffles the left tackle deck once again. Ozzy Trapilo stepped in on the blindside in Benedet's stead. Braxton Jones has been on IR since after Week 3 with a season-ending knee injury . Trapilo's health after returning from a patellar tendon injury will be under the gun as he potentially prepares for an extended role if Benedet misses time.
It didn't feel like Chicago was in complete control of New Orleans as the game progressed on Sunday. Building a 16-0 lead and easing off the gas pedal is not characteristic of a Johnson-coached squad. If anything, the Bears are the comeback kings, not the blown-lead kings over the past two years.
Chicago won the rushing battle, but only because of a reverse trick play to receiver Zavion Thomas for 30 yards. Williams was outgained by Saints quarterback Tyler Shough, who didn't have adequate protection on Sunday afternoon. Jeffery Simmons led the way for the Bears defense with three sacks and three quarterback hits, and if not for Chicago's efforts on that end, this would've been an upset opportunity.
At this point in the season, you're hoping to see a should-be contender dot its I's and cross its T's. Offensively, the Bears were unacceptable. Losing depth in the trenches and a body in the running back room and on special teams sets the team back despite the unimpressive win. For how long will be evident in the coming days.
Good teams get away with home duds like this against inferior teams every so often, but if this game isn't a warning sign that the product needs to be tightened up, Johnson will have plenty to answer for this offseason.

title: Jeffery Simmons Ties 2 Career-Best Marks in Week 11 Win, Continues to Prove Bears Right
full_text:
Jeffery Simmons has been everything the Chicago Bears could've hoped for over his first three games.
Simmons continued his hot start with the team in Week 11 against the New Orleans Saints when he was an absolute menace in the Bears' 21-13 victory at Soldier Field.
Simmons recorded four tackles, including three for loss, three sacks and three QB hits. According to Pro Football Focus , the Bears star recorded a team-high six pressures, also.
Since coming to Chicago, Simmons has recorded a whopping five sacks, including at least one in each game, and the Bears have permitted a total of 54 points in that span.
The Bears made a massive bet when they gave up two first-round picks for Simmons, which was a historic package for a defensive tackle. But, so far, Simmons has proven the Bears were wise to make that bet.
With his three sacks on Sunday, Simmons tied his career-high for sacks in a single game. He had accomplished that feat once before in 2021 against the Los Angeles Rams.
The other personal best Simmons matched was his sacks streak. With at least one sack in each of his last three games, Simmons has now done that four times in his career.
He did it once in 2022, and then twice in 2025. However, he posted 3.5 sacks during each of those streaks. This time around, Simmons has five.
As if all of that wasn't impressive enough, Simmons is the first Bears defensive tackle to record three sacks in a game since 2014.
Here's what Simmons said about his three-sack showing against the Saints:
“For me, as I learned as I got older and mature in this league, it’s just owning the moment," Simmons said , per Bears Insider's Michael Dwojak. "The plays will come to you when they really matter. I know this team brought me here and they expect me to win, especially my one-on-ones. So I take full advantage of them.”
One of those one-on-ones saw Simmons pull off a filthy swim move en route to a sack move while lined up at defensive end.
Simmons revealed that he asked edge rusher Austin Booker to switch spots before that snap.
"When you don't have a selfish room, everyone wants to win a football game. I said 'Book let's switch on this one,' and he said let's do it," he said , according to Josh Frydman of WGN News.
Simmons' contribution doesn't just stop at what he's doing on the field, though. The four-time Pro Bowler has quickly become a leader in the locker room, also.
"He’s quickly becoming a voice everyone hears," head coach Ben Johnson said of Simmons in his postgame comments.
The next step for Simmons is getting introduced to the Bears' rivalries with their NFC North opponents. That will happen on Thanksgiving in the game against the Detroit Lions.

title: Steelers' Cameron Heyward Adds Fuel to Joe Burrow's 2026 MVP Case With High Praise
full_text:
Longtime Pittsburgh Steeler and AFC North rival Cameron Heyward had high praise for Joe Burrow Tuesday afternoon on the Rich Eisen Show .
The six-time All-Pro defensive tackle called Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow the best quarterback the Steelers have played against so far this season.
Heyward praised Burrow’s timely delivery and consistency, noting that he has two strong receivers and that Cincinnati’s offense is performing well week after week.
"He's got two really good receivers (Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase), and their offense is humming. Week in and week out, they're delivering," said Heyward.
The Bengals offense has been humming. The Bengals offense has the fourth-most points scored in the NFL, averaging 30.3 points per game. The Bengals are also first in passing, thanks to Joe Burrow.
"Of the Quarterbacks we faced this year, Burrow's got to be at the top. You know, it's not really a shot at anybody, but when you look at what Burrow did this past week, he delivers the ball on time." Heyward told Rich Eisen.
Burrow is having an MVP-caliber season so far and leads the NFL in most major passing categories. Entering Week 11 Burrow was second in the NFL in passing yards with 2,795, only behind Jordan Love by 43 yards, and Love has played one more game than Burrow already this year, not having his bye week yet. Burrow leads the NFL in passing touchdowns with 27 and, most impressively, leads the NFL in completion percentage at an incredible 72.4%.
This was the second time Heyward had played the Bengals, having played them back in Week 3, defeating the Bengals 30-27. Eisen asked whether anything was different about Joe Burrow's approach on Sunday compared to earlier in the season.
"I don't think anything's changed in that. I think we were able to make some more plays, but you know, if you read out the scouting report, he did everything he said he was going to do, and man, the consistency is there. And you leave that game scratching your head and saying, 'What could you have done better?'" Heyward said.
Joe Burrow is turning heads across the NFL and putting on a show as he leads the Bengals to a 7-2 record and the top of the AFC North. Burrow continues to show week in and week out why he is the frontrunner for MVP, with plenty of highlights to back it up.
"You hate to be on somebody's clinic tape, but shoot, you've got to absorb it and move the hell on," Heyward said.

title: 'I Would Not Want To Play Cincinnati' - NFL Coaches, Executives Afraid of Bengals Approaching 2026 Playoffs
full_text:
The Bengals are striking fear into rival NFL executives.
The Athletic's Mike Sando polled coaches and executives across the league after Sunday's Week 11 action, and Cincinnati is the top team no one wants to face in the playoffs.
They have faced the 29th-ranked strength of schedule so far by opponent win rate and have only faced one contender: A 22-17 loss to Jacksonville earlier this season without Ja'Marr Chase for most of the game.
"The Bengals are the team no one wants to play, and also a team that hasn't played anyone of note beyond Jacksonville, which beat the Bengals 22-17 in Week 4," Sando penned before dropping a sourced quote. "'I would want to play Kansas City — I'd want to play Buffalo,' an exec from another team said. 'I would not want to play Cincinnati. Dexter (Lawrence) in the middle of that defense would be difficult. He would cause a lot of issues to your run game. (Boye) Mafe is a really good piece.'"
The NFL is starting to realize Cincinnati can defend much better than in years past and is finally blocking well for Joe Burrow.
"You know there's something different about the Bengals when their defense is mentioned as something other than a liability," Sando wrote. "'My gut is that Cincinnati's the best team in that group,' another exec said. Burrow has posted career bests through nine games in completion rate (74.7 percent), passing yards (2,795), touchdown passes (27), passer rating (117.7), EPA per pass play (0.27) and, critically, sack rate (4.5 percent). He's better than even odds to win MVP.
"For once, Cincinnati isn't the AFC contender with pressing offensive line problems, as Kansas City and Jacksonville both have issues at tackle. 'You still have your woes if you are getting 36 hung on you by Tennessee (as the case was in Week 8), but if they can just get league-average defense with that quarterback and those receivers, that is good enough,' another exec said. The Bengals rank 18th in defensive EPA per play ahead of Monday night's game at Washington."
The league is perking up, and Cincinnati just has to keep their heads down and keep focus.

title: Bengals Have Golden Opportunity to Create Separation in AFC North on Monday Night
full_text:
The Bengals moved into sole possession of first place in the AFC North last week with a victory over the Steelers. Now they have a chance to strengthen their lead this week following a favorable Sunday afternoon. The Steelers lost to the Eagles in a major 19-16 upset to fall to 6-4 on the year. Pittsburgh down to third in the division behind the Browns who move to second-place with the same record. The Steelers have lost back-to-back games for the first time this season.

The Ravens chances of mounting a comeback in the division meanwhile have all but extinguished as they lost a close game to the Panthers on Sunday to move to 4-7 on the year.

title: Key Commanders Defender Suffers Practice Injury Ahead of Monday Night Showdown vs. Bengals
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals are coming off of the most emotional win of their season. A decisive 38-18 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers last Sunday night has this fan base fully believing that this season could end in February.
After such a big win, it's important for the Bengals to keep their focus on the task at hand. Next up, it's another prime time showdown, this time with the Washington Commanders on Monday Night Football.
The Commanders are not having the season they were hoping for, and a potential injury to their secondary could make things even a lot harder for the team on Monday night.
On Friday, it was revealed that Commanders cornerback Amik Robertson was held out of practice. According to JP Finlay of NBC 4 Sports , Commanders head coach Dan Quinn revealed that Robertson was injured on the last play of practice on Thursday, and he decided to sit Robertson out of practice on Friday.
Pro Football Focus has Robertson as the 12th-ranked cornerback in the NFL this season. The last thing any team wants to have happen before playing the Bengals is injuries in the secondary, especially when it comes to a player who's playing at the level of Robertson.
Even if Robertson is a full go on Monday night, the Commanders are going to have their hands full. Last Sunday, the Bengals' offense looked like an unstoppable force while taking down their longtime rival.
Quarterback Joe Burrow is playing at an elite level. Actually, he should be the leader of all MVP conversations. The Bengals quarterback is second in passing yards this season with 2,795 and leads the league in touchdown passes with 27.
An offense this good isn't led by just one great performance. Wide receivers Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase are the best receiving duo in the NFL. Chase is fourth in the league in receiving yards with 878, and Higgins is sixth with 824. There's a world where both of these guys get to 1,500 receiving yards this season.
There's been a lot of talk about the Bengals not being successful in the run game. However, if they can continue to have this much success through the air, those conversations will start to get a little quiet.
Robertson's status for Monday night is one to keep an eye on. But something tells me the Bengals' offense would rather he be on the field just to prove their greatness.

title: Bengals Placing Defensive Talent on Injured Reserve Ahead of Commanders Game

title: Joe Burrow Draws MASSIVE Comparison to PEAK Tom Brady From Someone Who Would Know
full_text:
Joe Burrow is currently on the best run of his career to this point with 2,795 yards, 27 passing touchdowns, and a completion percentage of 74.7%. His level of play has drawn comparisons to that of Peyton Manning's historic 2013 season in which he threw 55 touchdowns, and Tom Brady's legendary 2007 season. CLNS Cincy's Mike Petraglia who covered the Patriots throughout all six of Brady's Super Bowl wins with the team joined First Word and claimed Burrow is playing comparably to Brady from '07 and 2010.
He also compared the Bengals offense to that of the St. Louis Rams 'Greatest Show on Turf' offense from 1999 and 2000.
"Joe Burrow is playing like Tom Brady '07 and 2010, he is playing that level of football," Petraglia said . "The other team that keeps coming back to me are the 1999-2000 St. Louis Rams 'The Greatest Show on Turf' because of the different and dynamic ways they can attack defenses."
Burrow is currently on pace for 51 passing touchdowns, a mark that would eclipse Brady's 50 from 2007, and Kurt Warner's 41 in 1999. He is also set to blow past both legendary quarterbacks with 5,279 passing yards, and a season-long completion percentage of 74.7 that would set a new NFL record.
The largest question surrounding the Bengals and Burrow's offensive success is whether or not it is a sustainable formula for success for the colder months of the NFL season. Petraglia however dismissed this idea and acknowledged the teams past success of throwing the ball effectively in December and January weather. He used the teams playoff games against the Chiefs and Ravens in 2021 and 2022 as examples of this while conceding that scoring fewer than 30 points is more realistic.
"The Bengals are able to throw in cold weather, wet weather, it doesn't matter, I think they're gonna be able to do what they do downfield," Petraglia said . "We've seen it before, go back to 2021, remember the games against Kansas City and Baltimore, those two games were not in warm weather, it was cold and they were able to go on the road and still put up points, are you gonna be able to put up 30-35 points in the playoffs? The Patriots in '07 scored 13 points in the Super Bowl, things change."
Should Burrow continue to play at the level he has so far this season, he should surely win his first MVP. Both Brady and Manning won the honor in their 50-plus touchdown campaigns before advancing to the Super Bowl.

title: Joe Burrow Downplays Historic Pace Amid Potential Record-Breaking Season
full_text:
Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow is well aware how well he and the offense as a whole have been playing.
What he wouldn’t acknowledge is that has any meaning heading into Monday night at Washington, or that the record pace he’s on has any bearing on what the second half of the season will look like.
“Every game has its own world and, and every game is gonna require something different out of us,” Burrow said. “Not every game has to be pretty for us to win, but certainly it helps when it is.”
The last few weeks have been better than good.
Burrow is on pace to break his own franchise records in almost every category in addition to having one of the best seasons in NFL history.
Through nine games, his stats are better than most of the recent MVP winners at this point.
“Pace doesn’t mean anything to me,” Burrow said. “We’re just past the halfway point. There’s a lot of football to be played.”
If there’s one thing from the first nine games that could be relevant Monday night, and moving into December, it’s how good Burrow has been against the blitz.
It’s something he’s always been good at, but like most parts of his game, it’s hitting astronomical heights this season.
He was 11 of 11 for 181 yards – 16.5 yards per attempt – in Sunday night’s 38-18 dismantling of the Pittsburgh Steelers.
And when blitzed over the last three games, Burrow is 30 of 33 for 391 yards with five touchdowns and one interception for a passer rating of 143.
Earlier this week, offensive coordinator Dan Pitcher said the offense’s mindset has been “please blitz us.”
Washington will acquiesce.
Led by defensive coordinator and former Bengals assistant Daronte Jones, the Commanders are blitzing at the third highest rate in the league this season.
“We have to be on our Ps and Qs in protection,” Burrow said . “I’ve got to know where my hot reads are and where I can get the ball out quickly. Gotta be ready for Cover 0.
“It starts with the protection plan, No. 1, and then you have to go out and execute it,” he continued . “Our running backs are two of the best at picking those blitzes up, and we always have a great plan and a great feel for how teams want to blitz and want to attack us. Our offensive line has obviously done a great job the last couple of weeks. And when you can pick those blitzes up, there's a lot of space out there.”
While the Commanders bring a lot of pressure, they don’t have a success rate to match.
They rank 12th in pressures (86), 17th in quarterback hits (53) and 23rd in sacks (18).
The Steelers threw a lot of pressure at Burrow on Sunday night but not only couldn’t get home, they got repeatedly burned.
That will be the goal again Monday night for Burrow and the offense.
“They certainly are an aggressive defense,” Burrow said. “When you face an aggressive defense, if you don't make them pay for  being that way, then they're going to continue to do it.”

title: Bengals Injury Report: Dalton Risner's Status Gets Murkier Following Latest Practice

The Bengals are keeping decent health rolling following the second practice of Commanders week, but illness is hanging around. Dalton Risner's (knees) status for Monday's game got hazier after sitting out a second consecutive practice this week.
