title: Where Browns Need Most Help in Upcoming 2027 NFL Draft
full_text:
The Browns are in a good position at 6-4 and have a chance to make the playoffs. While Cleveland is aiming to play in January, it should also keep an eye on the 2027 NFL Draft.
Cleveland still has issues to address, and here are some areas the Browns need to upgrade by the start of the 2027 season.
The Browns will be in the quarterback market come April, no matter how this season finishes. Deshaun Watson has done a solid job getting the Browns to six wins, but he's not the answer.
Watson likely won't be back with the Browns next season, as they'll probably cut him by March 13. Even if he is back in Cleveland, it will be on a shorter deal to be a bridge to the rookie.
The Browns were unable to draft a quarterback in the first round of the past two drafts, and next year will be crucial for addressing this need. The quarterback class might not live up to expectations as some people anticipated coming into the season.
Still, more first-round options will be available than in the previous two drafts, when only four quarterbacks were selected — two in 2025 and two in 2026.
The Browns will need to keep looking for offensive line help next year, even though they overhauled the entire offensive line last season. One position Cleveland has to look at is center.
Starting center Elgton Jenkins is on a two-year, $24 million deal with a possible out in the offseason. The Browns drafted Alabama center Parker Brailsford in the fifth round of the 2026 draft, but he suffered a hand/thumb injury in training camp that hindered his progress.
Cleveland could still believe Brailsford has a chance to be a starter, but the same franchise took Luke Wypler in the sixth round of the 2023 draft, and he's only made seven starts in his career. Many late-round picks don't see significant playing time in the NFL, so counting on Brailsford to be the starter might not be the best option.
Cleveland will need to address the defensive end position early in the draft. The Browns traded for Rams pass rusher Jared Verse in June, but he has yet to record a sack in 10 games. While it may be too early to panic about Verse, who is only in his third NFL season and recorded 12 sacks in 34 games with Los Angeles, the defensive end position will still require attention, regardless of his improvement this season.
Additionally, Alex Wright will not play this season due to a torn Achilles he suffered in August. Sam Williams, Isaiah McGuire and Derek Barnett are all set to become free agents. Significant uncertainty surrounds the pass rush.
It is unclear if Wright will return to his usual form after his injury, and it's unknown who else will be on the roster at the position if these three players join new teams.
Daniel is a sports writer from Northeast Ohio. He has followed the Browns, Cavs, Guardians, and Buckeyes for years and loves sharing his thoughts on the team.

title: Why the Browns Were Among the Biggest Week 11 Winners During a Bye Week
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns had Sunday off with their Week 11 bye week . Despite this, the team still had some things go their way after a couple of different games from around the league.
Let's take a look at some of the ways the Browns won during their week off:
Every season, no matter the team, if you are on bye week and get to watch your division rivals lose, it's a win for your team.
However, the losses from the Pittsburgh Steelers and Baltimore Ravens are even sweeter for the Browns, who now climb back into second place in the AFC North.
Pretty sweet results for the work they put in this week.
Now, not only did these losses help in divisonal rankings, they helped in a bigger way as well.
THE BROWNS DIDN’T PLAY TODAY AND THEIR ODDS TO MAKE THE PLAYOFFS HAVE RISEN TO 62% 🤯 👉 https://t.co/VQqxLTzl57 pic.twitter.com/l365JeLWCC
Now that Cleveland has the advantage over Pittsburgh, the Browns move up a slot and are now the sixth seed in the AFC playoff picture. According to league sources, Cleveland has a 58% chance of making the postseason after this week.
Looking at some non-AFC North games, the Browns also had some help from the Denver Broncos.
In their divisional matchup, Denver beat the Las Vegas Raiders 38-24.
This is huge for the Browns because not only do they host the Raiders in week 12 on Sunday Night Football, but they are competing for a wild-card spot with them.
Let's take a deeper dive into this next matchup against the Raiders and highlight another aspect of any given bye week.
With all of the factors mentioned already, this next game for the Browns is arguably the most important matchup yet.
Looking at some teams trying to jump into wild-card playoff spots, the New England Patriots sit right outside at number eight with a 5-5 record. After them, there's the Houston Texans with a record of 4-6, and then the Raiders in spot 10 with a 4-7 record.
For Cleveland, they have already beaten the Texans and Steelers, and with Drake Maye going down for New England, the Raiders are, in a sense, one of the final wins needed to solidify at least a tiebreaker over some close playoff competition.
Fernando Mendoza's first INT of the game is a pick-six pic.twitter.com/64mNEVsSzZ
As for the matchup itself, the Browns got another win from the bye week. That is extra time to study a rookie quarterback with hardly any NFL film.
Fernando Mendoza is now the guy for the Raiders following the Kirk Cousins trade at the deadline.
Against the Broncos, the score may say Denver won by two touchdowns, but that was thanks to a late-game pick-six from the Broncos' defense that got the score to that point.
In other words, Mendoza had a chance to lead his team to victory in his first career start, and finished the game going 18/37 for 267 yards, three touchdowns, and an interception.
No matter what, the Browns were very fourtunate to have a later bye week this season.
The ability to get rest in week 11 before attempting to make a playoff push in the middle of a five-game home stand is a gift sent from the schedule makers.
The Browns now have to capitalize on all the losses from close competition and come out with a win over the Raiders on Sunday Night Football.

title: 2 Winners, 2 Who Have Fallen Short from Browns’ 2026 NFL Draft
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns put together another quality draft in the 2026 installment of the festivities.
With a sizable collection of picks at their disposal, the Browns' front office made several trades and moved around the draft board before ultimately selecting 10 different players.
Here are the four players who have stood out the most from the draft class, both positively and negatively:
Wideout Denzel Boston was taken with the Browns' first selection of the second round, going with the No. 39 pick.
Immediately stealing the show, Boston, a former member of the Washington Huskies, has been one of quarterback Deshaun Watson's favorite targets. He made an immediate impact in his first few games at the professional level, recording 16 receptions for 330 yards and three touchdowns across his first five games.
Heading into the back half of his rookie campaign, he has 33 total receptions for 523 yards and three scores.
Going in the second round, he is showing first-round-level talent and is the frontrunner for the Offensive Rookie of the Year award.
There is still plenty of time for center Parker Brailsford to get his feet back underneath himself and establish a role on the Browns' depth chart, but because of early-career injuries , he hasn't been able to do that just yet.
Selected in the fifth round with the 146th pick, there were relatively high expectations for him as he was somewhat expected to be the No. 2 to Elgton Jenkins.
First reported on by Cleveland Analyst Terry Pluto, Brailsford was impressing the organization from top to bottom.
"The Browns were extremely impressed in spring practices with rookie Parker Brailsford," he wrote back in July. The rookie has a legitimate chance to win the starting center spot. He was a fifth-round pick who started 42 games in college..."
There is still time to turn things around, but Brailsford will likely have to wait until the offseason to attempt a revival in the Browns' depth chart.
Joining an already well-rounded defense and a safety room anchored by Ronnie Hickman and Grant Delpit, Emmanuel McNeil-Warren had a hill to climb to get legitimate playing time on Sundays.
However, after capitalizing on limited opportunities to impress, it was clear that McNeil-Warren has what it takes to play at the highest level of the game.
Across 10 games played and four started, the Browns' 58th pick in the draft has posted 50 total tackles, three for a loss and four pass deflections . His impact is really felt in the run defense, though, as he consistently lays heavy hits and fills lanes.
He is also rated as the highest-graded rookie this season, posting a grade of 89.9, according to Pro Football Focus. That mark is better than players like Kansas City's Mansoor Delane, Carolina's Zakee Wheatley and even Boston.
Emmanuel McNeil-Warren is looking special pic.twitter.com/zcF1Nj0Bsb
If he is able to keep his current pace up, he may be able to sneak into the Defensive Rookie of the Year race.
Cleveland's defense is young, impressionable and has tons of room to grow, and now with McNeil-Warren in the mix, they look even better than they did heading into Week 1.
Like Brailsford, tight end Joe Royer was dealt a bad hand to begin his career.
While there is no official confirmation of what is going on behind the scenes, he has not been able to play at all this season. The Browns fifth round pick, 170th overall, was expected to join the team and be a rising counterpart to star tight end Harold Fannin Jr.
Instead, that role has been filled by journeyman Blake Whiteheart.
When asked about Royer's status earlier in the year, head coach Todd Monken declined to open the conversation.
"I am not going to comment on that," he said.
Browns coach Todd Monken was asked if he expects rookie TE Joe Royer, who has missed all of training camp for personal reasons, to play for the team this season. Monken: “I’m not going to comment on that.”
Royer will hopefully get things cleared up before returning to the gridiron and becoming a critical piece of the offense.

title: Deshaun Watson's 2026 Campaign Is Putting Him Among Browns' Best QBs
full_text:
Deshaun Watson's production this season has been quietly putting him on pace to join the franchise record books.
Heading into Week 12 of the 2026 regular season, Watson has the Browns sitting at a 6-4 record, and the top spot in the AFC North is still within reach. Along the way, the 31-year-old has battled through injury to stay on the field , all while leading the team to six game-winning drives.
Down the stretch of games, he is one of the league's most clutch quarterbacks. In the final two minutes of fourth quarters, he is tied for the most completions (19) and most passing touchdowns (two), while leading the league in passing yards, interceptions and passer rating.
When the game is on the line, Watson has been stealing the show and delivering for Cleveland.
Deshaun Watson in final 2 minutes of 4th quarters this season 19 completions (t-most in NFL) 273 Pass Yards (most in NFL) 2 Pass TD (t-most in NFL) 0 INT (t-best in NFL) 141.8 Pass Rating (best in NFL) pic.twitter.com/DnYLKGMprV
But it seems that the attention he draws for his clutch genes may be overshadowing just how consistent his numbers have been this season.
Throwing for 2,118 yards, seven touchdowns and four interceptions on a 65.1% completion rate, he is on pace to put together one of the best statistical seasons for a Browns quarterback in the 21st century.
Watson, in the final year of his five-year, $230 million deal , is currently averaging 20.9 completions, 32.1 attempts, 235.3 passing yards, 0.78 touchdowns and 0.44 interceptions per game. Those numbers show that he may not be scoring an awful lot, but he is routinely getting the team down the field and protecting the football.
His interception percentage is at a measly 1.4%, which is tied for the second-lowest of his career, behind only his 2020 Pro Bowl season with the Houston Texans.
If he is able to keep up his current averages for the next seven games, which would put him at 16 regular-season games on the 2026 season, he would finish with 3,765 passing yards, 12 touchdowns and seven interceptions. He would also maintain a 65.1% completion rate, putting him just shy of the 4,000-yard mark.
So few interceptions would bring his interception percentage to the lowest mark in Browns history, while his total passing yards would be seventh . He would trail only Brian Sipe (1979, 1980, 1981), Bernie Kosar (1986), Baker Mayfield (2019) and Derek Anderson (2007) for the top spot.
But if he stayed over 200 yards per game and sprinkled in a few 300-yard outings, he could jump even further up the list.
Watson may have put the Browns in a unique situation since joining the team back in early 2022, one that many teams around the league will likely never have to go through, but to hold a black cloud over his head during a season that he's looked relatively strong in is unfair.
Not only is he projected to finish towards the top of many franchise-best statistical ladders, but the team itself is as well.
With six wins already through 10 games, the Browns already have more wins than in 15 other seasons since returning to the NFL in 1999. The franchise has finished with five or fewer wins in 15 of its 26 completed campaigns since then.
If the Browns even finish the year splitting the final six games, going 3-3, they would still finish with the fifth-most amount of wins over the last 25+ years. The only seasons the franchise finished with nine or more wins were 2002 (9-7), 2007 (10-6), 2020 (11-5) and 2023 (11-6).
In those seasons, the Browns were led by Tim Couch (2002), Anderson (2007), Mayfield (2020) and Watson/Joe Flacco (2023).
Watson isn't the lone reason the Browns have been able to find the success they have during the 2026 season, nor do his numbers tell the full story, but for a franchise that has been searching for a competent quarterback for much of the 21st century, it is hard to overlook just how significant his contributions have been and could be.
And if he finishes the season strong, the front office will have to take a long and hard look at what the future of the franchise looks like before ultimately deciding if he's worth extending.

title: Bye Week Injury Update: Where Cleveland Browns Stand After First 10 Games of Season
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have been battered and bruised this season.
But every time it looks like they are going to be outmatched, guys step up to fill the necessary voids.
Coming out of the Week 11 bye, the Browns look to be pretty much all healthy, intact and ready to finish the year strong. With a 6-4 record, all while remaining in the hunt for the No. 1 spot in the AFC North and a playoff position, the Browns are set to finish the year on a high note.
Here is where the Browns stand coming out of the bye week:
Quarterback Deshaun Watson missed a Week 9 meeting with the New Orleans Saints due to concussion protocol, a situation that popped up following the Browns' Week 8 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers.
One of the most concerning things that can happen is post-concussion syndrome, which often occurs when an individual gets another concussion quickly following their initial. Watson being held out of Week 9, though, allowed him to return in Week 10 to take on the Houston Texans, where the Browns would win 27-24.
With no issues in that game, it seems that Watson is all good and will be able to lead the Browns through the final seven games of the season.
On Wednesday, Nov. 18, ESPN Insider Daniel Oyefusi confirmed that the Browns were letting the players off for most of the bye week, allowing them to get much-needed rest and time to spend on their own.
Some of the team's biggest leaders and heavy workload carriers were not stretching or doing much during individual drills. That group included the likes of cornerback Denzel Ward, defensive tackle Mason Graham, linebackers Carson Schwesinger and Quincy Williams, tight end Blake Whiteheart and offensive tackle Tytus Howard.
Browns holding a short practice today before letting players off for the rest of the bye week. Ronnie Hickman returned to practice after missing the Texans game with a concussion. A handful of guys were not stretching or doing much during individual drills: Denzel Ward, Mason…
Schwesinger and Graham have already been banged up a bit this season, so giving them time to catch back up is important.
Along with that squad, a different group of players was not seen at all, with rookie wideout Denzel Boston and rookie offensive guard Austin Barber standing out. Both have been heavily involved in the Browns' offense through their first year in the league.
There is no real concern that they are dealing with anything of note, but both will be interesting to follow after the bye.
Along with Barber and Boston, defensive ends Isaiah McGuire and Derek Barnett, and offensive lineman Elgton Jenkins were not seen either.
Safety Ronnie Hickman missed the Browns' win over the Texans due to a concussion.
However, he did return to practice on Wednesday to begin preparation for a return following the bye week. While rookie safety Emmanuel McNeil-Warren and standout safety Grant Delpit have done a good job locking down the position with him off the field, Hickman will give the team a boost in depth when he returns.
He has played in nine games this season, recording 57 tackles, four pass deflections, two fumble recoveries and one interception.
The Browns have been lucky to not place many players on the injured list this season.
The most recent addition was fullback Michael Burton, who was added on Nov. 14 ahead of the Texans game. He is set to be out for at least four weeks due to a calf injury.
Along with Burton, defensive tackle Kalia Davis, guard Teven Jenkins and running back Rahiem Sanders stand out as notable players on the injured reserve.
The Browns next hit the field on Sunday, Nov. 29, in a matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders from Huntington Bank Field in Cleveland. The two sides will play in a primetime showing at 8:20 p.m. EST.

title: Browns Have an Under-the-Radar Contract Extension Candidate Emerging
full_text:
When the Cleveland Browns used a second-round pick back in 2025 on a linebacker from UCLA, it was hard to understand just how impactful that player could be in the Orange and Brown.
But just north of 25 games in his professional career, former Bruin Carson Schwesinger has been unstoppable.
He has recorded a whopping 258 tackles, 17 tackles for a loss, 5.5 sacks and 13 quarterback hits , all while playing an active role in defending the passing game with four pass deflections and two interceptions. He plays hard, fights through injuries and leads one of the league's best defenses game in and game out.
Carson's been an absolute demon out there 😈 pic.twitter.com/oT4IcVP3k8
Earlier in the year, it looked like Schwesinger was going to miss a game due to injury, but as always, he fought to play on Sunday. Head coach Todd Monken, who is in his first season with the team, recognized immediately that he's the type of player who will do anything he can to play.
"And Carson, what's interesting, early in the week the trainers were semi-optimistic," Monken said back in mid-October. "But they said, Well, it's Carson.' And every time I'd see Carson and I'd ask him, he'd get this silly smirk on his face like, 'Do you know who you're talking to?'"
Earning AP Defensive Rookie of the Year honors in 2025, Schwesinger looks on his way to potential All-Pro status, or even the Defensive Player of the Year award race , as the 2026 season approaches the back half.
#Browns Carson Schwesinger is the only LB currently in the NFL with -100+ tackles -3 sacks -3 Forced Fumbles Doesn’t matter where on the field you are. If you have the ball Carson will find you pic.twitter.com/kzGabdYeUI
While it is great to see a player succeeding at the level Schwesinger has, especially considering he wasn't even a Top 15 pick, let alone a first-rounder, his quick rise to stardom puts the Browns' front office in a peculiar situation.
Do you lock down the 23-year-old on a long-term deal as soon as he is willing to talk about it? Or wait till the final year of his deal to begin talks?
It feels like in today's era of the game, some players aren't rewarded as often as they should be, at least on the money side.
Someone like Schwesinger, who has such a vital role in the day-to-day operations of the Browns' defense, shouldn't fall into such a framework. Instead, the Browns should do everything they can to give him an extension this offseason, locking him down as the long-term staple of the unit.
Back in 2020 , the Browns showed that type of loyalty to defensive end Myles Garrett, who still had two years left on his rookie deal. They signed him to one of the sport's biggest deals, with the contract containing $100 million in total guarantees, the most ever paid to a defensive player.
While Schwesinger may or may not get that type of deal, one that breaks open the league's linebacker market, he should still be treated like a top player on the defensive side of the ball.
Oftentimes, deals like this will come for those at the quarterback position, such as Josh Allen, Joe Burrow, Patrick Mahomes and Justin Herbert, among others.
But that shouldn't hurt the 23-year-old's chances of getting paid the big bucks.
If the front office was willing to do it on Garrett, there is no reason not to have a similar stance with Schwesinger.

title: 4 Browns Players Rank Top 10 in Highest-Graded Rookies This Season
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns exited the 2026 NFL Draft, and almost immediately, the praise started to come in.
Not only did the Browns' front office attack every offseason need the organization was facing, but it also seemingly grabbed the best player off the board at the same time. Not having to balance one or the other, but instead ending up in the right spot at the right time, gave the team arguably the best draft of anyone.
And through the first 10 games of the 2026 season, many of the players selected have shone brightly.
On Thursday, Nov. 19, the Pro Football Network announced its current highest-graded NFL offensive rookies this season, with four Browns first-years making the list.
Ranking third, offensive guard Austin Barber (77.5), who wasn't even a starter until injuries thrust him into the spotlight, took the top spot for the Browns. Following him at the No. 6 spot in the rankings, wideout Denzel Boston (75.0) was slotted in, with offensive tackle Spencer Fano (74.9) just a spot behind at No. 7. The final spot on the list, the No. 10 ranking, was given to wideout KC Concepcion (73.8).
📊 The highest-graded NFL offensive rookies this season, per PFN’s Impact metrics: 1. OG Vega Ioane, BAL (79.2) 2. RB Emmett Johnson, KC (77.6) 3. OG Austin Barber, CLE (77.5) 4. WR Caleb Douglas, MIA (76.4) 5. OT Kahlil Benson, KC (76.3) 6. WR Denzel Boston, CLE (75.0) 7. OT… pic.twitter.com/9dbDmZEumR
Such praise for Cleveland's rookies should come as no surprise, especially as both the stats and film show just how impactful they have been every game day.
Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson wouldn't have likely had the comeback season he has had so far without Boston and Concepcion.
The two have combined for a whopping 981 yards across 10 games, with Boston leading the way with 523 yards. Concepcion isn't too far behind, though, recording 458 yards.
Their two totals are ahead of every other wideout selected in the 2026 draft. The next closest to both Boston and Concepción is the Tennessee Titans' Carnell Tate with 413, while Caleb Douglas of the Miami Dolphins and Malachi Fields of the New York Giants sit below 400.
Rookie receiving leaders heading into Week 11: 1. Denzel Boston, Browns - 523 2. KC Concepcion, Browns - 458 3. Carnell Tate, Titans - 413 4. Caleb Douglas, Dolphins - 367 5. Malachi Fields, Giants - 350 Can one or both of the Browns rookies eclipse 1,000 yards in their rookie… pic.twitter.com/JdILfr26aX
Both Concepcion and Boston will likely be in the running for the Offensive Rookie of the Year award as the race heats up in the coming weeks. However, unless someone else really starts to stand out and puts together one of the best rookie stretches in recent memory, it seems like the two will just be competing against each other.
While Cleveland's flashy wideouts continue to steal the spotlight, the big men up front, Barber and Fano, continue to protect Watson so that he can find them down the field.
The two get a good bit of praise within Cleveland, but certainly deserve more on the national end.
Barber jumped headfirst into the starting spot at right guard with a back injury sustained by Teven Jenkins early in the year. He has impressed , even though he wasn't expected to have such a role in his first year with the team.
Fano, on the other hand, had high expectations after being drafted in the top 10. Fortunately, while he has had to go through plenty of growing pains after shifting positions, he has been consistent enough to maintain the starting spot and still be looked at as a long-term piece of Cleveland's future.
Heading out of the first 10 games of their careers, Barber ranks as the 28th best guard in the league out of 77 eligible, while Fano is a bit further ahead on the offensive tackle side, ranking 16th out of 72. Both rankings are according to Pro Football Focus.
Back in action in two weeks, the rookies will have a chance to catch their breath during the bye week, with hopes of putting together a strong push down the back half of the season. Sitting 6-4, the Browns have plenty of room to chase the No. 1 spot in the AFC North and make the playoffs.

title: The Highest-Graded Rookie on the Browns May Not Be Who You Think
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have had rookies succeed everywhere on the field this season .
Denzel Boston may have saved their season by breaking tackles on his way to a touchdown in Tampa Bay. Todd Monken has schemed up plays for KC Concepcion to showcase his speed and playmaking ability. The offensive line has been anchored by Spencer Fano, and he has allowed them to operate smoothly late in games.
However, it seems that no rookie has been more impactful than Emmanuel McNeil-Warren.
The University of Toledo alum has been flying all over the field on defense this season. He has improved every game, highlighted by his play in the win against the Houston Texans. Pro Football Focus (PFF) ranked McNeil-Warren second in the entire 2026 rookie class.
Which rookies have caught your eye? pic.twitter.com/NVGvtDfEFh
He has 50 tackles so far this season, with 23 of those being solo tackles. He has made impactful plays at every level for the defense while playing safety.
In the Browns’ first matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers, he met the big and strong DK Metcalf in the middle of the field with physicality right as the ball arrived to get an important incomplete pass. Against the Tennessee Titans, he snuffed out a fourth-and-goal play and made a tackle for a loss, causing a turnover on downs.
His best play was nullified by an iffy pass-interference call, but it should not be ignored. He was playing center field at safety, and there was a one-on-one matchup on the outside. McNeil-Warren reacted and closed the gap quickly. He made a diving interception that will rival any in the league this season.
His flashy plays are more than just surface-level. PFF is a sports analytics company that focuses on the NFL. They use advanced statistics to grade every player in the league, and McNeil-Warren has passed their test.
The emergence of McNeil-Warren can lift the ceiling of this defense for years to come. The Browns have staples at every level of the defense for the foreseeable future. Mason Graham will be the central focus on the interior of the line, and behind him is former Defensive Rookie of the Year, Carson Schwesinger. McNeil-Warren caps off the back end of the defense .
Free safety Ronnie Hickman is an unrestricted free agent at the end of the year. They extended Grant Delpit’s contract in the offseason, so they are set at the position.
For a rookie, McNeil-Warren exudes confidence and instincts. He has the speed, intelligence, and physicality to become one of the best safeties in the NFL.
McNeil-Warren was graded 86.7 by PFF. Fano was also in the top-ten list at number seven with a 75.5 grade. They have Boston at 69.4, followed by Concepcion at 67.2. The rookie class has been as good as advertised so far this season, but McNeil-Warren is in a class of his own .

title: Analyzing What Deshaun Watson's 2027 Offseason Contract Extension Could Look Like
full_text:
Anyone who followed the Cleveland Browns closely knew that the 2026 season was going to be an interesting one.
Not just because it felt like nearly everyone had counted the Browns out, even after they put together a strong offseason, but because the quarterback situation was a big talking point. Would the team go with second-year signal-caller Shedeur Sanders or turn the keys of the offense back over to controversial Deshaun Watson?
Well, not only did they give Watson a chance to be the starter in the season opener, but he has done his job well enough to lock down the job for the entire year.
And now, one major question has started to arise: will the Browns' front office extend him this offseason?
The 31-year-old is in the final year of a five-year, $230 million contract . With how he is playing right now, leading the Browns to a 6-3 record while under center and keeping up the hunt for a playoff spot, it seems likely that the front office would at least consider it.
Here is what the contractual situation could look like in just a few short months:
This past offseason, t here were actually quite a few quarterbacks who hit free agency and commanded quite a bit of attention. Funny enough, a couple were even tied back to the Browns.
But weeks came and went and the Browns stood still, opting to stick with the quarterback room they already had.
Now, though, the front office might actually be able to use some of the discussions they saw behind-the-scenes to work through Watson's upcoming contract situation.
The Browns were never really in the running for Pittsburgh Steelers veteran Aaron Rodgers, but being over 40 years old and still playing at a high level, he somewhat sets a line for what Watson's value could be at. He commanded a one-year, $22.5 million deal.
Following Rodgers, 27-year-old Malik Willis, who is still relatively unproven, grabbed a whopping $22.5 million a year deal across three seasons with the Miami Dolphins.
Being almost four years younger than Watson and entering what is expected to be his prime, the contract makes sense, especially with where the quarterback market is at right now.
The final two deals that align somewhat with where the Browns should be at with Watson are Kirk Cousins, who signed a one-year, $11.3 million deal with the Las Vegas Raiders, and Marcus Mariota, who signed a one-year, $7 million deal with the Washington Commanders.
Both of those contracts make sense for where they were at in their careers; however, Cousins has quickly re-emerged as one of the league's most consistent quarterbacks. He's a good example of taking a low-to-mid-level financial risk on an aging quarterback, something Cleveland could end up taking into account.
When looking at the current quarterback market and comparing some of the deals that were signed last offseason, it is quite likely that Watson ends up inking a two- to three-year deal worth anywhere from $15-22 million a season.
The $15 million mark puts him just ahead of Cousins, while the $22 million high point puts him on pace for Rodgers- or Willis-type money.
That would make his total value worth anywhere from just $30 million across two seasons, all the way up to $66 million across three seasons.
If he can continue playing at the high level he has been this season, that type of contract would be worthwhile for a young team still finding its groove in a loaded AFC North. The bigger storyline, though, is whether this season has been a fluke for Watson or not.
The Browns' front office could end up deciding to lean towards a short-term contract, just to protect themselves and the amount of money they already invested in the controversial quarterback, or if wins really do matter, they could give him another nice deal to stay in Cleveland.
Watson's future in The Land rides heavily on how he finishes the 2026 season.
The Browns return to the gridiron on Sunday, Nov. 29, for a date with the 2026 No. 1 pick, Fernando Mendoza, and the Raiders . The two sides will clash at 8:20 p.m. EST from Huntington Bank Field.

title: Full Cleveland Browns 2027 Mock Draft: All Seven Rounds
full_text:
As the Browns sit at 6-4 in the playoff chase, draft discussions haven’t quite taken center stage in Northeast Ohio as we approach Thanksgiving.
But it’s never too early to start considering potential draft picks. With that in mind, let’s explore some names and ideas Cleveland might consider in the upcoming 2027 NFL Draft.
For this mock draft, we'll use the Week 11 draft order from Tankathon.com :
No. 18 (via Los Angeles Rams)- Arch Manning, QB, Texas
The Browns will be looking to draft their franchise quarterback in the first round after not being able to take one in the last two drafts. Cleveland might have to trade up to draft its quarterback. But for this exercise, we will not make any trades.
Cleveland has the benefit of having two first-round picks and will grab Manning here from the selection the Browns received in the Myles Garrett trade.
Manning may not declare for the draft, as he still has eligibility remaining. Many people believe he should return to school for another season. However, he has already been in college for four years and has been a full-time starter for the last two seasons.
Another season of college football might not be beneficial, and joining the NFL, even if it means sitting on the bench for a while, could provide him with a better opportunity to learn from an NFL coaching staff.
The Browns will be linked to Manning during the draft, as owner Jimmy Haslam knows Arch's uncle, Peyton, from his time as a quarterback at the University of Tennessee, where Haslam is a native and booster.
It doesn’t matter what head coach Todd Monken and general manager Andrew Berry want. If Haslam has his heart set on a Manning, he usually gets what he wants since he is the one writing the checks. Owners often draft quarterbacks in the first round, and Haslam is exactly the type who doesn’t stay out of the way too often and let the football people make the big-time decisions.
No. 20- Greg Johnson, Interior OL, Minnesota
The Browns had to rebuild their offensive line last offseason, bringing in five new starters. It looks like they have two rookies, left tackle Spencer Fano and right guard Austin Barber, who will be in Cleveland for a while. The Browns still need to add to the offensive line, and Johnson would be a nice fit. He can play both center and guard. Most likely, the Browns would use him at center.
Currently, starting center Elgton Jenkins is on a two-year, $24 million deal with a potential out after this season for $7.7 million in dead cap, according to Spotrac.
No. 53,- Matayo Uiagalelei, EDGE, Oregon
Since Cleveland doesn't select a pass rusher in the first round, it will choose one with its second-round pick. Uiagalelei was among a handful of Oregon players who returned to school instead of entering the 2026 NFL Draft.
In 10 games this season, Uiagalelei has recorded 10 tackles for loss, 9.5 sacks and 40 combined tackles.
No. 84- Melvin Siani, OT, Texas
The Browns will still be looking for a need at tackle, and Siani appears to fit their style. Siani is listed at 6-foot-6 and weighs 302 pounds. The 22-year-old tackle may not match the weight of current Browns tackle Dawand Jones, who came in at 6-foot-8 and 374 pounds at the 2023 combine. However, Siani possesses a large frame that could help him develop into a solid professional player.
No. 119 (via Seattle Seahawks)- Nate Frazier, RB, Georgia
No. 122- Owen Chambliss, LB, Nebraska
No. 123 (via New York Giants)- Lawson Luckie, TE, Georgia
The Browns focus on Georgia players in the fourth round, as Monken was the Bulldogs' offensive coordinator from 2020 to 2022 and helped them win two national championships. Monken still has connections inside the Georgia football program, and it is one of the best schools for producing tight ends and running backs.
Frazier could step in to help carry the running game alongside Quinshon Judkins, allowing Dylan Sampson to focus more on third-down work. Additionally, Luckie could help free up tight end Harold Fannin Jr. in the passing game. Fannin and Luckie could be used in multiple two-tight-end sets, creating mismatches for opposing defenses.
Cleveland has to get more depth at linebacker, and adding Chambliss, who has 55 tackles, five tackles for loss and a half-sack in eight games this season.
No. 148 (via Houston Texans)-Zeke Berry, CB, Michigan
No. 157- Jordan Faison WR, Notre Dam e
Cleveland uses its fifth-round pick to select two players from significant programs: Berry from Michigan and Faison from Notre Dame. The Browns don't necessarily need a starter at cornerback, with Denzel Ward and Tyson Campbell already in place, but they do need depth.
Adding Berry could be a valuable addition. The same goes for wide receiver, as the Browns have Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion starting.
But Cleveland is likely to part ways with Jerry Jeudy this offseason, creating opportunities to add a few receivers, both in the draft and through free agency.
No. 230- (via Texans)- Peter Clarke, TE, Temple
No. 241- Knijeah Harris, Guard, Florida
The Browns add another tight end since they have a deep need at that position. And they add Harris as a depth piece on the offensive line.
Often, seventh-round picks don't make the 53-man roster, and since Cleveland won't have many roster spots to spare with all its draft picks and possible free-agent additions, both players might be camp bodies.
Daniel is a sports writer from Northeast Ohio. He has followed the Browns, Cavs, Guardians, and Buckeyes for years and loves sharing his thoughts on the team.

title: Dallas Cowboys' Secondary Poised To Get Major Boost vs Eagles on Thanksgiving
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys did exactly what they were supposed to do on Sunday afternoon, steamrolling the Tennessee Titans at AT&T Stadium and coming away with the win. Dallas' offense hung up 51 points during the convincing win, so momentum is there as the team enters a short week.
In Week 12, the Cowboys will be returning for their annual Thanksgiving Day showcase, welcoming the NFC East rival Philadelphia Eagles as they wrap up a three-game home stand.
Entering the week, there is some good news for the Cowboys' secondary, with COO Stephen Jones revealing that the starting safety is expected to return on Thursday afternoon. Thompson, who suffered a hamstring injury against the Baltimore Ravens in Week 3, returned to practice last week for the first time since Week 3 and was close to playing against the Titans, but the Eagles are now a strong target date for his official return to action.
Thompson was one of the team's most highly touted signings during free agency, so the defense is excited to get him back in whatever capacity as soon as he can return.
"Absolutely. It was so close this week," Jones said about a potential Thompson return. "Just felt like since it was [his] first week back at practice, one day in pads there, that another week of practice, or a half a week it'll be, will do him good. But it'll be great to get him back."
If Thompson is able to get back on the field, even in a minimal role until he is able to ramp up completely, it will be an upgrade for the Cowboys' secondary. Even though Dallas won in Week 11, the defense still managed to allow 30 points, so there is clearly room for continued improvement.
This season, Thompson has appeared in four games with three starts, recording 17 total tackles and one QB hit. Returning against an offense led by former Cowboys practice squad quarterback Joe Milton III could be the perfect opportunity to get back on track.
Kickoff between the Cowboys and Eagles at AT&T Stadium is set for 4:30 p.m. ET on FOX. Kevin Burkhardt and Tom Brady will be back in the booth in Dallas, while Erin Andrews and Tom Rinaldi will be providing updates from the sideline throughout the evening.

title: Cowboys Week 11 Report Card: Pettine's Defense Shows Promise, Another Banger for Dak
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys did what they needed to do and took care of business with a 51-30 blowout victory over the Tennessee Titans in Week 11.
Dallas led from start to finish and there was never any semblance of a threat from the Titans. That's rare because the Cowboys haven't been able to dominate a game from start to finish throughout the entire season.
The Cowboys' passing attack was sensational, and there was even a glimmer of hope from the defense, at least in one facet, in what was senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine's play-calling debut with Dallas.
We'll talk about that and more as we grade the Cowboys following their impressive win over the Titans on Sunday.
The Cowboys put up their best showing of the season through the air in Week 11.
Dak Prescott was sharp as a knife , with the Cowboys signal-caller completing 28-of-33 passes for 325 yards and two scores. We also saw CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens break 100 yards apiece in a game for the first time this season.
Sure, it was against the league's worst pass defense, but Dak did exactly what you'd expect him to do in that situation. He has also been playing some of the best football of his career over the last three weeks, so this wasn't just some fluke.
The Cowboys are going to need a lot more of these types of performances if they're going to overcome their defense.
The Cowboys did manage to tally over five yards per carry in the win over the Titans, but that was thanks to KaVontae Turpin's two carries for 41 yards and backup Jashaun Corbin's five carries for 32 yards.
The one who matters most, Javonte Williams, failed to gain four yards per carry, marking the eighth time that has happened this season. He did find pay dirt twice, though, including once as a pass-catcher.
Dallas has to figure out why Williams can't get going consistently because being a one-dimensional offense is not a recipe for success.
If we're grading on a curve here, a "B-" is the equivalent of an "A+" for the Cowboys, who saw a bit of an improvement in pass defense in the first game under Pettine.
Yes, Cam Ward completed 21-of-30 for 248 yards and two scores, but he also completed a freak 59-yard touchdown pass to Carnell Tate and had some production in garbage time, including his second touchdown pass, after Dallas had lifted its starters.
I thought the coverage looked better, at least for three quarters of the game, and the pass-rush was bringing the heat regularly with a whopping 31 pressures, according to Pro Football Focus , and five sacks.
Now, the showing came against one of the worst teams in the NFL, but the TItans had been playing better football on offense in the two contests before this game, so there's that.
I am the very definition of cautiously optimistic, at least when it comes to the pass defense, but cautiously optimistic is a better place to be than where Cowboys fans have been all season.
The more things change, the more they stay the same.
The Cowboys once again failed to stop the run, with our old friend Tony Pollard racking up 5.2 yards per carry en route to 110 on the ground. He probably would've done much more damage if the Titans weren't playing from behind all afternoon.
The only positive is the Cowboys did a good job keeping Ward in the pocket and now allowing him to make plays with his legs, but that's not enough to erase another putrid showing in run defense.
KaVontae Turpin averaged a respectable 24.2 yards per kick return and turned one punt return into a 13-yard gain. Meanwhile, the Cowboys didn't allow an elite kick returner in Chimere Dike to break a long return, which helped the defense immensely.
It was a boring game for Bryan Anger, who didn't get the chance to punt once. Brandon Aubrey made all six of his extra points and the lone field goal attempt he had from 49 yards out.
This might be the highest coaching grade the Cowboys have gotten all season long.
Again, we're encouraged by what we saw from the defense under Pettine, but we need to see a lot more against better competition before we can get excited.
On offense, head coach Brian Schottenheimer called a fantastic game through the air, but he continues to have zero answers for how to put together a consistent run game.

title: Cowboys' 50-Point Offensive Explosion Officially Broke Titans' Robert Saleh
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys have struggled with consistency throughout the 2026-27 season, but when the offense is firing on all cylinders, nothing can stop them. That was on full display on Sunday afternoon during the team's 51-30 shellacking of the Tennessee Titans at AT&T Stadium.
Dak Prescott threw for 325 yards and four touchdowns, with CeeDee Lamb hauling in 11 catches for 132 yards and a touchdown and George Pickens adding 7 catches for 102 yards and a score.
On the ground, Prescott, Javonte Williams, and KaVontae Turpin all found the endzone.
The unit couldn't be stopped, and after the game, that led to a complete meltdown from Titans head coach Robert Saleh, who went on a NSFW tirade after his team's latest defensive failure. Maybe Saleh should try stripping himself of defensive play-calling duties ?
According to ESPN, the Titans became only the fourth team since 1970 to allow more than 40 points in three straight games , so it's easy to understand Saleh's frustrations.
Not even the Cowboys' defense has been that bad.
Robert Saleh couldn’t have been any more honest here pic.twitter.com/UT9UHRD7PR
"Obviously it's disgusting football; it's embarrassing football. But we have no choice but to get better - I mean, sh*t, it can't get any worse," Saleh said. "There's a lot of things that need to change... that starts with me. I have to figure it out.'
Prescott made his own kind of history during the team's dominant win over Tennessee. It marked the first time in Cowboys history that a quarterback has accounted for five or more total touchdowns in consecutive games.
Against the Titans, Prescott threw for four and rushed for one. Against the San Francisco 49ers last week , Prescott threw for 343 yards and five touchdowns. He is undeniably playing at an elite level.
Hopefully, Prescott will be able to keep the positive momentum rolling on Thanksgiving Day, when the Cowboys make a quick turnaround to welcome the NFC East rival Philadelphia Eagles to AT&T Stadium to wrap up a three-game home stand.
Kickoff between the Cowboys and Eagles on Thanksgiving is set for 4:25 p.m. ET, with Kevin Burkhardt and Tom Brady on the call. A win over the Eagles would give the team some positive momentum to cap off the month as we enter a crucial part of the season.

title: 6 Winners & 2 Losers From Cowboys Week 11 Blowout Win Over Titans
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys dropped 51 points this weekend against the Tennessee Titans , which is impressive. They also gave up 30 points on defense, which isn't impressive.
Still, the end result is what matters, and the Cowboys got back into the win column this weekend as they knocked off the Tennessee Titans. Now sitting at 5-6, the Cowboys find themselves again within striking distance of the NFC East and a critical Thanksgiving Game showdown with the Philadelphia Eagles just a few days away.
Before looking ahead to that game, let's take a look back at this showdown and highlight who stood out as both winners and losers for the Cowboys.
With Jake Ferguson out , James Mitchell was given more snaps this weekend, and he didn't disappoint. He had two catches in the first quarter for 40 yards, highlighted by a 27-yarder to kick-start the Cowboys' second drive of the game. His numbers might not have jumped off the page, but Mitchell has been able to deliver whenever asked this season, making him a winner this weekend.
It was just his second game back from injury, but it was easily the best of the year for KaVontae Turpin. The explosive wide receiver had been struggling for much of the season, but he put his speed on display Sunday. First, he ripped off a 19-yard run during the opening drive. He was again used out of the backfield on the second drive; this time he found an opening and ran a touchdown from 22 yards out.
Last week, CeeDee Lamb didn't have a catch in the first half, which feels like a criminal offense. This week, he was a monster during the first 30 minutes, hauling in 11 receptions for 132 yards with one touchdown. He also made history by becoming the first Cowboys player to record 1,000 receiving yards in six consecutive seasons .
Ever since signing with the Cowboys, Javonte Williams has done nothing but score touchdowns. He had 13 total touchdowns in 2025 and entered this game with 10 in 2026. He increased that total to 12 by scoring a rushing touchdown and a receiving touchdown. He now has 25 touchdowns in 27 games with Dallas, which is an unbelievable stat.
James Houston was second on the team with 5.5 sacks in 2025, but for some reason, he wasn't utilized much at all at the beginning of the season. Thankfully, his snap count continues to increase and he continues to deliver. In this one, Houston had two sacks and would have had a third if not for a holding penalty in the secondary. He doesn't have the big name, but Houston is easily the best pass-rusher off the edge in Dallas.
It was another unbelievable outing for Dak Prescott, who torched the struggling Tennessee defense in Week 11. Prescott picked the Tennessee defense apart, completing 28 of 33 passing attempts for 325 yards with four touchdown passes. He added another touchdown on the ground, leading Dallas to their 51-point outing. The Titans don't have a good pass defense, and Prescott exploited that all day long.
With DaRon Bland sent to the IR , the Cowboys will need more from Cobie Durant for the rest of the season. Going forward, he's going to hope for better luck.
Durant was on the wrong end of a ridiculous play. Tennessee receiver Carnell Tate caught a pass and went to the ground. Durant touched Tate, believing he was down by contact, but Tate was getting up and no longer "down." That allowed him to race to the end zone for a 59-yard touchdown. There might have been some hesitation from Durant to deliver a hit, attempting to avoid a flag, but this was a strong reminder to play through the whistle.
By now, we all know Christian Parker lost his play-calling duties as the Cowboys handed the keys to senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine . There were predictions that Pettine would be able to find success in Week 11, not necessarily because Pettine was there, but because they were playing a 1-8 team that is potentially tanking for the first overall pick.
Naturally, the defense looked better this week than in Week 10 when they faced the No. 1-seeded San Francisco 49ers, but they still gave up 30 points to an offense that should have been held in check. That gives more credence to the belief that Parker was a scapegoat for Brian Schottenheimer , who continues to escape true accountability.

title: How Dallas Cowboys' Defense Fared in First Game With Mike Pettine as Play-Caller
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys began a new chapter on the defensive side of the ball in the Week 11 win over the Tennessee Titans.
The new chapter featured senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine calling plays instead of defensive coordinator Christian Parker, who was demoted in the week leading up to the game.
In his play-calling debut in Dallas, Pettine's unit gave up 30 points for the third time in four games, but there's important context to add there that separates this effort from the previous ones in which the Cowboys gave up 30 or more.
Let's dive into the details of how the Cowboys' defense looked on Sunday.
The Cowboys' defense played some of the best football the unit has played this season over the first two quarters of the game. The Titans couldn't get anything going in that span and only mustered up three field goals.
The last of three Titans touchdowns came in the fourth quarter, but it was also garbage time and Dallas emptied out its bench on defense before quarterback Cam Ward found wideout Calvin Ridley for a 12-yard strike with 31 seconds left in the game.
So, the Cowboys' starters essentially gave up just nine points over three quarters, which was certainly encouraging to see.
The defense's worst quarter of the game by a country mile was the third quarter, when the unit gave up two touchdowns.
However, there is where context is important because the Titans needed a few assists to register those scores.
The first touchdown came after rookie defensive back Caleb Downs committed a 38-yard pass interference on fellow rookie, wide receiver Carnell Tate, which set the Titans up at the one. Tennessee went on to score on the next play.
Later in the quarter, the Titans scored a freak 58-yard touchdown after the Cowboys failed to touch Tate down. Cornerback Cobie Durant did touch Tate, but he had already gotten up, so it didn't count. Tate then proceeded to take off and score.
If not for two brutal mistakes, the Cowboys might have held the Titans to just 16 points, or at least less than 30.
The Cowboys notched five sacks in what was one of the best showings from the pass-rush all season.
Third downs have been a major issue for Dallas' unit throughout the 2026 campaign, but that wasn't the case on Sunday, when Tennessee was just 3-for-10, which is a 30% success rate.
According to Team Rankings , Dallas was allowing opponents to move the chains on third downs at a whopping 48.84% success rate, the worst mark in the NFL.
Another important stat to point out was the Cowboys' showing in the red zone. The Titans only managed to cash in on 2-of-5 red zone trips, a 40% success rate. That's over 27% lower than the success rate the Cowboys gave up over the first 10 games.
On the negative side, the Titans ran for 126 yards at 4.5 yards per tote, and that was with Tennessee trailing for the entire game, so it was status quo for the Cowboys' putrid run defense.
Ward completed 21-of-30 passes for 248 yards and two scores to zero interceptions, so he had a pretty good game on paper, but we already mentioned the freak touchdown, and some of Ward's production came in garbage time, so his showing isn't as impressive as it seems.
Was it an encouraging performance from the Cowboys' defense? Sure, especially over the three best quarters the unit played.
However, we'd be lying if we said this is enough to get us excited and believe Pettine is going to fix this unit. We would call Dallas' Week 11 performance on defense a baby step in the right direction.
We have to remember that this showing came against a lowly Titans team that is one of the worst in the NFL. That said, the Titans had been playing better offense of late, so that's the positive takeaway for Dallas' defensive showing.
We still need to see the Cowboys put together a full 60 minutes without the kind of lapses we saw in the third quarter, and they need to do it against a more competitive team.
Give us a few games of that and we'll start believing. Until then, we are extremely skeptical the Cowboys' defense can turn it around.

title: Cowboys Injury Update: Schottenheimer Provides Latest on 2 Defensive Starters
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys improved to 5-6 on the season with a 51-30 win over the Tennessee Titans in Week 11. The Cowboys had a lot go their way on offense, but once again, their defense left a lot to be desired.
They also saw two of their key starters go down with injuries. First, it was linebacker Dee Winters who had to be helped off the field following an apparent knee injury. After that, they lost Cobie Durant who took a hard hit to the head.
Neither player returned to action against the Titans, but head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Durant could have.
After the game, Schottenheimer spoke with reporters and said that Winters had a knee contusion, but didn't elaborate on his status. As for Durant, he said he was evaluated for a concussion but was cleared to play. Schottenheimer added that the Cowboys decided to play it safe with the game in hand, keeping Durant on the bench.
Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said LB Dee Winters has a knee contusion, and CB Cobie Durant was cleared to return after being checked for a concussion and could’ve returned, but the Cowboys elected not to put him back in the game. pic.twitter.com/dFePpizX6o
Durant is already filling in for an injured DaRon Bland, which would leave Dallas very thin at the position should Durant miss any time. With him out, the Cowboys turned to Ameer Speed, who has been a pleasant surprise this year.
Interestingly enough, the Cowboys turned to Justin Barron when Winters went down, rather than DeMarvion Overshown. Eventually, Overshown was on the field, but it appears he's fallen out of favor with the coaching staff ever since he was penalized for running onto the field in street clothes to celebrate during the win over the Indianapolis Colts.
Dallas has a short week as they will host the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 12 on Thanksgiving Day. They only have a few days to rest up before taking the field again, so these injuries need to be monitored.
Another injury popped up after the game as Dak Prescott was seen with his left hand in a wrap . Thankfully, it's not his throwing hand, so that's a plus. Also, Prescott didn't seem to be worried about it at all.
Prescott said that " it bent back on a bad hit he took in the second half." He added that it was a "blessing" that the injury wasn't more serious. Prescott has had injury concerns in the past, but has been able to play in every game over the past two seasons.

title: Dak Prescott Injury Concerns Surface With Hand Issue At Post-Game Press Conference
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys got back on track in Week 11, with a dominant win over the visiting Tennessee Titans at AT&T Stadium. Dallas was expected to win Sunday afternoon's game, and they delivered in a big way.
Dak Prescott and the Cowboys' offense hung a 50-burger on the Titans' defense, coming away with a 51-30 win. After the game, however, there were some concerns about Prescott's hand .
Prescott showed up to the post-game press conference with his left hand wrapped. Luckily, it was not his throwing hand, but there were still some concerns about his health because the Cowboys have a quick turnaround for Week 12.
In just four days, the Cowboys will return to action to cap off a three-game home stint with a Thanksgiving Day showdown against the NFC East rival Philadelphia Eagles . So, should Cowboys Nation be concerned?
Dak Prescott has his left hand wrapped but downplayed the significance of any injury as being minor. pic.twitter.com/GGxydsX47Q
When asked about his hand, Prescott said that " it bent back on a bad hit he took in the second half." However, Prescott says that he is fine and that it's a "blessing" that he wasn't more seriously injured.
Considering the quick turnaround he and the Cowboys have for Week 12, it's great that he isn't showing any concern. Prescott is playing at an elite level, so losing him for any amount of time would have been a disaster.
This isn't the first time that Prescott has shown up to the post-game press conference with a handwrap, so that's also a promising sign about his ability to go in a matter of days.
Dak Prescott has a cut on the back of his throwing hand during today’s game. His hand got stepped on. He downplayed the bandage, saying the wrap was just to keep down any potential swelling pic.twitter.com/njKlMQ8QHD
Against the Titans, Prescott threw for 325 yards and four touchdowns, while adding another score with his feet. He became just the fourth quarterback in NFL history with at least 300 passing yards and five total touchdowns in consecutive games, joining Tom Brady (2007), Ben Roethlisberger (2014), and Daunte Culpepper (2004).
While Prescott says he will be okay for Thursday, we'll have to continue monitoring his hand as the week rolls on. Kickoff between the Cowboys and Eagles at AT&T Stadium on Thanksgiving Day is set for 4:30 p.m. ET on FOX.

title: Biggest Takeaways From Cowboys' Blowout Victory Over Titans in Week 11
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys got back on the right track on Sunday in a blowout win over the Tennessee Titans at AT&T Stadium.
The Cowboys' offense was on absolute fire throughout the game and put together a full 60 minutes, something we have not seen a ton of this season. When it was all said and done, Dallas put up 51 points on the Titans en route to a 51-30 win.
The defense did allow 30 points yet again, but most of the damage came in one quarter and the unit was actually solid over the other three quarters in the first game with Cowboys senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine calling plays .
We'll go over that and more as we take a look at the biggest takeaways from the win over Tennessee.
Prescott continued his hot streak on Sunday with what was yet another fantastic showing for the Cowboys quarterback, who completed 28-of-33 passes for 325 yards and four scores en route to Dallas dropping a 50 burger on Tennessee.
It was the third straight game Prescott threw for over 300 yards and multiple scores. Prescott's nine scores the last two contests ties a franchise record for the most thrown in a two-game span.
The Cowboys are going to need a lot more games like the last three from Prescott if the defense doesn't drastically improve.
The Cowboys' defense showed improvement for most of the first game with Pettine as the play-caller, but not exactly enough to get us excited, especially when considering who the opponent was.
Dallas' defense was, dare we say, dominant in the first half, giving up just six points in the first two quarters. However, the wheels came off in the third quarter, as the Titans scored a pair of touchdowns out of the half.
But the Cowboys managed to put the clamps on once again in the fourth quarter and Tennessee only scored a touchdown in garbage time to get to 30 points.
The Cowboys' pass-rush showed as much life as it has all season after tallying five sacks and several pressures. The Cowboys held Tennessee to just 3-for-10 on third downs and 2-for-5 in the red zone, which stopped this game from being a defensive disaster.
Again, the showing was encouraging, but not enough to make us believe this defense is truly moving in the right direction.
Tell me if you've heard this before: the Cowboys committed way too many penalties.
Dallas racked up 11 penalties for a whopping 128 yards. Luckily, the Cowboys were able to overcome them against a bad team, but they won't be that lucky against better opponents.
The Cowboys entered the game with a total of 79 penalties , the seventh-most in the league. They will likely be moving up the list after Sunday's contest.
The Cowboys saw two starting defenders exit the game early due to injury.
First, Dee Winters suffered a knee injury in the first half and did not return, and then Cobie Durant suffered an apparent head injury in the second half after taking friendly fire from DeMarvion Overshown.
Speaking of Overshown, he did not start once again and was not put into the game upon Winters' exit. Instead, the Cowboys went with Justin Barron. It appears Overshown is deep in the dog house.

title: CeeDee Lamb Reaches Historic Dallas Cowboys Milestone in Week 11 vs Titans
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys have had their fair share of forgettable moments during the 2026 season.
But through it all, star wide receiver CeeDee Lamb is on pace for a career year, something that continued during the first half of Sunday's Week 11 matchup at home against the Tennessee Titans.
There's blame to go around for why Dallas has routinely come up short this season, but don't point the finger at Lamb, who reached a historical milestone against the Titans.
With a nine-yard catch in the first half against the Titans, Lamb officially reached 1,000 receiving yards for the season, the sixth straight time he's done so.
Lamb is now the only player in franchise history to reach that milestone.
It didn't take long for him to add to that total as the first half continued. As Dallas built a 27-6 lead at the end of the second quarter, Lamb had nine catches for 103 yards and a touchdown.
Headed into Week 11, Lamb had led the Cowboys in receiving in seven of the team's first 10 games.
This was highlighted by a pair of monster performanced against two AFC South teams in the Houston Texans and Indianapolis Colts.
In Week 4's win over the Texans, Lamb finished with 17 catches for 189 yards and the game-winning touchdown with 40 seconds left.
Five games later against the Colts in Week 9, Lamb dominated with 10 catches for 195 yards and a touchdown.
It's only fitting that his historic milestone came against another team from the same division. Early on in Sunday's matchup, the Titans experienced some of what the Texans and Colts had to go through while facing Lamb.
Amid all of Dallas' struggles, Lamb continues to say the right things.
Though the Cowboys came up short against the San Francisco 49ers last week, Lamb knew that Dallas was going to have a chance at winning that game -- and he was right.
"It would just prove us right. Just of how we think of ourselves throughout this building. A lot of people would be shocked, obviously, because of the record, and things that have happened leading up to this game," Lamb said.
"But for us, we know we haven’t played our best game, and we just got to go out there and do that. I feel like we play complementary football — defense gets stops, offense go score the ball — we will probably be having a different conversation."

title: Broncos Grades vs. Raiders: Bo Nix Continues to Climb
full_text:
The Denver Broncos pulled off another victory, though it wasn't by a single-score margin this time, defeating the Las Vegas Raiders 38-24 .
It was a weird game on both sides of the ball , and this week's player grades will reflect that. Explosives and big plays were the story of this game, with a lack of consistency almost everywhere.
Let's dive into the player grades from the Broncos' eighth win of the season, and their sixth straight victory.
What an exceptional game from Bolles, who excelled in pass protection and as a run blocker after a rough game two weeks ago that saw Sean Payton call out his team's upfront blocking. While I can’t say for sure, against the Raiders, Bolles may have been the first player I've ever graded in a game with fewer than five negative plays.
He had only two negatively graded plays: one as a run blocker and one in pass protection, in which he gave up his only pressure.
Pay the man. Multiple times this season, McMillian has come up big for the defense when it matters most.
While McMillian allowed six of seven targets to be caught for 55 yards and a touchdown, he also made the game-sealing interception, which he promptly returned to the house for his third career pick-six. He was a sure tackler, picking up three stops, and even applied pressure on a blitz.
Nix's one interception was a last-second Hail Mary throw at the half, which ended up breaking even on the grading scale. He had moments where he struggled, but he continues to make strides forward with his play.
The overly cautious quarterback who was a detriment to the offense over the first six weeks is officially in Nix's rear-view.
The linebackers' job was made easier with Brock Bowers being out, but Strnad may have taken the Broncos' pursuit of Daiyan Henley personally , and it showed in his play. Strnad was flying around the field and playing tough and physical against the run.
Strnad allowed three receptions on three targets, but two came with him mismatched against a receiver; he limited the impact by making a quick tackle after the catch.
Denver had some big moments against the run, and Singleton was doing well taking on blocks and plugging rushing lanes. Now, his job didn’t always result in a good play because of the guys around him, but outside of a pair of runs, Singleton is hardly to blame for the Broncos' issues stopping the Raiders' run game.
Engram showed up as a receiver multiple times, helping to move the sticks, especially on critical downs. With six catches on eight targets, he turned five of those receptions into first downs. There was also a lot to like about his run blocking, though it was a small sample size (five snaps).
The Broncos' offensive line did well overall, and Meinerz played a clean game, for the most part. He got caught by a blitzing linebacker for a sack while he had to help center Luke Wattenberg set his block first, but that was the only negative in Meinerz’s game.
With a 4.6 yards-per-carry average, Coleman picked up 111 yards on 24 rushes, plus another 18 yards on four receptions on five targets. It was a good game for the rookie, who has clearly established himself as the Broncos' top back, as J.K. Dobbins played one snap with one touch.
The only negatives from Coleman came as a blocker. If we took those 12 snaps out, he not only would have been the highest-graded player in this game, but also the Broncos' highest-graded player so far this season at 86.7, beating out Zach Allen's 84.2 grade in Week 2. Sufice it to say, the rookie is on the right track.
Ashton Jeanty's 68-yard touchdown catch that Robinson allowed was a massively negative play for the second-year rush linebacker, but his issues went beyond that. Robinson struggled to generate pressure, with zero in this game, and he was consistently stonewalled by power from the Raiders' tackles. His lack of strength showed in his inability to get off blocks cleanly.
Franklin has been a surprise this season with his blocking, but he struggled against the Raiders, and his two biggest issues as a receiver showed up again. While he was only targeted twice, one was a drop, and the other was an accurate deep throw that doinked off his helmet due to his inability to track the ball over his shoulder.
Bonitto finished second on the team with five pressures, but his run defense and tackling were so poor that he ended up as the second-worst-graded player on defense. With two missed tackles and issues getting off blocks in the run game and setting a hard edge, the Raiders consistently exploited Bonitto in the running game.
This was the first game of the season where Adkins was a liability to the offense. He had been the Broncos' best blocking tight end this season, but he was one of the worst blockers on offense overall against the Raiders, and he dropped passes as a receiver. Adkins had plenty of opportunity, as he played his highest snap count of the season.

title: Jonah Coleman Just Did Something No Broncos Rookie Has Done in 24 Years
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are 8-2 after defeating the Las Vegas Raiders 38-24 .
The win improved the Broncos' divisional record this season to 3-1, giving the tiebreaker once again over the Kansas City Chiefs for the AFC West lead. And because of that, the Broncos have vaulted back to the No. 2 position in the AFC playoff picture, firmly on a collision course with the Buffalo Bills for the No. 1 seed.
None of it would have been possible without Jonah Coleman's historic performance against the Raiders. Coleman achieved something that no Broncos rookie has in nearly a quarter-century.
Coleman carried the ball 24 times for 111 yards and three touchdowns on Sunday, becoming the first Broncos rookie to eclipse the century mark and score three times in a single game. The last Broncos rookie to do it was Clinton Portis in Week 15 of the 2002 season.
Coleman wasn't even born yet. That would come in August of 2003.
Coleman has now scored a rushing touchdown in three consecutive games, becoming only the 12th rookie in Broncos history to achieve that feat. Something tells me he's likely to extend the streak to four games later this week in Pittsburgh.
Rookies with 100 rush yards and 3 rush TD in a game over the last 5 seasons Jonah Coleman today End of list pic.twitter.com/4Wt7CGqWBc
After the game, Coleman wasn't all that interested in taking credit for his team's sixth straight win. Instead, he turned the attention to his teammates and the collective achievement.
“I think that the approach that we are taking now and the confidence that we came with, it’s really about us," Coleman said post-game from his locker.
Coleman believes the Broncos were always the better team; it was just a matter of proving it out on the newly-laid grass at Empower Field at Mile High that the Walton-Penner ownership group just bankrolled.
"We look at ourselves in the mirror and know we’re the better team," Coleman said. "We just have to play like it and execute like it at the end of the day."
The Raiders made it an interesting game, tying things up at 17 in the third quarter. But Coleman and the Broncos' offense answered with back-to-back touchdown drives, both of which were, of course, scored by him.
One of those back-to-back touchdown drives came at the bottom of the third quarter, with the other coming in the final frame. Denver hammered the death knell into the Raiders late in the fourth quarter, when cornerback Ja'Quan McMillian picked off Fernando Mendoza , and returned it to the house for a defensive touchdown, putting the game out of reach with 1:52 left to go.
There's something special about the Broncos in the fourth quarter. They've won 16 straight one-score games, and while this week's margin of victory was 14 points, the Broncos once again dominated the fourth quarter.
Coleman says the genesis of that fourth-quarter resilience is the Broncos' approach to training camp.
“I feel like our whole team as a whole gets stronger in the fourth quarter," Coleman said. "That’s why our training camp was the way it was. You know, six days in pads and one day of rest for times like this and when it gets to the fourth quarter.”
Coleman has put a stranglehold on the Broncos' RB1 position. J.K. Dobbins had just one carry (for zero yards) against the Raiders.
Since returning from injured reserve in Week 7 , Coleman has sparked the Broncos' offense, giving the unit new life, including quarterback Bo Nix. And with seven games to go, Coleman is now very much in the running for the Offensive Rookie of the Year award.
The NFL likes to hand that one out to quarterbacks, and it'll be hard to vanquish Mendoza — the No. 1 overall pick in this year's draft — in that race, but if Coleman keeps it up, he could do just that.
