title: Broncos' Biggest Winners & Losers in Wild 38-24 Win Over Raiders
full_text:
The Denver Broncos got it done against the Las Vegas Raiders on an emotional day that began with the news of the great Tom Jackson's passing .
The Broncos honored Jackson with a moment of silence and a video tribute during the game, and after beating the Raiders 38-24, head coach Sean Payton dedicated a game ball to the former Orange Crush leader's family.
It was a wild game, with the Broncos starting off relatively hot offensively, only to see Fernando Mendoza and the Raiders battle back with 17 unanswered points. The Broncos pulled away late in the third quarter, and padded their victory with additional points in the final frame.
As we sift through the aftermath of the Broncos' eighth win of the season, let's break down the team's biggest winners and losers in Week 11.
Coleman has given this offense a real shot in the arm since returning from injured reserve in Week 7. Against the Raiders, he carried the ball 24 times for 111 yards and three touchdowns, with four receptions for 18 yards.
Coleman not only snapped the Broncos' 19-game drought without an individual 100-yard rusher, but he became the team's first rookie to eclipse the century mark and rush for three touchdowns in a game since Clinton Portis did it in Week 15 of the 2002 season. Coleman wasn't even born yet (2003).
There's no question who the Broncos' RB1 is. And with Coleman as the tip of the spear, the Broncos' offense has finally begun to open up, and that continued in Week 11. The offense had to bail the defense out this time around, and it was largley due to Coleman's inspired day.
Franklin was targeted twice but failed to come down with either. The worst was a deep shot at the bottom of the second quarter.
Despite it being a perfect pass, Franklin struggled to track the ball over his shoulder, allowing it to doink ignominiously off his helmet to fall incomplete. That play came on a 3rd-&-10, and the Broncos needed it because Mendoza and the Raiders had suddenly put up 10 unanswered points.
Suffice it to say, some other receiver should be running those gotta-have-it deep routes moving forward.
Nix played well, though his receivers didn't do a great job of helping him out. The Broncos' offense was plagued with first-half drops, which contributed to several doomed possessions, and kept the door open for Mendoza.
Although Nix did finish with an intercepiton, it was on a hail mary to end the first half. It'll go down on his resume as a pick, but it's not as if he made a bad decision or throw. It was a prayer.
Nix led some impressive scoring drives, capitalizing on the space Coleman's rushing production provided. Nix went 19-of-35 as a passer, but at least three of those incompletions were drops, for 225 yards and a touchdown.
Nix had no problem challenging the Raiders vertically, but he really needs his receivers to do a better job of helping him out. Still, Nix had four explosive pass plays of 20-plus yards, illustrating his willingness to hunt with the football.
Nix is still undefeated against the Raiders (5-0), which is impressive on its face, but it's especially cool given that Denver had lost eight straight to its bitter division rival before he came to town. And lest you're inclined to pass over Nix to give Payton the credit, remember that in his first year as head coach (2023), he was swept by Josh McDaniels's Raiders.
Now, if we can just work on Nix's QB sneak game...
Speaking of drops, Waddle had a bad one on the Broncos' opening possession that would have not only extended the drive, but set the offense up with great field position. Waddle was also unable to connect with Nix on an end zone shot later on that, while maybe not technically a drop by the letter of the law, was a well-thrown pass that the veteran receiver has to be trusted to come down with.
Waddle made a few plays, but his inconsistent hands of late are becoming a genuine issue. He finished with three receptions on six targets for 61 yards, with a long of 24. His stat line could have been so much bigger.
Boy oh boy did Engram need this day. He looked like a different player, running with power and tenacity after the catch. He kept making the first guy miss to pick up positive yardage.
Engram finished as the Broncos' most-targeted player, catching six of his eight targets for 74 yards to lead the team in receiving. If the Broncos can get production like this out of their veteran tight end down the stretch, good things await.
Despite having two weeks to prepare for the Raiders and shore up his unit's leaky penchant for allowing the big play, Joseph's defense was exploited with multiple explosive plays at the hands of Klint Kubiak and Mendoza.
Nix and the offense handed the defense a 17-point first-half lead against a rookie quarterback making his second career start, but the Broncos allowed Mendoza to battle back into it and even tie the game in the third quarter.
The Broncos allowed a 68-yard touchdown reception to running back Ashton Jeanty on a well-timed wheel route, as well as a 46-yard carry as a runner. But wait, there's more... Denver allowed a 39-yard Mendoza strike to Tre Tucker, and a brutal 19-yard touchdown to third-string tight end Ian Thomas.
Fernando Mendoza throws his FIRST career passing TD 🔥 LVvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Kse8UFzJpd
It was disappointing, to say the least. The two thing you can't take away from Joseph's defense, though? The pass-rush pressure was consistent on Mendoza and once again, this defense came up big in the clutch — two hallmarks of Joseph's unit that have become a reliable calling card.
If Joseph doesn't figure out how to put a stop to these big plays, it won't bode well down the stretch and into the playoffs. The Broncos relinquished 370 total yards to the Raiders, and allowed them to score touchdowns on two of their three red-zone possessions.
Just days after fellow cornerback Riley Moss inked his four-year, $67 million extension , McMillian sent a message to the Broncos front office that he, too, wants the bag. McMillian finished with eight tackles — the second-most on the team — and came up big in the clutch.
With the Broncos protecting a seven-point lead in the fourth quarter, McMillian made a great acrobatic play to pick off Mendoza and return it 35 yards to the house to absolutely slam the door on on the Raiders. Speaking of hallmarks, that's certainly been one of McMillian's — the clutch-time play to completely change the game.
J-MAC COMING UP CLUTCH 📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/cWEvkEdgVX
McMillian did it earlier this season against the Seattle Seahawks, picking off Sam Darnold in overtime to set Nix and the offense up in field-goal range. And he did it in the divisional round of the playoffs last year, too, picking off Josh Allen in overtime.
It's a lot of salary-cap dollars to have tied up in the cornerback position, but this game only made it more clear: the Broncos need to get McMillian extended. But they're running out of time.
Cooper was a consistent force on the edge, pressuring Mendoza throughout the game. It didn't matter whether the Raiders chipped or double-teamed him; Cooper found a way to break through and get to the quarterback.
Cooper finished with two sacks and a team-high eight pressures, while also chipping in four tackles. He also batted down a pass.
After spending the first six weeks of the season on the commissioner's exempt list, it would appear that he finally has his game legs beneath him again.
It's rare to see one blocked punt in a game. They're exceedingly hard to get. Two in one game, though? Now that's rare.
It started with Jones blocking a punt in the first half. But Tillman got in on the action, too, later on. Credit to both players and a tip of the cap to special teams coordinator Darren Rizzi.
Mims is also in a contract year, and given that Denver didn't reach out to him about an extension during the bye , he needed to signal to the front office that he's just as deserving. But it's been a rough season…

title: 3 Eye-Opening Takeaways From Broncos' Win Over Raiders
full_text:
The Denver Broncos got the job done coming off their bye week, defeating the Las Vegas Raiders 38-24.
The Broncos remain undefeated coming off the bye under Sean Payton. This was a big game to win against the Broncos' most hated divisional rival because it put them back in the AFC West lead and at the No. 2 seed in the conference playoff picture.
In the Broncos' eighth win of the season, there were multiple positives, but one glaring negative that still needs to be addressed. Let's get to my three key takeaways from Week 11.
Payton made it clear during the bye that he was unhappy with the Broncos' blocking up front and floated potential changes to the offensive line . Those changes came with Matt Peart starting at left guard, but with Ben Powers rotating in every three series, and it worked out in a massive way for the Broncos.
Was it perfect? By no means, but it was the best game from the left guard position this season when you combine the two players.
Now, there were still issues with the blocking at times, and a film study clearly showed the blame going to the center and right side of the line more often than not. Peart played well, and Powers played extremely well, outside of a late 3rd-&-1 run.
The two combined for two whiffs (Peart) and seven bad blocks (three on Powers, four on Peart). Powers did get a lot of heat for a missed blitz by center Luke Wattenberg, where Powers had his own defender to face and couldn’t take the blitzer, and Peart had a missed blitz pickup, which was one of his two whiffed blocks.
Not counting the drives at the end of each half, Peart had five drives and Powers had six drives. Peart was on the field for 41 plays, accounting for 207 yards and an average of 5.0 yards per play, with two touchdown drives, a field-goal drive, a punt, and a turnover on downs.
As for Powers, he was on the field for 26 plays, totaling 154 yards (5.9 yards per play), with two touchdown drives and four punts. There were still issues with the offensive line, but a simple film study reveals it wasn’t because of either left guard. The duo combined for a great game.
The Broncos' defense has an issue that it has to figure out. Defensive coordinator Vance Joseph called his unit out for allowing an explosive play on third and fourth down against the Carolina Panthers, but the message doesn't appear to have been received.
While the Raiders' offense did well, they were full of explosive and near-explosive plays. That helped keep the Raiders alive, especially given the timing of when the Broncos allowed these explosives.
The Broncos have been consistently inconsistent all season long defensively, and they've been unable to eliminate explosive plays. Now, an explosive play is a rush of 10-plus yards and a pass of 20-plus.
The Raiders only had three truly explosive plays, but they had another three plays that were a yard off from qualifying. So, the Broncos didn’t allow many explosive plays, but they did relinquish too many big plays in yardage and in some very ill-timed situations, and that was without Brock Bowers in the Raiders' lineup, who was ruled out as a game-time decision .
When you take those plays out of the equation, the Broncos have a good defense. That's the problem, though: you can’t take those plays out, and they're damaging to the image and the bottom line.
Allowing those kinds of plays is a concern when it comes to this team's playoff outlook, and the concern should only be growing given how frequently the Broncos find themselves in one-score games, where one big play can flip a win into a loss for this team.
The Broncos have had offensive issues all season, but over the past few weeks, they've shown some encouraging growth. The Broncos continued that trend against the Raiders, and it quite literally came off the back of Coleman, who carried the ball 24 times for 111 yards and three touchdowns, while adding four catches for 18 yards.
Coleman became the first Broncos rookie running back to eclipse 100 rushing yards and score three touchdowns in a game since Clinton Portis in 2002. Coleman also snapped the Broncos' 19-game streak without an individual 100-yard rusher.
Hat trick for Jonah Coleman ‼️ LVvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/FQNYZWdwKH
Again, the Broncos' blocking did a better job overall and helped Coleman have the success that he did. The rookie also showed his power and balance as a runner to handle contact.
Coleman is the type of back you can trust to consistently get you four or five yards on each carry, and that reliability is driving improvements to other elements of the offense, including Bo Nix. It's no coincidence that Nix began turning a corner in Week 7, when Coleman returned from injured reserve .
SInce then, and including against the Raiders, Nix has been over 200 yards passing in each game. He's looked like his former self before his broken ankle in the playoffs last year.

title: Broncos to Honor Tom Jackson With Tribute vs. Raiders
full_text:
Denver Broncos legend Tom Jackson —who became a fixture on ESPN for nearly 30 years — passed away Friday , November 20, at the age of 75.
The Broncos announced his passing Sunday morning and planned to hold a moment of silence for him prior to their home game against the Las Vegas Raiders . A tribute video is also planned during the game.
Jackson was a Broncos fourth-round pick out of Louisville in the 1973 NFL draft and went on to become one of the key players on the vaunted Orange Crush defense, a unit that played a huge role in the franchise reaching its first Super Bowl.
That 1977 defense featured legendary players, including Jackson, Hall-of-Famer Randy Gradishar (whom Jackson presented in Canton, OH), Lyle Alzado, Rubin Carter, Louis Wright, Steve Foley, Bill Thompson, and more.
In Jackson's 14 seasons with the Broncos, he played in 191 games — ranking third all-time behind only Jason Elam and John Elway — and started 177 games. Jackson was a force on defense with 44 sacks, 10 forced fumbles, and eight fumble recoveries. He was also a presence in pass coverage with 20 interceptions, including seven in 1976, three of which he returned for touchdowns.
TJ, you made us believe from the very beginning. #BroncosCountry will forever carry on your legacy. pic.twitter.com/cYGnRr8eQz
Jackson was a three-time Pro Bowl selection from 1977 to 1979 and was named first-team All-Pro in 1977 and second-team All-Pro in 1978. He was inducted into the Broncos Ring of Fame in 1992, the 14th player to receive that honor.
Jackson was not only a force on the field, but he was known for his way with words, firing up his teammates and sending a message to opposing players and coaches. His teammates respected him for the leadership qualities he brought to the team, as evidenced by the Most Inspirational Player award he received six times from his fellow Broncos.
After Jackson retired from the NFL, he went on to become a fixture on ESPN . The former Bronco joined ESPN in 1987, right after he retired, and teamed with Chris Berman to co-host Sunday NFL Countdown and NFL Primetime . Jackson remained with ESPN until his retirement in 2016, but came back to join Berman for a special playoff edition of NFL Primetime in 2019.
Jackson spent a few months with Berman on a digital-only edition of NFL Primetime during the 2019 season, before stepping away from ESPN for good the next year.
The former Bronco was recognized for his contributions to broadcasting by the Pro Football Hall of Fame, which presented him with the Pete Rozelle Radio-Television Award in July 2015.
Any fan of the Broncos or ESPN viewer knew all about Jackson. He may be the epitome of what it means to be a Broncos legend.
The staff at Mile High Huddle / Denver Broncos On SI sends its thoughts and prayers to Jackson's family, friends, teammates, and all of Broncos Country.

title: Broncos Catch a Massive Break as Raiders Reveal Final Inactives
full_text:
The Denver Broncos will be without starting safety Brandon Jones for the second straight game.
Jones, listed as questionable with a hamstring injury ahead of the Broncos' Week 11 home bout against the Las Vegas Raiders , was officially ruled out as a game-time decision.
However, the Raiders will also be without a key player, as star tight end and No. 1 receiver Brock Bowers has also been ruled out of Sunday's action.
Here's a full look at both teams' inactives list for Week 11.
Ehlinger officially goes down as a healthy scratch, though he'll dress and could play as the Broncos' emergency quarterback, only if injuries were to befall Bo Nix and Jarrett Stidham. Aside from Jones, the only other notable aspect of this week's inactives list is the absence of rookie defensive lineman Tyler Onyedim.
Onyedim — the Broncos' highest-drafted player this year — was a healthy scratch for the first eight games before dressing and playing in Week 9's win over the Carolina Panthers. He only played 10 snaps, but they were impactful; he was an excellent run stuffer and he forced a fumble.
As for Jones, the Broncos just promoted Taylor Rapp to the 53-man roster, so with Talanoa Hufanga back in action, they're likely to be the starting tandem, with Devon Key as the third guy in.
👀 our inactives for #LVvsDEN . 📰 » https://t.co/V0cqI6Flug pic.twitter.com/t8nFKDLyeK
With Bowers out, the Broncos' defensive focus turns to stopping running backs Ashton Jeanty and Mike Washington, including as receivers out of the backfield. Tight end Michael Mayer is also a force to be reckoned with, and given that Denver has allowed the most receiving yards to running backs this season and the second-most yards to tight ends, linebackers Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad will have to play well today.
It's Fernando Mendoza's second career start . And he'll not only have to face the Broncos' defense, but he'll also do so without his security blanket in Bowers.
I expect a lot of horizontal passing to Jeanty and Washington today, but the Broncos can't let that lull them to sleep on Tre Tucker, the Raiders' top wide receiver.
This game kicks at 2:25 p.m. MDT, and will be broadcast on CBS.

title: Broncos Release Touching Statement on Passing of Ring of Famer Tom Jackson
full_text:
Broncos Country woke up to a shock on Sunday that the great Tom Jackson had passed away at the age of 75. Though we don't know the details, his passing did come as a shock to those who knew him.
Jackson, the 14th player ever inducted into the Denver Broncos Ring of Fame and one of the faces of the feared Orange Crush defense, was a three-time All-Pro outside linebacker and a three-time Pro Bowler. He was also a member of the Broncos' 50th anniversary team.
With the Las Vegas Raiders in town for a Week 11 matchup, the Broncos released a statement on Sunday morning honoring the late, great Jackson.
“The Denver Broncos are heartbroken by the passing of Ring of Fame linebacker Tom Jackson, a cornerstone of the legendary Orange Crush defense and one of the most beloved players in franchise history.
“An inspirational leader and fierce competitor, TJ was a proud member of the Broncos’ first Super Bowl team that helped establish a winning tradition in Denver. Off the field, Tom carried himself with class, warmth and humility, forging deep connections and lifelong friendships with teammates and throughout Broncos Country.
“TJ’s dynamic personality, quick wit and football knowledge made him a natural for television and paved the way for a Hall of Fame broadcasting career. For generations of fans, Tom was an iconic fixture on ESPN ’s Sunday NFL Countdown and NFL Primetime , sharing his thoughtful insight with an unmistakable sense of humor that defined an era of sports broadcasting.
“Above all, TJ loved the Broncos and was a cherished member of our family for more than 50 years. We extend our deepest sympathies to Tom’s wife, Jennifer, his daughters, Taylor and Morgan, and all of his family, friends and teammates.”
Jackson's contributions on the field as a Bronco for 14 seasons are legendary. He was a first-team All-Pro on the 1977 team that was Denver's first to make it to a Super Bowl.
Jackson played alongside Randy Gradishar for the 1978 Defensive Player of the Year's entire career in Denver. And though it was a long time coming, when Gradishar was finally elected to the Pro Football Hall of Fame , Jackson was there to present for his old friend and teammate and to unveil his bust.
Gradishar was the first, and still the only, member of the famed '77 Orange Crush defense to be enshrined in the Pro Football Hall of Fame. Jackson was overjoyed for his deserving old friend.
Jackson played in 191 games as a Bronco, totaling 1,531 tackles (935 solo), 44 sacks (10th-most in team history), 20 interceptions (three pick-sixes), and eight fumble recoveries. He played on two Super Bowl teams, also making it to Super Bowl XXI, which was John Elway's first, though the Broncos lost to the New York Giants.
Jackson retired after that season.
Later that same year as Super Bowl XXI (1987), Jackson auditioned for a job broadcasting alongside Chris Berman on ESPN 's fledgling Sunday NFL Countdown , and later NFL Primetime . Jackson distinguished himself as one of the top NFL analysts and journalists, and worked at ESPN until 2016, when he retired.
Jackson earned the coveted Pete Rozelle Radio-Television Award from the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2015. He returned to ESPN for a short stint with Berman on ESPN+ 's digital-only version of NFL Primetime, but left the profession again during the 2020 pandemic.
Jackson passed away during Raider Week . I won't call it fitting, because his passing came as such a shock, but there is a symbolism there, given the decades-old rivalry, and you can bet the Broncos will have a little extra juice on Sunday against the Raiders.
After beating the then-Oakland Raiders 30-7 in 1977, Jackson famously approached the opposing sideline and yelled at head coach John Madden, "It's all over, fat man!" That phrase became legendary in Broncos canon.
Jackson is one of the most iconic figures in Broncos history and a titan in sports media and broadcasting. We offer our deepest condolences to his family and friends.

title: 5 Broncos Sleepers Who Could Surprise Everyone Against Raiders
full_text:
The Denver Broncos emerge from their bye with a matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders , their most hated division rival.
Since Bo Nix came to town, the Broncos haven't lost to the Raiders, winning their last four matchups, but that success came on the heels of an eight-game losing streak against their bitter AFC West foe. Over the years, the Broncos have developed a bad habit of playing poorly against the Raiders, despite often being the better team on paper.
The Broncos are a better team than the Raiders this year, but that's on paper. The Broncos have to go out and prove it on the field.
Denver has a few players flying under the radar that Vegas might not be focusing in on. This time around, the Broncos may want to rely on these sleepers to catch the Raiders off guard and secure the win.
A win over the Raiders would give the Broncos a 3-1 record against AFC West opponents this year, and put them back in the division lead, so this is an important game. Let's examine each sleeper who could play a bigger role than perhaps the Raiders are expecting.
The Raiders' defense has many holes , and Bryant is in a prime position to exploit them. His impact can come not only as a receiver but also as a blocker, where he will have to do significantly better than he did in Carolina before the bye.
Denver has a chance to deploy Bryant as a mismatch weapon, so while he may be a sleeper, he could make a big impact.
There was a lot of hype when the Raiders signed Quay Walker and Nakobe Dean, but the Raiders have allowed the fifth-most targets, third-most receptions, 13th-most yards, and third-most touchdowns to tight ends this season.
That's not all on the linebackers, but they, Walker in particular, have played a large part in the Raiders' issues against tight ends, which opens the door for Engram to have a big game.
The Raiders don't have a lot of talent at wide receiver, which forces them to be creative in their passing game. Moss, fresh off signing a four-year, $67 million extension , should find himself against Jalen Nailor more often than not, even if it means Vance Joseph having his corners blanket a certain receiver.
That should be beneficial to Denver, but it would require Moss to hold up in coverage.
The Raiders' biggest wide receiver threat is Tre Tucker, who has a skill set the Broncos aren't the best equipped to handle. That said, McMillian (with safety help) would be the Broncos' best bet at limiting Tucker.
Tucker is averaging almost 16 yards per reception, but lines up on the boundary nearly 73% of the time, which could force McMillian to cover someone else unless Joseph decides to have his corners follow certain receivers, and this is one of the rare games where that should be the case.
Given how Denver has played against the Raiders over the past few years, field position is going to be vital. Remember, last year's Raiders game at Mile High was a rock fight that the Broncos barely survived (10-7).
Field position could come at a premium, which puts pressure on Mims. He's yet to break out with a big game as a receiver or a returner this season, which isn't great, given that he wants an extension . He has had some good returns, but Denver's best returns have come from others, like Kolbe Katsis and Sean Fresch Jr., so Denver needs Mims to find the consistency as a returner that made him a two-time All-Pro.

title: Broncos Reward Taylor Rapp, Make Two More Moves Ahead of Raiders Game
full_text:
The Denver Broncos have promoted safety Taylor Rapp to the 53-man roster.
The club announced the move on Saturday ahead of its divisional tilt with the Las Vegas Raiders . Along with promoting Rapp, the Broncos also elevated running back Cody Schrader and offensive lineman Gavin Ortega from the practice squad.
Signed to the practice squad earlier this season , Rapp has appeared in four games for the Broncos this year, with one start. As an eighth-year player, his veteran presence has made a huge difference amid the Broncos' injuries to starting safeties Talanoa Hufanga and Brandon Jones.
So far this year, Rapp has totaled 18 tackles (eight solo). He came up big for the Broncos in two of their biggest wins of the season, notching six tackles each against the Seattle Seahawks and Kansas City Chiefs.
The Broncos now have a whopping six safeties on the 53-man roster. Hufanga is expected back this week against the Raiders, but Jones is listed as questionable with a hamstring injury suffered in Week 8 that has already cost him one start.
Perhaps the Rapp promotion signals that Denver doesn't expect to have Jones back this week. We'll know in less than 24 hours.
Rapp was a Los Angeles Rams second-round draft pick in 2019. He was a starter on L.A.'s World Champion defense in Super Bowl LVI, so he's played in many big games.
Rapp has also spent time with the Buffalo Bills, most recently playing in many more high-stakes scenarios. He brought 97 games' worth of experience to the Broncos, with 73 starts. The Broncos really like the soon-to-be 29-year-old safety.
“Signing Taylor was purposeful for us. We needed a veteran safety who can play without reps," defensive coordinator Vance Joseph said after the Seahawks win on Thursday Night Football . "Obviously, that was a short week for all of us. For him to go in a game and play 60-plus snaps and play at a high level and make every call, it’s been impressive to watch.”
Schrader endeared himself to Broncos Country this past summer, especially with how well he played in the preseason finale. With both RJ Harvey and Tyler Badie on injured reserve, Jonah Coleman and J.K. Dobbins are the only running backs on the active roster, so elevating Schrader was a must.
This is the third straight game the Broncos have elevated Schrader, which means they're running out of elevations. If they elevate him again, they'll have to sign him to the 53-man roster.
Maybe this week, the Broncos will at least allow Schrader a touch or tow. He's yet to get a carry or reception and has only played two snaps in the two games he's been elevated.
Ortega is an undrafted rookie out of Weber State. He impressed the Broncos in training camp and the preseason, earning a coveted spot on the 16-man practice squad.
This will be Ortega's second elevation of the season. He was elevated against the Chiefs in Week 8, but did not dress. It was a paycheck bonus, so to speak, which shows you how much the Broncos seem to value this undrafted rookie.
Maybe the Broncos have different plans this week for Ortega. Time will tell.

title: Broncos Have Three Extension Priorities After Riley Moss—Here's the Order
full_text:
In the wake of Riley Moss's four-year, $67 million extension , the question on every Denver Broncos fan's mind is: who's next?
The Broncos moving to get Moss extended first spoke volumes. It not only showed the team's appreciation and value of the player that he is, but also how the Broncos prioritized his position has a boundary cornerback.
With Moss and Patrick Surtain II under contract for the foreseeable future, it's hard to point to a better cornerback duo anywhere in the NFL. And what's crazy is that Denver may also have the league's best cornerback trio.
I'll shed more light on that here shortly as I rank the players next in line for an extension at Broncos HQ. This team has several prime candidates it might not want to let get away.
I'm going to break down the three most pressing extension candidates on the Broncos' list of priorities in reverse order.
Mims was the first draft pick of the Sean Payton era. And the explosive returner lived up to that pedigree, earning All-Pro and Pro Bowl honors in each of his first two seasons and joining Von Miller as the only player to ever achieve that feat in Broncos history.
Mims's role as a receiver has been hit and miss. He's gone from various stages of usage, but when the Broncos have really had to rely on him, he's answered the bell.
Mims has always been a strong finisher, as evidenced by his 2024 and 2025 seasons. In the Broncos' playoff run last year, they dealt with multiple wideout injuries, losing Troy Franklin and Pat Bryant.
Mims stepped up, making some huge plays against the Buffalo Bills in the divisional round and the New England Patriots in the AFC championship game, and finishing as the Broncos' leading receiver in the playoffs — not Courtland Sutton, the team's Pro Bowler at the position.
MARVIN MIMS JR. FOR THE LEAD BUFvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/KxgLMR7wvr
As I wrote about on Friday, though, teams don't pay players based on past production. It might factor into the equation to an extent, but teams extend players based on what they expect them to produce in the future, and that can only be centered on the most recent body of work.
Unfortunately for Mims, he hasn't done much in his contract year, neither as a receiver or as a returner. He only has 10 receptions halfway through his contract year, and his 10.7 yards-per-return as a punt returner is currently a career low.
Mims has also dealt with some injuries this season, so it's not been a great way to engender an extension. But there's time yet.
As Mims talked about recently , his low receiving production isn't unique to him; every single pass-catcher on the roster — including Sutton and Jaylen Waddle — is on pace for a career-low year, due to Bo Nix's slow start amid the Broncos' exceedingly tough schedule to start the season.
However, with the schedule opening up and Nix turning a corner over the past three games, there's reason to believe the worm is turning. As the quarterback, Nix is the tide that raises all the ships around him, but even if Mims is unable to drastically improve his receiving numbers, he'll have to take some big steps forward as a returner to bring the Broncos to the table to talk extension.
Jones was signed to a three-year deal after the Broncos made the painful decision to release decorated safety Justin Simmons in 2024. Jones stepped in and did a great job of replacing Simmons's production and presence on the field.
I'm not sure anyone could replace Simmons's leadership, but Jones has established himself as a veteran voice in the locker room. After a strong 2024 season in Denver, Jones's 2025 campaign wasn't quite as good, but he's been excellent in his contract year.
Jones is currently dealing with a hamstring injury that kept him out of Week 9, but his absence has only magnified the Broncos' relative dearth of safety depth. It's clearer than ever just how important he is to this defense, whether Talanoa Hufanga is on the field with him or not.
When they're together, Jones and Hufanga form one of the NFL's best safety tandems. And when one or the other is injured, each safety is good enough to help keep the secondary ship afloat.
With Hufanga returning from his ankle injury this week against the Las Vegas Raiders, Jones is listed as questionable . Hopefully, Jones plays, but having Hufanga back should stanch the back-end bleeding we saw in Week 9 against the Carolina Panthers.
Jones and Hufanga co-lead the Broncos in interceptions, with two each. Their cap numbers this year are close, just over $9 million.
Brandon Jones picks it off! DENvsKC on ESPN Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/dc4IZfNCd8
Jones will turn 29 next April. I'd put his market value around $8 to $9 million per year, which is up from the $7.3 million average the Broncos signed him to in 2024. With Hufanga's contract expiring after the 2027 season, it will be interesting to see what the Broncos opt to do here with Jones.
If Denver had an heir-apparent, it would be one thing. But neither Devon Key nor JL Skinner has given the Broncos enough confidence to view them in that way. They drafted Miles Scott in the seventh round this year, but he's a developmental option, at best.
The Broncos can't keep everyone, and Jones may be a prime example of that. But even with Nix's future extension coming down the pike, the Broncos have a couple more years of salary-cap flexibility to keep the core of this team together, of which, Jones is very much a key part.
In the order of priorities, I can understand why Moss came first. Beyond the fact that boundary cornerbacks are extremely valuable in the NFL, he's also a former third-round pick whom the Broncos traded up to draft in 2023 as part of Payton's maiden draft class.
McMillian wasn't drafted, but that hasn't stopped him from carving himself out a key role on defense and becoming one of the NFL's top nickel cornerbacks. Nickels might not be quite as valuable as outside corners, but every single team covets one.
Rare are the nickels with inside/outside versatility, like former Broncos All-Pro Chris Harris Jr. was. That's not what McMillian is per se, though he can play on the boundary in a pinch, but one thing that separates him from the pack of nickels across the league is his nose for the ball.
And that's been a precious commodity for Vance Joseph's defense. Last year, the Broncos struggled to take the ball away, resolving to improve significantly in 2026, but McMillian was a reliable ballhawk with a penchant for making the big play in critical moments.
McMillian went undrafted out of East Carolina in 2022, but managed to stick around on the practice squad as a rookie. When Payton and Joseph arrived in 2023, McMillian's star began to burn brightly, as he vanquished veteran nickel K'Waun Williams to earn the top slot job on Denver's defense.
McMillian has never looked back. I could go through all of his stats, but the ones that best illustrate his value to the Broncos are his takeaways and sacks. In five NFL seasons (four as a starter), he has seven interceptions, five forced fumbles, and two fumble recoveries, to go along with 10 sacks.
Again, though, McMillian's clutch gene is spectacular. The best example came last season in the divisional round of the playoffs, when he intercepted Josh Allen in overtime to boost the Broncos to a 33-30 win over the Bills.
The most recent example of McMillian's clutch-time ability was his overtime interception of Sam Darnold in Week 6, which again set the Broncos up for a game-winning field goal to beat the defending World Champion Seattle Seahawks.
J-Mac coming up clutch 💪 📺: #TNFonPrime pic.twitter.com/iu9Hck8qGA
Now, what is a nickel cornerback, especially one of the NFL's best, worth on the open market? Perhaps somewhere between $10 to $13 million per year. That's a lot to pay for a Broncos team that already has roughly $40 million per year tied up in Moss and Surtain alone.
Still, players like McMillian are rare and hard to find. The…

title: Everything Lions QB Jared Goff Said After Defeating Buccaneers
full_text:
The Detroit Lions knocked off Tampa Bay to get to 8-2 on the season, and quarterback Jared Goff was right at the center of the effort.
Goff finished Sunday's game 20-of-28 passing for 279 yards and two touchdowns. Below is a transcript of everything he said in his posgame press conference following the win.
“I don't know, I think it just kind of happens sometimes. Obviously, I haven't made a career of it, but sometimes it presents itself, and I can go make the play. The avoiding sacks in the pocket? Yeah, it's something I try to do, but certainly not something that's in my repertoire regularly.”
“I think we had a good week of practice and felt really good with our plan, how we were going to try to attack them. It's a really good defense. They do a really good job at all three levels, and we had our hands full. I think they're so stout in the run game. I think they're first in the league that you kind of have to attack them in that way. It's certainly how we've done it the last few years when we've played them. It was good. It was good early.”
“No, I didn't, because the game could change. There have been games where we've tried to do that, and we end up running it for 200 yards. So no, I didn't feel any extra pressure, just one play at a time and throw it to the open guy.”
“I thought he had like 50 yards, I swear. I looked at it after, I'm like, 'holy smokes'. Yeah, it's just how the game goes. You start to wear them down, wear them down, wear them down. They're a really good defense, and they're human, though. They get worn down, and our O-line did a great job of doing that, wearing down that D-line. That's a stout D-line, and it was good at the end.”
“I mean, challenging is probably the wrong word. It's just maybe a little bit more responsibility, but that's why I like to play quarterback and have those responsibilities.”
“Yeah, it's a good question. I think I'm very aware of what they're trying to do to me. They're trying to hit me. They're trying to get me off my spot . They're trying to make me uncomfortable, and you kind of have to know that coming in. That you're going to counteract that on your own mentally of like 'I'm not going to allow them to do that, I might get hit, not the end of the world,' and just sit in there. That was a good example of that where – and it was a great example of Christian (Mahogany) kind of just holding on for the last second. It was (Buccaneers NT) Vita Vea, one-on-one. It's a tough block. And he just held on, held on, held on, and then I take the hit but get the throw off.”
“I didn't know it was him until I saw the clip after, to be honest. I knew he was close and I knew I was probably going to get hit. But when somebody's that wide open, you're hanging on it just a little bit longer than you may. Otherwise, I'll take a bigger hit if I know I'm going to get a 60-yard touchdown, and it's part of playing quarterback.”
“Yeah, I don't know if it has anything to do with (the defense). We're good up front right now and doing a really good job at it. I got a good little way to find my way in there, and we've done a good job.”
“Oh man, yeah. He is. He is, and he’s playing very confidently right now. And that’s where we want him. And he’s having fun. He’s laughing at everything. It’s fun when he’s playing this way, it changes our offense. And he knows that, and he’s been so good. So good as of late, certainly. And yeah, it’s fun to play with him right now.”
“Yeah, this is what – that’s how they drew it up when the schedule rolled out, so it’ll be fun. It’ll be really fun. That’s a good team. They’re very well coached. Got a lot of respect for how they do things offensively, defensively. It’ll be really fun. I’m sure they feel the same.”
"Yeah, it’s pretty good. Yeah, (Tyler Conklin) Conk’s added that little layer for us this year where he is a third tight end, but he can run routes, he can get out of the backfield and do some things, and it was good to get him that one, off schedule. And then Brock (Wright) and Sam (LaPorta) have just been so reliable. The seams were open today, and we hit them on a few of those. Thought Sam played so well, and he’s been deserving of getting more touches like that, and it was good to see him get the ball a little bit.”
“Yeah, I don’t know. I mean, I’m sure a team will see it on tape and be like, (Jameson Williams) he’s a deep threat. But, if he’s open I try to throw it to him, and I usually do if he’s open.”

title: Detroit Lions Week 11 Snap Counts Reveals Unique Usage of Safeties
full_text:
Detroit Lions All-Pro safety Kerby Joseph is back in the mix.
After missing over a calendar year due to a knee injury, Joseph returned to the field for the first time this season in the team's Week 11 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. His return caused something of a shakeup in the secondary, though not in the way some expected.
Chuck Clark , a veteran who the Lions signed in free agency this offseason, was the highest-utilized safety in Sunday's game. This came despite some believing he would be the odd man out upon Joseph's return. Instead, Clark, Joseph and Brian Branch all played at least 46 snaps, which indicates the Lions could be comfortable using a three-safety defensive package moving forward.
Clark played all 69 snaps, while Branch played 68 and Joseph logged 46. With Joseph back patrolling the deep part of the field, the Lions freed up Clark and Branch to roam around the field and occasionally blitz. Clark made good on his opportunities, as he recorded a sack.
Joseph will continue to acclimate as the season progresses, which could lead to some moderate changes amongst the snap count. However, it appears that coordinator Kelvin Sheppard is comfortable having all three on the field together.
Offensively, Detroit continues to roll with jumbo packages involving rookie defensive tackle Skyler Gill-Howard as a fullback near the goal line. Additionally, they are developing a tendency involving the usage of running back Sione Vaki, who was on the field for 13 plays but recorded just one carry.
Other snap counts of note include the cornerback room, as Roger McCreary and Rock Ya-Sin each played over 90 percent of the snaps with D.J. Reed sidelined for a third-straight week. Without Reed and Ennis Rakestraw, the cornerback rotation of recent weeks appears to be devolving.
Here are the Lions' snap counts for their Week 11 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Sports journalist who has covered the Detroit Lions the past three NFL seasons. Christian brings expert analysis, insights and an ability to fairly assess how the team is performing in a tough NFC North division.

title: 5 Risers, 2 Fallers After Lions Victory Over Buccaneers
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have won six games in a row.
On Sunday, the Lions dispatched the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 31-21 to improve to 8-2 on the season. They're currently tied for first with the Chicago Bears, who they'll square off with on Thanksgiving in front of a national audience at Ford Field.
The team has had to endure several injuries along the way to key players, but have found a way to keep it going throughout the adversity.
Here are risers and fallers following the Lions' Week 11 win.
The Lions have needed Moore to step up after recent injuries, and Moore has delivered. He got his first big break when DJ Wonnum missed the team's Week 9 win against Miami, and he delivered two sacks.
In the following week, Aidan Hutchinson suffered a season-ending injury on the team's first drive and as a result Moore was thrust into more action. Again, he notched two sacks to give the team optimism about his ability to provide in the wake of the loss of their star.
Against Tampa Bay, Moore teamed up with linebacker Malcolm Rodriguez for a critical fourth quarter sack. After a slow start to the season, Moore is on a hot streak and is proving the Lions right for their decision to trade up for him.
Scruggs has been in a unique spot since the Lions traded for him during the offseason. Initially believed to be interior line depth and a competitor for the left guard spot, he was forced to slide over to center after Cade Mays suffered a wrist injury in training camp.
This has turned out to be a blessing in disguise, as Scruggs has played at a high level for the entire season. Mays is on injured reserve again, and as a result Scruggs has wound up starting eight of the team's 10 games at center.
Currently in the final year of his contract, Scruggs appears to be playing his way into a potential extension.
It's hard to call Gibbs a riser based on the fact that he's been dynamic since he entered the league in 2023, but what he's doing trly deserves recognition. He's already over 1,000 rushing yards for the season, and is making all sorts of history along the way.
Gibbs has already set the record for most touchdowns by a player in their first 60 games, and he's only played 59 up to this point in his career. He's already logged a third-straight 1,000-yard season, and remains the league's leading rusher through 11 weeks.
The Alabama product has yet to earn All-Pro honors, but appears to be trending in that direction with his performance in the team's first 10 games.
The Lions have needed players to step up throughout their array of injuries, with Jack Campbell leaving a massive void in the middle of the defense. While Nowaske hasn't directly replaced Campbell as the MIKE, he has stepped up nicely into a bigger opportunity.
Nowaske came up big in Sunday's game, with a sack and two tackles for loss. The former undrafted free agent has settled into a nice role for Detroit's defense, both on special teams and defensively. His athleticism gives the Lions the ability to utilize him in coverage as well.
Kerby Joseph returned to action for the first time this season on Sunday, and as a result many thought Clark could be heading for a smaller role. However, Clark played a huge role in the win over Tampa Bay with a sack.
Detroit was utilizing some three-safety packages with all three of Joseph, Clark and Brian Branch on the field. Clark was also wearing the green-dot helmet Sunday, meaning he was the on-field player with communication from defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard.
Clark appears to be a player the Lions can rely on, given that he was elevated to captain status this week. He should be a vital player for the stretch run.
The Lions had a role for Abney throughout the start of the season, as he played both cornerback and safety throughout that time. However, he has been relegated to a healthy scratch the last two weeks as the team has gotten reinforcements in the secondary.
Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph are both healthy, and Andre Cisco has entered the fold as the Lions acquired him before the trade deadline. That leaves Abney in a difficult spot moving forward, with the most realistic path forward being playing more cornerback.
Mays was signed to a three-year contract in the offseason to be Detroit's center of the future. However, the investment has not worked out up to this point. Mays spent the first five games on injured reserve, and was sent back to IR on Saturday after missing the previous two games with an ankle injury.
That, along with Juice Scruggs playing at a high level, has put Mays in a tough spot. It's unclear if he'll return this season, but at this point even if he did the Lions may be more inclined to stick with Scruggs at the pivot position moving forward.

title: Everything Dan Campbell Said After Detroit Lions Beat Buccaneers
full_text:
The Detroit Lions defeated the Tampa Bay Buccaneers Sunday, 31-21, to move to 8-2 on the season with their sixth-straight win.
Below is a transcript of everything head coach Dan Campbell said after his team won during the postgame press conference.
“Alright. Really proud of the guys , man. Proud of the coaches, the players. That's two. That's two. We got one to go here. And then we'll catch our breath and then get ready for the rest of it. But that's a formidable opponent, man. That's competitive. That's one of the best defenses in the league right there. We knew they were able to possess the ball. (Buccaneers QB) Baker (Mayfield) playing, man, he's got enough juice to make some of these downfield throws to hurt you in the pass game. But I thought we played complementary football. I did, man. I loved the way we came out and I felt like, man, the ebbs and flows are feeling right, right now. We're finding strength, we're gaining strength, we're leaning on each other, and there's a lot of confidence right now in what we're able to do. So, I feel us getting better. And it's felt that way for about four weeks now, just continuing to climb. And it's the right time. So, took care of the football today. You always want to get some out on defense. We weren't able to do that, but we did get a punch-out. But just really proud of the guys. I thought they were locked in all week, no excuses, and they were ready to go today. And I know they'll be ready to go for this one coming up.”
“We knew (Jared) Goff would come out and play well. Just knowing him in general, he's been playing at a high level, but he also, look, he gets irked too when he doesn't play a perfect game. And so, he was ready to go, and we told him that we're going to put the ball in your hands here early. And he and the skill players, let him get it to our skill and open it up a little bit and then we'd find the run game as we went. And that was a little bit of the plan here. But he just played at such a high level, man. I say this every week, but I mean, the amount of stuff we put in this week, just, the audibles, the kills, the looks, the pass game, the protections. I mean, it's enormous and he just handles it all with, I don't want to say ease, but it looks like ease. I mean, you wouldn't know any different. And then, just some of the throws he made, his movement in the pocket to escape, find throws, run. He's playing at such a high level. So, he was really our catalyst today. I thought the big boys, man, protected well overall. And I did think they came off the ball, man. I thought they played physical. That's a good unit. (Buccaneers Head Coach) Todd Bowles is outstanding coach. I got a lot of respect for Todd. And that unit, man, that's a tough out, man. It's a tough out, that defense. It's one of the best defenses in the league and it's the way they play and the scheme and all of it. So, it was a good job, but offense stepped up. We made our plays, but defense really set the tone. They took the ball first, got on the field, were able to get a stop there. And anyway, it was big. It was big.”
“Well, I think, look, those guys up front are just – Let me say this again. Man, we're growing up front. We're getting better. We're growing. Man, we are youthful, but that youth is growing up fast. Penei (Sewell) is our anchor. Juice (Scruggs) has played some football, but he's new to us at center, but he's getting better. And those other three, (Christian) Mahogany and (Tate) Ratledge and (Blake) Miller, they're gaining strength, man. They're getting better . And so that's crucial. And I just thought they came out ready to go today. And I think a lot of it is, as you're working through some of this, you're getting the looks, you're getting the feel, these are some of the things they're wanting to hang their hat on. This is the flavor of the day defensively. And then you start working a little bit. Find some creases for (Jahmyr) Gibbs, what's the best runs for him, create some space. What is he feeling good about. And the O-Line, what can we feel like we see the best overall? And then you just start hanging your hat on them a little bit.”
“Yeah, huge. I mean, look, that's been the biggest growth for us has been defensively. Just the improvement that we've had in that group. And that's even after losing guys. We lose some critical players to us, but yet we're still gaining strength. And that's the sign of a championship team, man. And the right kind of coaches, right kind of players. Doesn't mean it's perfect, doesn't mean it's always going to be perfect, but man, we are competitive and we challenge on the perimeter. We can create pressure. We can stop the run. And the greatest strength right now is really us as a team is, it's us. It's everybody. It's the team. And defensively, the strength of our defense is the defense. It's all of them. We're playing together. We're using our help. The rush and coverage go hand-in-hand. So it's big, man. The defense is playing great. And when you're able to do that and continue to grow and continue to get better, then offensively we can kind of play any way we need to, depending on per the opponent, per what we think, the way we can move the ball or score. And so, we can kind of become a chameleon a little bit. That's a good thing. That's a good thing. It's been a minute since we've been able to do that.”
“Yeah. I mean, I think, like I say, our guys are competitive, man, and they don't want to be counted out. And nobody cares. There are no excuses. And the only way to gain respect is just go about your business, man, and make plays and play together and prove your worth, man. And that's the best way. The talk's not going to do it. Nothing else matters. So, I just thought our guys attacked it, man. That whole group I thought played together and really elevated each other. (Alim McNeill) Mac, I thought was disruptive in there. (DL) Tyleik (Williams), again, made a lot of plays. (Skyler Gill-Howard) Sky obviously (DJ) Wonnum, Derrick Moore, there was a lot of guys who contributed. Levi (Onwuzurike), (Tyler) Lacy. I mean, Lacy, the first play, play-action pass, man, that's a big play. He's disruptive, he's strong, he can push the pocket. So, it was good, man. They stepped up. And like I said, it's a versatile room. We've kind of got a lot of flavors in there, man, different types of players that can all affect the game in a positive nature for us.”
“Well, some of it I feel, like, is where he's – It's a little bit of his game that I feel like has even grown a little bit as he's gone. Just his composure and his ability to see the field, not get stressed. I'm looking downfield. It's not there. I feel this. Just his kind of pocket awareness, man, because he does. He's got pocket presence, pocket awareness. He can maneuver a little bit. And so, yeah, I think it's underrated. I mean, you have to be able to maneuver in there a little bit and keep your eyes down field. And then look, if it doesn't come, those don't always happen, the runs, but he made some plays today. He's certainly capable of that.”
“Well, honestly, this was easy. Turn on the tape. I mean, it really is. The tape speaks for itself. Go look at these guys. They had just gone down two scores against Chicago last week and they just started pounding it with (Buccaneers RB Bucky Irving) seven. Boom. They just started pounding. You go down two scores. There's no stress. They're going to hand it off one more time. And man, all of a sudden, 12, eight, 16, and they just started opening it up and then they get down there and bust it in. So don't think this team's going away. Our guys knew that. This team's not going to go away. They're going to keep leaning on you. I mean, you're going to have to go earn this win. So, our guys understood that across the board, man. Our O-Line and D-Line were going to have to win this in the trenches and it was not going to be easy. And I mentioned it before, it helps. We've got enough…

title: Grades: Lions Surge in Second Half, Answer Defensive Questions
full_text:
The Detroit Lions were able to hold off the Tampa Bay Buccaneers Sunday.
After a slow first half, the Lions' run game woke up in the second half against the Buccaneers' stout defense. Add in a big play in the passing game, and some late game discipline, and it was the perfect recipe for Detroit to move to 8-2 on the season.
Here are grades for each position group based on performance in Sunday's game.
Goff was surgical for the most part Sunday, completing 20-of-28 passes for 279 yards and a pair of touchdowns. He opened the scoring with a dart to Amon-Ra St. Brown to cap off a 14-play, 90-yard drive in the second quarter, and would add a big one to Jameson Williams in the third.
On the pass to Williams, Goff stepped up in the pocket amidst pressure and delivered a strike to Williams down the field for a 57-yard touchdown. He also showcased some escapability throughout the game, such as a scramble to convert a third-down in the second half.
Goff avoided throwing an interception for the first time since Week 7, and looked to be back on track after some mistakes in recent weeks.
It was tough sledding on the ground for the Lions in the first half, as Jahmyr Gibbs was held in check by the league-leading run defense of the Buccaneers for the most part. However, he came alive in the second half as the Lions began to impose their will at the line of scrimmage.
Gibbs notched two touchdowns after halftime and had multiple impressive runs. One of his best came one play before his first touchdown, when he appeared to be stifled in the backfield before squeezing through a small gap for a 4-yard gain before scoring on the next play.
The Alabama product would add two more highlights later in the game, the first being a 26-yard run that may have been a score if not for a shoestring tackle by Ifeatu Melifonwu. He would score for the second time three plays later, dashing to the pylon after some creative motion from Drew Petzing.
After a pair of quiet games, Jameson Williams made a big impact and led the charge throughout Sunday's game. He finished with four catches for 93 yards, and dusted the Buccaneers' secondary on his 57-yard touchdown in the third quarter.
Amon-Ra St. Brown hauled in a 14-yard touchdown pass to open the scoring and totaled 37 yards on his five catches. St. Brown also had an impressive game blocking, as did wide receiver Isaac TeSlaa. Though TeSlaa did not have a catch, he did have a role in sealing the win by recovering the final onside kick.
You can’t stop that pic.twitter.com/3EAykcsVq1
All three of Detroit's tight ends had big moments in Sunday's game. Sam LaPorta had three catches for 62 yards including a 47-yard catch and run on the opening drive. He also had the key block on Gibbs' second touchdown, when the Lions diverted their tendency and ran away from the motion and strength of the formation.
Brock Wright had two catches for 42 yards, which doubled his season total as he had exactly 42 receiving yards on the year entering Sunday's game. Tyler Conklin added an 18-yard catch at the end of an impressive display of mobility from Goff.
The Buccaneers' defense presented a tough challenge on Sunday, and for the first half Detroit had to rely more on the passing game than its trademark ground game. Jared Goff was sacked just once, and did a solid job navigating pressure when the Lions had some struggles.
In the second half, the Lions were able to get going on the ground. They were able to utilize some unique looks with different motions and packages to help offset the challenges presented by the Buccaneers, and as a result they were able to be more two-dimensional after halftime.
The Lions answered some questions in their first game after Aidan Hutchinson's season-ending injury. DJ Wonnum and Derrick Moore once again both recorded sacks, and the line was able to put plenty of heat on Baker Mayfield.
Detroit did have some issues containing Mayfield, who used his legs to make some big plays including a big scramble before a touchdown pass at the end of the first half. Levi Onwuzurike had two tackles, while Ahmed Hassanein had one in his NFL debut.
Detroit's linebacker depth shone at big points throughout Sunday's game. Trevor Nowaske had a huge performance, with a sack amongst two tackles for loss and four total tackles. Derrick Barnes had six combined tackles.
Malcolm Rodriguez earned a half-sack when he teamed up with Derrick Moore on a takedown of Mayfield, and finished with six total tackles as well as a pass defensed. K.J. Britt also got in the mix with a tackle for loss.
Aside from some difficulties at the end of the first half, the Lions' secondary was mostly solid. Chuck Clark notched a sack, while Brian Branch notched six tackles and two passes defensed including a massive hit on Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving.
Kerby Joseph made his season debut, and the Lions utilized a three-safety package at points throughout the game. Joseph had two solo tackles, and his presence gives the Lions some flexibility within their scheme.
Rock Ya-Sin and Roger McCreary were both beat for touchdowns, with Ya-Sin being beaten up the sideline at the end of the first half. However, Ya-Sin also led the defense with 10 total tackles including nine solos.
Jake Bates missed a field goal from 53 yards out on Detroit's first possession, but came back to hit a 56-yarder later in the half. Jack Fox had a big day, as he averaged 57 yards on his two punt attempts with a long of 65.
Jacob Saylors and DeAndre Carter each returned a kickoff, with Saylors going for 29 yards and Carter going for 22. Malcolm Rodriguez was called for a penalty on a kick return for an illegal blindside block.
The Lions' scheme gave them the advantage on Sunday. Drew Petzing and Kelvin Sheppard both had solid days, with Petzing generating some unique looks to counter the Buccaneers' defense while Sheppard pulled all the right strings for the defense.
On that side of the ball, Sheppard made the most of his available personnel as they adjust to life without Hutchinson and Jack Campbell, among others. Players like Wonnum, Moore and Nowaske came up big, while the three-safety look could be a staple for the team moving forward.
Offensively, the Lions had to rely on the passing game more in the first half, but Petzing made some adjustments that got the ground game going after the break.
Now, the Lions will be tasked with getting ready to go for their biggest game of the season up to this point. The Bears present a unique challenge, and as a result Dan Campbell and company will have to make the most of a short week ahead of the Thanksgiving game.

title: 8 Winners, 3 Losers From Lions Win Over Buccaneers
full_text:
On Sunday, the Detroit Lions played host to longtime former team captain Alex Anzalone and his new team, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The Lions looked to overcome a stingy Tampa Bay defense , particularly against the run.
After the Lions jumped out to a 10-0 lead, Baker Mayfield and the Bucs fought back, getting in position for a go-ahead drive in the fourth quarter. However, the Lions stood tall and thwarted Tampa Bay, forcing a punt and a turnover on downs on the next two Buccaneers possessions. The Lions’ offense struck for touchdowns on both of its drives, ultimately cruising to a 31-21 win.
Here are the winners and losers, as the Lions start their short week before Thursday’s Thanksgiving contest.
There were plenty of questions to be asked about the EDGE room following the injury to Aidan Hutchinson in Munich. Wonnum did his part to answer the bell, with a sack and forced fumble on the opening play of the game. While the Buccaneers ultimately recovered the ball, the Lions proved that this pass-rush was the real deal, even without their star.
Later in the game, Wonnum was able to bat away a tunnel screen, coming within inches of snagging the ball out of the air and running it a few yards for six points.
Williams has had a solid, although quiet, first half of the season. The former Lions first-round selection had accounted for over 500 yards entering Sunday, ranking 28th in the league.
The Alabama product responded with his third game of over 90 yards on the season while getting his sixth touchdown. In the third quarter, Williams had a 57-yard score on a post route, running away from Buccaneers backup corner Benjamin Morrison. The 57-yarder was tied for the longest Lions play of the season, although a Williams flip into the end zone gave the Ford Field faithful a scare after Hutchinson’s celebration injury .
Gibbs entered Sunday’s game as the leading rusher in the NFL, but faced a tough task with the top rushing defense in Tampa Bay. While the Buccaneers bottled Sonic up, he was able to showcase his strength late, punching the ball in to give the Lions a 10-point lead with less than 5:30 to play.
After the Lions’ defense forced a turnover on downs, Gibbs had a 26-yard burst to approach 100 yards rushing. He finished the drive off with his second touchdown to give the Lions an overwhelming 17-point lead with 1:55 to play; not bad for a player who had six carries for just 18 yards at halftime.
Big-time players show up at big times. Nowaske has had a quiet start to the season, and added his first sack on the season on third down with under 4:00 to play as Tampa Bay tried to rally from down 10 points.
Derrick Moore flushed Mayfield from the pocket, with Nowaske showcasing the trailing speed to close off Mayfield from his receivers and the sideline, dragging the quarterback down. With the former Heisman Trophy winner slow to get up, it forced a quick snap on fourth down as the Lions got another sack.
While Moore did not repeat his two-sack outings from the last two weeks, he got close. Moore slid in for the injured Hutchinson, and was all around Baker Mayfield all day. The Lions’ most recent second-round selection recorded two pressures at the midpoint of the game, helping keep the Lions in the lead.
With the game within two scores late, Moore flushed Mayfield from the pocket into a Nowaske sack on third down, before being one of three Lions to converge on Mayfield during a fourth-down all-out blitz. Moore was the first to hit him, getting credit for a half-sack alongside Malcolm Rodriguez, with Derrick Barnes also in on the play.
The newest Detroit captain , in light of injuries to Hutchinson and Jack Campbell, had a strong day. Clark was all over the field, breaking up a pass and recording a sack on the day.
Clark, a 10-year NFL veteran, was the instant choice for the captaincy by Dan Campbell and the Lions, per the broadcast. He proved his teammates right, leading the team in a strong game with less than 200 yards passing surrendered and Tampa Bay’s final touchdown being the only thing to save face. After his sack, Clark was seen pointing at his captain logo on his way back to the Lions sideline.
The Lions and Buccaneers are familiar foes, and a trend has emerged from the grudge matches between the teams. Tampa Bay has seen their linebackers picked apart in coverage by Goff, particularly when targeting tight ends.
The committee of LaPorta, Brock Wright, and Tyler Conklin all had their own moments to shine, with LaPorta standing above the rest with three massive catches for 62 yards on the game, including a field-flipping 47-yard catch and run, which could not be capitalized on for the opening score of the game.
Goff got back into his early season form on Sunday, with an efficient 20-of-28 yards passing for 279 yards. The quarterback should have had better numbers, too, as two of his incompletions hit his receivers in the hands.
The Pro Bowl quarterback took what the defense gave him, and exploited Buccaneer backup Benjamin Morrison after starting corner Jacob Parrish went down injured. Goff saw Jameson Williams get free multiple times.
When Tampa responded by having Amon-Ra St. Brown matched up with the corner, Goff instantly found his All-Pro receiver for the opening touchdown.
Goff used his legs when needed, and took advantage of solid protection from his offensive line, only being sacked a single time while rushing for 12 yards on five carries.
It was a solid day for the Lions secondary, holding Baker Mayfield under 200 yards passing on the day. However, the corner missed a crucial assignment in the final 10 seconds of the opening half. With Tampa Bay inside the Lions’ 25-yard-line, all Ya-Sin needed to do was not get beat to hold the Buccaneers to a field goal.
Instead, Ted Hurst III got by Ya-Sin for a touchdown to pull the NFC South team within a field goal as the teams headed to the locker rooms.
It was a strong day for the offensive line, with Goff only being sacked a single time. However, Miller was the player responsible for the second-down sack, pushing the Lions behind the sticks and leading to a punt. That gave Tampa Bay the ball back in the fourth quarter while down only three points.
McCreary, much like Ya-Sin, got lumped into the list as a result of actions in the final 10 seconds of a half. McCreary and the Lions were trotting out, playing prevent defense as Tampa Bay tried to rally without timeouts and down 17 points in the last two minutes. The goal was simple: to drain the clock out on Tampa.
The former first-round pick got tasked with the rookie Hurst, who again burned a Motown corner for a touchdown in the waning seconds of a half. In fairness to McCreary, his touchdown came as a result of two defensive pass-interference calls, one each against safeties Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph.
Sports writer since 2022. Emmett Matasovsky started covering the Detroit Lions in 2025. He has extensive experience covering Michigan State Spartans athletics, including MSU basketball and football. Has demonstrated passionate, in-depth coverage of college athletics.

title: Key Takeaways From Detroit Lions 31-21 Victory Against Buccaneers
full_text:
The Detroit Lions faced a tough test Sunday against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Detroit's high-powered offense met a Buccaneers defense that is among the league's best, particularly against the run game. Additionally, Tampa Bay entered Week 11 leading the league in interceptions, while Lions quarterback Jared Goff came into Sunday's game with some ball-security issues.
Over the last three games, Goff had thrown four interceptions. This made taking care of the ball a primary point of emphasis, with former Lions linebacker Alex Anzalone tied for the Buccaneers' team lead in picks this year with four.
Before the game, Lions head coach Dan Campbell praised the efforts of Anzalone in Tampa Bay's defense.
"As we know, he's a student of the game, headsy player," Campbell said in a pregame interview. "Just understands defense in general, he's got a good grasp of what they're doing now. He's gotten better every week. He knows what it is. Very good coverage player, smart, instinctive. We know Alex well."
After 60 minutes, the Lions improved their record to 8-2.
Here are several takeaways from the Lions' 31-21 home victory.
Detroit won the opening coin toss and elected to defer to the Buccaneers. After forcing a quick three-and-out, the Lions offense took the field for the first time.
Goff quickly found tight end Sam LaPorta on a 47-yard gain.
Unfortunately, the Buccaneers' defense were able to swat down a couple of Goff's passes, stalling Detroit's opening drive.
Kicker Jake Bates missed a 53-yard field goal, denying Dan Campbell's squad points on their opening drive.
The Buccaneers were able to go on a 12-play offensive drive that featured a 14-yard rush by running back Kenneth Gainwell.
Mayfield was also able to connect on short passes to wideouts Emeka Egbuka, Chris Godwin and Tez Johnson in order to make their way to the red zone.
On 4th-and-1, the Buccaneers made the decision to go for it from the Lions nine-yard line.
Linebacker K.J. Britt, who was added to the roster recently from the Patriots practice squad, stuffed Irving, keeping the game scoreless.
Detroit's offense capitalized on the defensive stop, as the 32-year-old quarterback led the team on a 14-play, 90-yard touchdown drive.
The former No. 1 overall pick distributed the football to Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams and Jahmyr Gibbs kept drives alive.
Dan Campbell's squad converted on three occasions on third-down and short yardage situations.
For the eighth time this season, Goff connected with St. Brown for a touchdown, as the talented wideout secured a 14-yard reception to give the Lions a 7-0 lead.
Detroit was able to benefit from an early back injury to Buccaneers cornerback Jacob Parrish, who left the game in the second-quarter and did not return.
8th time this season pic.twitter.com/K9IaFuVvbS
The Lions' defense was playing very well for the majority of the first half. They held Tampa Bay to 138 total yards and limited running back Bucky Irving to just 12 on the ground. Detroit was also able to sack Baker Mayfield twice, once from Chuck Clark and once by DJ Wonnum.
However, the LIons were unable to keep the Buccaneers off the scoreboard for the entire half. Mayfield scrambled for a big gain with less than a minute remaining, and hit Ted Hurst III for a touchdown with four seconds remaining to cut Detroit's lead to 10-7 at halftime.
Goff was able to extend Detroit's second offensive drive of the second half with a 10-yard scramble. Throughout the game, Goff was able to evade pressure to deliver the football and make plays early in the game.
Detroit was able to extend their lead to 17-6 in the third-quarter when Goff connected with Williams on a deep 57-yard touchdown reception.
Earlier in the week, Campbell expressed he wanted his football team to be smart in regards to celebrating positive plays.
Supporters held their collective breaths when the speedy wideou t flipped head first into the end zone.
Williams was able to produce his fifth career touchdown of 50 yards or more, which is tied for sixth-most in Lions franchise history.
You can’t stop that pic.twitter.com/3EAykcsVq1
After an 83-yard touchdown was negated by a holding call in the first half, Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving helped to cut Detroit's lead to 17-14 in the third-quarter.
On their second offensive possession of the second half, Irving recorded 43 rushing yards on six carries. He also was involved in the passing game.
He capped off the 12-play, 70-yard drive with a one-yard scamper, his sixth touchdown in the past four games. On that drive, Detroit's defense missed several tackles, allowing the Buccaneers to gain several added yards.
Through three quarters, Tampa Bay was 8-for-12 on third-down.
Outside of a seven-yard pass to St. Brown that netted an additional 15 yards due to a Buccaneers face mask penalty, the Lions called Gibbs' number on eight of the nine play scoring drive midway though the fourth quarter.
Gibbs found the end zone on a one-yard scamper that gave the Lions a 24-14 lead with less than six minutes remaning in the game.
The Lions top offensive weapon added a 36-yard scamper and another short touchdown later in the fourth quarter to help Detroit win their fifth home game of the 2026 season.

title: Setting Lions Fans Expectations for Sione Vaki Against Buccaneers
full_text:
The Detroit Lions will be looking to get their run game going Sunday against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Their run-first identity will be challenged by the Buccaneers' top-ranked run defense. Vita Vea anchors the run defense efforts from the interior defensive line, while former Lions linebacker Alex Anzalone will look to shut things down at the second level.
The Lions currently have the NFL's leading rusher in Jahmyr Gibbs, who has proven to be one of the most dynamic talents in the league. However, he has also had to carry the ball more than any other running back which creates natural concerns about his durability.
With Detroit playing on a short week following this game, offensive coordinator Drew Petzing may elect to take the ball out of Gibbs' hands for stretches throughout the game. With that Thanksgiving game against the Bears potentially being for first-place, Detroit no doubt wants to have him available.
As a result, Detroit could get more opportunities for third-year backup running back Sione Vaki. The Utah product has played a significant role this year, as the injury to Isiah Pacheco has put Vaki into the backup role.
Sports Betting Dime's Drew Ellis believes Vaki could have noteworthy contributions spelling Gibbs against the stout Buccaneers. Ellis is projecting Gibbs to go over his projected rushing yards total, which is currently set at 15.5 (-106 via DraftKings Sportsbook).
"The third-year running back has started to carve out a role with the Lions offense and has seen his yards per carry improve as of late," Ellis told Lions OnSI. "With the offensive line looking stronger in the run game, it’s helped Vaki provide productive carries. Given Detroit is in the middle of three games in 11 days, with Chicago waiting on Thursday, it’s important that the Lions not overwork Jahmyr Gibbs against Tampa Bay."
On the season, Vaki has amassed 36 carries for 163 yards. He has improved seemingly every week, and had six carries for 28 yards last week against the Patriots. His most notable performance came in Week 8 when he ran for 65 yards on 11 carries against another stout defense in the Minnesota Vikings.
With Detroit playing another strong defense, they could rely on Vaki to get some tough yards spelling Gibbs.
"I look for Vaki to approach double-digit carries against the Bucs," Ellis added. "Given that, he should be able to hammer home at least 16 rushing yards in those opportunities to hit the over. Vaki runs hard and is playing with more confidence."
