title: Key Matchup Detroit Lions Must Win Against Tampa Bay Buccaneers
full_text:
On Sunday afternoon, the Detroit Lions will have their hands full containing the Buccaneers’ No. 1 rushing attack .
Tampa Bay's ground game, spearheaded by No. 1 back Bucky Irving, has amassed the most yards (1,475) through the first 10 weeks of the 2026 campaign. Irving, himself, has compiled 825 yards on 167 carries – 4.9 yards per carry – to go along with seven touchdowns.
The third-year back is also coming off a 97-yard, two-touchdown effort in Week 9 against the Chicago Bears. There's no question that Irving, who's presently on pace for a career-best campaign, will be a challenge to stop for defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard's unit.
Meanwhile, the Buccaneers’ No. 2 back, Kenny Gainwell, is also a capable runner. And thus far this season, he's produced 305 yards on 63 carries, good for an average of 4.8 yards per rush attempt.
I would not be surprised one bit to see Tampa Bay offensive coordinator Zac Robinson dial up the run game early and often, especially with QB Baker Mayfield being banged up (plantar fasciitis).
As for the Lions’ defense, it's allowed the fifth-fewest rushing yards (814) and the seventh-fewest rushing touchdowns (six) in the NFL through nine games.
It's a credit not only to Sheppard's ability to scheme against the run, but also to defensive lineman Alim McNeill's ability to anchor the line.
The defensive tackle has been the definition of a run-stuffing presence for Detroit's defense this season. In fact, he's earned a run-defense grade of 69.7 from Pro Football Focus for his efforts. It ranks as the 16th-best run-defense mark among 134 qualified interior defensive linemen.
Plus, he's been extremely proficient as a pass-rusher, with seven sacks (the most among interior DL) and 37 total pressures (the second-most among all interior DL). And for his efforts, he's earned a PFF pass-rush grade of 76.3, the 13th-best mark among players at his position.
McNeill views Tampa Bay's running backs as a physical bunch.
"They know exactly what they want to do and the identity that they're trying to create," the sixth-year defensive tackle told reporters earlier this week. "And if we want to stop the run and prove who we really are, this is the team to do it against.”
Entering this Week 11 matchup , the Buccaneers have been averaging 163.9 rushing yards per game. I believe they'll leave Ford Field on Sunday with 113 yards on the ground and a single rushing TD.

title: Packers-Rams Matchups: Familiar Face Could Be the Unlikely Deciding Factor
full_text:
The Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams will play in the first iteration of the Thanksgiving Eve special when toe meets leather on Wednesday night.
In a stroke of luck from the schedule-makers, this is a must-win game for both teams . The Packers and Rams are 6-4 and tied for the seventh seed in the NFC playoffs. The winner of this game will hold the ever-important head-to-head tiebreaker. Considering the Packers have lost a tiebreaker to the Vikings and don’t hold one against the Lions, they need all the help they can get.
The Rams, like the Packers, are in a tough division and will have to play San Francisco and Seattle one more time before the season ends
Here’s our look at the matchups, and where the Packers hold the edge.
This matchup had potential to look very different when the season started. Puka Nacua and Davante Adams combine for one of the top receiver combos in football. The Rams won’t have either player for Wednesday’s game. Nacua is on injured reserve with a knee injury that will sideline him for several months. Adams had surgery on his hamstring, which he injured in October, and has not practiced this week.
Nacua has only played in seven games and Adams in six. They’re still by far the Rams’ top two receivers. The next closest player to Adams’ 480 yards is tight end Tyler Higbee, who has 304. Among receivers, Nacua has 70 catches, Adams has 60 and everyone else combined has 27.
McVay and reigning MVP quarterback Matthew Stafford have their work cut out for them to generate big plays against a Packers defense that is playing well.
Tupac Shakur once had a song called “All Eyez On Me.” This week, all eyes will be on No. 1. Micah Parsons is eligible to return after not playing since tearing his ACL and meniscus last December in Denver.
The Packers have missed him, and are hoping the juice he provides can bring their defense to another level. The key for Green Bay’s defense as Parsons becomes more acclimated is to not become too Parsons-centric as they were a season ago. Jonathan Gannon has been excellent at dialing up blitzes and putting his best players in positions to succeed. He needs to continue to do that even with Parsons returning.
If Parsons is activated and does play against the Rams, he’ll likely be on a snap count. Even if that’s true, the Packers will be thrilled to have their best player back on the field in any capacity. Combine that with the Rams’ lack of proven weapons at receiver, the Packers should be able to control Stafford.
The Rams’ rushing offense is a two-headed monster led by Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. Williams has 616 yards on 139 carries and Corum has 547 yards on 103 carries. Both are tough, physical runners that are hard to get on the ground. Williams and Corum have combined to force 51 missed tackles, according to PFF.
“You can’t tackle them. That’s what they’ve shown,” defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon said. “They’ve got really good contact balance. They’re both very strong, they’ve got really good vision, they’ve got good patience with their run scheme.
“I think what goes unnoticed is how they make it go with the acceleration when they need the acceleration, the hesitation when they need the hesitation to let the blocks declare. I’ve got a high opinion of both of these guys.”
The Packers’ run defense will need to buckle its chin straps to get them on the ground. They could get a boost this week with the potential return of Zaire Franklin to the middle of the defense. For all of Franklin’s shortcomings in coverage, physical run games are what he thrives against.
Green Bay’s defense has held up well against almost any run game they’ve faced this season. The Rams will make things difficult, but the Packers’ defense has proven trustworthy this season.
The Packers’ offensive line is reeling coming out of last week’s debacle against the Vikings. The Packers had all week to plan for Minnesota’s pressure packages and crumbled. This week, they’re facing a different style of beast.
Perhaps literally. Kevin Zeitler said the Rams had a legendary group on their defensive line. Matt LaFleur called the stars of the Rams’ front “creatures.”
Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald are going to waltz into the Hall of Fame when their careers end. Donald came out of retirement to play with Garrett and chase a Super Bowl. Garrett has played just three games but has three sacks. He trails Byron Young, who has 5.5 sacks, for the team lead. Donald has been quieter with 1.5 sacks and 4.5 TFLs, though all of the sack production came in the Rams’ last game.
“A couple of times definitely over the years, [and it’s] absolutely stress-inducing every single time,” Zeitler said of Donald. “The guy’s a monster – always has been, always will be as long as he’s out on that field. It will take every single thing we’ve got as a team and as individuals to get it done.”
When the ball goes in the air, the Rams’ secondary has some talent. They’re missing big offseason acquisition Jaylen Watson, but he’s been replaced admirably by Josh Wallace and Emmanuel Forbes. Their star, however, is Trent McDuffie, who has allowed a passer rating of 29.1 when targeted.
Can the Packers find enough time for Jordan Love to get the ball to some of his pass catchers? Will those pass catchers get away from the sticky coverage the Rams’ secondary provides?
This may not be a great matchup for Green Bay’s offense.
Green Bay’s run game will have a quote from Adam Stenavich on its tombstone whenever this season ends.
“We didn’t block anybody,” Stenavich said in response to a question about a toss play to Kaleb Johnson against Minnesota.
This will go down as the greatest 1-yard run in NFL history. pic.twitter.com/NQtPNRCQiU
The Packers’ run game remains putrid. Josh Jacobs is practicing but is not expected to play; his presence in his two games in the lineup didn’t matter, anyway. Johnson has given the run game a little bit of a boost, but how low is the bar when 10 carries for 42 yards is considered a good day at the office?
“Running the ball, I think that’s the easy part for him,” quarterback Jordan Love said. “I think that’s what he does. Obviously, that’s why he’s in the NFL. And I think it’s just all the little thing – the pass pro, understanding our system, picking stuff up day in and day out – that’s going to keep making him better. But he’s made some really fantastic runs, a lot of explosive plays.”
Can the Packers get anything going on the ground as a means to slow down the vicious pass rush the Rams can unleash?
That feels unlikely. The Rams are 11th in rushing yards allowed per game and 10th in yards allowed per carry. They’re tough. They’re physical. Simply put, they line up 11 guys on defense. Those defenses have given the Packers’ run game trouble this season.
Trey Smack giveth. Trey Smack taketh away. That has been the case for the rookie kicker all season. Smack missed a 53-yard field goal early in the first half that started the snowball effect. The kick was not particularly close as it leaked to the right early.
Green Bay’s kick-return game took another blow on Sunday with Skyy Moore returning only to leave again with an ankle injury. His status for Wednesday is uncertain at this point, though it’s a positive sign that he’s practiced this week.
The Rams have had their own issues at kicker. Their solution? Former Packers kicker Brandon McManus, who was released after the team drafted Smack. He’s made all five field-goal attempts and all 14 extra points.
The Rams’ special teams have been a pressure point in Los Angeles during Sean McVay’s career. So far this season, that has not been all that different.
The difference here, however, comes at kicker. In a cruel twist of irony, the Rams are more stable with the man Smack replaced.

title: Packers Didn’t Get Much Playoff Help But Did Receive Resounding Message
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – With a tenuous grip on the final playoff spot in the NFC, the Green Bay Packers did not receive much help from their friends on Sunday.
The Detroit Lions? They beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
The Chicago Bears? They beat the New Orleans Saints.
The Minnesota Vikings? At least they lost to the San Francisco 49ers, but the 49ers delivered a loud-and-clear message to everyone in the NFC on Sunday night.
The Packers’ backs remain firmly against the wall as their Thanksgiving Eve showdown at the Los Angeles Rams looms on Wednesday.
“We definitely feel the urgency,” receiver Christian Watson said. “I think even at the beginning of the year, just having the early NFC North games and that stuff, every game is just as important to me as a player, but we’re definitely feeling the urgency.
“Obviously, we can’t amp it up too much and go out there and try to do too much or anything. Just got to do our job and let everything else handle itself, but the urgency’s definitely there. We know what's at stake, we know that the opportunity we have in front of us, we’ve just got to take care of it.”
Here’s the state of the NFC after Sunday.
1. San Francisco 49ers: 9-1 (beat Vikings).
2. Detroit Lions: 8-2 (beat Buccaneers).
3. New York Giants: 6-3-1 (beat Jaguars).
4. Carolina Panthers: 5-5 (beat Ravens).
5. Chicago Bears: 8-2 (beat Saints)
6. Minnesota Vikings: 7-3 (lost to 49ers).
7. Green Bay Packers: 6-4 (bye)
8. Seattle Seahawks: 6-4 (bye).
9. Los Angeles Rams: 6-4 (bye).
The importance of Wednesday night is clear. Whoever wins will have a one game lead in the standings plus own the tiebreaker. It’s not an elimination game, but Week 12 could be a pivotal one in the playoff race.
The Packers/Rams winner will be 7-4, the Packers/Rams loser will be 6-5 and the Seahawks could potentially fall to 6-5 because they will play at the 49ers on Sunday.
The Game of the Week turned out to be the Mismatch of the Week. Brock Purdy sliced and diced Brian Flores’ defense to the tune of 21-of-26 passing for 255 yards and three touchdowns. After sacking Jordan Love eight times, the Vikings sacked Purdy only once.
“It’s one of those things where I told our team, when you play a good team like that and you don't play your best, you're going to get beat,” Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell said. “The beauty of it all is we're 7-3 with the ability to really control our own destiny the rest of the way.”
Brock Purdy went 16-for-18 for 195 yards and 2 TDs against the Vikings' blitz. His 88.9% completion percentage was the highest against a Brian Flores blitz since Week 1, 2019 (Lamar Jackson). When pressured on blitzes, Purdy finished 8-for-9 for 100 yards. Powered by @awscloud pic.twitter.com/1KRPL6efDC
The Vikings will play five of their last seven games at home.
“We got beat, but there's not a guy in that locker room that I believe will lose any ounce of confidence about where we could potentially go,” O’Connell said.
The 49ers, meanwhile, showed the Packers that getting to the playoffs might not mean much. Last week, the Packers lost 30-10 at home to the Vikings, who played without tight end T.J. Hockenson and linebacker Blake Cashman.
Get the ball out of your quarterback's hand quickly against the #Vikings defense, you say? pic.twitter.com/hnJwzsb6O9
Well, the Vikings got pummeled by the 49ers. The Vikings had Hockenson and Cashman and a more comfortable Kirk Cousins, but it didn’t matter. Their vaunted defense was destroyed by Purdy and coach Kyle Shanahan, something Jordan Love and Matt LaFleur could not figure out in their two games.
It was a resounding message to every team, and especially the Packers, that the 49ers might be the team to beat. Just like Packers-Vikings, 49ers-Vikings was essentially over at halftime.
The NFC North-leading Lions won their sixth consecutive game and improved to 5-0 at home by beating the Buccaneers 31-21.
Jared Goff was 20-of-28 passing for 279 yards and two touchdowns and running back Jahmyr Gibbs added 98 rushing yards and two more touchdowns. Even without Aidan Hutchinson, Detroit’s defense stayed hot, holding the Buccaneers to 274 yards and a garbage-time touchdown.
“Yeah, huge. That’s been the biggest growth for us has been defensively,” Lions coach Dan Campbell said. “Just the improvement that we've had in that group. And that's even after losing guys. We lose some critical players but yet we're still gaining strength.
“And that's the sign of a championship team, man. Doesn't mean it's perfect, doesn't mean it's always going to be perfect but, man, we are competitive and we challenge on the perimeter. We can create pressure, we can stop the run. And the greatest strength right now is really us as a team. It’s us.”
The win sets up one of the biggest Thanksgiving games in Lions history. The winner will lead the NFC North. The loser will fall to the wild card.
“That’s how they drew it up when the schedule rolled out, so it’ll be fun,” Goff said. “It’ll be really fun. That’s a good team. They’re very well coached. Got a lot of respect for how they do things offensively, defensively. It’ll be really fun. I’m sure they feel the same.”
The Bears without quarterback Caleb Williams were crushed at Lambeau Field in Week 5. Now, including a 21-13 win over the Saints on Sunday, they’ve won five in a row.
The Bears gained only 311 yards, but Jeffery Simmons had three sacks and Montez Sweat put the game away with a safety.
“We win in multiple ways,” Williams told reporters after the game. “And that's good for us as a team, to know that when we get in these situations throughout the year and late in this year, we’ve got each other's back. And we know that we can win in a multitude of ways.”
The Bears will play at Detroit on Thanksgiving. They are undefeated in games started and finished by Williams.
“Every game counts as one, but this one, because it's a divisional one, you could say it's one-and-a-half,” coach Ben Johnson said. “It's a big one, but we keep saying it every week. It's the next one (and) the next one's the biggest one. So, that's really our sole focus.
“These guys will go home tonight. They'll enjoy the night, and then it'll be a quick turnaround. We'll be able to catch up on rest after Thursday. But for the next little bit, it's going to be a race to get ready for this next one.”
The NFC North, which is 23-5 in games outside the division, remains a gauntlet. The Lions and Bears are 8-2, so two games ahead of Green Bay. The Vikings are 7-3, so one game ahead of Green Bay but, really, it’s a two-game margin because of the Vikings’ season sweep.
In the race between the Packers, Rams and Seahawks for the seventh and final spot, the Rams’ have the second-toughest remaining strength of schedule at .606, the Seahawks are fourth at .570 and the Packers are seventh at .557.
While coach Matt LaFleur stuck with the 1-0 mantra, quarterback Jordan Love spoke with honesty on Saturday.
“We talk about the mindset is, ‘You’ve got to go win every game,’ but this is a big game,” Love said. “Both teams 6-4, obviously a lot riding on end-of-season playoff seeds, stuff like that. So, yeah, we talk about it. It’s a game we’ve got to go out there and handle business. We’re both going to be hungry teams.
“Really, you’ve got to win every game down the stretch and, obviously, it’s the one-game mentality. But you look at some of the teams we’re playing – you don’t want to call them must-win games – but we’ve got to go handle business. These are the games I feel like set you up for the end of the season. But you’ve got to go out there and handle business, for sure.”

title: Packers-Rams Sunday Injury Report: Key Stafford Stopper Says He’s ‘All Good’
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Green Bay Packers cornerback Brandon Cisse was knocked out of last week’s loss to the Vikings with a rib injury.
Before the end of the first half, Cisse jogged out of the locker room with the intention of re-entering the game. The training staff said no.
“We’ve got protocols and all those things, but I wanted to go back in,” Cisse said after Sunday’s practice in preparation for the Thanksgiving Eve game at the Los Angeles Rams.
Cisse was one of seven starters who were limited participation at Sunday’s practice. It was the team’s second practice of the week – it was conducted in pads inside the Don Hutson Center – but the first injury report.
“Yeah, I’m all good,” Cisse said.
All 52 players on the roster practiced. That’s all 53 if you include edge rusher Micah Parsons, who appears set to make his season debut .
“Huge,” receiver Christian Watson said about Parsons’ potential impact. “He’s one of the best players in the National Football League. So, to get him back out there, just his presence out there will be big time for us. Obviously, just the energy that he’ll bring just with his play style and even his energy on the sideline will be huge. So, definitely excited for him to be back out there.”
Including Cisse and Parsons, seven potential starters were limited participation. The others were linebackers Zaire Franklin (shin) and Isaiah McDuffie (rib), running back Josh Jacobs (finger), center Sean Rhyan (ankle) and guard Kevin Zeitler (triceps). Also limited were receivers and special-teams weapons Bo Melton (thigh) and Skyy Moore (ankle).
This was the second consecutive practice for Jacobs following last week’s surgery on a broken ring finger. Coach Matt LaFleur was pessimistic about Jacobs playing against the Rams, though.
“He did some individual, but he’s going to have to show a lot of progress today and tomorrow to be available,” LaFleur said before practice.
With the assumption that Jacobs will not play, Kaleb Johnson could be in for a bigger load after leading the team with 10 rushes for 42 yards last week.
“Whenever my number’s called, no matter if I’m starting or not, going in and performing,” Johnson said. “[That’s] what got me here. So, it’s really just being me, really – the little stuff, picking up protections, being reliable. That’s really it.”
The new No. 1 line for the stretch run could include Rhyan returning after a three-game absence and Zeitler making his first start for his home-state team.
“They’re making progress,” LaFleur said.
The Rams will line up with a watered-down passing attack with Davante Adams and Puka Nacua on injured reserve. They still have reigning MVP quarterback Matthew Stafford, though, so a full-strength secondary would be important for Green Bay.
Cisse has been one of the top rookie cornerbacks in the league. His seven-game streak of not allowing a touchdown pass was snapped when he was injured on the Vikings’ first touchdown last week.
When Cisse jogged out of the locker room and to the sideline, he asked for his helmet but his wish was not granted.
“I think it’s frustrating but just one of those things,” Cisse said. “It’s definitely harder for me at that time because I really, really wanted to be out there, really wanted to help and I just couldn’t do anything. So, that was frustrating because my life is kind of centered around football so, even when I went home, it’s all I’m thinking about. Yeah, it was frustrating.”
While he had to watch the final three quarters from the sideline, why was it so important to him to get back on the field?
“I think it’s just the kind of competitive drive in me,” he said. “I want to be out there every chance I get and I just want to be able to keep on making plays and helping my teammates.”
The Rams won’t have their dynamic duo of receivers with Puka Nacua (knee) and Davante Adams (hamstring) out. Combined, they’ve caught 100 passes for almost 1,200 yards. The other receivers on the roster have caught 25 passes.
“Obviously, you feel for him,” quarterback Matthew Stafford told reporters when asked about Nacua. “For a guy that puts a ton of effort into trying to be out there every single Sunday for us. He plays as violently as anybody in the NFL, especially in his position. He puts his body on the line for us.
“Unfortunately, he had to get some things fixed and cleaned up. I hope all that is in the best interest of his long-term health because that's what I care about as a human being and his future. He’s been a great teammate of mine and I want him to feel good again and if that's the best course of action, that's the best course of action.”
The receiver corps isn’t their only problem on offense. Left guard Steve Avila (hamstring) and center Coleman Shelton (hamstring) did not practice on Sunday. They have not allowed a sack this season.

title: Packers Sunday Update From Practice: Micah Parsons Hits ‘Next Marker’
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Sunday marked perhaps the last barrier standing between Micah Parsons and his first football game in more than 340 days.
The Green Bay Packers stayed inside the Don Hutson Center on Sunday for their one padded practice of the week before Wednesday night’s game at the Los Angeles Rams. Parsons, who has been building up his reps the last couple weeks, was on the field.
“I think it’s very important,” coach Matt LaFleur said before practice. “I think it’s the next marker that you got to check off.”
The key for Parsons not only how he practices on Sunday but how he feels on Monday following the most rigorous practice of the week. At this point, Parsons seems to be all systems go to face the Rams. It would be his first game since Dec. 14, a span of 49 weeks.
LaFleur wouldn’t talk about snap counts or gameday limitations. For what it’s worth, Parsons played in 30 of a possible 67 snaps in his Packers debut last year against Detroit. Parsons didn’t participate in training camp for the Cowboys last year, so he essentially played about half the snaps following two weeks of practice.
He will have had three practices before Wednesday’s game.
“I’d love to answer that question, but I think that would be doing our team a disservice at this point, you know what I mean?” LaFleur said. “I’ll happily answer it after the game, but I don’t want to put our plan out there for everybody in terms of if he does clear all the hurdles and is available. But we will have a plan in place.”
LaFleur has seen some peak-level Parsons on the practice field but, like Parsons himself a few weeks ago, he tried to downplay expectations.
“He is an elite player,” LaFleur said. “He’s an elite athlete, but I do think, like you see with many of these guys [coming off major injuries] – and I never want to put limitations on anybody, but he hasn’t played football in a really long time. So, I think you’ve got to be conscious of that. And there’s probably going to be some plays that don’t look like him, and then there’s going to be some plays that do.”
All 52 players on the roster – 53, if you assume Parsons will fill that roster spot – practiced for a second consecutive day.
That includes running back Josh Jacobs, who is coming back from a broken ring finger that required surgery.
As was the case on Saturday, LaFleur downplayed the possibility of Jacobs playing on Wednesday, though he didn’t rule it out. These practice reps this week might be about keeping him sharp for the game against the Saints the following week.
“He did some individual, but he's going to have to show a lot of progress today and tomorrow to be available,” LaFleur said.
Along with Parsons and Jacobs, cornerback Brandon Cisse (rib), receiver Bo Melton (quad), receiver/returner Skyy Moore (ankle), linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin), right guard Kevin Zeitler (triceps) and center Sean Rhyan (ankle) practiced again on Sunday. Those seven players either did not play against Minnesota last week or dropped out of the game.
With Rhyan and Zeitler trending the right way, the Packers might be rolling out their seventh starting unit this season.
“They’re making progress,” LaFleur said.
LaFleur said Aaron Banks, the team’s $77 million left guard, has been practicing at left guard and right guard this week. That would seem to indicate that Zeitler will be making his starting debut and Banks will be the swing guard.
The return of Franklin would be important considering the Rams’ two-headed monster in the backfield of Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. They’ve combined for 1,163 yards and 11 touchdowns.
“It was truly just a freak accident,” Franklin explained on Sunday . “Something that I really couldn’t even describe. I shoot the gap clean, somebody just kind of kneed me in a weird way. I’m thinking it’s just dead leg. I actually finished practice. I practiced two more periods on a broken leg. And then once I got the X-ray and it was broke, I was looking like, I almost couldn’t believe it. It just looked fake.”
The Rams will not have their two premier receivers, Davante Adams (hamstring) and Puka Nacua (knee).
So, the Rams will pivot to Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell and a bunch of tight ends.
Among the next men up at receiver, Mumpfield has 14 catches for 253 yards and one touchdown, Atwell has eight catches for 130 yards, Xavier Smith has two catches for 40 yards and one touchdown and C.J. Daniels has one catch for 22 yards.
With Nacua and Adams out last week against Arizona, Mumpfield caught three passes for 81 yards, Atwell had a 31-yard catch, Smith scored a 22-yard touchdown and Daniels had his 22-yard catch as quarterback Matthew Stafford threw for 249 yards with a 122.1 passer rating.
“What do these guys do best?” Rams coach Sean McVay told reporters on Saturday. “I thought Konata Mumpfield showed a lot of really cool stuff. We've been around Tutu for a while. We know what he can do. It was great for C.J. Daniels to get his first extended action, awesome for ‘X-Man’ [Smith] to be able to make plays. Brennan Presley was back there returning kicks.
“With the five guys that we do have up, I think they have good complementary skill-sets, but I think there are certain things that they do really well. We'll continue to lean into those things while also not pigeonholing ourselves into saying that they can't continue to add to what their game and their complementary skill sets are. … Those guys played with confidence. They enjoyed it. They played with a swagger. It was fun to watch those guys.”
The Rams designated defensive tackle Kobie Turner to return from injured reserve this week. He had no sacks in six games this season but nine as a rookie in 2023, eight in 2024 and seven in 2025.

title: Packers Might Turn to New Offensive Line to Handle Old Problem
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers have churned through six starting offensive lines. That includes four individual starting left guards and three right guards.
A seventh combination – and fourth starting right guard – might be on the way, just in time to face the legendary Aaron Donald and the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday night.
Kevin Zeitler, who was going to start at right guard against the Vikings before suffering a triceps injury at practice, returned to practice on Saturday. So did center Sean Rhyan, who missed the last three games with an ankle injury.
So – potentially – the Packers will line up for a must-win game against the Rams with an interior trio of Laken Tomlinson at left guard, Rhyan at center and Zeitler at right guard.
“We’ve got a lot of guys in that boat where they’ve got to prove it, prove function throughout the course of the week, and they’ve got to feel confident that they can go out there and get the job done,” coach Matt LaFleur said when asked specifically about Zeitler, though the answer applied to Rhyan, as well.
LaFleur last week said Zeitler suffered a “freak” injury at practice. So, what happened?
“Beats me,” Zeitler said. “I couldn’t believe it. I don’t think anyone could believe it.”
So, instead of making his first start with the Packers, Zeitler was inactive.
“Just triceps giving out for the first time ever and it’s like just shitty timing,” he said. “Also happening later in the week versus early. Luckily everything’s overall pretty good, and we’re just going to get through this week, and we’ll see where we’re at.”
Zeitler will have to prove his triceps is fine during the practice week and that he’s the better option compared to Travis Glover, who wound up starting at right guard last week after missing two games with a knee injury, or Aaron Banks, the former starting left guard who was taking some right guard reps when reporters were present on Saturday.
“We’re just going to attack this week full speed, get everything done we need to be done, get through the week, and we’ll figure it out by the end of the week,” Zeitler said.
The Wisconsin native and former University of Wisconsin standout was signed after the Packers’ Week 3 debacle against the Falcons. The 36-year-old arrived in Green Bay having made 213 starts, so the assumption was he’d quickly work his way into shape and into the starting lineup.
Instead, Zeitler is getting ready for a Week 12 game but played only 20 snaps.
Maybe – and with how the Packers have handled their line this year, “maybe” is the key word – this will be the line they will roll with in hopes of getting to the playoffs and making a run.
“It’ll be good,” Zeitler said. “We’ll just keep it rolling. We’ll keep building. We’ll keep figuring each other out. Hopefully, everyone gets healthy, and we can all start building on this final stretch of the season.”
Sean Rhyan was injured during the opening series at Detroit and missed the last three games. Saturday marked his first practice since the injury. He said Day 1 went “good.”
“Great being back out there with the guys, moving around, playing some ball again,” he said.
Like Zeitler, Rhyan will have to show he’s healthy enough to get through a game.
“I’m going to do the best I can,” he said. “Obviously, I want to be available for my team, but I don’t want to go out there and possibly jeopardize myself or my teammates because I can’t support myself, get thrown down into somebody else, one could turn into two and so on.
“Rehab’s been going really well. Been just slowly climbing, hanging out, just trying to work through it. First day back out. We’ll see how it feels tomorrow.”
At the time of the injury, the Packers had won three consecutive games with Laken Tomlinson at left guard, Rhyan at center and Travis Glover at right guard. With John Williams playing most of the Detroit game and then starting the next three, the Packers went 2-2. That includes last week’s blowout loss to the Vikings in which the line was overwhelmed physically and mentally.
“Yeah, it’s unfortunate,” Rhyan said. “This is like my first real time missed really ever in my career playing football due to injury, so it’s been kind of a learning experience of really not being able to do anything because you’re not allowed to.
“So, it’s been weird, but it’s been tough watching. I never want to see our unit get the flak that it has been getting, just because of things that are out of our control. But we’re working back. Hopefully, we’ll get everything straightened out, snap back from last week and continue on with the seven weeks we’ve got left.”
The challenge could hardly be bigger. Sensing a chance to win a Super Bowl, Aaron Donald came out of retirement. After a two-year absence, he has played in eight games. He had the first 1.5 sacks of the year last week against the Cardinals.
The ability of Rhyan and whoever is starting at guard to handle Donald will impact how much help can be given to the tackles to deal with another living legend, Myles Garrett.
“Well, I don’t want to say too much, but I think just as an athlete when you leave something for a couple of years and then come back, especially at the highest level, it takes you a little bit, but it seems like he seems to be snapping back right to kind of where he was,” Rhyan said. “A couple of things have changed, but I think he’s done a good job realizing that and kind of adjusting the way he plays because he’s older now. Still a smart player.”
With the return of Rhyan and the potential addition of Zeitler, the Packers might have the ingredients to fix their worst-in-the-league offensive line.
Regardless of who’s on the field, it’s long past time to put a winning product on the field. No quarterback has faced more pressure than Jordan Love and no rushing attack has been less productive, with Green Bay’s 67.0-yard average close to the worst in NFL history.
“The only thing we can do is do it out on the field,” Zeitler said. “It wasn’t pretty last week. I don’t think anyone can say otherwise. I think everyone’s acknowledged it in our room. We’ve got to turn it around. The only thing that matters is things changing on the field. We can talk all we want, but nothing matters until it changes and gets done.”

title: Packers LB Zaire Franklin Explains ‘Freak’ Injury That Sidelined Him for Month
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – After a four-game absence, Green Bay Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin returned to practice on Saturday and intends to play against the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday night.
“I’ve been through a lot of things in my life, but I will say it was definitely one of the harder moments, just not being able to be out there with the guys,” Franklin said after practice. “It’s just a position I’m really not used to, but God makes no mistakes and I’ve been prayed up and I’ve been working my ass off to get back on the field. So, now we’re here.”
Franklin suffered a fractured shin during the Thursday practice before the Week 7 game at the Lions.
“It was truly just a freak accident,” he explained. “Something that I really couldn’t even describe. I shoot the gap clean, somebody just kind of kneed me in a weird way. I’m thinking it’s just dead leg. I actually finished practice. I practiced two more periods on a broken leg. And then once I got the X-ray and it was broke, I was looking like, I almost couldn’t believe it. It just looked fake.
“The only thing that was going through my mind was, ‘Damn, I can’t practice tomorrow?’ It’s been a journey but I’m glad we were able to push through. Thank God for keeping my head down and really been leaning on my family. I’m just glad to be back.”
He practiced with a broken leg?
“I feel like there’s a difference between being hurt and being injured,” he said. “I’m just so used to being hurt so I just put it in that category immediately until I couldn’t walk the next day. Then I said, ‘Oh, damn, I might be injured.’ But thank God we were able to work through it.”
Zaire Franklin returned to practice today. pic.twitter.com/JWQrKmKW5X
Franklin stayed active behind the scenes with Isaiah McDuffie and Ty'Ron Hopper. While he said there is only so much he could do without being on the field, his leadership the past few weeks was appreciated.
“The leadership is obviously the first thing that sticks out,” position coach Sam Siefkes said this week. “He’s been in the league for, what, eight years, so that part I think upticked with him being injured, which was cool to see. He was coaching the guys who were playing in Duff and Hopp and kind of being another person that can help them on the sideline as well as the meeting room.
“That part I give him a lot of credit for, because it’s tough when you’re in those situations, especially when he’s only missed a game. It’s easy to kind of take a back seat and kind of feel sorry for yourself, but he didn’t do that one ounce. For him to be able to take even another step in his leadership role was an awesome thing for him to put forth.”
Franklin had been practically impervious to injury throughout his career. After being drafted by the Colts in 2018, he had missed only one game in his first eight seasons. He started 67 of a possible 68 games during the 2022 through 2025 seasons.
So, it was weird for Franklin to not be practicing and playing. And now he is in the unfamiliar position of having to work his way back from an injury.
“It’s been humbling a little bit,” he said. “I’m just so used to pushing through every single thing until something came up that I wasn’t meant to push through. Just leaning on the training staff, trusting my body, trusting myself, but also knowing that I got that other side of me, that other edge to push through what I need to.
“I feel like the staff did a great job, my team and everybody off the field did a great job of helping me get back, ready to play. Just looking forward to getting back out there with the guys.”
Franklin will practice again on Sunday and Monday to knock off some of the rust and reintegrate himself into one of the better defenses in the league. While he commended McDuffie and Hopper for holding down the fort without him, Franklin presumably will be back in full-time duty as a defensive captain against the Rams on what he called a holiday “made up” by the NFL to create another opportunity to put games on TV.
“I’ve played on Christmas but I don’t think I played Thanksgiving,” he said. “So, this is a new thing. I’m looking forward to it. Are they going to have turkey? It’s Thanksgiving Eve, though.”
Maybe there will be a turducken, he wondered.
“That’s what I need. Need that. Need that, for sure,” he said.
Franklin played in all 17 games in 2022, 2024 and 2025 with the Colts. That was his intention with the Packers, too. Instead, after missing four games, the max he can play is 13.
Unless the team makes it to the playoffs and makes a run.
“I genuinely believe everything happens for a reason,” Franklin said. “I had a close friend tell me that I came here to play 17; I just got to play 17 a different way. We missed four; that means we got to get the extra four. I’m just glad I’m back, ready to play.”

title: Packers Re-Sign Running Back as Part of Practice Squad Moves
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers re-signed running back Pierre Strong to their practice squad on Saturday.
To clear a roster spot, they released edge player D.J. Johnson.
The Packers had five running backs on their roster. With Chris Brooks returning from injured reserve last week and Josh Jacobs dealing with a short-term absence following his broken finger – he practiced on Saturday – Strong was the odd man out .
It was a news-packed day at Packers practice. Here's the latest from the practice field. ⬇️ https://t.co/IZGBqMsnO5
Strong initially signed to the Packers’ practice squad at the end of training camp in 2025, when he was released by the Browns. He spent all of last season on the practice squad and wound up starting this season on the practice squad following the team’s trade for Kaleb Johnson.
With Jacobs on the exempt list and Brooks landing on injured reserve, Strong was signed to the 53-man roster. He played in five games, rushing 25 times for 59 yards (2.4 average) with a long run of 8 yards and catching 10-of-12 targets for 61 yards (6.1 average).
Strong was inactive last week against Minnesota, with the Packers rolling with Kaleb Johnson, MarShawn Lloyd and Brooks.
“Obviously, he's a quick player,” position coach Ben Sirmans said recently of Strong. “He's got a overall good football IQ. He plays on special teams, which you saw the tackle he had off the interception, so you have to have some toughness about you and not afraid of contact.
“And then the other thing that I like about him is when he's on the field, he tries to take advantage of his opportunities to try to create a situation where he can be on the field even more. So, those are things that I did expect from him based off what he's done and what his background is.”
Of 74 backs with at least 25 carries, Strong ranks 72nd in yards per carry.
Johnson, on the other hand, is averaging 3.6 yards after contact.
“Just by controlling the day to day and trying to learn and grow and get better at owning his responsibilities,” coach Matt LaFleur said on Saturday of Johnson. “I think it’s always tough when you come in – that timing – for most people, especially in that position, just learning all the nuances of the protections. It was a little bit different than what he’s been doing. So to see that progress has been encouraging.”
While LaFleur said he does not anticipate Jacobs being ready to play against the Rams on Wednesday night, he did add: “We’ll see how he progresses, as well. He would definitely have to prove the function in order to play.”
D.J. Johnson was a third-round pick by the Panthers in 2023 after playing both on the edge and tight end at Oregon .
Johnson played in 13 games with three starts as a rookie and 14 games with two starts in 2024, when he had a half-sack and 44 tackles. He was released early in the 2025 season and has not played in a game since.
The release of Johnson leaves the Packers with Arron Mosby and Nyjalik Kelly as edge players on the practice squad with the return of Micah Parsons to the 53-man roster on the horizon.
LaFleur was at least a little noncommittal on Parsons returning on Wednesday, though everything is pointed in that direction.
“I think we’ll have a better indication the closer we get to this thing,” LaFleur said. “Certainly, he’ll be out there and his ability to go out there and perform at practice will be the ultimate indicator.”

title: Hugely Positive Packers Injury Report From First Practice of Rams Week
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The best ability is availability. The Green Bay Packers kicked off their practice week on Saturday with all 52 players on the active roster going through drills on the practice field.
That doesn’t mean the Packers are completely healthy headed into their Wednesday night game at the Los Angeles Rams. However, seven players who either did not play against the Vikings last week or dropped out of the game were back on the field following their make-believe bye week.
Micah Parsons continues his path to making his season debut. pic.twitter.com/wj7pv8Zq57
The list starts with star edge rusher Micah Parsons, who is entering his third week of practice. Presumably, he will be the 53rd player on the roster for the huge showdown against the Rams, with this week representing the finishing touches on his comeback from last year’s knee injury.
“I think we’ll have a better indication the closer we get to this thing,” coach Matt LaFleur said before Saturday’s practice. “Certainly, he’ll be out there and his ability to go out there and perform at practice will be the ultimate indicator.”
Running back Josh Jacobs was back after missing the Vikings game with a broken finger sustained a week earlier against New England. Jacobs will be able to play through the pain, but the key will be whether he will be able to play with critical ball-security while wearing a protective device following surgery..
Josh Jacobs is practicing after missing one game with a broken finger. pic.twitter.com/o6UOvMnF1J
“I’m not anticipating that [he will play against the Rams], but we’ll see how he progresses,” LaFleur said. “He would definitely have to prove the function in order to play.”
If Jacobs is out, Kaleb Johnson might be the team’s No. 1 back. After barely playing in two games and then not playing at all in two games due to a couple fumbles, Johnson has rushed for 110 yards the last two games. The rest of the team had 75 rushing yards.
“I think he’s grown, I think he’s learned a lot from the time he’s gotten here till now,” LaFleur said. “He’s done a better job in just owning his responsibilities and doing his one-eleventh. That’s encouraging.”
The Packers have had six starting combinations on the offensive line this season. Is No. 7 on the way?
Center Sean Rhyan, who suffered an ankle injury on the opening series at Detroit and missed the last three games, returned to practice. He’d add a more physical and experienced presence than John Williams.
“He’s a guy that’s played a lot of ball,” LaFleur said. “That’s not to take anything away from the job John’s done; I think he’s done a really admirable job going in there, having never really played it before and done a pretty good job. But there’s a reason he’s the starter, right? And there’s a reason we brought him back because he’s played good ball for us, and I think that can help.”
Meanwhile, Kevin Zeitler, who would have started at right guard against Minnesota if not for a triceps injury sustained during the Thursday practice, was back at practice.
Zaire Franklin returned to practice today. pic.twitter.com/JWQrKmKW5X
Starting linebacker and defensive captain Zaire Franklin, who missed the last four games with a shin injury sustained at practice before the Detroit game, returned to practice, as well. That was no surprise considering he went through a pregame warmup before the Minnesota game.
“Another guy that’s got to go through the week and we’ll see where he’s at at the end of this thing,” LaFleur said.
While Isaiah McDuffie, Ty’Ron Hopper and even Nick Niemann did a nice job filling the void, Franklin’s experience and physicality will help the defense and allow Hopper and McDuffie to serve larger roles on special teams.
Cornerback Brandon Cisse (rib), receiver Bo Melton (quad) and receiver/returner Skyy Moore (ankle) dropped out of the Minnesota game. All three players were back at practice.
Cisse, of course, is the standout defensive back and a key part of a defense that ranks fourth in yards allowed per passing play and fifth in opponent passer rating. Moore’s impact as a returner was missed when he went on injured reserve with a high-ankle sprain. He returned against the Vikings but was injured on his third kickoff return.
If Moore is not ready, the team re-signed receiver Coleman Owen to the practice squad. Owen handled the punt-return duties when Moore was on IR.
While the Packers practiced on Saturday and it’s a Wednesday in their world, the NFL will have the teams publish injury reports on Sunday, Monday and Tuesday. While everyone practiced for Green Bay, there’s a lot to be determined before Tuesday’s injury report and Wednesday’s inactives list.
“We've got a lot of guys in that boat where they’ve got to prove it, prove function throughout the course of the week, and they’ve got to feel confident that they can go out there and get the job done,” LaFleur said.
The Packers have a total of 13 players on injured reserve or the physically unable to perform list. Parsons is the only player whose return-to-play window has been opened. So, it’ll be at least another week before defensive tackles Jonathan Ford (calf) and Warren Brinson (groin) will be available.
LaFleur provided a non-answer answer when asked about edge player Collin Oliver, who was injured in the second preseason game at Denver and started the season on injured reserve with a return-to-play designation.
“He’s still progressing through and making progress,” LaFleur said.

title: Grand Theft Draft Pick: Packers’ Biggest Steals Since Last Grand Theft Auto
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – This week’s release of Grand Theft Auto VI is the biggest entertainment launch in history. It’s estimated it could cost U.S. businesses $1 billion in lost productivity.
Considering the nature of the game, that got us to thinking about the biggest draft steals for the Green Bay Packers, and where they’ve made a killing since GTA V debuted in September 2013. So, here is Grand Theft Draft spanning the release dates.
Talk about being thrown into a pressure cooker. The Packers – fresh off a trip to the NFC Championship Game – traded up in the first round of the 2020 draft to select quarterback Jordan Love at No. 26 overall. The task? Eventually replace Hall of Famer-in-waiting Aaron Rodgers, who replaced Hall of Famer Brett Favre.
Love was the fourth quarterback selected behind No. 1 overall pick Joe Burrow, No. 5 pick Tua Tagovailoa and No. 6 pick Justin Herbert. Love’s 96.8 passer rating trails only Burrow (102.9) in the draft class.
Drafting a quarterback is a crapshoot, regardless of the circumstances, but especially so once you get beyond the top prospects.
Over the last decade, 57 quarterbacks have been selected outside the Top 12 of the draft and started at least one game. Love’s 96.8 passer rating trails only Brock Purdy, Lamar Jackson and Dak Prescott. The league median is 78.4. And that’s just the quarterbacks who were good enough to start.
Quarterbacks taken in the proximity of Love’s spot at No. 26 are few and far between. Over the last two decades, only 23 quarterbacks taken between No. 15 and No. 40 threw even one pass, with Love trailing only Jackson in passer rating. The league median from that group is 82.7.
Davante Adams is one of the greatest receivers in NFL history. The 53rd pick of the 2014 draft and the ninth receiver off the board, Adams is a six-time Pro Bowler. Among all receivers drafted in the second round in NFL history, Adams ranks second with 1,047 receptions, fourth with 13,113 yards and first with 121 touchdowns. Adams needs only 30 receptions to pass Anquan Boldin and he’s 30 touchdowns ahead of everyone else.
Adams ranks 14th in NFL history in receptions and sixth in receiving touchdowns. The Packers no doubt will be thrilled to see Adams in street clothes on Thanksgiving Eve against the Rams.
Tucker Kraft practically wins this by default.
Starting with the 2014 draft, the GTA-window third-round picks by the Packers were tight end Richard Rodgers and defensive tackle Khryi Thornton in 2014, receiver-turned-running back Ty Montgomery in 2015, outside linebacker Kyler Fackrell in 2016, defensive tackle Montravius Adams in 2017, linebacker Oren Burks in 2018, tight end Jace Sternberger in 2019, tight end Josiah Deguara in 2020, receiver Amari Rodgers in 2021, lineman Sean Rhyan in 2022, Kraft in 2023, linebacker Ty’Ron Hopper and running back MarShawn Lloyd in 2024, receiver Savion Williams in 2025  and defensive tackle Chris McClellan in 2026.
That’s one bust after another after another, a run of ineptitude interrupted only by some occasional mediocrity.
Kraft emerged as one of the best tight ends in the NFL before last year’s torn ACL. The hope organizationally – especially given Kraft’s contact extension – is he will turn to that elite level.
David Bakhtiari is the steal of steals among fourth-round picks. Bakhtiari, who might have been a Hall of Famer if not for the knee injury that ruined his career and sank the Packers’ Super Bowl hopes in 2020, was drafted in 2013 but a handful of months before the release of GTA 5 .
So, focusing on the window between release dates, we’ll go with safety Evan Williams ahead of a strong list that includes 2022 picks Zack Bako Bewele and Romeo Doubs.
Williams, the 111th pick in 2024, has emerged as not just one of the best young safeties in the NFL but one of the best safeties, period. Williams has 78 tackles, three interceptions and eight passes defensed this season. No other defensive back with 60-plus tackles has more than one interception.
From the 2024 draft class, Williams leads all Day 3 draft picks with seven interceptions and 233 tackles. In the entire draft class, he’s first among defensive backs in tackles and tied for third in interceptions.
“Evan’s a football player. Evan’s a real football player,” secondary coach and defensive pass-game coordinator Bobby Babich said. “Anytime you have that combined with the football mind and that intelligence, usually the product that they’re going to put out there. As long as they care about the game as much as you think they do, that product’s going to be one that everybody likes to watch.”
This was a two-man battle between center Corey Linsley in 2014 and running back Aaron Jones in 2017. We’ll go with Jones because of his longevity.
From the 2017 draft class, Jones leads the way with 8,147 rushing yards, just ahead of Christian McCaffrey (8,108). Since entering the NFL, he trails only 2018 first-round pick Saquan Barkley (8,652) and 2020 second-round pick Jonathan Taylor (8,358).
Jones played with the Packers through 2023. He ranks second in franchise history with 5,940 rushing yards, behind only Ahman Green and Hall of Famer Jim Taylor, and first among running backs with a 5.0-yard average.
There have been no standouts drafted in the sixth round by the Packers since kicker Mason Crosby in 2007. The Packers drafted Isaiah McDuffie with the 220th pick in 2021 and gained a solid, reliable contributor. He ranks 10th in the draft class with 383 tackles; the nine players ahead of him were all top-125 picks. He has at least 109 tackles more than every player drafted after him.
“He’s a pro’s pro,” defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon said last week. “He’s awesome throughout the week. He’s awesome on gameday. He gives really good insight when we come off [the field] what’s going on, what he’s seeing, the communication piece of all that. And he’s made a lot of plays. Playing well.”
The Packers were more than happy to let Rasheed Walker go in free agency this offseason, but he was a Godsend after David Bakhtiari’s career was ruined by a knee injury.
At a position group filled mostly by first-round picks around the league, Walker was the 249th out of 262 players drafted in 2022. He started 48 games as Jordan Love’s blind-side protector from 2023 through 2025. He had a lot more good snaps than bad.
The Packers drafted 22 players in the seventh round from 2014 through 2026. Walker and cornerback Carrington Valentine were the only starters. In fact, you’ve got to go back to center Scott Wells (2014) as the only Packers seventh-round pick who was a full-time starter for at least as many seasons as Walker.

title: Packers Report Card at Bye Week: One ‘A’ In Our Unit Grades on Defense
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers will take a 6-4 record out of their bye week and into a Thanksgiving Eve showdown at the Rams.
Jonathan Gannon’s defense is a mediocre 14th with 22.1 points allowed per game, due in part to the offense’s two horrific performances against the Vikings skewing the bottom line. Only the Vikings and Jaguars (seven apiece) have allowed 20-or-fewer points in more games than the Packers (six). They rank 11th in total defense but second in takeaways, fourth in sacks and fourth in passes defensed.
With the table set, here is a Packers midseason report card on defense.
This position, of course, was the major question mark entering the season. How would Green Bay’s defense survive the first four or six games without Micah Parsons? Well, as it turns out, the defense has survived 10 games without Parsons.
The Packers flipped the switch on Lukas Van Ness’s fifth-year option, a $13.752 million gamble on a player who had a total of 8.5 sacks in his first three seasons. Through 10 games this season, he has six sacks. That gives him a decent chance of getting to at least 10 sacks – a significant milestone for a pass rusher.
Fellow starter Barryn Sorrell has two sacks. The backups, Brenton Cox and Dani Dennis-Sutton, have been productive. Cox has only 1.5 sacks but is second on the team with eight quarterback hits. Dennis-Sutton, a fourth-round rookie, is tied for second on the team with three sacks and is third with seven quarterback hits.
Those four each have 159 pass-rushing snaps, a threshold met by 70 edge rushers. Van Ness ranks eighth in pass-rush win rate and 11th pass-rush productivity, a PFF metric that encompasses sacks, hits and hurries per pass-rushing snap. Sorrell is 44th in win rate and 59th in PRP, Cox is 23rd in win rate and 18th in PRP, and Dennis-Sutton is 50th in win rate and 16th in PRP.
Something that doesn’t show up in the stat is their edge-setting ability, and they’ve done well in that regard.
“That was a question that was routinely asked throughout camp is how is this edge group going to be able to perform without Micah,” Van Ness said last week.” I think we were all very aware that we’d have to pick up our end of the bargain until Micah returned. I’m proud of the way we’ve done that.
“I feel like from Day 1, we just attacked camp – from OTAs to camp to all the way throughout the season – and I think you’ve seen that production week after week after week. I’m proud of the way we’re trending. Just got to keep it going.”
Green Bay’s defensive tackles have contributed little statistically but are an unsung reason for the team’s overall success.
Led by Karl Brooks, who has three sacks and six tackles for losses, the defensive tackles have contributed 7.5 sacks and 12 TFLs, according to the official stats, and 43 pressures, according to PFF. Chicago’s Jeffery Simmons has six sacks and nine TFLs by himself, and Denver’s Zach Allen has 38 pressures.
The defense has been strong, though, whether it’s stopping the run or rushing the passer, and this group is a reason why. The depth has been critical with Javon Hargrave, Jonathan Ford and Warren Brinson on injured reserve.
They’ve been good but they can be better. Brooks has three sacks in the last two games. That’s a good start. Devonte Wyatt, however, has been invisible following last year’s season-ending injury.
To get him off the fifth-year option, the Packers gave Wyatt a three-year, $54.9 million contract extension through 2029. He has three sacks and four TFLs. They’ve been rewarded with nine pressures, which is tied for 76th among defensive tackles.
“His juice, his energy on the field, off the field is very contagious and is electric,” position coach Vince Oghobaase said in defending Wyatt this week. “I do know D-Wy is a very prideful guy who wants to be great. He’ll work his tail off and he’s been doing that.
“Sometimes the impact guys have interior-wise is not always going to be seen on the stat sheet and I’m aware of that and he’s aware of that. Obviously, we all want the stats – the sacks, the TFLs and all the tackles but that’s not always how the game shakes out. As long as you are impacting the game, you are doing your job.”
During training camp, it was clear that the Packers’ best top-to-bottom position group was the linebacker corps. That’s exactly how it’s played out – and it’s saved the team’s season.
With Edgerrin Cooper out for the season with a torn Achilles and Zaire Franklin missing four games with an injured shin, Isaiah McDuffie and Ty’Ron Hopper have come to the rescue. And when one of them has been banged up, Nick Niemann has provided solid snaps.
McDuffie leads the group with 56 tackles, including one sack and three for losses. Franklin has 41 tackles, including two for losses. Hopper has 26 tackles but has two interceptions and ranks sixth on the team with six pass breakups. Cooper still is tied for second on the team with three sacks and six tackles for losses.
They have tackled at a high level, played with physicality and carried out the plan, regardless of who’s in there.
“I think resiliency, obviously, is the first word that comes to mind,” linebackers coach Sam Siefkes said. “You mentioned the next man up, it’s kind of been the epitome of that I think for the majority of this season. It’s just next guy be ready to play no matter when it is, and we’ve had a lot of guys that have had to step up and I think have done a nice job playing in those roles.”
If grading on a curve because of circumstances, this would be an A. But, for the bottom line …
If there was one reason to doubt the Packers heading into training camp, it was the cornerback group’s ability to hold up without an elite pass rush. In 2025, Keisean Nixon ranked fifth in touchdowns allowed (seven) and first in penalties (12), Carrington Valentine was benched a couple times because of his horrendous tackling and Brandon Cisse was at South Carolina.
What a difference a coaching staff makes, apparently.
Nixon was challenged during training camp and responded. He’s allowed one touchdown and been guilty of three penalties. Cisse, a second-round pick, might be the best rookie corner in the league. Valentine lost the starting job to Cisse but has played well off the bench – including as a tackler.
“On gameday, he’s one of the most locked in as far as what’s happening in the game that I’ve ever been around,” secondary coach and defensive pass-game coordinator Bobby Babich said of Nixon. “He’s a football guy. He loves the game of football, which is where it all starts.”
Cisse has one interception and nine passes defensed. His seven-game streak without allowing a touchdown ended on the play in which he was injured against Minnesota. Nixon has one interception and eight passes defensed. He’s allowing just 9.0 yards per catch. In limited action, Valentine is allowing 8.0 yards per catch and looks like a new player with his physicality and tackling.
Overall, Green Bay has allowed the fifth-fewest completions of 25-plus yards. They are fourth in yards allowed per attempt and fifth in yards allowed per completion. The one knock might be that Cisse and Nixon have missed too many tackles, but the mentality has been there.
“One thing that stands out is the love they have for one another,” position coach Daniel Bullocks said. “Obviously, it’s a talented group, but the love that they have for one another, the respect they have for one another, what they demand from one another.
“The great defensive backs rooms that I’ve been a part of, there’s three things that’s in common. Guys eliminate explosive plays; they do a great job of that. And taking the ball away, No. 2, another thing they do a good job there. And also they tackle. Those guys love football and you talk about our play-style, they represent all of that.”
Everybody knew this was the team’s best unit, but maybe even they’ve surpassed expectations. Xavier McKinney has an NFL-leading six interceptions and Evan Williams has three.…

title: Week 11 Couldn't Have Gone Better for the Texans— Here's Why
full_text:
The Houston Texans had about as good of a Week 11 as you could've imagined.
And it's not just because of how their game against the Indianapolis Colts went earlier in the week.
The outcome of that matchup was a positive one, no doubt. The Texans' offense had much more life than it did last weekend against the Cleveland Browns, the defense looked much closer to the version we knew it to be in 2025, and it all resulted in a resounding 26-3 victory over a division rival they lost to earlier in the year.
That in itself was a big success for the Texans. However, things managed to get even better as Houston was sitting back at home on their mini-bye for Sunday, and saw the action go down for the rest of the league.
Long story short, about everything that needed to go the Texans’ way to begin their late-season push for the postseason––happened.
If you were to take a look back at our Week 11 Rooting Guide for the Texans, there were four games kicking off on Sunday which had a select few outcomes that would've helped Houston directly when it comes to climbing up the standings:
Shockingly enough, all of those happened!
J.J. McCarthy kept his winning ways alive and guided the Giants to an upset win over Jacksonville. Saquon Barkley led the Eagles to an upset over Pittsburgh. Jonah Coleman and the Broncos offense overwhelmed the Raiders. And a crazy Ravens-Panthers game ended with Jacoby Brissett coming up just short of a fourth-quarter comeback victory.
The Texans couldn't have drawn it up any better. Even at 4-6, they sit in a pretty solid spot within the AFC standings with two months to go in the season. And now, they head into Week 12 riding a good bit of momentum with the chance to get back-to-back wins for the very first time this year.
The Texans' playoff hopes have life, and on the field, the team might finally be catching their stride on both ends of the ball after a cathartic win over the Colts.
But, at the same time, they're also many steps away from actually climbing into a top-seven seed that they need for that postseason appearance.
At 4-6, the Texans are still two games out of a playoff spot. Winning out through their next seven games would certainly be ideal in cementing their spot within the postseason, but there's a good argument that three of Houston's next four games on the schedule might be their most important yet.
The Texans face the Ravens in Week 12, the Steelers in Week 13, then have their second game of the year against the Jaguars in Week 15. All three of those games have major implications on Houston's position in the AFC Wild Card race, and potentially even a slim chance at winning the AFC South.
Jaguars let the Texans inch closer to their lead in the AFC South 😳 pic.twitter.com/ZNBVA4lHry
The Texans need to go on a run ASAP. And a loss in one of those games would be especially impactful for where they end up in the standings after Week 18.
Thankfully, the Texans showed real signs of being able to put together some successful performances on both sides of the ball as of last week's game against the Colts.
But consistency has been an issue for Houston all season long, hence their lack of stringing together one back-to-back win on the season so far. Now comes the time to continue those types of dominant efforts moving forward––especially over the next month’s stretch of games.

title: David Montgomery's Big Game vs. Colts Is Exactly What Texans Needed
full_text:
The Houston Texans saw a lot of positives throughout their Thursday Night Football win over the Indianapolis Colts.
C.J. Stroud continued to look like a dark horse MVP candidate en route to his 77.8% completion rate and three touchdowns. The defense looked a whole lot closer to the version we saw in 2025. And now, momentum could be starting to build for a few wins to be rattled off over the next few weeks to help Houston's hopeful playoff push.
But of the standout performances we saw from this Texans roster earlier in the week, one of the more encouraging stat lines came from veteran running back David Montgomery, who finally popped for his best game since Week 1 against the Buffalo Bills .
And now, such a night should have the Texans feeling a whole lot better not just about their run game moving forward this season, but about their initial investment in Montgomery in the first place.
Heading into the night against the Colts, Montgomery had been on pace for his worst season as a pro by far.
In the five games he had played before Week 11, Montgomery was averaging just 2.7 yards per carry alongside his 27.6 rushing yards per game. He had a lowly 1.6 rushing yards before contact, and had rushed for just five total first downs. It didn't help seeing him sidelined for four games with a groin injury he suffered in Week 5.
Things weren't looking great for Montgomery's long-term stock in this Texans offense. However, the narrative finally shifted for Montgomery on Thursday night.
Montgomery was due to be the number one ball carrier in the backfield with Woody Marks sidelined with a concussion. He was up against a lackluster Colts defensive line, and he took advantage of his opportunities in a big way.
He took ahold of a season-high 26 carries for 107 rushing yards; his third 100-plus yard game since 2024. He averaged over four yards per carry for the first time this season. In the passing game, he chipped in for three receptions and 17 yards.
Montgomery was a stabilizing force in a Texans offense that took command of the Colts' defense, and was key in allowing Houston to maintain control down the stretch, and do so as effectively and efficiently as he's looked all season.
While the Texans have certainly leaned into their strengths as a team who likes to attack the air–– thanks to C.J. Stroud's impressive production this season–– establishing a reliable run game has still been a task Houston needs to hit on for this offense to reach its full potential.
We've seen over the course of 2025, and even in moments throughout this season, how the Texans' offense can suffer when their run game is non-existent.
Gaining traction on early downs becomes a challenge; the offense gets put behind the sticks for multiple third-and-longs, and creates an uphill battle for Stroud and Co. to overcome. Avoiding such situations only becomes more important the deeper Houston gets into the season, and especially so if they arrive in the postseason.
But if Montgomery can maintain the hot hand, Marks can return to the lineup as a reliable counterpart, and the offensive line holds up as it did on Thursday night, there's a real route to this Texans run game becoming a respectable piece of their scoring attack.
And if that's the case, that'd be a massive lift to their hopes of claiming a few wins in a row down the second half stretch of their season, and putting together one of the more well-rounded and potent offenses around the NFL.
Maybe Montgomery's night was simply a product of the Texans' matchup against the Colts and their underwhelming defense–– so it's important not to be too carried away about how this rushing offense could look over the next few games.
Really, only takes one game for Houston to average less than three yards per carry as a unit, and the consensus feelings about their abilities on the ground come right back down to earth with it.
Yet, if next weekend against the Baltimore Ravens winds up looking similar for Montgomery ( and hopefully Marks, as he gets out of concussion protocol ), the conversations will only be getting louder about how good this Texans run game could really be.

title: Why Texans WR Nico Collins Was Fined Nearly $15,000 by NFL
full_text:
The Houston Texans are currently sitting at home this weekend on a nice mini-bye after taking care of business in their Thursday night matchup vs. the Indianapolis Colts in a dominant 26-3 victory.
However, even while the Texans are taking some time off before continuing their hopeful run to the postseason for the second half of the regular season, that didn't stop the NFL from handing out a hefty fine to one of Houston's top stars, wide receiver Nico Collins.
According to NFL insider Tom Pelissero, Collins was fined $14,926 for unsportsmanlike contact and a "violent gesture" while celebrating a touchdown from Texans tight end Dalton Schultz.
The NFL fined Texans WR Nico Collins $14,926 for unsportsmanlike conduct (violent gesture) while celebrating Dalton Schultz’s touchdown last week in Cleveland. Collins was also flagged. pic.twitter.com/TEn8qM8NvK
The fine for Collins actually stems from the Texans' Week 10 game against the Cleveland Browns , where Schultz caught a touchdown on his only reception of the day, coming off an 11-yard catch from C.J. Stroud.
After the big play, Collins ran into the end zone to show some love to his veteran tight end, and in the process, showed off a celebration that emulated flashing a firearm––an action that the NFL seemingly didn't appreciate much.
As a result, the NFL handed over a pretty big fine for the Texans wideout. The celebration would also result in a flag thrown during the game for an unsportsmanlike conduct call.
Overall, it was a small blip on the radar for Collins in what was one of his strongest days of production for the season , as he hauled in nine of his 16 total targets for 94 yards and a touchdown against Cleveland, despite coming in a losing effort.
But it's actually not the first time that Collins has been fined a large chunk of money for a celebration. It's also not his first rodeo getting fined for a gun-related celebration either.
Less than 12 months ago, Collins had a similar moment transpire against the Colts in Week 13 of the 2025 season––when the Texans wideout hauled in a reception for a first down, to then get up and point two fingers forward while flexing his thumb as a trigger.
That play got Collins fined a whopping $14,491; just under $500 less than the amount he was fined for his actions this season in Week 10, and his second fine for a "violent gesture" in less than 12 months.
If you want to find an even more head-scratching fine sent out from the NFL to Collins, the Texans wideout was fined nearly $5,000 back in 2024 against the Tennessee Titans for throwing a ball into the stands after a touchdown score to a young fan.
Were any of those celebrations from Collins worthy of a financial slap on the wrist by the NFL? That’s certainly up for debate.
However, it's a clear message sent from the league that they're cracking down on celebrations as they have frequently done throughout the season; whether that be for something like firearms, or for simulating a drink of alcohol, as many players got fined for earlier this season.

title: Texans Week 11 Rooting Guide: Who Houston Needs to Win During Mini-Bye
full_text:
The NFL playoffs still sit over two months away from going down.
Yet, for the Houston Texans, it might not be too early to look ahead at how their roadmap to making a late run to a postseason appearance might unravel . And that includes breaking down who around the AFC might need to falter for the Texans to make a climb up the standings themselves.
The Texans already took care of business earlier this week against the Indianapolis Colts to rise to 4-6. Now, they're able to sit back at home on a mini-bye, watch the rest of the league face off on Sunday for Week 11, and have some rooting interests that might help their case of getting in the mix for those top seven seeds in the AFC.
With that in mind, let's take a look at which teams the Texans should be hoping to win and lose over the course of Week 11 that could help their own chances moving forward in the weeks ahead:
While the Texans could be too far out of reach to sniff the AFC South title for a second straight season, a loss from the Jacksonville Jaguars this weekend against the New York Giants certainly wouldn't hurt their chances of making a late run for it.
With a win from the Jaguars, the Texans will sit four games back from the Jaguars of that division title. Having seven weeks to go on the schedule after this weekend, that doesn't leave much room for Houston to catch up.
However, the Texans do have the current head-to-head tiebreaker over the Jaguars thanks to their Week 6 win in London, and these two teams face off once again in Week 15. So there is a sliver of hope for Houston, but it likely requires a loss from Jacksonville this weekend to have any serious chance of coming to fruition.
The Philadelphia Eagles are suffering from one of their worst seasons in recent memory as they head into this weekend's matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers with a lowly 2-7 record. So seeing an upset win from Philly become a reality might just be wishful thinking from the Texans and fans alike.
However, if the Eagles were to do just that, it's a massive push in the right direction for Houston's playoff chances. The Steelers are one of the Texans' premier threats competing for one of the AFC's three Wild Card spots, and a loss from them in Week 11 would leave Houston just two games apart.
Add in the fact that the Texans play the Steelers in a pivotal Sunday night matchup in Week 13. A loss this week could put Houston much closer to being within reach of catching them in the standings, potentially even allowing the Texans to take the lead over Pittsburgh if they stumble over the next two weeks.
A win from the Denver Broncos here against the Las Vegas Raiders would give the Texans some solid cushioning when it comes to separating themselves from the pack of those now below them in the AFC standings.
Right now, the Raiders have the same 4-6 record as the Texans, but Houston holds a tie-breaker over them thanks to their 3-1 division record. Las Vegas only has a 1-1 record against AFC West opponents.
But with a loss against the Broncos? The Raiders would not only sit a half game back from the Texans in the AFC standings, yet they'd also lose even more ground in that battle for a divisional tiebreaker. It's minor, but any edge Houston can get in the standings matters with the record they currently have.
Here's a very similar case to cheer against the Baltimore Ravens. The Texans are currently tied with Baltimore at a 4-6 record, yet also hold the current tiebreaker thanks to their respective divisional records.
A loss to the Carolina Panthers would drop the Ravens to 4-7, and a half-game back from the Texans. That's a great start for Houston to work with. However, what's even more impactful for the Texans' playoff chances is for them to claim a win over the Ravens in their upcoming Week 12 matchup.
A loss from Baltimore this weekend to the Panthers, on top of another defeat to Houston next week, takes the Ravens to eight losses, while also helping the Texans take an even bigger lead over them in the standings.
