title: 3 Offseason Decisions That Have Already Paid Off  for Jaguars: From Travis Hunter to the Backfield
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars are entering Week 11 with a 7-2 record and high hopes in the AFC South and beyond. A big reason they have even gotten to this point, though, is due to how they have approached the last few offseasons.
The 2025 offseason was of course highlighted by the hirings of Liam Coen, James Gladstone, and Tony Boselli, and the massive trade up for Travis Hunter. The 2026 offseason was a bit quieter, but that doesn't mean it didn't feature several critical decisions that have shaped the Jaguars into the team they are now.
So, which offseason decisions did the Jaguars make that have helped lead them toward a potential top playoff spot in the AFC? We break it down below.
It sure feels like Travis Hunter is already one of the best cornerbacks in football. By the way, he just played his 16th career NFL game and has started just nine games as a primary cornerback in his career. Hunter's ability to become one of the NFL's most exciting players at the position has been defined the most by his ball skills and ability to generate explosive plays for the defense, but his down-to-down play has been excellent as well.
Travis Hunter is a burgeoning STAR pic.twitter.com/Tk5KfHpd6l
There was no other time where this was as apparent as in Week 6 against the Houston Texans, with Hunter catching a fourth-quarter touchdown on offense while also recording a red-zone interception of C.J. Stroud on the next drive. If things had gone differently with a bounce here or there, Hunter would have been the story of the week after saving the Jaguars nearly singlehandedly.
Then there were plays like the one he made against the Tennessee Titans last week. After the Jaguars' offense threw an interception, Hunter got it right back for the Jaguars with an elite feat of athletic ability and pure coverage instincts. It was perhaps the best play of his stellar sophomore season thus far, and a staggering reflection of how far he has already come.
Travis Hunter dives for the interception! 🔥 JAXvsTEN on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/RKvGzhsi9H
Hunter's path toward becoming a weapon at the cornerback position, though, started with an offseason decision. The Jaguars said from the jump at the end of the 2025 season that Hunter's direction would be defense, with offense still a part of the equation. There is little doubt that Hunter would not also star at receiver, and he has made big plays there. But the Jaguars accurately determined that they needed Hunter more so at cornerback, and he has proven them right every step of the way.
The Jaguars had a few key free agents leave this offseason , with All-Pro linebacker Devin Lloyd leaving for the Carolina Panthers and former first-round running back Travis Etienne joining the New Orleans Saints. Lloyd has had a strong season for the Panthers, though the Jaguars can certainly feel good about the decision to unleash Ventrell Miller considering he has now also had a career season. The decision to let Etienne leave was panned at the time though, with questions about both second-year running back Bhayshul Tuten and new free agent addition Chris Rodriguez Jr.
Jacksonville's rushing efficiency has tailed off in recent weeks, and the team has generally been more productive using the threat of the run to set up the pass. But that doesn't mean the Jaguars' decision to not spend big money on the running back position hasn't paid off after the Jaguars have used the money to help keep other key pieces like Travon Walker, Montaric Brown, and potentially Parker Washington and Jessie Bates III and others moving forward.
The Jaguars have also seen Bhayshul Tuten establish himself as one of the NFL's best running backs depsite the running game not being top-tier. Tuten has been much more efficient on an individual basis this year than what the Jaguars got out of the position a year ago, and he is among the NFL's leaders in yards after contact and missed tackles forced.
It is not as if there seemed to be any actual consideration to trading Walker Little for the Jaguars. The veteran offensive lineman was extended at the end of the 2024 season in the final big act of the Trent Baalke era, a move that people questioned at the time due the timeline of the Jaguars' regime. Little started the Coen era as the team's left tackle last year before injuries forced him out of the lineup and Cole Van Lanen into the left tackle spot. Van Lanen was then given a big extension before a Week 18 injury, with the Jaguars securing him after a hot run at the blind side spot to end the season.
While the Jaguars swapped Van Lanen and right tackle Anton Harrison at the tackle spots to start the season, Little entered the year as an experienced and highly-paid backup. For a team in need of cap space, it made sense at the time to wonder if the Jaguars would shop Little to a team needing a starting left tackle. Instead, the Jaguars kept Little through the offseason and training camp, and the move has paid off in a big, big way.
Little stepped back into the starting lineup at left tackle in Week 6 against the Houston Texans after a season-ending knee injury to Harrison the week prior. Little has been downright elite at left tackle since then, allowing just two pressures at the tackle spot since Week 6 -- tied with Van Lanen, Garrett Bolles, and Amarius Mims as the third-fewest pressures allowed in the last month. Only Penei Sewell and Darnell Wright have allowed fewer pressures.
Little has become a key part of the Jaguars' offensive success since becoming a starter, and he has helped made sure the Jaguars' offense didn't take any step backs after the loss of Harrison. The Jaguars' decision to keep Little on the roster despite conventional wisdom suggesting they do otherwise has perhaps saved their offensive line in the midst of injuries.

title: Chiefs' Week 11 Winners and Losers in Win Over the Cardinals
full_text:
Say what you will about beating the Jets, Falcons, and Cardinals in a row, three teams with a combined 9-23 record, but good teams beat up on bad ones. According to research from our KCSN colleague Tucker Franklin, the Chiefs have not won three straight games by three touchdowns or more since 1997. No matter how you slice it, that is an impressive stretch of football, and 8-2 is nothing to scoff at in the NFL.
The game was effectively settled in the first 15 minutes: Kansas City ran 27 plays for 152 yards, while Arizona managed three plays for three yards, putting Kansas City up 14-0. The most notable performances may shape the end-of-year award conversations, along with a couple of roster questions that could get louder as the schedule gets harder, mainly along the offensive line.
Here are the biggest winners and losers from Week 11.
Quarterback Patrick Mahomes is the ultimate winner here, and not only because of his numbers. He was protected better than in recent weeks, and his weapons played as well as they have all season. He was pressured only seven times, and he wasn't as reliant on running backs and tight ends as he had been before Week 10.
He attempted 31 passes in the first half alone, completing about two-thirds of them for 233 yards and two touchdowns. He then watched a Justin Fields and Jaydn Ott-led offense from the sideline after Xavier Worthy scored on the first play of the fourth quarter.
He finished 27-for-39 for 324 yards, three touchdowns, and no interceptions, with a 7.5 average depth of target. The latter is his third-highest mark of the season, all while posting his quickest time to throw, at 2.33 seconds.
Rashee Rice caught all six of his first-half targets for 53 yards and made several third-down grabs, including one where he took a big hit and held on. Newcomer Josh Downs had four catches for 59 yards, including a 26-yard gain, and Cyrus Allen added 41 yards on two catches. Worthy bounced back with 38 yards and a score. Travis Kelce caught two touchdowns and also led the team with 74 yards.
Over his last four games, Mahomes has thrown 13 touchdowns, thrown no interceptions, and averaged more than 300 yards per game, further establishing his name in the MVP conversation. His two head-to-head matchups with MVP candidates Josh Allen and Joe Burrow, in two of the next three weeks, will be the ultimate barometer.
Not enough can be said about George Karlaftis' season, and Chiefs Kingdom may even be underrating it a bit. Box scores and analytics show he has been one of the best pass rushers in the NFL.
He is tied for seventh in the NFL in sacks, leads the league in batted passes, and is third among defensive ends in total pressures. All eight of his sacks have come since the bye week, meaning eight in the last six games, with seven contests left.
Sunday was his best day yet, with 2.5 sacks, a season high. He shared a half-sack with Chris Jones, then added a sack and a strip-sack in the second half, plus a quarterback hit. His six pressures led the team according to PFF, and only Felix Anudike-Uzomah had more than one.
He has at least one sack in each of his last four games, with multiple sacks in two of them, and he has the most sacks in the NFL since Week 8, with seven. Karlaftis is also 2.5 sacks shy of the 10.5 he posted in 2023.
The Defensive Player of the Year award is narrative-based, like the MVP, so if he performs the same against high-flying offenses like the Bills, Rams, Bengals, and 49ers, there is a non-zero percent chance that he can enter DPOY conversations.
The awards theme continues with rookie running back Emmett Johnson , who has entered the Offensive Rookie of the Year discussion, at least in Chiefs circles. That may have something to do with how many first-year offensive players are underperforming, but it does not mean his production in limited opportunities is unwarranted.
Receivers KC Concepcion, Carnell Tate, and Denzel Boston, along with running back Jonah Coleman, are all having solid seasons, but after another strong day filling in for Kenneth Walker, Johnson is on pace for more than 1,000 yards from scrimmage and eight touchdowns. That is remarkable considering that his running mate already has 1,044 yards from scrimmage and 11 touchdowns.
Kenneth Walker missed his second straight game with a groin injury, and Johnson carried the ball 23 times for 105 yards and caught four passes for 38 yards. He scored for the fourth straight game and forced seven missed tackles.
It is not too often you take an Offensive Player of the Year Candidate out of the offense and said offense doesn’t skip a beat, but that is exactly what has happened. We’ll see if Walker is good enough for Buffalo, but Johnson is worthy of another start if not.
How can a left tackle who has started all 10 games and a right tackle who has missed the past two weeks be losers in a 34-7 win? It is because of what is happening around them and what they are not doing.
Kahlil Benson's work this season has been both impressive and admirable. An undrafted rookie filling in for Josh Simmons without derailing the offense is an accomplishment in itself. That said, he did allow a team-high four pressures, and nobody else on the line allowed more than one. As much as he has stabilized the offensive line this season, he ranks second-to-last in the NFL in pressures given up, with 34, according to PFF.
Who knows how safe Benson’s starting spot really is, but Jaylon Moore may be in the same boat. He wasn't exactly a world-beater before his ankle injury, and the Chiefs recently signed Fred Johnson , a 6-foot-7, 326-pound tackle from the Eagles. Johnson, with 833 career snaps at left tackle and 893 at right tackle, could compete with both Benson and Moore.
Not only that, but swing tackle Josh Ezeudu is also making a case. Over parts of the last three games, including two starts, he has allowed just three total pressures. These are good problems for a team to have, but neither tackle has ideal job security heading into the part of the season that really counts.
I am lumping these two together because they are in the same situation on opposite sides of the ball. Royals is getting snaps but not targets, and Canady is only getting opportunities in a pinch. Canady is a rookie, and Royals may as well be one given his 2025 season.
Neither had a horrible game, but both did little with their chances compared to their counterparts. Royals was third among receivers in snaps again but had no catches on one target. Downs and Allen played fewer snaps and combined for nine targets, six catches, and 100 yards. That doesn't help the Royals' long-term outlook.
Canady played just five snaps in a decided game, and those five snaps really could not have gone much worse. He was targeted three times and allowed two catches for 35 yards, all against Harrison Wallace III. The Ole Miss rookie came in with one catch for nine yards. Wallace led Arizona with four catches for 57 yards, and Canady played a big role.

title: Another Great Emmett Johnson Start May Have Been Thanks to His Chiefs Teammates
full_text:
Most of the time, being down one of the very best running backs in the sport borders on disaster for an NFL offense. For the second weekend in a row, though, that didn't apply to the Kansas City Chiefs even a bit.
As prized free agent signing Kenneth Walker III continued to deal with a groin injury , the club sat him once again. Not only was that a wise call given the magnitude of the upcoming schedule, but it also signaled belief that rookie Emmett Johnson could still get the job done in relief.
Some 34 points and 435 total net yards later, it's clear that Kansas City made the right call. Johnson turned in his second tremendous start in a row and didn't allow the offense to experience any dip in performance, asserting himself as an Offensive Rookie of the Year candidate in the process.
After Week 10's win over the Atlanta Falcons, the message from the Chiefs was that Johnson simply had his meticulous preparation meet the right opportunity . On Sunday versus the Atlanta Falcons, the fifth-round pick said his levels of comfort and output were influenced by his teammates.
“Very comfortable,” Johnson said. “I feel like just the guys trusting me up front, Pat (Mahomes) and all those guys having trust in me, I think it just makes my job a lot easier to go out there and be myself.”
“Yeah that’s cool, but I just wanna win a Super Bowl.” Emmett Johnson when asked how he feels about being mentioned in Rookie of the Year talks. pic.twitter.com/ISfhQvPIuh
He also tips his cap to Walker, who's seen and done everything ranging from being in a committee of sorts to winning Super Bowl MVP, for bringing out the best of him and being a perfect on-field role model.
“He’s done a lot, man,” Johnson said. “I think just how we practice [and] how we push each other every single day, we get the most out of each other. I think that’s the biggest thing about me and Kenneth — we’re both hungry guys. We go out there and work our butts off. We both want to help the team to win, so him just being there in practice really pushes me to be the best version of myself when I’m on the field.”
Johnson led the way right out of the gate for the Chiefs in Week 11 and never truly looked back. The Nebraska product toted the ball 23 times for 105 yards on the ground and also hauled in four passes for 38 yards. In all, he's the first player this century ( and the first since 1994 Marshall Faulk ) to log at least 100 rushing yards and 30 receiving yards in each of his first two professional starts.
Of course, it wouldn't have been a Johnson game without some elusiveness and wiggle showcased on the gridiron. Per NFL Pro , the first-year man forced eight missed tackles by Arizona defenders, further supporting his league-leading 41.1% clip on the season. Johnson's blend of contact balance, short-area burst, leverage, durability and conditioning has him thriving.
A year or two ago, Kansas City would've dreamed for one player that was even 80% of Walker or Johnson's caliber. Now, Mahomes and company are benefitting from the luxury of perhaps football's best one-two punch at the halfback spot.
The scariest thing of all? There's likely still a final evolution coming in which the Chiefs can find the most optimal way to use both players once Walker's back.

title: Despite Being 'All Business,' George Karlaftis Was an All-Star for Chiefs in Week 11
full_text:
Earlier in the 2026-27 campaign, much was made of the Kansas City Chiefs' lack of sack production. In recent weeks, Steve Spagnuolo's defensive line capitalized on some fortunate matchups and now looks like a unit possessed.
Leading the way this time, however, isn't All-Pro tackle Chris Jones. It's fifth-year man George Karlaftis, who contributed yet another positive performance in Week 11's 34-7 bludgeoning of the Arizona Cardinals.
With the victory, Kansas City extended its streak of scoring at least 34 points and surrendering fewer than 14 to three games. Only the 2007 New England Patriots and 1942 Chicago Bears had longer stretches, reaching four.
The veteran defensive end is playing a significant role in that greatness, which head coach Andy Reid made sure to point out. Speaking to the media on Sunday afternoon, he emphasized that Karlaftis is making a name for himself despite usually flying under the radar.
"Listen, George is all business," Reid said. "Whether it's practice, walkthrough, game, 100 miles an hour. Smart, tough, all those things. He's relentless. If you're going to play him, play against him, he's not the flashiest guy, but he's going to keep bringing on you. He's developed some moves and some skill there that he's worked hard at."
The proof is in the numbers for Karlaftis. After notching a sack in Week 6's win over the Los Angeles Chargers, he went quiet against the Seattle Seahawks but has been on an absolute tear ever since. He's recorded at least one sack in each of his last four outings, securing multiple twice.
Sunday marked a season-high for the former first-round pick (2.5), seeing him get to 40-year-old Cardinals quarterback Josh Johnson on several occasions. One of them was a strip-sack, and another pressure and hit combo later on also reminded Arizona that he was in the vicinity.
Pro Football Focus ' preliminary tracking credited him with a team-leading five pressures. No one else had more than one (as of the publishing of this story).
If there's one thing Kansas City has made clear this season, it's that it doesn't regard sacks as the end-all, be-all. Jones himself explained such a few weeks ago before the club's hot streak. Karlaftis seems to echo that sentiment, even as his total gets to eight on the year and inches closer and closer to a new personal best.
Most sacks since Week 8: 1. George Karlaftis - 7.0 2. Jeffery Simmons - 5.0* 2. Quinnen Williams - 5.0 *Joined Bears in Week 8 (had bye in Week 10)
The process and results are intersecting for one of the Chiefs' top breakout players. Then again, the normally quiet Karlaftis spoke extensively about why his unwavering belief is how that's now the case.
"I mean, it's always just keep going," Karlaftis said. "Never get discouraged when you're not getting home. There have been times when you go multiple games, months. My rookie year, I went all the way to Thanksgiving without getting a sack. Always keep swinging. I'm always throwing my fastball [and] always trying to get after the quarterback and affect the quarterback, really, any way we can.
"When the defensive line's playing all together, front and back end with the DBs and linebackers [and] everybody's playing together, good things happen. It's really a team effort. Sacks might be an individual statistic, but it takes everybody to get them. The one we had today, R Mason (Thomas) did a great job getting the win to the quarterback, so it's not just an individual stat in my opinion."

title: 10 Instant Observations From Chiefs' Huge Victory Against Cardinals
full_text:
Fresh off consecutive 35-point showings against the New York Jets and Atlanta Falcons, the Kansas City Chiefs hosted another struggling franchise in Week 11 and nearly matched that output.
They certainly made the Arizona Cardinals look like a team in disarray, as both sides of the ball starred in a blowout victory.
Thanks to Kansas City's offensive stars doing their part and Steve Spagnuolo's defense taking advantage of a shorthanded Arizona attack, the outcome of Sunday's game was never truly in doubt. By the time the dust settled, head coach Andy Reid's squad emerged with a 34-7 outcome in front of the home crowd.
With the triumph, the Chiefs improve their record to 8-2 on the year. Let's jump into 10 instant observations and takeaways from Week 11.
In last week's 10 instant observations story, we pointed out how the Chiefs made an effort to get rookie halfback Emmett Johnson involved early and often. With starter Kenneth Walker III out due to a groin injury, the club didn't shy away from maximizing the skill set of its fifth-round pick and leaning into giving him a hefty workload. That trend was maintained in Week 11's contest.
Johnson touched the ball seven times on the opening drive of this one, mustering 36 yards on the ground and eight through the air as a receiver. He broke off a 15-yard scamper to kick things off, followed by a screen pass for eight and a seven-yard rush later. The Nebraska product also saved what would've been a loss of four and turned it into no gain, which assisted in sustaining an eventual touchdown series.
Overall, it's been a more-than-quality season for one Travis Kelce thus far. The future Hall of Fame tight end is more efficient on a per-catch basis than he's been in quite some time (or, in some regards, ever ). Last weekend's win over the Falcons did see him reaggravate a nagging ankle/calf injury and play a season-low 20 snaps, though.
Kelce made up for lost time on Sunday, hauling in a touchdown from quarterback Patrick Mahomes to give him three for the campaign and 109 for his career. The latter mark includes the postseason, breaking a tie with former New England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers great Rob Gronkowski.
The 37-year-old is now in sole possession of third place for scores at his position. Ahead of him are former only Chiefs great Tony Gonzalez and longtime San Diego/Los Angeles Chargers standout Antonio Gates.
"Killa Trav" added a second touchdown right after the two-minute warning, marking his 11th game with at least two touchdowns and his first since 2022. It's safe to say he turned back the clock for Week 11.
One of the greats. AZvsKC on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Jj2y8kT2ia
Since returning from a Week 4 hamstring injury , the Chiefs have quietly gotten wideout Rashee Rice the ball plenty on offense. In three games this month prior to Sunday, he had respective target totals of eight, seven and six while averaging 61.3 yards in that span. The acquisition of fellow receiver Josh Downs at the NFL trade deadline left many — including myself — wondering if Rice's share would change, yet Kansas City made him a focal point early versus Arizona.
Rice went six-for-six on targets in the opening half on Sunday, racking up 53 yards. He made multiple key third-down snags, including one where he took a massive hit from defensive back Kei'Trel Clark but managed to hang on. With the former Day 2 NFL Draft pick rounding back into form a bit and multiple others clicking, this was an inspiring performance.
After failing to throw a touchdown but tossing an interception in back-to-back games against the Los Angeles Chargers and Seattle Seahawks, Mahomes couldn't have responded in much better fashion from a statistical standpoint. He ripped off 10 touchdowns with no picks in the ensuing three outings, centering himself in the MVP conversation in the process.
No. 15 continued to ride the hot streak on Sunday, particularly in the first two quarters.
Patrick Mahomes last 6 quarters 43-66 581 Pass Yards 7 Pass TD 128.4 Pass Rating LOCKED IN pic.twitter.com/PyRHZgiOPb
Mahomes threw the ball a whopping 31 times before the halftime break, completing 67.7% of those attempts for 233 yards and a pair of touchdowns. According to RBSDM , he produced 0.44 EPA/play with a +7.2% completion percentage over expected. Not only that, but his 7.5-yard average depth of target signaled him looking more like a multi-level threat than the checkdown artist many proclaim him to be.
Kansas City took a big-time gamble on its talent identification and development when it parted ways with cornerbacks Trent McDuffie (trade) and Jaylen Watson (free agency) during the offseason. That signaled a firm belief in the ability of rookie Mansoor Delane and second-year man Nohl Williams, which has paid off for the most part to begin the 2026-27 season.
Williams has not only been the best defensive back on the team, but there's a case to be made that he's served as a top cornerback in the sport through 11 weeks of play. His blend of length, physicality, timing and instincts is hard to beat.
It also helps that he can make plays like this when needed:
"Perfect form tackle" @NohlWilliams 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/9nlkJGOCSc
Williams did have a rare coverage lapse in the first half on Sunday, but his excellent coverage on a deep pass to wideout Simi Fehoko showcased his vertical skill. Later on, he contributed to a fourth-down stop on the same player to force a turnover on downs. There's no denying at this point that the former third-round selection is one of the better value contracts in the NFL.
Down the stretch of last season, former first-round defensive end George Karlaftis nursed a thumb injury that sapped some of his effectiveness. It appears to have been a bigger deal than he let on, as he's been amazing relative to expectations this season as a fully healthy player. That was already the case before Week 11, but the stats are lining up with the tape more now.
Karlaftis had a half-sack in the second quarter, taking down journeyman quarterback Josh Johnson along with defensive tackle Chris Jones. He then recorded a sack and strip-sack on Johnson in the second half and added a quarterback hit on a third-and-7 later on for good measure. In what's been a career campaign for Karlaftis, the 25-year-old added another feather to his cap this weekend.
In his Kansas City debut, Downs went for four receptions on five targets and had a touchdown on a beautiful back-shoulder throw from Mahomes. He didn't absorb too much in terms of workload, but he made the most of his limited snaps and was more effective than ever in multiple regards.
Sunday saw Downs turn in another four-catch and five-target contest, this time racking up 59 yards. Whether it was breaking off 26 yards on a slick fake run-pass option or picking up intermediate chunks of 13 and 16, the soon-to-be free agent flashed what he can be once he completely masters the offense.
It doesn't get much better than this level of start to your tenure with a new team.
If you're going to be hard on a player when they're struggling, you've got to keep the same energy and acknowledge when they turn in a good performance. This is one of those instances, as kicker Harrison Butker did as well as anyone could've asked in Week 11.
The veteran was perfect on his extra point attempts and also drilled field goals of 44 and 40 yards in the first half. While the kickoff coverage unit struggled, Butker assisted by taking down cornerback Max Melton in the opening frame.
As former Baltimore Ravens star Justin Tucker remains on the practice squad , Butker made major progress on Sunday by giving the team absolutely zero extra reason to make a change.
Whenever you can bench your starting quarterback early in the fourth quarter and have it be a good thing, it means your team took care of business in a major way. That was the case for Kansas City against Arizona, as Mahomes' services weren't needed in the last stages of…

title: Chiefs vs. Cardinals: NFL Week 11 Preview, Score Predictions
full_text:
In consecutive weeks, the Kansas City Chiefs have flexed their muscles and dominated an opponent that's operating on a different level than them. Will that trend continue in Week 11?
Visiting head coach Andy Reid's crew are Mike LaFleur and the Arizona Cardinals, who managed to capture two wins in three games earlier this campaign but have since dropped back-to-back outings. Down to their fourth quarterback of the year, their work is cut out for them against a surging Kansas City squad.
With kickoff on the horizon, which side will come out on top today? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 11 of the regular season.
Joshua Brisco: In each of the last two weeks, I’ve been able to genuinely argue that the Jets and Falcons were better (or at least more dangerous) than their meager records would indicate. The 3-7 Cardinals are probably worse than their record, especially while they’re preparing to be quarterbacked by a new-in-town 40-year-old super-journeyman. There are no excuses for the Chiefs to stumble in this game.
The Chiefs have put up 35 points in each of their last two wins while holding the Jets and Falcons to 12 and 13 points, respectively. With the Buffalo Bills on the horizon, I expect a similarly stout defensive performance, but I wouldn’t be surprised if the Chiefs are content to park the bus offensively if they hold a second-half lead over Arizona.
Jordan Foote: Given their recent shellackings of the New York Jets and Atlanta Falcons, it's hard not to think the Chiefs will emerge with a comfortable Week 11 victory over the Cardinals here. Arizona is simply too devoid of talent on either side of the ball, leaving only a bizarre outcome that borders on a miracle being the club's main path to a win.
Kansas City's banged-up roster is still miles ahead of Arizona's, with the duo of Patrick Mahomes and Emmett Johnson alone being enough to move the chains. On the other side of the ball, Josh Johnson is an experienced vet, but Steve Spagnuolo may have something in store for him.
Give me the Chiefs to roll to 8-2 on the year as the toughest part of their schedule approaches.
Joshua Schulman: There’s very little meaningful analysis to provide against an opponent of this caliber. The Cardinals are down several key starters and have been one of the NFL's worst teams over the past handful of weeks.
With 40-year-old journeyman Josh Johnson set to fill in for the injured Carson Beck, I’m expecting the Chiefs to steamroll Arizona. Look for Emmett Johnson to have another big game as Kenneth Walker misses his second consecutive game .
Tyler Brown: For the third straight week, I think the Chiefs win by three touchdowns. Emmett Johnson could be in line for another career day, and the only thing that may hold him back is a big lead that gets Jadyn Ott into the game. Arizona is ranked 28th in rushing defense.
With the offensive line being tinkered with , I expect Patrick Mahomes to experiment with his receiving corps as well. It will be interesting to see whether Josh Downs and Cyrus Allen get a large uptick in snaps, but I am not sure it matters. Any receiver on the depth chart could have a big day against this defense.
The Cardinals' offense is as limited as it gets. Trey McBride is their only real weapon, with a wide receiver group where not a single one has topped 100 yards total on the season. Running back Tyler Allgeier is a competent runner but doesn't threaten a defense.
Lastly, Josh Johnson, a 19-year veteran journeyman, is under center for a team already on its fourth quarterback. Steve Spagnuolo's key will be limiting McBride, and with the Chiefs' cornerbacks holding down the outside, they should be able to do that.

title: Chiefs Confidence Meter: How I Feel About the Team Against Cardinals in Week 11
full_text:
Thus far in the 2026-27 campaign, the Kansas City Chiefs have taken care of business each time they've squared off against an inferior opponent. The consensus agrees that Week 11's showdown with the Arizona Cardinals classifies as another one of those spots.
Coming to town is Arizona, which has lost back-to-back contests to fall to 3-7 in the first year of the Mike LaFleur era. With the club's quarterback situation changing multiple times (more on that in a bit) and rookie running back Jeremiyah Love being banged up all campaign, the visitors haven't helped their struggling defense nearly enough.
Still, even a squad led by a rookie head coach figures to fight hard this weekend versus a Kansas City crew that's missing multiple key starters . Can the Chiefs overcome that and rise to 8-2, or will the Cardinals play spoiler and have it prove to be a trap game?
Let's break down how both sides match up and put a bow on this Week 11 preview with a confidence meter rating on a scale ranging from 1-10.
The Kansas City offense had a return to form a week ago when quarterback Patrick Mahomes and company exploded for 35 points against the Atlanta Falcons. In that contest, Mahomes threw for a whopping 348 yards, completing deep passes to everyone ranging from Rashee Rice to Cyrus Allen and Andrew Armstrong in the process.
A key takeaway from that showing was the performance of rookie running back Emmett Johnson, too. The fifth-round pick ran all over Atlanta to the tune of 101 yards, but it was his receiving output that once again stole the show. Johnson converted on six of his seven targets, adding 70 yards and two scores in the process.
The Cardinals' defense has struggled immensely and enters the weekend sitting dead last in points per drive (2.7) and 28th in yards per possession (32.6) given up. Much of that is due to a passing defense that, according to RBSDM , is 32nd by a mile in dropback EPA per play (0.273) and allows a 48.1% passing success rate (25th).
Arizona is lacking talent on that side of the ball, as safety Budda Baker and defensive end Josh Sweat are about the only two players most football fans would commonly agree they know right off the bat. Coordinator Nick Rallis' unit is routinely behind the eight-ball by being 24th in early down EPA/play (0.039) and 29th in total pressure rate (33.6%).
This is a defense that lives in base 57.3% of the time, the second-highest clip in the league. Heavy boxes are the name of the game for Arizona, so don't be surprised to see Johnson get stuffed a few times. If that happens, however, look out for Kansas City's play-action and screen games to get him involved as a receiving option.
A revelation of playing some bad teams lately is the Chiefs' defense looking much more formidable. Steve Spagnuolo's collective of players has been nothing short of brilliant in recent weeks. While the Cardinals deserve respect, it's difficult to not see that trend continuing for at least another Sunday.
The Chiefs have held FIVE of their first nine opponents to 13 points or fewer this season 💪 No other Chiefs team since 2002 has done that 👀 pic.twitter.com/VdNqJJZct9
In the last four weeks, the Chiefs' defense is sixth against the run (-0.136 EPA/play) and seventh in passing success rate given up (39.3%). In the same window, opposing quarterbacks have football's fourth-lowest completion rate over expected (-6.2%) when throwing against Kansas City.
Non-Love rushers for Arizona aren't exactly anything to write home about. Veteran Tyler Allgeier is producing an ugly 32.98% success rate, via SumerSports , that resides 44th out of 51 halfbacks with at least 50 attempts. Backup Bam Knight is averaging -0.14 EPA/rush and carries a virtually nonexistent 3.31% target share out of the backfield.
A one-dimensional offense down to its fourth quarterback on the year isn't a good thing.
Speaking of which, it'll be 40-year-old Josh Johnson set to get the nod for the Cardinals under center after rookie Carson Beck started dealing with back spasms. Johnson, a fifth-round pick way back in 2008, has attempted 57 passes in the last two regular seasons but has only completed 63.2% of them for 389 yards, a touchdown and two interceptions.
Fifty-nine signal-callers were on the field for 50 or more plays a season ago, with Johnson ranking sixth in EPA/dropback at 0.239. Pretty much the only path the Arizona offense has to yielding exquisite results is him catching lightning in a bottle, though, which just doesn't seem likely at all.
Special teams coordinator Michael Ghobrial is in his first year with the organization in this role after previously fulfilling the same duties for the New York Giants in 2024 and 2025. His units have produced nice numbers in the past, although that hasn't really carried over to Arizona yet.
The Cardinals are 27th in average starting field position on offense and 26th on defense. Placekicker Chad Ryland, in fairness, has connected on all but two of his 24 field goal tries and all but one of his extra points. That's one thing the team can hang its hat on.
Punter Blake Gillikin's 39.2 net yards per punt leave plenty to be desired, on the other hand, putting him 31st out of 33 qualified players. He was the worst punter in the sport less than a month ago:
Been MIA, but here you go: punter rankings after week 7! pic.twitter.com/B74tzA6O9R
The main saving graces for the Cardinals are that the Chiefs rank 25th in average starting field position allowed in the last four weeks and also have serious kicking woes with Harrison Butker still in the lineup. If this is a close game, special teams could make a significant difference.
If Kansas City is a serious team, it can't afford to drop Week 11's game. A gauntlet of clashes begins after that, including tilts against the Buffalo Bills, Los Angeles Rams, Cincinnati Bengals and others. It truly is an "any given Sunday" league, which is why our score isn't quite a 10, but the Chiefs are better than the Cardinals in just about every regard.
For Arizona, the Love experiment hasn't worked out to this point. His backups are providing minimal reason to be excited about the direction of the rushing attack. While being forced to change his planning efforts during the week isn't ideal, Spagnuolo figures to be ready for Johnson after previously preparing for Beck.
Needing to keep stacking wins in a loaded AFC West and AFC, head coach Andy Reid's team could use one last tune-up before the real stretch of the campaign kicks off. Playing in front of the home crowd with a Thanksgiving contest on the horizon is a perfect time to escape with a win — no matter how convincing — and shift focus to getting healthy ahead of a short week.
Weirder things have happened, but this writer would be absolutely floored if KC lost.

title: Chiefs vs. Cardinals Matchups: An Experiment Up Front and a Singular Problem for KC’s Defense
full_text:
After losing to the Denver Broncos in Week 8, the Chiefs were slated for three games everyone had circled since the schedule came out in May. They faced the New York Jets, then the Atlanta Falcons, and now the Arizona Cardinals, before meeting their arch-rival Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving evening.
The potential ease of that stretch has lived up to its billing, with those three opponents holding a combined record of 8-22. After the Denver loss, they were labeled as three must-win games, given how tight the divisional race had become.
The Chiefs won the first two by at least three touchdowns, and in Week 11 they face perhaps the easiest challenge of the bunch. The Cardinals are in disarray and already down to their fourth quarterback of the season . Kansas City expected Arizona to start rookie Carson Beck, who led Miami to a national championship last season after a successful collegiate career at Georgia, until back spasms ruled him out earlier this week. Instead, 19-year veteran journeyman Josh Johnson will take the reins at Arrowhead.
That makes for an extremely favorable matchup as the Chiefs try to move to 8-2. Arizona has a guy or two that Kansas City needs to key in on, so here are the two biggest matchups on each side of the ball.
Offense: Chiefs pass protection vs. Cardinals pass rush
Let's be clear: the Cardinals' pass rush is not good, so this matchup is more about Kansas City than Arizona. The Chiefs allowed single-digit pressures in Weeks 2 through 6 but have not done so since.
Patrick Mahomes has been elite at avoiding sacks. Among qualified quarterbacks, his pressure-to-sack ratio of 9.7 percent tops the league, according to PFF. That is a Mahomes stat, not one that speaks glowingly of the offensive line.
Who starts up front is a giant question mark this week. Right guard Trey Smith and right tackle Jaylon Moore have been ruled out, Mike Caliendo has struggled mightily filling in, and the Chiefs signed veteran lineman Fred Johnson this week, who has plenty of starts under his belt. Andy Reid said, "They're all going to have a shot to get in there and go," so Sunday may be a bit of an experiment.
The Chiefs will more than likely win this game regardless of their offensive line play, but you would love to see them keep Mahomes clean four days before one of the biggest games of the season. As for who they are facing, defensive end Josh Sweat and defensive tackle Walter Nolen are the two above-average talents.
Eight-time pro bowler and four-time All-Pro safety Budda Baker actually leads Arizona in sacks, with 3.5. Allowing him to affect the game as little as possible, whether it be throwing away from him or linemen and running backs picking up his blitzes, will be key to taking away their opponents' best player.
That said, four of the Cardinals' five leading pressure-getters are interior defensive linemen, and Kansas City's interior offensive line is its weakest link right now. Left guard Kingsley Suamataia struggled mightily in pass protection last week, as did Caliendo, and even all-pro center Creed Humphrey allowed two pressures. Whoever is in the lineup will have to perform well if the Chiefs want to see the second-team offense in the back half of this game.
To be clear, running back Emmett Johnson is likely the game's top performer, with Arizona allowing the 28th-most rushing yards per game. But nothing would be more encouraging than an offensive line that protects Mahomes while he builds chemistry with a revamped receiving corps. They will not have a better matchup to prove themselves all season.
Defense: Chiefs back seven vs. tight end Trey McBride
To say tight end Trey McBride is Arizona's only receiving weapon would be putting it lightly. After trading Marvin Harrison Jr. and placing Michael Wilson on injured reserve, their wide receiver depth chart reads Devin Duvernay, Simi Fehoko, and Reggie Virgil, none of whom has 100 yards on the season. Backup tight end Elijah Higgins, fresh off a multi-year extension, is currently their second-best weapon.
McBride already has 78 receptions, second in the NFL among all receivers, and 635 yards, which trails only Brock Bowers among tight ends. Higgins is not as good as Michael Mayer, but the Chiefs struggled against two-tight-end sets in Week 4 against Las Vegas, when Bowers and Mayer combined for 14 catches, and each topped 80 yards.
The Cardinals do not have quite that good a duo, nor do they have Kirk Cousins throwing the ball, but Johnson will lean on the two of them, mainly McBride. That likely means the Chiefs put their cornerbacks on an island, given how big an advantage they have on the outside, and dedicate resources to the middle of the field.
Unlike Bowers, McBride lines up in the slot or in-line 88 percent of the time, so he mostly draws linebackers and safeties, creating mismatches. With Nick Bolton and Drue Tranquill not the most talented coverage linebackers, safeties Chamarri Conner, Alohi Gilman, and Jaden Hicks, along with slot corner Chris Roland-Wallace, will need to draw assignments or at least provide help over the top.
With top pick Jeremiyah Love sidelined, Kansas City will also need to contain running back Tyler Allgeier, a competent runner, but limiting McBride is Steve Spagnuolo's key to the game.

title: Injuries to Drake Maye and Puka Nacua Lighten the Challenge of the Chiefs' Upcoming Gauntlet
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs' late-season schedule is a gauntlet. After three consecutive noon games against the struggling New York Jets, Atlanta Falcons and Arizona Cardinals, the Chiefs will hit the road for three away games starting next week, visiting the Buffalo Bills, Los Angeles Rams and Cincinnati Bengals before returning home to host the New England Patriots and San Francisco 49ers.
That's a stunning five-game gauntlet, but two of the NFL's most influential injuries will make the challenge slightly less steep against two of KC's upcoming opponents.
On Friday, the NFL world officially learned that Patriots quarterback Drake Maye fractured his right fibula , which will sideline him for the foreseeable future. While ESPN 's reporting notes that "Maye could return toward the end of the season," it seems unlikely that he would be back in time for a trip to Arrowhead Stadium for Monday Night Football on December 21.
Without Maye, New England's offense is led by backup quarterback Tommy DeVito—an obvious downgrade for the 5-5 Patriots.
Meanwhile, Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua certainly won't be on the field against the Chiefs in Los Angeles one week after Thanksgiving due to an injury and suspension . Without getting into the details of the (injury/suspension) designation, the already-injury-riddled Rams will be missing at least one key weapon when they host KC.
Veteran receiver Davante Adams could potentially return in time to face the Chiefs , but that's far from a certainty. On the defensive side of the ball, former Chiefs cornerback Jaylen Watson has been ruled out for the rest of the year due to a shoulder injury.
Even beyond the quarterback carousel that the Cardinals will be riding on Sunday in Kansas City , the Patriots' and Rams' injury reports are enough to recalibrate expectations for both of those December tests.
Of course, the Chiefs' trip to Buffalo to face the Bills on Thanksgiving looks just as challenging as it did when the schedule was released, the Bengals are healthier than they typically seem to be by this point in the season, and the 49ers' laundry list of injuries hasn't slowed them down yet, so most of that month-long stretch remains daunting.
Especially as the Chiefs manage injuries of their own , it's worth remembering that the NFL is a battle of attrition more often than a meeting of two perfectly healthy teams playing their best football.
The Chiefs thumped the Atlanta Falcons without Kenneth Walker. The passing game has gotten back on track after losing Tyquan Thornton (and Rashee Rice for a shorter period of time). Kansas City's preseason first-team offensive line hasn't played a single snap together, as four of the five starting positions have had injury or availability questions this season.
Still, the Chiefs and other injury-impacted squads remain among the best teams in the league, and Kansas City will need to hold their spot in the standings as their Thanksgiving-through-December gauntlet ramps up.
Tied at the top of the AFC West with the Denver Broncos, the 7-2 Chiefs could pull even with the 8-1 Bills if both teams win this week and the Chiefs pull off the Thanksgiving road win on Thursday. That would leave the Christmas Day showdown between Denver and Buffalo as the next domino that may need to fall in the Chiefs' favor if they hope to nab the AFC's No. 1 seed and corresponding first-round bye. Even then, is it fair to expect a nearly perfect stretch of football from KC as they face off with a series of the NFL's best teams? Probably not.
But if there's anything the NFL teaches us every season: there's no guarantee as to what any of these teams will actually look like until the games begin.

title: Chiefs Suddenly Face a Cardinals Team in Complete Quarterback Disarray
full_text:
In a matchup the Chiefs were already heavily favored in , they received another huge break on Thursday with the Arizona Cardinals' latest injury development.
Mike LaFleur's squad was down to its third quarterback in as many weeks after the franchise traded away Jacoby Brissett at the deadline and lost Gardner Minshew II for the season with a torn UCL in his throwing arm. They turned to third-round rookie Carson Beck last week in a loss to the Rams, an outing in which he only threw for 108 passing yards without a touchdown. However, Arizona's precarious quarterback situation worsened today. The Cardinals injury report from Friday revealed that Beck did not practice due to back spasms, putting his status up in the air for Week 11. That puts 40-year-old journeyman Josh Johnson in line to make the start against Kansas City this weekend (yes, that Josh Johnson).
The #Cardinals are planning to start veteran QB Josh Johnson on Sunday vs. the #Chiefs , as Carson Beck deals with a back injury. The 40-year-old Johnson arrived in Arizona on November 11th. pic.twitter.com/TC2SHuc0vl
Johnson, who has been a member of 15 NFL teams throughout his 19-year career, has only made three NFL starts in the current decade. He filled in a pair of games for the Commanders last year after Marcus Mariota got hurt and led the Ravens once in 2021.
Not only has Johnson become the Edwin Jackson of the NFL, but he's even played in three different professional leagues (UFL, AAF, and XFL). The veteran is about as well-traveled as any player in the league's history. The bigger story here is that the Chiefs hold yet another advantage over Arizona in a showdown in which they opened as double-digit point favorites. The Cardinals are merely playing for draft position right now and were hoping to develop Beck over the final handful of games, but even that plan is in jeopardy should his injury linger long-term.
For a Cardinals offense that had only mustered nine points across its past two contests and recently placed star skill-position players Michael Wilson and Jeremiyah Love on injured reserve, they couldn't afford any more bad news on the injury front. Now, they'll likely have to roll out a new signal-caller who is on the back end of his playing career and hasn't even spent two weeks with this current group since being signed off the Bengals' practice squad.
As fun as a story like Johnson's is, the Chiefs are going to do everything in their power to make his life miserable on Sunday. Steve Spagnuolo's pass rush has finally come alive in recent weeks, totaling eight combined sacks against the Jets and Falcons.
There's still a possibility that Beck suits up if he overcomes his 'questionable' designation before kickoff. Either way, Arizona is staring at another potential blowout loss, regardless of who gets the ball under center.

title: The Morning-After Thunder: Chargers D Breaks, Herbert is Hurt, Draft Picture Narrows
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers were unable to follow up on their victorious effort from Week 10 when they faced off against the New York Jets on their home field this week. The Chargers, unfortunately, found a new way to lose this week with the defense seemingly shorthanded and exhausted.
The Chargers were missing multiple starters from their defense against the Jets, just days after they put forth a dominating effort against the Baltimore Ravens on Monday Night Football. The Jets' rush offense, between running backs Breece Hall and Braelon Allen, landed body blows and jabs on the Chargers defense at an exhausting pace. The same defense that held Derrick Henry to ten yards on ten carries just six days earlier, could not stop the Jets ground attack, even when the game was on the line.
The loss drops Los Angeles to 1-9 on the season and any miracle run of winning nine in a row for a shot at the playoffs has quickly been killed off. There are many potential reactions to this game from the Chargers perspective, let's run through several of them.
The Chargers may have dropped a game to the Jets but the victory may have cost New York a chance to draft a quarterback without having to use their draft war chest to trade up. The current draft order is relatively unchanged with the Titans still holding down the top spot followed by the Chargers and Dolphins.
The Chargers, having lost, now face the reality that they are likely picking in the top five in the draft in 2027. Head coach Jim Harbaugh finally acknowledged that the process now includes an eye to the future in his postgame press conference. The Chargers now have a more firm handle on a top-three pick in losing to the Jets with both the Jets and Colts having three wins. The game between the Chargers and Dolphins Christmas weekend will likely determine who gets the better draft pick.
The end of the game was baffling from a time management point of view for the Chargers and Jim Harbaugh. The Chargers went on their final scoring drive, taking possession with nearly ten minutes left in the game and took a slow, methodical approach down the field and finally scored with under two minutes left in the game. Where was the urgency?
The long drive essentially forced the defense into a one first down and the game is over type scenario and left no room for error. The Jets were able to close it out but there was an odd sense of lack of situational awareness from the team.
It is obviously too little, too late for the 2026 Chargers but they seem to have found an identity on the ground and sprinkled in with the passing game the offense looked ok. Having Ladd McConkey back on the field proved to be critical as he accounted for two touchdowns. The tight ends were involved in the attack and Tre' Harris made several grabs as well. It was at least functional and the original vision could be seen through the smoke.
The jump in scoring with McConkey back on the field underscores the need for additional weapons for the Chargers next offseason. Even if the Chargers miss out on drafting Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith, this class is fairly loaded at the wide receiver position.
The Chargers made several moves this offseason specifically for Mike McDaniel as he went to retool the offense and prepare for his system install. The first signing was grabbing Cole Strange from free agency to assume a starting guard role, he has now been benched mid-game and lost his starting job this week to veteran Kayode Awosika.
It was a fun note when it happened, but McDaniel actually made wanted posters for fullback Alec Ingold and running back Keaton Mitchell to ask general manager Joe Hortiz to go get them in free agency and Hortiz obliged. Ingold is almost certainly done for the year on IR and Mitchell has seen his snaps and role dramatically cut down.
It is hard to fault rookie wide receiver Brenen Thompson who, for what seems like a different soft issue injury every week, has been unable to get on the field. Thompson was specifically requested by McDaniel as a prospect to be drafted and again, Hortiz obliged. The bottom line is, the offense that McDaniel thought he was building, never took shape but has seemingly evolved more towards the Rams or 49ers offense, a move that should have been made long ago.
NFL analyst Warren Sharp rightly identified a major problem for the Chargers and their 2026 schedule back in the spring following the schedule release. The NFL gave the Chargers a devastating rest disadvantage this season and in hindsight, it sould have been taken more seriously at the time.
NFL 2026 Net Rest Edges net rest = total days of extra rest vs a team's opponent, summed over the course of the season (negative=bad) -24: LAC -23 -22 -21 -20 -19 -18 -17 -16 -15: PHI -14 -13: LV -12 -11 -10 -9: NYJ -8 -7: NO -6: IND, LAR, MIA, PIT -5 -4: CIN -3: BAL, JAX -2:… https://t.co/Yo03poZurv
The Chargers had a late-night travel schedule following a cross-country Monday Night Football matchup in Baltimore and did not arrive home in Los Angeles until just before four A.M Tuesday. The Chargers played a tough game on Monday, had a brutal turnaround and it looked like they were sluggish on the field. The same defensive line that dominated Baltimore got beaten up by the Jets offensive front.
The Chargers are getting a very clear picture of their roster, with so many bodies going down, the depth is stretched thin. Missing multiple starting defenders proved too costly for them but the offense is at least showing signs of life.
Los Angeles' reality may finally be setting in and now with Justin Herbert in the NFL's concussion protocol the season is that much more bleak. At least the Chargers seem well positioned for a top-three pick in April.

title: Chargers Players Rising, Falling After Week 11 Loss, Benched Starter and Breakouts
full_text:
Now that the Los Angeles Chargers are officially unable to capture a winning season with nine losses this year, this team needs to really start considering its future and moving on to next season. This process can start as soon as now, evaluating players who deserve more attention and players who do not.
So, after this 27-24 loss to the New York Jets, who is rising? Who is falling?
David Njoku finds himself back on the field for the second week in a row after suffering what looked to be a season-ending fibula injury . In a weak Chargers passing offense, Njoku was able to record two catches for 21 yards while being an effective run blocker for a heating-up Chargers run game.
Expect for Njoku to continue gaining snaps in this offense, as this coaching staff obviously prefers his abilities over the once exciting young TE, Oronde Gadsden II.
Travis Burke was not expected to immediately start and contribute for the Chargers, as he has done thus far this season. Even with this unexpected nature of playing time occurring, Burke has been quite solid in his starts thus far, especially as a run-blocker.
As a pass blocker, his warts against speed have been seen, but this week against the Jets highlighted it more than ever. David Bailey, a speed-first rusher, was able to get Burke multiple times, whether it was Burke giving up a sack or the offensive plays being stalled out due to pressure from the right side.
Ladd McConkey was finally able to see himself on the field for a full game, which feels like this is the first time since Week 1 he has been able to do so. In a passing game that lacked explosive plays and general volume, McConkey was able to make the most of his day, recording five catches for 37 yards and two touchdowns.
If you have McConkey in fantasy, it may be a safe bet to start considering him as a flex option in your lineup. If you are the Chargers, it is nice to see your WR1 finally on the field and producing as he is expected to, even after all the injuries.
Cole Strange, where do we even start? As what seems like a weekly inclusion as a faller on these lists, he finds himself on this list once again, hopefully for good. Strange was benched in favor of Kayode Awosika, yielding his playing time to be nearly zero this week.
Awosika did not play amazingly, but it was better than what we have seen from Strange all season long. Moreover, on a PAT attempt from Cameron Dicker late in the game, Strange was on the field as an extra blocker. On this play, Strange collected a 15-yard penalty. Even in a handful of snaps, Strange still finds a way to hurt this team.

title: Justin Herbert Injury Revealed: Chargers QB Enters Concussion Protocol After Loss
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers have now lost another game, adding to their horrid record of 1-9. This was dealt by the hand of the New York Jets, another team with very few wins on their record with a now 3-8 season.
Unfortunately, the bad news does not stop their for the Chargers, as QB Justin Herbert finds himself reportedly in concussion protocol, after the tough, physical loss the Jets. It is currently unknown where or when the possible concussion could have occurred.
Justin Herbert is in concussion protocol.
With Herbert taking eight quarterback hits, which include six sacks, as well as having eight carries that went for 32 yards, it is very likely that Herbert suffered a brutal hit to the head that made the league call in to ensure his health.
Herbert also suffered a major hit on his touchdown run before the half, giving all the more reason for Chargers fans to be concerned about his well-being. More to follow.
In a lost season, we at least have this. https://t.co/5OJkILrgTh
With the league having to evaluate the injury, it falls under a five-step process :
1. Symptom Limited Activity 2. Aerobic Exercise 3. Football Specific Exercise 4. Club-based Non-contact Training Drills 5. Full Football Activity/Clearance
Once Herbert passes these steps, he will be able to play, but the question of his game status for the Chargers' upcoming matchup against the New England Patriots lingers. If Herbert were to miss the Nov. 29 game against the Patriots, it should be expected that backup QB DJ Uiagalelei would start, with practice squad QB Jake Browning as the backup.
Trey Lance is currently unable to suit up, as he was placed on injured reserve with a groin injury on Sep. 25. If Lance is deemed healthy enough to return, the Chargers could burn another injured reserve return designation, then only having one left for the following players:
S Derwin James LT Rashawn Slater G Branson Taylor G Trevor Penning FB Alec Ingold CB Rodney Shelley QB Trey Lance C Tyler Biadasz (season-ending)
On the bright side, the Patriots will be without their starting QB, Drake Maye, as Maye was placed on injured reserve and will miss his matchup against the Chargers. Fans could very well be on pace to watch a backup QB brawl.

title: Chargers’ Keaton Mitchell, David Njoku Suffer Injuries vs. Jets
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers lost two pieces of Justin Herbert’s offense when running back Keaton Mitchell and tight end David Njoku suffered injuries early during Sunday’s game against the New York Jets.
Mitchell, the rotational back alongside Omarion Hampton, suffered a back injury. Njoku, just back from recent injuries, suffered a shoulder setback.
Below, we’ll provide updates on both injuries as they become available.
Keaton Mitchell, David Njoku injury impact
Mitchell caught one pass for six yards before exiting with his injury. He had entered the year as a free-agent addition for coordinator Mike McDaniel who dramatically ate into the workload of former first-rounder Omarion Hampton.
Entering Sunday, Mitchell had carried the ball 49 times for 182 yards and no scores with another 18 catches, 103 yards and one score as a receiver. His missing time will lead to more looks for Kimani Vidal behind Hampton.
Another McDaniel free-agent target, Njoku joined and started eating into the snap counts available to Oronde Gadsden, a breakout from last year. But a fibula injury during Week 2 sent him to injured reserve and he’s appeared in just two games this year. On Sunday against the Jets, he caught just one pass for 13 yards before exiting.
Njoku missing time would mean more looks for Gadsden and Charlie Kolar, with Patrick Herbert and Josiah Deguara on the practice squad.

title: Chargers Free Agent Bust Finally Benched Heading Into Week 11 Jets Matchup
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are 1-8 heading into their Week 11 matchup against the New York Jets, a team that is also not likely to make the playoffs, but at least a team that has some self-respect and a level of feistiness that they play their opponents with.
With the Chargers sending out the message that this team is serious about turning it around and winning football games, even with their atrocious record, it seems that this team needs to make one obvious yet major move to help their chances of winning football games and truly turn this around.
That move finally happened, benching Chargers free agent interior offensive lineman signing, Cole Strange.
Strange, signed to a two-year, $13 million deal now finds himself on the bench 11 weeks into the NFL season. His connection and likely reason for coming to the Bolts was to be an experienced veteran who knows offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel and his scheme well.
Even with knowing the scheme, it seems that Strange is still struggling, garnering negative feedback from fans weekly, as well as being asked about often in press conferences that mention struggling units...the most notable of which is the interior offensive line tasked with protecting star QB Justin Herbert.
So far this year on 547 offensive snaps, Strange has earned a 46.8 overall PFF grade, 71st among 77 qualified offensive guards. Furthermore, his PFF pass-blocking grade is 37.7, which ranks 69th, with his run-blocking grade of 57.0 ranking 55th.
Beyond being near the bottom of the league in PFF grades, he has also allowed 23 total pressures in pass protection, which includes three sacks and three hits allowed to opposing pass rushers. He has also been flagged for 6 penalties thus far.
The man tasked with replacing the struggling right guard is the now-healthy veteran offensive lineman, Kayode Awosika . Coming from the Detroit Lions, Awosika has played 85 snaps this season, initially starting at left guard (alongside Trey Pipkins III in the platooning situation seen early in the year), earning a 59.2 overall PFF grade, a 63.9 pass-blocking grade and a 56.6 run-blocking grade. He only has two pressures given up, none of which turned into sacks.
Chargers appear to have benched Cole Strange, if warmups were any indication. Kayode Awosika was the starting RG. Worth noting McDaniel called the situation "fluid" and hinted at the possibility of playing both.
Awosika has missed time due to a fibula injury , but now finds himself returning and ready to take over for the struggling Strange. Hopefully, this changeup allows for the Bolts to have a stronger protection plan for Herbert.

title: Chargers Confidence Meter: Can the Bolts Win Back-to-Back Games?
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers have an opportunity to make a statement when they take on the New York Jets on Sunday. This is the type of matchup where the Chargers should feel good about their chances, but that does not mean they can afford to overlook their opponent obviously.
So, can the Chargers beat the Jets? Absolutely.
The biggest question is whether the team can put everything together for four quarters instead of making things harder than necessary. There is a reasonable opportunity here for the Chargers, but they still have to take advantage of it .
One thing they should prioritize is establishing its identity early.
The Chargers cannot afford to spend the first half trying to figure out what kind of game they want to play. They need to be aggressive when opportunities present themselves. Make smart decisions offensively, and avoid giving Geno Smith and the offense unnecessary chances to gain confidence.
Justin Herbert will naturally be an important part of the equation.
His ability to make plays, recognize defensive looks, and keep the offense moving gives them an opportunity to create separation. The Chargers also need their running game to remain involved. Being able to balance the offense would make things more difficult for the Jets and prevent the entire game plan from depending on one approach.
The Jets should not be allowed to hang around simply because the Chargers make avoidable mistakes. Tackling, communication, and limiting explosive plays will all matter. If the defense can consistently put the offense in favorable situations, the Bolts should have a good chance of controlling the overall flow of this matchup.
There is a difference between expecting to win and assuming a victory is guaranteed. The Chargers should approach this matchup with confidence, but they must understand that their performance will ultimately determine the outcome. The Jets are still an opponent capable of making things uncomfortable, particularly if the Bolts struggle to finish drives or turn the football over. The truth is, the Jets have a better record and on paper have played better but that doesnt mean everything.
My expectation is that they have a legitimate chance to win this game and should be viewed as the team with the advantage. The Chargers do not need a perfect performance. They simply need to play responsible football, take advantage of scoring opportunities, and avoid beating themselves.

title: Is Ladd McConkey Playing Today? Jets vs. Chargers Updates for Week 11
full_text:
Another week, more Ladd McConkey injury questions for the Los Angeles Chargers .
This time, it’s the run-up to kickoff when the Chargers host the New York Jets in Week 11. McConkey, who didn’t travel with the team during the prior week’s win over the Baltimore Ravens, continued to fight back issues that cost him the better part of the Chargers’ last two games.
Here’s a live-updating look at the latest on McConkey before the Chargers play the Jets.
UPDATE: The Chargers announced inactives before kickoff, not listing Ladd McConkey. He is active, but how much he plays, if at all, is unknown.
Not to keep hitting the dead horse, but the Chargers now have some serious questions to face about Ladd McConkey’s future .
McConkey has never started a full 17 games in a season, nor has he ever played more than 78 percent of his offense's snaps in a season. He’s played just 206 reps over six games this year.
The running tally for McConkey includes, but is not limited to knee, calf, rib, foot, back and concussion issues across the last three seasons.
So, don’t expect much from McConkey, even if he is active against the Jets. And with how Mike McDaniel’s offense has flopped for most of the season, there’s little reason to buy up any other names from a fantasy football standpoint, either.
The receiving high for the Chargers through nine games, after all, is Tre Harris with 26 catches. Top running back Omarion Hampton has scored four times, but averaged just 3.8 yards per carry over just 124 chances.
Even in the win to move to 1-8 last week, Justin Herbert went a quiet 12-of-18 for 129 yards with one rushing touchdown. Hampton had a good game with 22 carries for 105 yards and a score, but that’s an outlier, not a weekly thing.
Unfortunate all around, really: McConkey should be considered a question mark into 2027 and beyond, just like the entire offense, too.

title: Can the Underdog Jets Pick Off the Favored Chargers?
full_text:
On Monday night at M&T Bank Stadium, the Los Angeles Chargers snapped an 11-game overall losing streak that dated back to Week 17 of 2025. Jim Harbaugh’s Bolts managed a 23-20 victory over the last place team in the AFC North.
The Baltimore Ravens were led by Jacoby Brissett, the team’s fourth different starting quarterback this season and a player that the Chargers had seen back in Week 1 when he was a member of the Arizona Cardinals. He managed to throw for 340 yards but also served up an interception, part of two turnovers by Jesse Minter’s club.
Meanwhile, the Chargers managed to do something they hadn’t done all season—play a game without giving up the football. Justin Herbert threw for 129 yards, but also rushed for 51 yards—including a 22-yard score. Running back Omarion Hamton, who fumbled in the first quarter but recovered the ball, ran for 105 yards and a score. The duo accounted for 156 of the Bolts’ 160 rushing yards on Monday evening.
Let’s not bury the lead here. During their 0-8 start, Harbaugh’s club committed a whopping 19 turnovers. They gave up the ball at least twice in seven of those games. Herbert served up 11 interceptions and lost two of his seven fumbles—a total of 13 turnovers. Entering Sunday’s action, only now-former Indianapolis Colts’ quarterback Daniel Jones (13) has been picked off more times this season.
Safety is my favorite position: Bears-Jets has been prime viewing Minkah Fitzpatrick 14 tkls, INT Dane Belton 12 tkls Dillon Thieneman 7 tkls (team lead) pic.twitter.com/hyPOh2nBPj
Then there are 2-8 New York Jets, one defeat away from an 11th consecutive losing campaign. You may recall that Aaron Glenn’s club set two disturbing NFL record this past season with zero interceptions and four total takeaways.
Azareye'h Thomas with an INT BUFvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/oSsC1E1ChR
Things haven’t been much better when it comes to the former number. While the Jets lead the league with 10 opponent fumble recoveries, veteran safety Minkah Fitzpatrick (Week 4 vs. the Bears) and second-year cornerback Azareye’h Thomas ( last Sunday vs. the Bills ) have the team’s lone interceptions in 2026. Hence Glenn’s team has picked off a total of two passes in 27 contests during his reign as head coach.
Monday night’s victory at Baltimore not only marked the Chargers’ first contest without a turnover this season, it was also the first game this season in which Herbert did not throw an interception. Can he repeat that kind of performance on Sunday at SoFi Stadium? And will Harbaugh’s squad make it consecutive victories for the first time since the club reeled off four straight wins a year ago from Weeks 13-16?

title: Chargers’ Bud Dupree Release Drama Just More Proof Organization is Lost
full_text:
Tired of hearing about what a mess the Los Angeles Chargers are this season?
Sorry, but the hits just keep coming.
Over the last month, the Chargers have seemed more concerned with the messaging they send through the media than anything else. That, while doing the trade deadline botch, a mishap that featured the Chargers going back on their word about keeping things the same and instead attempting to trade a younger piece of the puzzle to the AFC West rival Denver Broncos.
While all this was going down, veteran edge defender Bud Dupree had a really telling quote that hinted at dysfunction in the locker room .
And as it turns out, Dupree has been asking for a way out of town for a long time now.
According to ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler , Dupree requested his release this past week…something he did before the season, too.
It begs the question: What’s the point?
The Chargers are holding on to an end-of-roster 33-year-old defender who has hardly played this year and, by the sounds of his quotes when reporters are around, isn’t exactly helping things in the locker room.
Dupree isn’t just an end-of-roster player who felt like an obvious cut candidate while forming the final roster, either. He’s on an expiring contract, so it’s not like the Chargers have much to gain by keeping him. Him playing into the comp pick process seems unlikely.
Speaking of that, the Chargers have these other edge rushers on the roster right now:
While keeping Dupree, the Chargers also gave up on a former draft pick like Kyle Kennard and passed up on any number of possible free agents, waiver wire claims or even trade acquisitions.
It somehow goes deeper, too: The Chargers extended Dupree after he wasn’t all that great in 2024, either, adding another year to what was originally a two-year pact.
And yet here we are again, with this feeling like a case of the Chargers worrying about messaging and image over anything else. There’s no other reason to keep him other than the front office doesn’t want to show players that they can just ask for a way out (and maybe they’re worried about what Dupree might say on the media circuit when he’s not an employee anymore).
It’s all really silly, with Dupree being a good example of the poor roster building by the Chargers over a number of years and the miserable priorities of an organization that just can’t seem to get out of its own way.

title: Fantasy Football Start or Sit: Expect Tre' Harris to Have Another Big Game
full_text:
The Chargers have an easier matchup this week…well, that's what fans hope it will be. The Bolts face the Jets on Sunday, following their first win of the season versus the Ravens .
Multiple players, especially Tre’ Harris, should have standout games , which in turn, could help fantasy managers this week
Here are six Chargers players you should start and sit this week.
Hampton is one of the Chargers players I feel best about this week.
He’s coming off an impressive performance against Baltimore, and his physical running style gives him a chance to control the game. What I like most is his ability to make plays even when the offense isn’t firing on all cylinders.
The Chargers should give him plenty of opportunities, and I expect him to be a major part of their game plan. He’s a strong starting option this week.
Harris is someone fantasy managers should seriously consider putting in their lineups. He’s beginning to show what he can bring to this offense, and his performance against Baltimore was encouraging. I like his ability to make contested catches and create opportunities downfield. The biggest question is how consistently the Chargers will get him involved, but I believe he’s earned more opportunities.
Herbert hasn’t been as productive as fantasy managers would like, but I’m not ready to give up on him.
He’s still capable of making difficult throws and creating plays when the pocket starts breaking down. His ability to contribute with his legs also gives him some additional fantasy value. I expect Los Angeles to look for ways to get its passing attack moving.
McConkey is one of the most talented receivers on this roster, but his back injury makes this a difficult week to trust him. Even if he suits up, there’s no guarantee he’ll be operating at full strength. Fantasy managers can’t afford to gamble on limited production when healthier options are available. I’d rather take a safer approach and leave him on the bench until there’s more confidence in his health.
Johnston has the physical tools to become a dangerous receiver, but his inconsistency is a problem for fantasy managers. He can make an impressive play, but that doesn’t always translate into dependable production.
With other receivers competing for opportunities, it’s difficult to predict when he’ll have a productive afternoon.
Mitchell has plenty of speed and can be dangerous when he gets room to operate. However, his role in this offense makes him difficult to trust right now.
Hampton appears to be the primary running back, which limits Mitchell’s opportunities to make a fantasy impact.
Unless the Chargers significantly increase his workload, I don’t see enough upside to justify starting him. Keep him on the bench this week.
