title: Rams Monday Morning Rambling: The Stakes Couldn't Be Higher Against Packers
full_text:
It’s hard to call any game a must-win during the regular season, especially one in Week 12. That’s exactly where the Los Angeles Rams find themselves as they get ready to play the Green Bay Packers on Thanksgiving Eve following their bye week.
There’s no doubt that the NFC is not only good at the top, but also very deep. After their win on Sunday Night Football against the Minnesota Vikings, there’s an argument that the San Francisco 49ers are the best team in the NFL.
Over the next two months, the Rams, Packers, and Seattle Seahawks will all be battling for one playoff spot. With one spot available for three teams, there is a chance that both teams from last year’s NFC Championship Game completely miss the postseason entirely.
Heading into Wednesday’s game against the Packers, the Rams have a 34 percent chance to make the playoffs. A win would give them a tiebreaker over the Packers and a 47 percent chance to make the postseason. Losing at home on Wednesday would drop their playoff chances to 16 percent.
That’s not to say that the Rams couldn’t make the playoffs if they were to lose on Wednesday. However, it would certainly make things more difficult as they enter the toughest stretch of their schedule without their best offensive player.
The Rams have the team to win five of their final six games, but a loss to the Packers would make already thin margins even thinner. A tiebreaker against a team the Rams are competing with for a playoff spot would go a long way. It’s also arguably their most winnable game over the next two weeks as the Rams rank sixth in DVOA and the Packers rank 13th. Next week, the Rams will play the seventh-ranked Chiefs before playing the top-ranked 49ers.
After fighting back from 2-4, the Rams have won four games in a row and are right in the thick of the playoff hunt. Despite all the injuries, bad luck, and everything else in between, the Rams have done well to keep their season alive heading into Thanksgiving.
The Rams entered the season with Super Bowl expectations and things certainly haven’t gone as planned. Still, the Rams remain a team that won’t break. This may not be Sean McVay’s best team, but it might be his most resilient. If the Rams want to stay in the thick of things and prove they belong among the NFC’s contenders, winning on Wednesday is a must.
When the Rams were without Puka Nacua before the bye week against the Arizona Cardinals, Sean McVay implemented Pony Personnel. Now, with Nacua out for the season, it’s going to be interesting to see if the Rams build on that. Based on what McVay said over the weekend, it could be something the Rams continue to use.
“I do think that this season with some of the guys, especially at our skill positions that are missing, requires a flexibility and a fluidity and that seems like it's prevalent in a lot of years but more so even this one,” McVay said.
Prior to this season, Sean McVay was 0-4 against Nick Sirianni and the Rams beat the Eagles. McVay is 0-5 against Matt LaFleur, but they haven’t faced each other since 2024. McVay slayed the Sirianni demon earlier this season and finally beat a LaFleur brother before the bye week. Can he slay another dragon before the Rams go on a run into December?
There is no doubt that Wednesday’s game between the Rams and Packers will have serious playoff implications. As mentioned earlier, both of these teams are fighting for the final playoff spot in the NFC. A win for either side would provide an extremely valuable tiebreaker. That’s not something that the Rams can afford to think about heading into Wednesday, but it’s a very important game.
The Rams are set to get Kobie Turner back for the game against the Packers . Turner’s value to the defense is extremely underrated and Wednesday will be the first time that the Rams will have him, Braden Fiske, Byron Young, Aaron Donald, and Myles Garrett all healthy and playing in the same game. Turner’s season got off to a slower start, but the Rams will certainly be glad to have him back.
Over the past month, the Rams have done well to remain committed to the run game. Since Week 7, the Rams have a -2.2 percent pass rate over expected. They’ve been extremely balanced on offense and will need to lean into that against the Packers. The Packers’ defense has allowed a 43.3 percent rushing success rate this season, which ranks 27th in the NFL. That’s something that the Rams should be able to exploit.
The Seahawks were on their bye this week along with the Rams, while the Cardinals got blown out by the Chiefs. However, the 49ers continue to prove that they might be the best team in the NFL. Not many would have expected the 49ers to beat a good Vikings team, 35-10. Kyle Shanahan looks to be a man on a mission and Brock Purdy is playing at an MVP level.

title: The Rams' Season Isn't Cooked Yet, Even Without Puka Nacua
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are 6-4 and on a four-game win streak as they come out of their bye week. While the Rams might be playing their best football of the season, they simply can’t seem to escape the injury bug. After losing wide receiver Puka Nacua for the remainder of the season , some are declaring the Rams’ season dead.
“The Rams would be challenged by that schedule even with their full complement of players,” wrote Bill Plaske of the LA Times. “Without their best, they are bust. The Rams are cooked, and, in a way, it’s nobody’s fault but their own.”
Not having Nacua will certainly make things more difficult. The Rams had to adjust their offense in Week 10 against the Cardinals, moving to more 20 personnel . It’s fair to wonder if that’s sustainable and if the Rams can keep that going against better teams as they enter the second half of the season.
Still, football changes in December and January. High-powered passing attacks are great in September and early October. However, good defense and running the ball have always prevailed later in the season.
That’s the type of football that the Rams were built for. Over the last month, the Rams rank second in rushing success rate and fifth in EPA per rush. They have the running back duo that can carry the offense. The Rams adjusted their offense to use both Blake Corum and Kyren Williams on the field together.
“I think that's what this season entails and requires. I thought it was really cool for a lot of guys to be able to get involved in a variety of ways,” said head coach Sean McVay. “I do think that this season with some of the guys, especially at our skill positions that are missing, requires a flexibility and a fluidity and that seems like it's prevalent in a lot of years but more so even this one.”
For a team that has often relied on its offense under McVay, they may rely on the defense to carry them to the postseason. Despite the injuries on offense, the defense is finally getting healthy. Myles Garrett has played back-to-back games, Aaron Donald is starting to find his rhythm, and Kobie Turner is returning from injury.
The Rams are set to have all three players available for the first time this season on Wednesday against the Green Bay Packers. Trent McDuffie has managed injuries, but has played like one of the best cornerbacks in the NFL when he’s been healthy.
During the Rams’ four-game win streak, the defense has been one of the best units in the NFL. They rank fourth in defensive EPA per play, second in defensive success rate, and fourth in defensive DVOA. The Rams have the No. 1 run defense in the NFL in EPA per play and No. 4 pass defense.
In 2020, the Rams had the No. 1 defense under Brandon Staley and it was that group that carried them into the playoffs. The Rams may need that type of performance from their defense again if they’re going to make the postseason.
With that said, it isn’t crazy to think they can do it. In three out of the last five games, the Rams’ defense hasn’t allowed a touchdown. Since allowing 37 points to the Buffalo Bills, the Rams have allowed 13.4 points per game in their last five.
While the Rams may seem ‘dead’ after losing Nacua for the season, they still have a team built for December and January football. They may seem like a team that could falter down the stretch and finish behind the Seattle Seahawks and Green Bay Packers, but they play those two teams a combined three times.
That doesn’t mean it’s going to be easy, but if the Rams can play good defense and remain efficient on offense, they’ll give themselves a chance.. Through all the injuries, the Rams have scratched and clawed their way back into the hunt. The Rams have shown all season they aren’t going to go away quietly.
It's easy to look at the Rams' injuries and difficult remaining schedule and write them off. They’ll be without their best player on offense as they face the most difficult schedule in the NFL. The Rams have developed a physical identity on offense behind a good run game and have a defense capable of taking over. They may not be the Super Bowl favorite they were expected to be, but that doesn't mean their season has to be over.

title: Rams Sunday Morning Notebook: Puka Nacua Controversy, Kobie Turner's Return From Injury, and More
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are coming out of their bye week with plenty of storylines as they prepare to take on the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday. While the Rams are riding a four-game winning streak, much of the conversation this week has centered around Puka Nacua and his season-ending injury . Let’s get into that and more in this week’s Sunday Morning Notebook.
There’s no doubt that wide receiver Puka Nacua has been the topic of conversation this week. The Rams placed Nacua on injured reserve before he was suspended by the NFL, and then it was later announced that he had undergone season-ending surgery.
Nacua’s suspension came with a lot of controversy, especially with him also being on injured reserve. Even before Nacua underwent surgery and was ruled out for the season, his suspension wasn't expected to cost him any additional games beyond those he would already miss on injured reserve.
According to The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones , the suspension was reached via settlement between the NFL, NFLPA, and Nacu’a representation.
“Nacua accepted the league’s three-game punishment — which could be more accurately described as a three-game check forfeiture — and the league walked away with what it considers a precedent-setting victory, even if it’s not viewed that way on the outside,” said Jones.
Nacua’s surgery has also come with its share of controversy with some not believing that the team was fully on board with it . Even after the surgery was announced, it was thought that Nacua could possibly return for the playoffs with Sean McVay saying that he would be out a few months.
ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported on Sunday morning that three doctors recommended that Nacua undergo the procedure. Schefter also noted that the timeline is expected to be 4-5 months, which would put Nacua out for the remainder of the regular season and playoffs.
While the Rams will be without Nacua for the remainder of the season, they are expected to get some reinforcements back from injured reserve starting Wednesday against the Green Bay Packers. The Rams have officially designated Kobie Turner for return and Justin Dedich will also be back.
“Unless there's something unforeseen that occurs, we'll have both those guys. They'll be up and ready to roll,” said McVay on Saturday.
Both players will provide a boost for the Rams. The Rams have missed Turner’s presence on the interior. If the Rams get Turner back on Wednesday, it will be the first time they’ll have him, Aaron Donald, and Myles Garrett on the field at the same time.
Additionally, Dedich will at least provide depth on the offensive line. It will be interesting to see if he starts at left guard in place of Steve Avila or if the Rams go with Bill Murray. Dedich could also potentially play at center in place of Coleman Shelton, but guard is more likely. Again, the Rams will at least get some much-needed depth on the interior of the offensive line with Dedich’s return.
Earlier this season, the Rams took a lot of criticism for how they handled their travel plans to Australia. While the San Francisco 49ers arrived nearly a week before the game, the Rams arrived just over 24 hours before the game. During the week, the 49ers integrated with Australia’s culture and got involved in the community. That experience was part of what the Rams missed.
Over the past several years, the NFL has put a lot of time, effort, and money into the international games. The Rams not showing up until right before the game was almost a slap in the face to the league. They took a similar approach last year when they stayed for a week in Baltimore before traveling to London to play the Jacksonville Jaguars.
IThe league has discussed potentially requiring teams to spend a minimum number of nights in the host city before international games. That likely won’t go over well with some coaching staffs, but part of the NFL’s international initiative is for the teams to build a connection in the host city. The Rams have spent time previously in Australia, but showing up a day before the game doesn’t make the cost of travel worth it.
This is going to be something to monitor over the next few years and could potentially be a point of discussion in the next CBA.

title: Blake Corum Is Making the Rams Rethink Their Running Back Hierarchy
full_text:
Over the past month, the Los Angeles Rams have had one of the best rushing attacks in the NFL . During the Rams’ four-game winning streak, they rank second in the NFL in rushing yards and third in rushing success rate. The Rams also rank fifth in EPA per rush.
That’s a big difference from what the Rams were earlier in the season. During the first six weeks of the season, the Rams ranked 13th in EPA per rush and 12th in total rushing yards. A big reason for the Rams’ turnaround in the running game has been not just a greater commitment to the run from Sean McVay, but also the utilization of running back Blake Corum.
Corum has provided a spark to the run game that it lacked for the first month and a half of the season. The Rams had a combined 14 runs that went for 10 or more yards in the first six weeks. Seven of those came from Corum. Over the last four games, the Rams have 13 runs of 10 or more yards, with Corum responsible for eight of those.
“It's cool having this conversation because I definitely agree that he has provided a spark,” said offensive coordinator Nate Scheelhaase after Week 9.
Since Week 7, Corum leads the NFL with 0.28 EPA per rush as he’s scored in all four of the Rams’ wins. The next closest player is Justice Hill at 0.18 EPA per rush. Corum’s 67.9 percent rushing success rate is also the best in the NFL over that span. The gap between Corum at No. 1 and Jaylen Warren at No. 2 is larger than the gap between Warren and Jordan Mason at No. 32.
Corum is also fifth in rushing yards and yards per carry. His impact is especially noticeable in his explosiveness, where he ranks sixth in the NFL since Week 7.
Against the Arizona Cardinals, Blake Corum led the Rams with 17 carries. Given that Corum is the hot hand, it’s fair to wonder if that should be the case going forward. Corum has simply been the more effective runner and been what the Rams need in the run game.
That’s not to say that the Rams should bench Kyren Williams. However, Corum has provided a spark and been a big reason for the success of the run game over the last month.  For much of the season, Williams has been the clear lead back with Corum operating as the change-of-pace option. Corum has earned a larger role.
The answer to the Rams’ run game has never been one or the other between Williams and Corum. When both running backs are used, the Rams’ running game is at its best. Williams still has value in the offense as someone who can help keep the offense on track.
“You don't know what's happening, and you get to see a different person each and every single drive," said Williams earlier this week . "I think it's allowed us to keep our offense efficient, allowed us to keep us ahead of the chains so that Coach McVay can go into his playbook and call the plays that he wants to do.”
With that said, the Rams need a player who can create explosives, and that player has been Corum. It’s fair to say that while both players should be used, the workload that has typically favored Williams should flip.
One reason Williams has typically gotten a majority of the snaps is because of his impact in the passing game, especially in pass protection. Corum still needs to improve as a pass-catcher. However, in pass protection, Corum has been one of the best in the NFL this season. Corum’s 71.7 pass-blocking grade via PFF ranks ninth in the NFL. Williams is the primary passing-down back, but Corum still has 41 pass-block reps.
That should give the Rams more confidence in keeping Corum on the field in different situations, especially as the Rams start to incorporate more Pony Personnel in the offense . Without Puka Nacua for the remainder of the season, the Rams need to continue with what has worked.
That means remaining committed to the run game and making Corum a featured piece of the offense. Corum has shown that he is more than just a complementary piece. Williams still has an important role, but the Rams shouldn't ignore what the numbers are telling them. Right now, Corum is their most effective running back, and it's time for the distribution of carries to reflect that.

title: Did Puka Nacua and Rams Disagree on Season-Ending Surgery?
full_text:
When the Los Angeles Rams placed Puka Nacua on injured reserve following his MCL and PCL injury in his knee after Week 9, the thought was always they would get him back for the stretch run in December. However, on Friday head coach Sean McVay announced to the media that Nacua would be getting surgery on his knee and be out for a couple months. That would seem to imply that Nacua is out for the remainder of the season .
“Puka Nacua decided to get surgery on his MCL on Tuesday so that'll be a couple months for him,” said McVay. “He and his agent wanted to be able to get the full scope so that you can really have the appropriate amount of information and then be able to make the right decision.”
It’s interesting how McVay phrased what he said and the decision for Nacua to have surgery. McVay started by saying that Nacua decided to have surgery, and didn’t seem to include the team in that discussion. He then went on to say that Nacua and his agent wanted to be able to get the full scope, once again leaving the team out of his wording.
That seems to imply that the Rams and Nacua’s camp weren’t necessarily on the same page with the decision for him to get the surgery. Again, the original idea seemed to be from the team to get Nacua back for their Week 15 game against the Dallas Cowboys. Now, Nacua will be done for at least the entire regular season, if not also the majority of the playoffs.
He sought several medical opinions for the MCL tear, which he initially gave a week or so to see how it would heal on its own, hoping he could rehab and return," reported Tom Pelissero . "But the final medical guidance was unanimous: Surgery was necessary. It has been just a few days since, but it appears there’s virtually no chance that Nacua will be on the field again this season."
Taking the surgery route certainly makes sense from Nacua’s side. This is a big offseason for Nacua as he is currently playing in the final year of his rookie contract and set to be a free agent. As one of the best wide receivers in the NFL, Nacua will likely get one of the more lucrative contracts for a wide receiver.
Nacua’s current market value according to Spotrac has him at $47.6 million per year. That’s life-changing money for any player and a once-in-a-lifetime contract opportunity for Nacua.It makes sense for Nacua to prioritize his health and protect that potential payday, whether it comes from the Rams or another team.
Still, it’s not a great look if Nacua and the Rams weren’t on the same page with his surgery, especially with the team in the middle of the playoff hunt. Back in early August, Nacua hired a new agent. He then missed back-to-back games in Weeks 2 and 3 after aggravating a groin/hip injury from training camp in practice.
At this point, there has been no certainty from the Rams’ side that they plan to extend Nacua. There may be some expectation that they do, but the Rams also haven’t been in a rush to get something done. The franchise tag could be an option. After Nacua’s off-field issues last offseason, the team wanted to see him take steps in the right direction.
“I don't know that I can really say this timeline or stuff like that because I don't think you want to dangle a carrot that way,” said McVay back in training camp. “I think he's inspired to do right because his heart is right. I think the contract and things like that will take care of itself because he's an incredible player.”
During training camp, Nacua said all the right things and has seemingly taken steps in the right direction since. Still, dealing with injuries, especially a knee injury, it’s only natural that the contract would be looming over him and his agent’s decision to some extent.
The question becomes how the seemingly split decision for Nacua to undergo season-ending surgery affects his relationship with the Rams. The Rams have been hesitant to commit to Nacua long-term despite his production on the field. Meanwhile, Nacua has every reason to protect himself financially with a potentially life-changing contract on the horizon.
To be clear, that doesn’t mean that the Rams won’t extend Nacua in the offseason or make him a priority. At the same time, the Rams made decisions at the trade deadline with the idea that Nacua would be back. Two weeks later, he’s now opted to effectively end his season.
As the Rams enter the stretch run and fight for the playoffs, they’ll have to do so without one of their best players. It would be unfair to suggest that Nacua chose surgery solely because of his contract situation. However, it would also be naive to think that his future wasn't at least part of the discussion. With the season effectively over for Nacua, the focus shifts to what his future looks like with the Rams.

title: Puka Nacua Injury Exposes Rams' Biggest Roster Management Failure
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams have continuously ignored the wide receiver position since the offseason . They didn’t sign a veteran wide receiver in free agency and waited until the sixth round in the NFL Draft to add depth.
Despite having opportunities throughout training camp to sign a veteran, the Rams stuck with the status quo. They also passed on acquiring a wide receiver at the trade deadline with the idea that they would get players back healthy.
However, while the Rams will get Davante Adams back within the next few weeks, that mindset always seemed risky. The Rams have been one of the most-injured teams in the NFL this season. If there’s one thing they haven’t been able to do, it’s stay healthy. It seems like when the Rams have gotten one player back healthy, they have lost two more.
Now, the Rams are set to be without wide receiver Puka Nacua for the rest of the season. One of the players they were banking on getting healthy in a few weeks isn’t returning. At this point, it seems naive to believe that they’ll stay healthy, let alone when those players are Terrance Ferguson and Davante Adams.
Ferguson couldn’t make it through one full practice after the Rams opened his practice window before injuring his hamstring. Adams underwent surgery on his hamstring, but it's the same one that has bothered him for the last two years
It’s always easy to look at roster decisions with the benefit of hindsight. With that said, depth at the wide receiver position is something that the Rams have needed since the early spring.
Ignoring the position and banking on injury-prone players to stay healthy always felt like roster mismanagement. Now, the Rams are set to enter the hardest part of their schedule and will be relying on players like Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, Xavier Smith, and CJ Daniels.
While the Rams managed without Nacua last week, it was also against the Cardinals. Sean McVay was able to scheme around it by introducing Pony Personnel . It could be more difficult against the Green Bay Packers and Kansas City Chiefs, who both have top-10 pass defenses by EPA. The Rams were also able to catch the Cardinals by surprise. That won't be the case now that their Pony Personnel is on film.
At this point in the season, the Rams will have to wait for a veteran to potentially get released or rely on the depth that they’ve had confidence in up to this point, for better or worse. Ideally, the Rams are able to make a push for Brandon Aiyuk, but he seems set on wanting to play with Jayden Daniels and the Washington Commanders.
Despite being one of the most injured teams in the NFL, the Rams took the mindset of just waiting for guys to get healthy and are now paying the price. Replacing Nacua was never going to be easy. He’s one of the best wide receivers in the NFL. The Rams haven't had a contingency plan for Nacua, who hasn't played a full season since his rookie year, or Adams, who dealt with a hamstring issue and missed time last season
The Rams couldn't have predicted that Nacua would suffer a season-ending injury. However, they should have been better prepared for this possibility given his and Adams’ injury history. Instead, they continued to gamble on getting healthy rather than addressing an obvious need. With the most difficult part of their schedule approaching, that risk could end up being one of the biggest reasons the Rams fall short of the playoffs.

title: Rams' Playoff Hopes Take Major Hit With Puka Nacua Out for Season
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams will be without wide receiver Puka Nacua for the rest of the season. After suffering a PCL and MCL injury in Week 9 against the Washington Commanders, Nacua underwent surgery on Thursday and is set to be out several months.
The NFL was unaware that Rams WR Puka Nacua had undergone knee surgery Tuesday when it suspended him for three games Wednesday, per source. pic.twitter.com/bwVg4X3A9q
There was initially some hope that Nacua could return when the Rams played the Dallas Cowboys in Week 15 on December 20, as that was when he was first eligible to return from injured reserve. However, with Nacua opting for surgery, he will miss the remainder of the season.
Nacua missing the remainder of the year is a big loss for the Rams offense. The Rams were hoping to get healthy over the next few weeks as they make a late push for the postseason. While the Rams are set to get Davante Adams back over the next few weeks, they will still be thin at the wide receiver position.
The Rams relied heavily on Nacua this season when he was healthy. He’s the only Rams wide receiver with over 500 yards despite missing three games. Nacua has three games this season with over 15 targets and three games with over 10 receptions.
On Thursday, Nacua was suspended by the NFL for three weeks for an off-field incident during the offseason. According to Adam Schefter, the NFL was unaware that Nacua had undergone surgery when they handed out his suspension.
With Nacua out for the season, it will be interesting if the Rams continue to take the approach of waiting for players to get healthy or if they make a move at wide receiver. Signing a player like Brandon Aiyuk when he becomes available would make sense as he could fit into that role. However, the Rams have trusted their depth all year and with Adams coming back soon, they may see that as enough.
The Rams adjusted the offense last week to utilize the running backs in the passing game. Head coach Sean McVay implemented Pony Personnel to get both running backs on the field at the same time. Matthew Stafford went 12-for-16 for 202 yards and a touchdown with an EPA per dropback of 0.89.
Throughout the season, the Rams simply haven’t been able to escape the injury bug. After trading for Myles Garrett in the offseason, he missed the first eight games of the year. They signed cornerback Jaylen Watson in free agency and he’s set to miss the rest of the season with a shoulder injury.
The Rams have shown an ability to overcome adversity throughout the season, but losing Nacua for the remainder of the year may be their biggest challenge yet. They’ve managed to remain in the playoff hunt at 6-4, but replacing his production won't be easy as they get set to take on one of the toughest schedules in the NFL over the next seven weeks.

title: Rams Midweek Report: Injured Reserve Decisions, NFL's Strong Message to Puka Nacua, and More
full_text:
A large theme for the Los Angeles Rams this season has been injuries. They’ve been one of the most-injured teams in the league, and it seems like as soon as one player gets healthy, they lose two more. However, they've remained in the playoff hunt .
Over the next few weeks, the Rams will hope to get healthy and that some of their luck changes. However, that will also come with some potentially critical roster decisions.
Entering the season, each team is given eight return designations from injured reserve. This means that a team can put a player on injured reserve, and after four weeks the team can opt to designate that player for return while activating their 21-day practice window. A team has 21 days to add them to the active roster. If a team makes the playoffs, they are given two more designations.
Throughout the season, the Rams have had to use a few of their designations. Prior to Week 1, the Rams used return designations on offensive linemen Justin Dedich and Keagen Trost to avoid losing them for the season.
The Rams activated Trost in Week 6 ahead of their game against the Arizona Cardinals. Before Week 9 against the Washington Commanders, the Rams designated Ronnie Rivers, Terrance Ferguson, and Myles Garrett to return.
With just those returns, the Rams have used up five of their eight return designations. There has been some confusion with Ferguson because he hasn’t been moved out of the practice window. However, even if Ferguson’s practice window expires and the Rams don’t bring him back, that’s still a used return designation.
That leaves the Rams with some difficult decisions to make. They are projected to designate Kobie Turner, Davante Adams, and Puka Nacua to return. If that’s the case, the Rams wouldn’t have any return designations left.
Where this becomes complicated is in the case of Coleman Shelton, who is out 4-6 weeks. Because the Rams can’t designate another player to return, the Rams either have to work with one less roster spot or be ok with losing Shelton until the playoffs.
It also goes back to the decision for the Rams to bring back Rivers. The Rams brought back Rivers despite him being their RB3 and a special teams contributor. That’s a role that the Rams should have been able to replace via an available free agent.
Given the amount of injuries the Rams have had, every return designation and roster decision matters. While Rivers has been a valuable depth player, the Rams used a limited resource on a replaceable role. Now, with Shelton potentially needing to go on injured reserve, that decision could have significant consequences with the Rams out of return designations.
On Thursday afternoon, the NFL announced a three-week suspension to wide receiver Puka Nacua for violating the league’s personal conduct policy. Nacua’s suspension coincidentally will take place while he’s on injured reserve, and he won’t miss any time that he would have missed otherwise.
The timing of Nacua’s suspension is certainly odd. It can certainly be argued that the NFL missed the mark or didn’t read the room correctly. However, none of that makes it some sort of conspiracy that the NFL is favoring the Rams.
There is some precedent here as it has happened four times since 2018. In 2018, 2024, and 2025, David Perry, Sam Williams, and Daniel Ekuale all got handed suspensions while on IR or after suffering a season-ending injury. Mike Woods in 2023 was suspended while also on the non-football injury list.
It’s rare, and maybe the NFL needs to change it, but it’s not an exception because the Rams made some shady deal in a dark alley with the league.
With that said, the NFL has come down hard on Nacua. According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, the league communicated that, “Any further violation of the Personal Conduct Policy, including failing to satisfy the conditions of his diversion program, will subject him to additional and more substantial discipline, including banishment from the League.”
Sticking with Nacua, a big topic of conversation this offseason will be whether or not the Rams decide to pay him. Nacua is in the final year of his rookie deal, and as a fifth-round pick, he doesn’t have a fifth-year option.
It will be interesting to see if the Rams pay Nacua this offseason. As one of the best wide receivers in the NFL, it would seem crazy not to. For all of his off-field issues last offseason, he has seemingly turned a corner this year. There may be some concern, but after the suspension and conversations in the building, there is likely some understanding that something needed to change.
However, outside of the off-field situation, Nacua is set to miss at least six games with injuries this year. It would be the second time since 2024 that Nacua has missed six or more games. The Rams also played one of their best offensive games of the season in Week 2 without Nacua and did so again last week against the Arizona Cardinals.
“He's 25 years old and a brilliant player, but his play style makes you wonder about his longevity,” said ESPN’s Dan Graziano. “All of that is to say: I could at least imagine a scenario in which the Rams let him hit free agency, or franchise him and listen to offers.”
The Rams have done well to pay their players, and they certainly understand how important he is. If the Rams give him an extension, it’s hard to see it not being team-friendly to some extent. With that said, the franchise tag likely isn’t out of the question either.
Last week, the Rams rolled out Pony Personnel on offense for the first time in the Sean McVay era. The Rams ran 17 plays out of 21 or 20 personnel as Matthew Stafford went 12-for-16 for 202 yards and a touchdown with an EPA per dropback of 0.89. The Rams had a 56 percent success rate out of 20 personnel.
It seems unlikely that Pony Personnel becomes the main identity for the offense, but that doesn’t mean that the Rams won’t build on it going forward.
“The Rams' two-RB sets aren't going away any time soon,” said ESPN’s Dan Graziano. “Coach Sean McVay is going to lean into the areas where his personnel is the strongest, and right now Kyren Williams and Blake Corum are delivering in the run game.”
In Week 9, the Rams were in 11 personnel at a 42.5 percent rate. That was down to 4.5 percent on Sunday against the Cardinals. Instead of three wide receivers with one tight end on the field, the Rams subbed the tight end for another running back. It seems very possible that going forward, many of the Rams’ three-wide-receiver sets will come out of 20 personnel.
This is really contingent on the Rams staying mostly healthy on the offensive line. The loss of Coleman Shelton will hurt, but the Rams may be able to get by with Limmer. A loss at tackle and the Rams could start to see things begin to snowball. However, if they can get by, the Rams’ defense is playing at a level right now where 11-6 is possible. If that happens, it should be enough to make the playoffs.
The Rams were able to scheme around the loss of Nacua on Sunday against the Cardinals. However, they still need a third wide receiver and Brandon Aiyuk makes the most sense. The Rams may need to wait to sign him until after the game against the Green Bay Packers, but they need wide receiver depth going into the final stretch.
It’s hard to see the Rams ever making the change, but there’s an argument to be had that Shaun Dolac should be starting at linebacker. Nate Landman hasn’t played up to the contract that the Rams gave him last season. Dolac has limited snaps, but whenever he has played, he’s played well. It may be worth giving him an opportunity, especially if he can create turnovers like Landman, as he showed last week.
There’s obviously no injury report this week with the Rams on their bye week. Still, this seems like a good time to look at some of the Rams’ current injuries and see when they might be back in the lineup.

title: Rams Catch Major Break With Timing of Puka Nacua Suspension
full_text:
Throughout much of the summer, there was some speculation that Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua could get suspended for some of his off-field issues from the offseason. On Tuesday, the NFL officially announced that Nacua will be suspended for the next three games. According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, he will be eligible for reinstatement on December 14.
The timing of the suspension is somewhat lucky for the Rams. Nacua will serve his suspension while on injured reserve. If everything works out, Nacua won’t miss any games with his suspension that he also wouldn’t have missed while he was hurt.
This isn't the first time that the NFL has suspended a player while they are on injured reserve. Last season Pittsburgh's Daniel Ekuale was suspended five games despite being out for the season. In 2024, Sam Williams of the Dallas Cowboys was suspended three games while being out for the year. It's certainly rare, but not unprescented.
Nacua was placed on injured reserve last week and was eligible to return for the December 20th game in Week 15 against the Dallas Cowboys. His minimum injured reserve absence will extend beyond his suspension. Nacua will also still be allowed at the facility for medical treatment for his knee injury that he suffered in Week 9 against the Washington Commanders.
Puka Nacua will still be allowed at the Rams team facility to rehab his knee and toe injuries during his suspension https://t.co/CKE56BjxHM
On New Year’s Eve, Nacua allegedly bit a woman on the shoulder. While Nacua hasn’t denied that he bit the woman, he has characterized the physical contact as “horseplay.” Following the incident, Nacua checked himself into a holistic rehab facility for a short stint and didn’t miss any of the Rams’ offseason program.
Nacua hasn’t been criminally charged, but the NFL doesn’t require criminal charges to suspend a player, but it doesn’t take a charge for the NFL to decide whether a player is worthy of being suspended. Late in the summer, Nacua’s civil trial was pushed to 2028.
Prior to the start of the 2026 season, Schefter reported that the NFL had been reviewing Nacua’s case. With the suspension now official, it's clear the NFL felt it had enough evidence to discipline Nacua without waiting for the civil trial. It’s also worth wondering if the NFL is close to a decision on Alaric Jackson following his off-field issues this summer. Jackson was arrested for felony domestic battery, although the charges were eventually dropped and the case was assigned to a pre-filing diversion program.
Nothing changes from the Rams' perspective. They were already planning on being without Nacua for the next three games.  Had the NFL announced the suspension earlier in the season, the Rams could have been forced to play without Nacua for three additional games. Instead, the suspension overlaps with his injury recovery.
The Rams will hope to get Davante Adams back in the lineup for the Thanksgiving Eve game against the Green Bay Packers. Until Nacua is back, the Rams will continue relying on Konata Mumpfield, CJ Daniels, and Tutu Atwell.

title: Rams 2026 Rookie Report Card: Grading Every Draft Pick at the Bye Week
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams have reached their bye week at 6-4 , making this a good time to evaluate their 2026 rookie class. While the Rams have gotten some contributions from their younger players, they have once again taken a patient approach.
That makes evaluating this rookie class somewhat difficult. First-round quarterback Ty Simpson has yet to be active on gameday, while second-round tight end Max Klare has seen limited opportunities. However, the Rams have gotten some surprising contributions from an undrafted free agent. With 10 games in the books, let's hand out midseason grades for the Rams' 2026 rookie class.
Through the first 10 weeks of the season, quarterback Ty Simpson has yet to be active on gameday. That shouldn’t come as too much of a surprise considering how the Rams tend to bring their rookies along slowly and Stetson Bennett's experience gives him an advantage. Still, with the Rams leading 34-6 in the fourth quarter on Sunday, it would have been nice for their rookie quarterback to get some snaps.
There’s been a lot of discussion about how the Rams should have drafted a wide receiver with the 13th overall pick, especially given the injuries at the position. However, if Simpson works out, that remains the best pick in that spot. It’s hard to grade Simpson because he hasn’t played, but he seems to be following the development path that the Rams have set for him. Grade: B
Much like Simpson, it’s hard to fairly evaluate Klare. This is the spot where a discussion of whether the Rams should have taken a wide receiver instead makes the most sense. Klare is the TE5 on the roster and hasn’t gotten a lot of playing time.
Even still, the Rams are going to have some openings at tight end going into next season. Tyler Higbee could retire and both Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen are set to be free agents. When Klare played in the second half against the Los Angeles Chargers, his blocking in 13 personnel changed the game. The Rams may have a good player here, but the lack of opportunity has made this pick easier to criticize. Grade: C-
The issue with many of the Rams’ rookies is that they just haven’t played. Still, the Rams did bring Trost off of injured reserve when they were without Alaric Jackson for a game. That could signal that they are at least comfortable with him as a depth piece. With Steve Avila and Coleman Shelton out for the next few weeks, it will be interesting to see if the Rams give Trost an opportunity at guard or opt for a more experienced player while continuing to develop him at tackle. Grade: B-
It wasn’t until last week against the Arizona Cardinals that the Rams finally got a good look at CJ Daniels . Daniels played 60 percent of the snaps and had one catch for 22 yards. Matthew Stafford also targeted Daniels in the red zone. As Daniels plays more, he should get more comfortable in the offense. There was a lot to like with Daniels in training camp and the preseason. We’ll see how much the Rams use him with Puka Nacua out until mid-December. Grade: C
The Rams hit the jackpot with Wesley Bailey as an undrafted free agent. Any contribution from an undrafted free agent is positive. The fact that Bailey made the roster was impressive given how competitive it was. Bailey has two sacks and two forced fumbles this season. Last week against the Cardinals, he had an interception. With depth players like Josaiah Stewart and Desjuan Johnson, Bailey has earned a large role in the pass rush rotation. Grade: A+

title: Raiders Positional Breakdown: How Each Unit Performed Against Broncos
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders nearly erased a 17-point deficit to beat the Denver Broncos on Sunday. It would've been the team's largest comeback win since 2000. Instead, the Broncos held on to win their sixth straight game this season and their fifth straight against the Raiders.
Below are the grades for each of Las Vegas' position groups following Sunday's loss.
I am convinced that if Mendoza entered Week 11 with more starts under his belt, they would have beaten Denver. With more meaningful game experience with his teammates, Mendoza would have completed several of the critical throws he missed in his first road start.
The pick-six at the end hurt, but I feel that was the culmination of a rookie quarterback and an offense working so hard to climb out of a 17-0 hole that it finally caught up with them. That is why getting the offense going earlier in games is so critical in general, but is especially so for Las Vegas.
It would help take the load off the Raiders on the back end. One extra score earlier in the game, even a field goal, would have taken pressure off Mendoza on the final drive and maybe the interception does not happen.
The Raiders entered Week 11 with the second-fewest rushing yards in the league. They had 707 rushing yards in the 10 games before Sunday. They ran for 143 on Sunday against the Broncos. Both Ashton Jeanty and Mike Washington made impactful plays on Sunday.
Jeanty added to his already impressive receiving totals, which ranked among the top of the league among running backs entering Week 11. His 90 receiving yards, which included a 68-yard touchdown catch, kept the Broncos honest and off balance for most of the day.
Mendoza's handful of runs helped as well. This was the kind of performance on the ground that the Raiders' offensive line and running backs needed against a solid team.
Connor Heyward has made an impact on special teams.
The stats will show the sacks that Denver registered, but many of those were because Mendoza held the ball too long. He was holding the ball long because he didn't have many options on those given plays, but the fact that he could hold the ball too long meant he had the blocking to do so.
Most of the sacks were on the rookie quarterback, and Las Vegas had arguably its best game on the ground this season, regardless of stats, because the offensive line played well overall in Week 11.
Las Vegas undoubtedly missed Brock Bowers, but Ian Thomas' touchdown further confirmed that they have arguably the best group of tight ends in the league. Still, Thomas and Michael Mayer could improve at blocking.
Mendoza's timing with his receivers is something they could have had by now if he had started sooner. Still, Jack Bech had an impressive performance, nearly registering 100 receiving yards while making several tough catches.
Mendoza can work with Bech, Tre Tucker, and Jalen Nailor; he just needs more time with them in games to work on their timing. There is a reason Mendoza and the offense started to get on a roll. The timing quickly improved in real time on Sunday.
Given the numerous injuries Las Vegas' interior defensive line had entering the game , and the injuries they suffered in the game, the defensive line played admirably. It was actually shocking to see so many of Las Vegas' interior defensive linemen get hurt on Sunday.
However, that may be just what the front office needed to realize just how big an issue the interior defensive line has become. The unit forced multiple critical stops on Sunday. They have some pieces to work with, but they need more .
Overall, Las Vegas' defense had a solid outing.
Quay Walker showed improvement on Sunday. He played well against the run and pass.
He and Nakobe Dean showed what they can do when the defensive backfield and defensive line do their job. The Broncos' success running the ball in the second half should confirm how badly Las Vegas needs interior defensive linemen who can help keep Dean and Walker clean.
Las Vegas' failure to adequately address their defensive line and defensive backfield this offseason would be a disservice to the investments they have made at linebacker.
For the second week in a row, Las Vegas' defensive backfield limited the big plays through the air. They did a better job in Week 11 than they did in Week 10, proving that when they eliminate the big plays and Las Vegas' offense sustains drives, they can remain competitive for four quarters.
The Raiders' defensive backfield has now stacked two productive games together. They made their mistakes, but they weren't game-changing mistakes, which is progress. Las Vegas' young defensive backfield took a step in the right direction on Sunday.
Las Vegas had an early punt that was blocked deep in their own territory, which got the Broncos started. The unit also allowed one of AJ Cole's punts to be tipped shortly before halftime. Those two plays were vital in the loss.
Still, on punts that were not impacted, Cole was effective, as he usually is. He flipped the field a couple of times on Sunday. Cole is elite, and Matt Gay had another solid outing.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: 3 Overreactions to Raiders Near-Upset vs. Broncos
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders put up another valiant fight late in the game, but a costly interception ruined any upset bid as they fell to their rival, the Denver Broncos, 38-24.
There was a lot that should give Raider Nation hope , as head coach Klint Kubiak has his team on the right path despite yet another loss to an opponent with a winning record. His rookie quarterback flashed immensely, while his defense showed stinginess late, giving them a chance at the end.
With that in mind, I want to share some of my overreactions to Sunday's game in Denver as the Raiders fell to 4-7 on the season with a matchup against the Cleveland Browns on primetime next weekend.
Coming into this game, I was nervous about what the Broncos could do to Mendoza and the Raiders— it gave off a feeling of a potential nightmare game for Las Vegas. Instead, the rookie quarterback led his team to a near victory against their AFC West rivals. The pick-six was rough to see, but everything we saw from Mendoza was a quarterback adjusting to the speed of the game and making first-year player mistakes at the position.
Mendoza went 18-of-37 for 267 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception while adding 22 yards on the ground. I was impressed with what I saw, especially without Brock Bowers and other key players as the game went on. He is going to be just fine, and he already has operational control of the offense despite all of the mistakes he has made and will make along the way.
This was the second week in a row that the Raiders got close to winning a big game against a quality opponent. I believe if Mendoza had avoided the pick-six, he would've driven the ball downfield to tie the game, with a chance to win in overtime.
Kubiak must feel he is close, too. The way his defense showed up and how he called the offense showed me that his team is getting much closer. They aren't there just yet, but we have seen crazier things, especially as the Raiders travel to Cleveland for Sunday Night Football.
You know how good it feels to see running backs break off five-to-seven-yard runs consistently? That is what the Raiders offense was doing against the Broncos' defense, averaging six yards per carry for 143 yards on just 24 attempts.
I'm not sure how long this run game will be back for, but let's enjoy it while it lasts. It was great to see Ashton Jeanty rip off a 46-yard run and for Mike Washington Jr. to earn hard yards after contact on just nine attempts. Keep it going, and the Raiders offense could be a special unit for the rest of the season.
Jared Feinberg, a native of western North Carolina, has written about NFL football for nearly a decade. He has contributed to several national outlets and is now part of our On SI team as an NFL team reporter. Jared graduated from UNC Asheville with a bachelor's degree in mass communications and later pursued his master's degree at UNC Charlotte. You can follow Jared Feinberg on Twitter at @JRodNFLDraft

title: Raiders vs. Broncos: Shocking Winners & Losers From a Painful Loss
full_text:
DENVER, Col.—The Las Vegas Raiders (4-7) lost last night to the Denver Broncos (8-2) 38-24, and in a league with no moral victories, the game was much closer than that.
The fact that the Silver and Black have a rookie QB that NFL executives raved about in the pre-draft process is great, but not having a WR1 is brutal.
The Raiders were optimistic that superstar Brock Bowers would return, but he was ruled out as well. At the end of the day, this loss came down to the fact that while the Raiders' effort was valiant, they didn’t have enough players to win.
The only rookie QBs selected No 1 overall to have a game with 250 Pass Yards and 3 Pass TD within their first 2 career starts Joe Burrow Trevor Lawrence Fernando Mendoza pic.twitter.com/Nqpta3hNs4
According to PFF, “The only rookie QBs selected No. 1 overall to have a game with 250 Pass Yards and 3 Pass TD within their first 2 career starts Joe Burrow, Trevor Lawrence, Fernando Mendoza. ”That isn’t bad company.
That said, they remain ahead of schedule with preseason expectations , and they do give legitimate reasons for hope.
Since before the season started, I have reported that the Raiders DL is a work in progress and that they know it has to be upgraded; it didn’t help when one of the thinnest and weakest parts of the team was down a starter coming into the game, with DT Tonka Hemingway out—a promising sophomore.
But in the game tonight, they lost their other starter and two other DTs, costing them four of their top five DTs. Kubiak wasn’t happy given the disappointing details.
“[DT] Tim Keenan III has an MCL. [DT] JJ Pegues came out of the game, and [DT] Adam Butler came out of the game with a concussion. I’ll take any of your questions.”
More upset tonight than at any time in his tenure, I had to ask Kubiak about the already anemic unit, being down four of the top five at that one position. It isn’t an excuse; the Raiders still had a legitimate chance to win, but it is also factual. His answer was forthright.
“That’s the NFL. Guys go down, and other guys get opportunities, but it is difficult. If you’re a young player, you see that your next snap is one snap away. It’s definitely difficult.”
I have told you since before training camp that the Raiders were not good enough to beat their opponents, and themselves. Last week they almost upset a significantly better team than the Broncos in the Seattle Seahawks, with zero penalties. Last night, they had nine. Kubiak wasn’t very happy with that, but I had to ask him.
“That’s not going to win any games. That’s unacceptable. You have to go look at the tape and look at everyone individually, but you’re not going to win with nine penalties.”
Another self-inflicted wound was that Mendoza had six passes batted down. He is a taller young man, and that hasn't hurt him in the past. It did Sunday, and I asked him about it.
“I’ve never really had that issue before. I believe that Denver, their defensive line, they have all-stars and Pro Bowlers across their D-line. They did a good job, and it’s something that we’ll look back on the tape and see if there was anything that was indicating them to do that. I look forward to taking the coaches’ guidance on that.”
First TD pass for Fernando! #LVvsDEN | 📺 CBS pic.twitter.com/4THWIHK85S
Fernando Mendoza was 18 of 37 for 267 yards; he threw for three touchdowns, had one interception, and a passer rating of 89. He looked better and calmer, while taking five more sacks; the vast majority were on him.
For example, Kirk Cousins took 11 sacks in 9 games; Mendoza has 9 in 2. But Kubiak talked about his maturation after the game.
“He’s playing on the road in a really tough environment, one of the loudest environments in football. So he got some good reps there. It wasn’t great early in the game. We had to burn a timeout, but as the game went on, I thought he did better.” Kubiak gave credit to Mendoza for finding a rhythm. “I think that he was very well prepared. He got that first one out of his system, and then on to the next.”
Broncos head coach Sean Payton raved about the Silver and Black rookie after the contest. “It’s a great question because field level, I was really impressed with the off-schedule stuff. You watch a game last week, you watch the preseason, he took some sacks last week. You’re playing early on with [QB Kirk] Cousins and he’s playing well. I was more impressed with his size and his escapability than maybe I saw on tape.”
Some of the highest praise for Mendoza came from the Broncos terrific LB Alex Singleton, who had nothing but love for the Raiders rookie. “He’s a first-round pick, first overall for a reason. He’s going to be a good player. He added, about Mendoza reigniting the AFC rivalry, “Yes. That’s his job, right? That’s what you want. I don’t know if I should—my dad grew up in L.A., so my family might have been Raider fans. (Laughs) So I saw it from one way.”
But don’t bother telling Mendoza about any of the love. He wasn’t impressed with himself at all, but he was frank. “I believe I saw the field better. I believe that my accuracy was better this week than last week. Stepping into throws rather than drifting back. There are things… Don’t get me wrong, although I believe it was an improvement, there are a lot of things I need to improve on for next week.”
Yes it was 🙂‍↕️ https://t.co/IP5hV8f9oz
The Raiders sophomore WR had a breakout game. He had eight catches on nine targets for 88 yards and one touchdown. His emergence with Mendoza is noticeable, and he rewarded the coaches for their confidence in him. Mendoza is certainly a fan.
“[WR] Jack [Bech] is a great guy. He’s one of my best friends on the team. I have a lot of great friends on the team, and he’s someone who is notorious for staying after practice, catching extra balls. He’s been a fantastic player and teammate as well, so when he gets the attention, he rises to the occasion. Sometimes as a receiver it’s tough because they cover you, or the coverage they play doesn’t allow your route to be open. So whenever that happens, he still has a great smile, an attitude and a will to win.”
The humble Bech didn’t want to talk about his connection with Mendoza. To him, his friend has a connection with the entire franchise.
“I think it’s his connection with everybody in this locker room, the way he… Like I said, not only has he gotten better on the field from April, but the way he’s just taking that leadership role, he’s really has connected really well with all the players on this team and all the coaches. We all have faith and confidence in him.”
Kubiak was willing to praise his sophomore wideout. “He’s always been gritty, always been a great teammate. Then you get opportunities against a really good defense, and he made plays. So I’m happy for him. I’m not surprised. He makes those plays in practice, and with [TE] Brock [Bowers] out, he gets opportunities to go produce.”
The Raiders led last week against the aforementioned reigning Super Bowl champions until Brock Bowers went out injured at halftime. His presence was greatly missed today, on the road in a hostile environment, and on a team with no WR1. Mendoza bluntly discussed the loss of his star.
“[Raiders TE] Brock [Bowers] is an amazing player. He’s an All-Pro player. He’s spectacular. You can’t say enough good words about him. However, the No. 1 thing, especially as his teammate, I want him to be healthy. So whenever he’s ready to go, I’m excited to get on the field with him and keep on growing my chemistry with him. He’s a fantastic player, and I can’t wait to have him back whenever he’s ready.”
Deuces ✌️ #LVvsDEN | 📺 CBS pic.twitter.com/0yh0pFwSwt
Since Klint Kubiak was a candidate for this job, I told you his entire offensive system is predicated on the ability to run the football. Something that the Silver and Black haven’t been able to do since week three. They did today. They ran for 143 rushing yards and were a factor the Broncos had to deal with.
Kubiak was pleased to finally find that…
