title: Projecting Vikings' Week 11 Inactive List: Who's Most Likely to Miss SNF vs. 49ers?
full_text:
Sunday Night Football's matchup between the 7-2 Vikings and 8-1 49ers feels like the most important game on the Week 11 schedule. Not only are two of the top teams in the NFC going head-to-head, but it will also be a great measuring stick for the Purple and Gold to test their stellar defense and new offense.
The prime-time contest is being held on neutral ground in Mexico City, but is considered a home game for San Francisco. The game will feel different since it is being played at 7,352 feet above sea level, higher than the highest stadium in the United States, Empower Field at Mile High Stadium in Denver, CO, with an elevation of 5,280 feet. That is a huge difference from U.S. Bank Stadium, which is approximately 840 feet above sea level.
This game will feel different for the Vikings in a lot of ways, but the team still needs to be prepared . That means having the best possible players available is essential, and choosing the right players to be inactive is essential.
Here are five players who are likely to inactive for the Vikings on Sunday Night Football.
Jordan Addison didn't practice all week and has been ruled out with his thumb injury. Minnesota is hoping they don't have to place him on short-term injured reserve, but this is the second week in a row that Minnesota will not have his services.
Jauan Jennings will likely fill in for Addison, and it will be interesting to see if he can develop a connection with starting quarterback Kirk Cousins. After a quiet start to the season, it would be nice to see Jennings become a factor for Minnesota.
Another player ruled out for Minnesota is quarterback Kyler Murray. Although he started the season as the Vikings' starter, he lost that job to Cousins and will be a backup when he is healthy enough to return to the team.
Minnesota should not be in a rush to get him back from injury since the team doesn't have a role for him at the moment. In fact, even if he fully recovers from his hamstring injury, head coach Kevin O'Connell will need to decide whether he or Wentz should be Cousins's backup.
Although he played in the Vikings' last two games, defensive lineman Elijah Williams has been a regular on Minnesota's inactive list. He saw playing time recently because of the ankle injury to Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins, but he is expected to play Sunday night.
Williams has played well in the last two games , so making him inactive will be a tough decision. If there wasn't so much depth and youth on the defensive line, he would definitely be suited up to play this weekend.
Tiernan has suited up for four games for the Vikings this year but has mostly been inactive. That's not surprising since he's played a total of 32 snaps this season: 14 on offense and 18 on special teams.
Since Minnesota's starting offensive tackles are good to go on Sunday and swing tackle Ryan Van Demark is also expected to play, there isn't much need for Tiernan to suit up unless the team needs him on special teams.
As has become the norm in Minnesota, Max Brosmer will be the Vikings' emergency quarterback. He will suit up, but he will only enter the game as the QB3 if Cousins and Wentz are unable to play against San Francisco.
Although he is suited up and can enter the game, he still counts as inactive because he can only enter the game in an emergency situation. Expect to see the 25-year-old quarterback on the sidelines and hope that he isn't needed on Sunday night.

title: Vikings at 49ers: Who Wins and Why in Week 11
full_text:
Bragging rights for the top team in the NFC are on the line Sunday night in Mexico City, and the winner between the Vikings and 49ers will bow to no one—at least for a week.
Minnesota has found new life under Kirk Cousins, and flaunted its newfound success by dismantling the Packers in Week 10. Meanwhile, San Francisco has been scoring over 40 points per game this month, and doesn't look to be slowing down anytime soon. It's the Vikings and Niners in Week 11, so let's get into who wins and why in this Sunday Night Football clash.
Two weeks ago this would've been a nightmare situation with Carson Wentz (or Max Brosmer) leading the offense into battle against the 8-1 Niners. But with Kirk Cousins now under center—and with a whole 12 days into the playbook—the Vikings offense figures to be respectable at the very minimum after putting up 30 last week at Green Bay.
Still, San Francisco did face Cousins just two weeks ago in his final game with Las Vegas, and picked him off three times in an ugly 38-17 loss. We'll chalk that up to Cousins needing to play heroball after his defense allowed almost 40, but the Niners clearly know how to attack him. Being without Jordan Addison certainly won't help either, but San Francisco isn't without their own issues.
The 49ers have allowed 29 or more points four times already this season, including to teams like the Cardinals and Falcons. The opportunity to score points is there, and only the Dolphins, Chargers and Panthers have fewer sacks than San Francisco. But All-Pro linebacker Fred Warner is scary, and the Vikings will need the grip strength of The Hulk to combat his five forced fumbles on the year.
Ultimately, this battle feels like a wash, and both squads will get their licks in. But where the real war lies is on the other side of the coin.
It's the best offense in the league going up against the best defense , and anything is possible. The 49ers are averaging 42 points over their last two outings, and the Vikings haven't given up more than 23 in a game all season. Something's gotta give.
The good news for the Vikings at least, is that Kyle Shanahan hasn't played Brian Flores well in the past. Brock Purdy was sacked six times and the Niners fell to the Vikings 17-23 in the last matchup in 2024, and this 2026 Minnesota defense is arguably the best Flores has ever had. There's no question that the Vikings will find ways to get to Purdy, but he's also in the running for MVP for a reason.
Mr. Irrelevant is completing 70% of his passes with an impressive 20/5 TD:INT ratio, and he's been doing it all without his best receivers for the most part. Mike Evans, who could return this week, has been out since Week 7, and Deebo Samuel finally returned last week after missing time too. Not to mention Ricky Pearsall will miss the entire season. The running back duo of Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black are also averaging a smooth 4.5 yards per carry with 12 combined rushing scores.
Still, if Minnesota can find ways to keep Purdy guessing, there's a good chance that the blitzes get home, and that's clearly been a winning formula.

title: 3 Aging Vikings Veterans Who Clearly Need Rookie Replacements in 2027
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings are a contender during the 2026 NFL season, but it is never too soon to think about the future of the franchise. As players get older, the team needs to prepare to move on from some veteran players before they start becoming a detriment to the team.
The Vikings have prepared at some positions. For example, star safety Harrison Smith is 37 years old and likely in his final year in the NFL. Minnesota has already prepared for life without the "Hitman" by drafting Jakobe Thomas in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft.
There are three players on Minnesota's roster whom general manager Nolan Teasley will want to replace with a rookie for the next season. All three players have contributed to the team, making their replacement an essential task.
Long snapper Andrew DePaola is in his seventh season with the Vikings and his 12th season in the NFL. He has been named to the Pro Bowl three times, All-Pro First Team twice, and All-Pro Second Team twice. He is the oldest player on Minnesota's roster and has been a solid part of the special teams unit since his arrival.
The Vikings have a 25-year-old kicker and a 26-year-old punter. When two of the special teams trio is so young, Minnesota will want to find a young long snapper to grow and develop with the other specialists to provide consistency for many years to come.
Although this is his first season with the Vikings, Kyle Van Noy is the second-oldest edge rusher in the NFL, behind only Khalil Mack of the Los Angeles Chargers. The veteran defender is thriving in a backup/rotational role in Minnesota, registering 2.5 sacks while playing 35.5 percent of the team's defensive snaps.
His 71.5 Pro Football Focus grade shows his effectiveness this year, and his 78.9 run defense grade only increases his value. Unless the Vikings feel confident in Chaz Chambliss, Bo Richter, Tyler Batty, or one of the team's practice squad edge rushers filling that gap, the position could be addressed early in the 2027 NFL Draft.
Thirty-three isn't ancient for a quarterback, but Carson Wentz may have played his final game as a Pro in Week 9 against the Buffalo Bills. Wentz looked like the wear and tear on his body caught up to him in that historically bad performance , and Minnesota needs to prepare for a future without him.
Quarterback is the most important position in football, and having a quality backup is essential. Even though the future starter is still up in the air, drafting a passer to develop would be smart, even if the Vikings bring back a veteran like Kirk Cousins or Kyler Murray after this year.

title: 3 Most Important Things Vikings Fans Must Watch for South of the Border vs. 49ers in Week 11
full_text:
It’s often said that NFL teams wishing to make a deep playoff run need to play their best ball in December. For the 7-2 Minnesota Vikings, that timeframe may have been moved up a month. Sunday’s game against the 49ers in Mexico City marks the end of a brutal four-game stretch and a chance to come out 2-2 against four of the league's best teams.
The Vikings are riding the high of a quarterback boost at the trade deadline , a move that paid immediate dividends as the Vikings offense looked significantly better against the Packers. Still, it was far from a perfect outing, and head coach Kevin O’Connell is certainly hoping for an even better showing this week.
With Minnesota’s top-tier defense battling San Francisco’s elite offense, fans will have plenty of reason to pop some popcorn Sunday night. Let’s break down the top three things to watch closely.
It’s not often a late-November game carries this much weight , but the Cousins trade has significantly raised the ceiling of this 2026 Vikings squad. With competent offensive play, they can truly compete with the best in the league, and this year’s 49ers team meets that criteria.
San Francisco’s offense is averaging 31.2 points per game, the second-best in the league, while Minnesota’s defense is giving up a league-low 14 points per contest.
The playoff-seeding implications are also significant, even this early in the season. With the NFC quickly turning into an all-out war, the winner of this match will be set up nicely for a clear shot at the NFC’s top seed.
Odds for the 1 seed with a W/L this week. This is such a huge game: https://t.co/ur7HGxE6SL pic.twitter.com/Bv05UO8mNR
If you can’t wait for the atmosphere of playoff football, this game will be as close to the real thing as you can get in November.
Kirk Cousins hasn’t been a Las Vegas Raider for a week and a half now, but his last game in silver and black definitely left a bad taste in his mouth. Now, he’ll have the chance to make it right. Cousins and the Raiders faced off against the 49ers at Levi’s Stadium on Nov. 8, just two days before he was traded to the Vikings. His performance against San Francisco’s defense was a far cry from some of the impressive games he’s had this season.
The @49ers intercept Kirk Cousins and start the second half with a BANG 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/yv1RbSin4A
Cousins would end the day 22-of-32 for 216 yards, one passing touchdown, three interceptions, and a 58.9 passer rating. He also managed to score on a QB sneak, but I’m not sure O’Connell wants to rely on the legs of a 38-year-old pocket passer in this week’s matchup.
The veteran QB has the unique advantage of knowing what went wrong last time he met the 49ers, and he’ll certainly be in the film room with coaches, breaking down what he can do better this time around. Another shot against one of the best teams in the league, in an international primetime game, with massive playoff implications, isn’t exactly a pressure-free situation. But if Cousins comes out victorious, he’ll take another step toward proving his doubters wrong.
Sunday will be a massive opportunity for two former 49ers. Wide receiver Jauan Jennings and running back Jordan Mason were both on the opposing sidelines last time the Vikings and Niners met. Now, they’ll face off against their former teammates for the first time since their respective departures.
Mr. Jordan Mason, ladies and gentleman 👏 📺: #SFvsMIN on CBS/Paramount+ 📱: https://t.co/waVpO909ge pic.twitter.com/3Siu49Kcnm
The Vikings acquired Mason from the 49ers via trade in March 2025 and signed Jennings as a free agent this past May. Both played important roles in the San Francisco offense during their time in the Bay, so their insight will be critical for Brian Flores and his defense. So far, Jennings has appeared in six games this season, while Mason has only appeared in five. Sunday seems like the perfect time for both to be on the field against their former team.
I expect both to have plenty of opportunities to impact the game, but Jennings may be due for a true breakout with Jordan Addison injured.

title: Vikings-Daniel Jones Reunion Makes No Sense Despite Immediate Speculation After Release
full_text:
Just days after the Vikings engaged in trade talks for Daniel Jones (h/t ESPN' s Adam Schefter), the Colts have now released the quarterback following a brutal 26-3 loss against Houston.
The Colts rebuffed trade interest in Daniel Jones from the Minnesota Vikings and Baltimore Ravens. And 10 days after the NFL’s trade deadline, the Colts now have released Jones.
After getting spurned by the Colts, the Vikings moved on, landing Kirk Cousins from Las Vegas instead—a move that has clearly already paid dividends . Indianapolis clearly has made an absolute mess of this situation, turning away potential deals only to cut Jones a week later. Teams have until 4 p.m. ET on Monday to put in a waiver claim for him, according to NFL insider Mike Garafolo.
But should the Vikings now look to pick up the Colts' former starter?
As ESPN 's Field Yates proved, the Vikings are an obvious candidate for Jones, who spent time on the practice squad in 2024 and was very nearly Minnesota's starter in 2025 until Indianapolis swooped in with a better offer. While the familiarity is there, and so was the interest as recently as last week, adding Jones now comes with plenty of complications.
Presuming Daniel Jones clears waivers on Monday at 4 PM ET, I wonder if the Vikings will bring him aboard as their back-up QB. He finished the season there following his Giants release. https://t.co/top26wUrg8
The first big hurdle is that Jones will be guaranteed $10 million in 2027 by whichever team claims him. That may be a price the Vikings are unwilling to pay with Cousins already in line as a possible bridge starter for next year. There's a real chance Minnesota takes a rookie quarterback in next spring's draft, and rostering Jones along with Cousins—who also has a $10 million guarantee—does seem a bit overkill for a team that still needs to extend several key starters .
Beyond the money, Jones—how do I put this delicately—isn't good at football right now. He ranks dead last this season in QBR and has twice as many turnovers as he does touchdowns. Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz weren't exactly lighting the NFL on fire either, but it's a tough argument to make to say that Jones would provide better play than either at this point.
Jones hasn't thrown for over 200 yards in more than a month, and his mobility—once a great facet of his game—is essentially non-existent after the Achilles tear. Murray is still theoretically ascending in this new offense, and Jones clearly isn't the same player from before.
Perhaps head coach Kevin O'Connell and the Vikings think they can fix Jones, but is it really worth the time in Week 11 with Cousins still re-acclimating ? The answer is surely an emphatic 'No.' Adding to an already busy quarterback room just feels like a headache that the offensive staff doesn't need at this point in the season, and the cons far outweigh the pros.
Ultimately, the Vikings may be tempted to get a player for 'free' just days after looking to give up draft compensation for him, but with Cousins now established and Murray on the mend, adding Jones makes little sense. The time, money and effort needed to give Jones any semblance of value to the Vikings is more trouble than it's worth, and 'Indiana Jones' shouldn't become 'Minnesota Jones' any time soon.

title: Vikings' Afterthought Could Get His Long-Awaited Opportunity Amid Isaiah Rodgers Injury Concerns
full_text:
Week 11 is a huge time for the Purple and Gold as the Vikings prepare for a pivotal Sunday Night Football matchup against the all-powerful 49ers . It's the kind of game that will validate the legitimacy of Minnesota's Super Bowl aspirations, making it clear that both sides of the ball must step up to beat San Francisco this weekend.
Players can only help if they're dressed to do so, though. Although certain Vikings have made themselves indispensable to the team's plans each week, others are struggling to even see a handful of snaps come their way.
That's the case for one rookie defender, who's clearly fallen out of defensive coordinator Brian Flores's plans now that the second half of the 2026 campaign is underway.
The Vikings' latest draft class has had varying levels of success this season. Guys like Caleb Banks, Domonique Orange, Jake Golday, and Max Bredeson have found weekly roles (big or small), while Caleb Tiernan and Demond Claiborne have had opportunities to prove themselves. Even Jakobe Thomas's outlook is on the rise after finally being activated in Week 10.
Taking the above into account, one has to wonder if first-year cornerback Charles "Chuck" Demmings will see legitimate defensive action this season.
Demmings's usage has been sparse, as he's barely played any defensive snaps. But things could change for the rookie after the latest injury news coming out of Minnesota.
On Friday, the Vikings' latest injury report revealed that CB Isaiah Rodgers (quad) is officially questionable for Week 11's clash with the 49ers. He was limited in Thursday and Friday's practices after missing Wednesday's session.
Final #Vikings injury report OUT: WR Jordan Addison and QB Kyler Murray QUESTIONABLE: CB Isaiah Rodgers and S Jay Ward pic.twitter.com/c0rANSvTNV
Rodgers has played 83% of defensive snaps (467) and owns the 14th-best coverage grade (73.7) among 105 cornerbacks on Pro Football Focus , so it's safe to say a potential absence would be felt.
At the same time, any missed time for Rodgers could be an opportunity for Demmings to prove himself.
Drafted 163rd overall in April, Demmings quickly became a Vikings fan favorite throughout the offseason . Between his personality-filled interviews and the fact that his coverage frustrated Justin Jefferson during practice, there was hope that the S.F. Austin product could be a legitimate contributor in Minnesota's secondary as early as his rookie season. He added to that optimism by finishing the preseason with a 64.5 coverage grade after allowing only 2-of-6 passes for 38 yards and a 56.3 passer rating while recording a break-up, per Pro Football Focus .
Instead, it's safe to say that Demmings has become an afterthought at best.
The 23-year-old CB has played two defensive snaps (compared to 29 on special teams) in his four appearances, both opportunities coming against the Buccaneers in Week 3. He's only played one game since then, and while a few absences were due to a hamstring injury, he's also been a healthy scratch multiple times.
As great as it'd be to see what Demmings can do in regular-season action, he'll likely remain a victim of circumstance for the rest of the season. The Vikings' cornerback room is too deep and talented to justify taking away someone else's playing time for him. As Sports Illustrated 's Trevor Ripley said earlier this week : "Who is going to pull Isaiah Rodgers, Byron Murphy, or James Pierre for Charles Demmings?"
The CB trio has exceeded expectations this season, and removing one from the equation would be a massive blow to Flores & Co.'s defense. Injuries in the secondary could also create opportunities to see the field, but nothing is guaranteed—especially when the Rodgers-Murphy-Pierre connection hasn't missed a game yet.
That said, Rodgers will become an unrestricted free agent in March, and while some fans want to re-sign him, a potential exit would open the door for Demmings to challenge for a bigger role next summer. Then it'll be up to him to put what he learned this season into action.
For now, Sunday Night Football could be a preview of what that future might look like if Rodgers isn't healthy enough to take on San Francisco.
If he gets a chance this weekend, it'll be interesting to see whether Demmings can erase any talk about him being an afterthought. He has the talent to develop into a solid contributor one day, but Rodgers's injury might speed up that process. The Vikings need players who can make an immediate impact and help with their championship dreams, and Demmings is now in a position to prove he can be that guy.

title: 3 Bold Vikings Predictions Before Week 11 SNF vs. 49ers in Mexico City
full_text:
Even if you’re not a fan of the Vikings or 49ers, Sunday night’s primetime match in Mexico City is the definition of a “must-watch.” Two of the best teams in the NFL colliding on the international stage, with playoff seeding and bragging rights on the line, is everything the NFL dreamed of when it set the 2026 schedule last spring.
The stakes could not be much higher for a late-November game, and I expect both teams to put on a show. With a newfound Kirk Cousins-sized confidence boost in Minnesota , the Vikings should be set up well to meet the moment.
Here are three things I see happening Sunday night at Estadio Banorte.
The 49ers have been one of the most balanced offenses in the NFL, averaging a league-high 399.8 yards per game. They’re averaging the seventh-most passing yards per game at 255.8 and the third-most rushing yards per game at 144. San Francisco is also second in the league with 31.2 points per game.
Simply put, the 49ers' offense can move the ball any way it needs to.
The Minnesota Vikings defense ranks 1st in dropback success rate allowed, per @SumerSports The San Francisco 49ers offense ranks 1st in dropback success rate and has the highest dropback success rate of any team through 10 weeks since the 2018 Saints
The Vikings' defense, on the other hand, has allowed the fewest points (14) and the second-fewest yards (236.1) per game to opposing offenses. They’ve also held their own against some of the league's best offenses, holding Detroit, Buffalo, and Green Bay to 19, 23, and 10 points over the last few weeks. Now that they have a dependable QB to keep the offense on the field, they’ll be able to catch their breath in the high altitude of Mexico City. Minnesota's defense will need all hands on deck to slow down an elite offense, but Brian Flores will certainly have his unit ready.
Give me the Vikings defense to hold the 49ers under 330 total yards and 24 points.
The Vikings signed Jauan Jennings this past May for two main reasons: to open up the run game as a blocker and to be a reliable third wide receiver after Jalen Nailor’s departure in free agency. So far, neither has materialized the way head coach Kevin O’Connell and interim general manager Rob Brzezinski had hoped.
Jennings has also missed the Vikings’ past two games with a calf injury, after previously missing Week 2 to attend to a personal family matter. Now, with Jennings set to return against his former team and WR2 Jordan Addison missing time, the former 49er has his chance to shine .
Jennings’s struggles this season have largely been due to poor quarterbacking. The 29-year-old has certainly been open, and Cousins may be the perfect passer to actually get him the ball. I predict that Jennings finds new life and scores at least one touchdown against his former team on Sunday night.
This may already be the NFL’s game of the year. The well-balanced 49ers against the blitz-happy Vikings is a matchup made for the primetime stage. But who says this has to be their only meeting?
In fact, if both teams continue on their current paths, a late-round playoff matchup may be an inevitable sequel.
We simulated the rest of the season using PFN’s NFL Playoff Predictor. 🔮 Here’s the projected playoff bracket 👀 pic.twitter.com/QBo8zogNJ6
There’s a lot of football to be played, and neither team is in the easiest of divisions, but these are two squads built for postseason success. You may need to bookmark this one, but I predict that Sunday will not be the last time we see Minnesota and San Francisco battle this year.
Whoever takes round two may end up having Valentine’s Day plans at SoFi Stadium.

title: 3 Vikings Contract Extensions That Must Be Hammered Out in 2nd Half of Season
full_text:
We're nearing the end of November, and the Vikings are focused on what's left of the 2026 NFL season. With a 7-2 record and the rejuvenated energy of starting quarterback Kirk Cousins's return , expectations are high that the Purple and Gold will be contenders in the second half of the campaign.
However, it is never too soon to prepare for the future . Several Vikings contributors are scheduled to become free agents at the conclusion of this season. General manager Nolan Teasley and the Minnesota front office will want to work out extensions for key players as soon as possible.
The longer Teasley waits to offer an extension to these players, the more their price tag will likely rise. Locking down these three players first would go a long way toward preparing for the 2027 NFL season to be able to evaluate the salary cap situation moving forward.
Vikings edge rusher Andrew Van Ginkel is tied for second in the NFL in sacks this season with 8.5. The combination of him and Dallas Turner has been a recipe for success this year in defensive coordinator Brian Flores's defense.
Van Ginkel's 66.8 Pro Football Focus grade might not look special , but his 32 quarterback pressures, two forced fumbles, two fumble recoveries, and one interception go a bit further in showing what he means to Minnesota's defense.
Andrew Van Ginkel just took it right from him! MINvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/qROgreyURh
The 31-year-old defender is currently playing on a one-year, $23 million contract, but is playing 81% of the Vikings' defensive snaps and is important in Flores's squad and should be a top priority to bring back.
Like Van Ginkel, Blake Cashman has been a cornerstone of the Vikings' defense this season. He has played 94.3% of possible defensive snaps this season. Although he missed last week's game against the Packers while recovering from a concussion , he should return to the lineup soon.
Cashman has an 86.8 PFF grade this season, ranking him second among qualifying linebackers. He has excelled in coverage, earning an 82.6 PFF grade, but has also thrived as a pass rusher, generating 16 pressures and four sacks while blitzing.
Blake Cashman steps up for the sack 😤 INDvsMIN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/MSl2dfO6k7
The 30-year-old defender is in the final year of his three-year, $22.5 million contract with Minnesota and is in line for a raise for his play over the last few seasons. The Vikings' front office should prioritize keeping him on a multi-year extension.
The secret about Jalen Redmond is o ut . Although he is scheduled to become a restricted free agent after this season, getting an extension done now would save Minnesota from having to match any offer sheet another team offers him.
Redmond ranks fourth among defensive linemen with an 83.7 PFF grade. generating 25 quarterback pressures, resulting in 19 hurries, three hits, and three sacks. His 90.0 PFF run-defense grade ranks him first among all defensive linemen this year, underscoring his effectiveness.
Jalen Redmond was incredible against the Bills. 5 pressures, half a sack, and his usual great run defense. He's playing at an All-Pro level this season. pic.twitter.com/7bEsuRnyDV
It is shocking that Redmond is on a one-year, $1.075 million deal this year. The Vikings will need to give the 27-year-old defender a generous offer to reward him for playing on this relatively small contract and keep him around on Minnesota's defensive line.

title: Patriots Could Catch Major Break This Week vs. Chargers
full_text:
The New England Patriots are likely turning to their backup quarterback this week . But lucky for them, the Los Angeles Chargers might also be doing the same thing.
After the Chargers' 27-24 loss to the New York Jets on Sunday, it was announced that starting quarterback Justin Herbert was in concussion protocol and was being evaluated for a concussion. Because of the five-step plan that's in place for any player in the protocol, that puts Herbert's game status for Week 12 in the air.
So who might match up with Tommy DeVito next week ? Meet D.J. Uiagalelei, the Chargers' backup.
Uiagalelei was signed by Los Angeles as an undrafted free agent last season and spent all of 2025 on the practice squad. The 25-year-old inked a futures contract with the team in January after the season.
This past summer, Uiagalelei was competing with former first round pick Trey Lance for the QB2 job, losing out and getting released during roster cuts. Lance was later placed on IR in October and Uiagalelei made the leap to the backup role.
He hasn't played much since entering the league. In Week 9 against the Houston Texans, he went 2-for-7 with 24 yards and one passing touchdown in injury relief for Herbert. That's been the only game action he's gotten in a regular season/playoff game.
This week could be a tough test for him, considering how — on paper — the Patriots defense can make things difficult for opposing quarterbacks. The last two weeks, however, the Patriots allowed 45 and 35 points to the Packers and Lions, respectively.
After coming off a bye week, that group should be ready to go if they're lined up against Uiagalelei.
The reason why this game was flexed out of Sunday Night Football is now becoming more and more obvious. The Patriots sit at 5-5 and are without Drake Maye for the foreseeable future. The Chargers' 1-9 is tied for the worse in the NFL and now they'll also potentially have to start a backup.
This has all the makings for being a wonky game for both sides, and a real opportunity for DeVito to prove to New England that he can handle the elevated workload under center.
As a backup, he's made appearances in three games this season, completing 16 passes on 32 attempts for 132 yards and one touchdown. He also threw an interception two weeks ago against Detroit across the middle.
We'll learn more about Herbert's status as the week progresses, but for now, time to pencil in DeVito vs. Uiagalelei into your scorecards.

title: Patriots' Playoff Outlook Improves Following Sunday's Week 11 Slate
full_text:
The New England Patriots didn't play this week and sat at home on their bye week. Despite a rough two weeks where they've allowed 80 points and lost Drake Maye and A.J. Brown to injuries , they got some good news when it came to their standing in the AFC.
Three teams that are competing with the Patriots for a spot as a potential wild card team all lost on Sunday, opening the door for the Patriots to potentially steal a playoff spot as the postseason push rolls on.
The Pittsburgh Steelers, Baltimore Ravens and Las Vegas Raiders all lost their games and the Patriots — who already played the Steelers and Raiders this season — gained some very important ground in the AFC, something that could loom large when the calendar flips to December and January.
Here's a look at how the Patriots ended up having a good Sunday in Week 11.
The Patriots already have played Steelers this year, beating them 20-3 in Week 2 . Despite the Steelers having a better record, their loss to former Patriots quarterback Joe Milton and the Philadelphia Eagles dropped them to just one game above New England.
Milton, a sixth-round draft pick by the Patriots back in 2024, went 11-for-21 for 141 yards in a 19-16 win. Pittsburgh's offense really couldn't keep up and after D.K. Metcalf got ejected in the second half, the Steelers really fell behind.
It also helps the Patriots that an NFC team emerged victorious against an AFC team. Should Pittsburgh and New England finish with the same record at the end of the season, the Patriots would hold the head-to-head tiebreaker and finish above them in the standings.
Another former Patriots quarterback, Jacoby Brissett, suited up elsewhere for the Ravens, but wasn't able to win the game. A matchup with the Carolina Panthers was filled with turnovers, trick plays and a lot of excitement, and the home Panthers ended up winning 35-33. Brissett's fourth down throw was picked off by Tyrel Dodson to seal it.
The Ravens entered Sunday below .500 with a 4-6 record and fall further down in the AFC North. They've really struggled amid a six-game losing streak and are now at risk of tumbling out of contention.
The Patriots and Ravens don't play this season and are likely competing for one of the wild card spots at the bottom of the playoff picture. However, they may end up going head-to-head for free agent quarterback Daniel Jones, who was released by the Indianapolis Colts this week . Both teams are reportedly willing to show interest in him after they've dealt with quarterback injuries.
The Raiders came back from 17-0 down, but a trio of Jonah Coleman touchdowns led to the Broncos pulling out a 38-24 victory from the Mile High city. It was the second-career start for first overall pick Fernando Mendoza and the Raiders dropped to 4-7 with the loss.
Just like the Steelers, the Patriots have the head-to-head tiebreaker over Las Vegas . They lit up the scoreboard in a 45-17 win at Gillette Stadium in Week 6, where Mendoza came in for his first NFL snaps in mop-up duty.
The Patriots didn't end up jumping up into the playoff picture , as the Cleveland Browns — who own a better record than the Patriots — were also on their bye week. But it was a net-positive Sunday for New England. Here's a look at how the standings look pre-Sunday Night Football.

3. Cincinnati Bengals, 7-2
4. Jacksonville Jaguars, 7-3
5. Kansas City Chiefs, 8-2
7. Pittsburgh Steelers, 6-4
In The Hunt: New England Patriots, 5-5
In The Hunt: Houston Texans, 4-6

If the Patriots can stay afloat in the AFC and beat the winnable games on their schedule (on the road against the Chargers and Jets, and at home against the Dolphins), things could get really interesting for the AFC's sixth or seventh seeds.
As it stands right now, winning the AFC East for the second-straight year seems unobtainable, especially with the Bills beating the Dolphins 26-9 at home. For now, the Patriots will be competing for a chance to stay alive in any way possible.

title: 3 Patriots Who'll Need to Meet Larger Expectations After Bye Week
full_text:
After this week, the New England Patriots are set to rattle off seven-straight weeks of football games. How they look will be a major factor into whether this team gets into the playoffs without starting quarterback Drake Maye .
Back-to-back losses by this Patriots team has put them at .500 heading into their Week 11 bye, and something has to change. The defense allowed 80 points in the last two games combined and the offense is seeing the challenges of having to play without some of their best players healthy.
With some really difficult games looming on the schedule, here are some Patriots players who'll need to step up and meet some of the high expectations set out for them — including one player who is now forced into the starting lineup.
Though no fault of his own, DeVito will be under the microscope moving forward. Tasked with replacing Maye during a playoff push isn't an ideal scenario, and when you factor in how he looked against Detroit last week, the hopes might not be all that positive right now.
But how will the backup-turned-starter perform? Will he step up and start playing competitive football? Will he wilt away and the Patriots continue to lose? Does he play well enough to keep New England afloat when January rolls around ? We'll see, but the Patriots' newest starter will have plenty of eyes on him.
Barmore is the fourth-highest paid player on the Patriots roster, earning $21 million a year. He hasn't lived up to that price tag in 2026, as the veteran defensive tackle's snaps continue to drop in recent weeks. He played a season-low 22 snaps last week and is playing less than Cory Durden up front.
After this season, Barmore doesn't have any more guaranteed money on his contract that he signed in 2024. He'll need to start getting on the field more and making a larger impact to potentially earn a roster spot once 2027 rolls around.
The year began with Gonzalez inking the largest contract for a cornerback in NFL history. He's also making $33.75 million a season, making his per year deal the richest on the Patriots. In the last two games, he has been the worst version of him since being drafted. Gonzalez has allowed 12 receptions for 271 yards and three touchdowns, according to NFL Next Gen Stats.
Gonzalez has dealt with a shoulder injury and did nab his first interception of the season against the Lions, and his future with New England is certainly set in stone. But based on how he's played, the Patriots will certainly need to realize that teams are going to start picking on one of the league's top man-to-man corners a lot more.

title: Drake Maye's Initial Injury Timeline Gives Patriots Reason for Optimism
full_text:
Could Drake Maye end up playing again this season ? That door hasn't been officially shut yet.
According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , the New England Patriots quarterback is out for "at least six weeks" after breaking his fibula in last week's 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions. The plan for the Patriots is to roll with backup quarterback Tommy DeVito as the starter.
Maye got hurt after getting sacked on the game's opening drive last week and left the game shortly afterwards. He didn't travel back to the United States with the Patriots and instead stayed back in Munich, Germany for more testing. He's since returned, but won't be ready to play for at least a month.
Six weeks takes the Patriots to Jan. 3, where they may potentially play against the Denver Broncos at home (the game isn't officially set yet and could be flexed to the day before). When it comes to Maye's health, that's the first priority that the Patriots need to worry about.
But at the end of the day, if the Patriots could end up sneaking into the playoffs with DeVito as their quarterback, Maye might be able to push it to get back onto the field. That's a far cry from some reports that suggested he'd be out for the remainder of the year.
Now, of course, Maye could still end up missing the rest of 2026. If the Patriots, who are currently sitting at 5-5, don't end up beating the likes of the Minnesota Vikings, Kansas City Chiefs, Buffalo Bills or Broncos, the season could end at Week 18.
For now, it will be DeVito taking snaps as the starting quarterback as the Patriots look ahead to a Week 12 road matchup with the Los Angeles Chargers.
"I think he'll be ready to go coming out of the bye," Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said Monday. "I think that he'll be able to look at some things and understand, whether that's being able to transfer up into the pocket, get us in the right play, get the ball out quicker or look at protections or rotation, whatever that may be. I think that'll all improve. So, I have a lot of confidence in Tommy. I know his toughness is going to be through the charts, and his competitiveness will be exactly what we need."
Rookie Behren Morton is the only other quarterback on the 53-man roster. The Patriots could also show interest in veteran Daniel Jones, who was recently released by the Indianapolis Colts .
If the Patriots place Maye on injured reserve, that means he'd be required to miss at least four games. They also only have three return designations left in the regular season, and two of them are likely going to Romeo Doubs and Alijah Vera-Tucker.
At the end of the day, Maye's injury puts a damper on a season with high expectations. But the door remains open a bit.

title: 2 Key Patriots Named to Top Free Agent List for 2027
full_text:
With the 2026 season looking like it's starting to fade away, let's take a quick look at how the New England Patriots might have to approach the 2027 offseason.
A recent list from Sports Illustrated ranked the top 50 pending free agents heading into next offseason, and a pair of key Patriots veterans were mentioned. Offensive guard Mike Onwenu, who's out for the year with a broken ankle, was ranked No. 16, while safety Kevin Byard was ranked No. 44.
Both players entered the season being key players on either side of the ball, but like most of the Patriots season this year, hasn't turned out the greatest. Here's a look at both players' roles in the Patriots organization, and what could happen after the season.
The Patriots reworked Onwenu's contract ahead of the season, and the starting right guard has been the longest-tenured player on the team. But he broke his ankle early into Week 2 against the Pittsburgh Steelers and was subsequently placed on IR. Now his status for 2027 is up in the air.
"Onwenu taking a hefty $7.5 million pay cut could mean his days in New England are numbered. Still, he’s a quality, versatile lineman who has given Drake Maye more time to operate compared to other players on the Patriots’ offensive line," SI's Gilberto Manzano wrote. "In seven seasons with New England, Onwenu has made 92 career starts, including several games at tackle."
He's one of the league's most versatile offensive linemen and has been a key part of some of these recent New England teams. And after he went down, the offensive line started to fall apart. Backups Greg Van Roten, Ben Brown and Walter Rouse all have dealt with injuries and the hole left by Onwenu on the right side is being felt big time.
He's 28 years old and is still playing good football, but the Patriots have to be aware of the hefty price tag that's looming over Maye's head. The Patriots also have a decision to make when it comes to starting right tackle Morgan Moses, who has a potential out after this year.
Byard spent time with Mike Vrabel when he was the head coach of the Tennessee Titans, but hasn't really looked like the same player. He's been consistently on the field and always vocal with the media, but other than his two interceptions, has struggled in bringing players down.
"The 33-year-old Byard has shown his age at times in his first season with the Patriots. But he makes up for what he lacks in coverage with his ball skills," Manzano wrote. "He has two interceptions and five passes defensed, and it bodes well that he has been entrusted to play 95% of the defensive snaps. In 2025, Byard had a league-high seven interceptions with the Bears."
Along with Craig Woodson, Byard has been a constant in the Patriots secondary, one of two primary defensive backs to not miss a game this season (cornerback Marcus Jones has also played in 10 games). Against the Detroit Lions last week, he really struggled when it came to playing in space, but his ability to take the ball away helps this unit.
The Patriots signed Byard to a one-year, $7 million deal in free agency ahead of the season, but he may end up being a player who'll be put on retirement watch depending on how the rest of the year goes.

title: Patriots Must Shut A.J. Brown Down for the Remainder of 2026
full_text:
I've been very positive when it came to the A.J. Brown situation with the New England Patriots this year. I thought the trade was the right move to make back in June. I had high expectations after watching him shine in training camp. I kept up a positive outlook when he returned off of injured reserve.
But with the wide receiver now reportedly set to miss several weeks with a hamstring injury, it's time to call a spade a spade. Based on early returns, the Patriots, 10 games in, have lost the Brown trade and it's time to shut the receiver down for the rest of the season.
It's been a mess, and it's only going to get worse if the team doesn't pull the plug.
With Drake Maye out with a fractured fibula and likely set to miss the rest of the season, the year is a lost cause — regardless of what happens at quarterback. Keep Tommy DeVito under center, promote Behren Morton, sign Daniel Jones. Doesn't matter. The 5-5 Patriots are still alive for the postseason, but the beeps on that vital signs machine are slowing down.
It's time to just have Brown finish the season on IR. There's no reason to trot him out there on Sundays.
The Patriots knew he had injury issues in his past, and executive vice president of player personnel Eliot Wolf felt confident in the team's assessment of him when they sent two draft picks to the Philadelphia Eagles back in June . He looked great in the summer and the Maye-to-Brown connection was going to take this offense to new heights.
Then comes a high-ankle sprain suffered in the opener. He's out for four games and that chemistry with his quarterback, out the window.
Then when it's time to get him back after missing four games, his performances against the Jets and Bears were dismal. Six receptions, 85 yards and multiple drops.
Then the knee issue — something he's dealt with when he was with Tennessee and Philadelphia — flared up. It forced him to miss two more games. Brown was clearly fighting through injury and the team, strapped for healthy players amid their injury-riddled campaign, probably forced him back too soon.
Then a hamstring injury comes up after making his second catch against the Lions in Germany. He walked off the field, headed into the blue medical tent and then promptly into the Patriots locker room. The Patriots lost 35-10, their second-straight loss.
At this point, the Patriots need to look at Brown, all bruised and battered, and not make this any worse. He's played in four games, caught 11 passes and is dealing with three times the lower-body injuries than he has touchdowns.
Operating under the assumption that the Patriots won't make the playoffs, they have just three IR return designations — and two of them are likely going to wide receiver Romeo Doubs and offensive guard Alijah Vera-Tucker, who are both eligible to be activated next week. Brown is able to be placed on IR again, but would have to miss another four weeks.
Is it even worth using up a potential return on a receiver who's spent more time on the injury report than the end zone this year?
The Patriots are facing a gauntlet of a schedule after their bye and with whoever is throwing passes, it's not going to be a good outlook for the oft-injured Brown.
I've been very positive about Brown, the lifelong Patriots fan, making an impact in New England in 2026.
But right now, the best move that the team can make is just to rip the cord from the power socket on the year and get him ( and his quarterback/next-door locker mate ) healthy for 2027.

title: Patriots Have No Excuse Not to Pursue Daniel Jones After Colts Release
full_text:
After a disaster of a performance on Thursday Night Football, the Indianapolis Colts officially released quarterback Daniel Jones.
They've now promoted Anthony Richardson to the starting spot and now Jones, who was in the second year of his two-year, $88 million contract with the Colts, is subject to waivers (and free agency, if he doesn't get claimed).
Do the New England Patriots, still reeling from the ankle injury of Drake Maye, try to get Jones under center and try and right the ship? They should.
First off, the Colts totally botched Jones' situation. Clearly struggling and needing to try and rebuild for the future, the team passed on trading both Jones (who had reported interest from the Minnesota Vikings and Baltimore Ravens) and running back Jonathan Taylor. One week after the deadline, and Jones is no longer a Colt.
With that being said, the Patriots have just Tommy DeVito and Behren Morton in the building at quarterback sans Maye . DeVito has started games in the NFL before (replacing Jones on the New York Giants back in 2023), but didn't look all that inspiring against the Detroit Lions last week in Germany.
The Patriots are 5-5 and yes, still very much in the thick of the AFC postseason picture. Jones offers a style of quarterback play that, if used correctly, could correlate with a Josh McDaniels-style of offense. He's had experience with Brian Daboll, a disciple of McDaniels, and could slot in under center in New England.
But this year isn't a good assessment of Jones' play. Through 11 games, the 29-year-old is 205-for-351 (58.4%) with 1,974 passing yards, seven touchdowns and 13 interceptions — the most in the NFL. Last night against the Houston Texans in primetime, he went 12-for-27 with 144 yards and a pick.
Not all that great. When you consider the defenses the Patriots are going to facing heading into the stretch run (Minnesota Vikings, Kansas City Chiefs, Denver Broncos), it might not get that much better.
The Patriots can't afford to miss out, though. DeVito didn't play well in his elevated opportunity and rookie Morton hasn't taken a snap in a regular season game. Sure, they might have the playbook down pat heading into Week 12, but Jones' ceiling, albeit low, is still higher.
Jones is subject to waivers now, and any team that puts in a claim for him would take on about $2 million in 2026 salary, plus more than $10 million in injury guarantees in 2027. If he goes unclaimed, the chances that a team throws a dart at him on their quarterback dartboard increases.
The Patriots have the 16th waiver claim and the Ravens — who traded for Jacoby Brissett at the deadline — have the 14th. The Vikings also swung a deal for Kirk Cousins, so both of those teams feel like longshots to add him. There really isn't any other major suitor in play right now.
The Colts haven't been good and Jones is a big reason why. But with the Patriots teetering on a midseason collapse and needing to find a quarterback capable of playing (and fast), it's worth kicking the tires on the veteran.

title: Patriots HC Mike Vrabel Describes Leadership Plan Heading Out of Bye Week
full_text:
For Mike Vrabel, he's focused on fixing the problem. The problem for the New England Patriots through 10 weeks? It's a myriad of things, which includes tackling, injuries, offensive firepower, covering and a whole lot of miscues that cause a team to be 5-5.
But the Patriots head coach isn't going to try and patch things up with his voice. This week, when asked about what his message was to the fans after a second-straight bad loss to an NFC North team, Vrabel said he's more worried about improving.
"I think the biggest thing is that I believe in trying to say less and try to do more," Vrabel said Monday. "So, to sit here and try to sell some message, I think that our fans in the year and a half that we've been here recognize when we have our chance to win the football game, put ourselves in position, don't stall out drives, don't make mistakes, don't give up big plays, get stops on third down, all those things that we know that leads to winning, especially against good teams."
But as the Patriots sit quietly on their bye week, and their quarterback Drake Maye potentially done for the season, the fanbase could use a jolt of energy. 45 points allowed to the Packers, then 35 to the Lions. Nothing seems to be going right for the Patriots ... and these next few weeks are going to be major chances for Vrabel to show that the team's culture and identity remains in tact.
Even in their wins, they haven't been totally consistent. Showing they can start to be a consistent team without Maye and try to scrape together some wins is a step in the right direction.
"We haven't had consistent performances. So, a lot of things lead to the performance, and that's the turnovers, the split-second decisions, the critical mistakes, the missed tackles, the drops," Vrabel said. "There's a bunch of stuff, and it all leads to being inconsistent. So, we need to have consistent actions.
"Again, we've talked about preparation. How we prepare is great. I thought that we had a good week, but the only thing that matters is how we perform and how we play on Sunday. So, we'll still have to continue to prepare, and we'll just have to find ways to play better and play more consistent."
As of now, it's safe to assume backup quarterback Tommy DeVito — who has starting experience — will take the reigns under center. He's capable, though it didn't come across against Detroit in Munich. If the defense can right the ship and start to look like a Vrabel-led team oozing with culture and confidence, this season doesn't have to be over for the Patriots.
But based on how they've looked, that might be a tall task for even Vrabel to fix.

title: Patriots' Robert Kraft, Bill Belichick Inch Closer to Pro Football Hall of Fame
full_text:
The Pro Football Hall of Fame announced Thursday that two of the biggest names in New England Patriots history — Robert Kraft and Bill Belichick — have moved one step closer to football immortality.
Both the Patriots chairman/owner and longtime head coach were named the finalist in their respective categories ahead of this winter's final selection meeting. Kraft, the contributor candidate, has been on the ballot for quite some time. Belichick, the coaching candidate , is in his second year as a possible inductee.
Kraft and Belichick will be two of 15 possible candidates that will be voted on by the Pro Football Hall of Fame selection meeting ahead of Super Bowl LXI. Per newly-installed bylaws, a candidate must receive 80% or more of the vote to be inducted. The 15-group ballot will be trimmed down to seven, and voters must select six of the seven for induction.
Here's a quick look at the qualifications of both Patriots legends, and how they've (somehow) been left out of the halls of Canton, Ohio, to this point in time.
Belichick's nine Super Bowl appearances and six Super Bowl wins as a head coach are NFL records, and yet somehow he was left out of induction last year in his first year of eligibility . His 302 regular season wins are third-most in league history and his 31 playoff wins are the most ever. There isn't a coach more qualified to earn a bust in Canton than Belichick.
And yet, he was snubbed a year ago and drew a lot of cricitism. Since then, the Pro Football Hall of Fame has changed a lot of how the voting process happens, including shrinking the voting pool, removing the senior category for players. Now, candidates like Belichick and Kraft are on the same ballot as the players.
The legendary head coach, who's now leading the University of North Carolina, was hired in 2000 to replace Pete Carroll on the sideline. Since then, he was able to build the league's greatest two-decade dynasty and help orchestrate the growth of the greatest player of all time (Tom Brady).
Belichick left the Patriots following a 2023 season in which the team went 4-13 and ended up with the third overall pick. The 74-year-old beat out Tom Coughlin, Mike Holmgren, Dan Reeves and Mike Shanahan for the final spot.
Kraft has been a name in Hall of Fame conversations for more than a decade, and for good reason. Since purchasing the Patriots in 1994, the team has played in 11 Super Bowls — more than any other NFL owner — and won a league-high six.
Last year was the first time that Kraft , who grew up as a Patriots fan, made it past the contributor subcommittee. His absence from the Hall of Fame continued to make headlines each year, as Kraft's contributions to the league (including several TV deals and helping to end the 2011 lockout) have positively pushed the NFL forward.
Kraft advanced in the contributor category, beating out Ralph Hay, Virginia McCaskey, Doug Williams and John Wooten. He'd become the Patriots' first non-player/coach to be inducted into the Hall of Fame if selected.
"I think the ability to continue to grow this area, to grow what is Patriots, the Patriot Place and everything that surrounds this place. The success speaks for itself," Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said about Kraft on Nov. 4. "I think he's always continuing to grow the game. I think having these conversations as a coach now with Robert about the media deals, the ability to grow the game, trying to strengthen our relationship with the players and what's best for the game of football.
"I mean, he admittedly started out as a fan of the team and then obviously was able to buy them. I started out as a fan of the Browns. I didn't end up buying the Browns, but I played in the NFL, so I guess we all have a dream. He's certainly done a lot."
They could both be enshrined alongside former Patriots tight end Rob Gronkowski, who's eligible for the first time this year. He was the most recent inductee into the Patriots Hall of Fame this year .

title: 9 Former Patriots Selected in 2027 UFL Draft, Including Fan-Favorite QB
full_text:
Even with the NFL in full swing, there is always more football to be played. The United Football League, back for another season, just finished its 15-round draft for the 2027 season — and there are plenty of familiar faces that were selected.
Over the course of two days, nine former New England Patriots players — spanning from draft picks to futures signings — heard their names called by one of eight UFL teams. This year, New England got their own UFL team, with the Rhode Island Breakers set to debut in Pawtucket.
Here's a look at every former Patriot who'll now be suiting up this spring.
Once the apple of New England's eye, the 2023 undrafted free agent was a name to watch that season . An electric player at Louisville, Cunningham came to the Patriots as their third-string quarterback. He was given a few chances to also make the team at wide receiver, but only suited up in one game. Cunningham bounced around between the active roster and practice squad before being signed by the Baltimore Ravens.
The final draft pick of Jerod Mayo's first and only draft class with the Patriots, Bell was a project tight end who was more of a developmental player. He made the 53-man roster out of training camp and played in 15 games, but the Florida State alum caught two passes for 20 yards before being cut the following summer.
Carvin had a very short stint in New England, only being a member of their practice squad in 2024. After a ton of shifting up front, the Patriots signed Carvin on Aug. 24 and he remained with the team until Oct. 8. He'd later sign with the Jacksonville Jaguars (two seperate times) and the Houston Texans.
The first former Patriot to play for Rhode Island, Crossley was a part of the roster in some capacity for the last two years. An undrafted rookie out of SMU, the cornerback signed with the Patriots shortly after the 2025 draft and was a part of their practice squad. He would sign a futures contract to remain with the team in 2026 and after a pretty solid training camp/preseason, was cut this summer.
Like Carvin, Herring was nothing more than a practice squad player. The former Delware defensive back — who spent the start of his rookie season with the Green Bay Packers — signed with New England in September of last year after a workout. He'd be released roughly three weeks later.
Butler was a member of the Patriots training camp roster this year after sticking around on the practice squad last year as a rookie. Initially, the offensive guard parlayed a successful rookie minicamp invite into a spot on the roster — and he was a potential practice squad candidate this year after roster cuts in August.
Out of anyone on this list, Battle has the most playing time. Over a two-year stretch from 2024 to 2025, Battle played in six games with the Patriots, recording five tackles and three pass breakups (all of which came in Week 18 of 2024). He was on New England's practice squad for their trip to Super Bowl LX last February, but signed a futures deal with the Miami Dolphins after the game.
The son of Pro Football Hall of Famer Jerry Rice , Brenden had a week-long stint in New England in 2025. The 24-year-old wideout signed with the Patriots' practice squad on Nov. 4 and was prompty released on Nov. 11. He'd later sign with the Seattle Seahawks, Las Vegas Raiders and Green Bay Packers.
The Patriots had two Butlers on their preseason roster this summer, and now both of them are heading to the Orlando Storm. The Patriots signed Butler, a rookie out of San Diego State, in early August and he was mainly a depth safety/special teamer during his time in New England. He'd be released with an injury designation — pushing him to injured reserve — before the Patriots reached a settlement.

title: Kellen Moore Addresses Saints' Offensive Struggles After Bears Loss
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints had their opportunities to pull off an upset against one of the NFC's top teams Nov. 22, but the same offensive problems that have plagued them throughout the season proved costly once again.
After the Saints ' 21-13 loss to the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field, head coach Kellen Moore expressed frustration with his team's inability to capitalize on scoring chances, protect the football and execute in critical moments.
New Orleans fell to 3-7 after its offense committed two turnovers, and an injury-riddled offensive line gave up 6 sacks while repeatedly failing to finish drives, despite a defense that kept the game within reach.
The offensive struggles have become an increasingly concerning trend under Moore , particularly the team's inability to start fast. The Saints average just 0.9 points in the first quarter through 10 games, putting them in difficult situations before their offense can establish consistency.
Moore also addressed the team's ongoing ball-security problems, questionable fourth-down decisions, quarterback Tyler Shough 's performance and substitution issues that contributed to wasted timeouts and kept rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson off the field for an extended stretch.
"That's the NFL, and that's the frustration with it," Moore said. "I thought we battled. ... We just weren't able to make enough plays to win this football game."
The Saints will look to end their three-game losing streak when they travel to face the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday, Nov. 29.
Q: The Saints are averaging just 0.9 points per game in the first quarter. Have you tried everything to fix the slow starts?
Moore: "Obviously, it's as frustrating as anything. Again, we're not starting fast. I think we basically had one possession, and we stalled out. We drove it again and then stalled out once we got into plus territory.
"I feel like that's been too common in our opening drives. That's the challenging thing. It's not three-and-outs. It's just being able to finish a drive off."
Q: The offense had several possessions in Bears territory but struggled to capitalize. What's the biggest issue?
Moore: "Again, it's about sustaining drives and giving ourselves the chance to get the points at the end.
"We did have the one turnover on downs where we tried to get the touchdown instead of settling for the field goal. Then we just had some chances that we weren't able to take advantage of."
Q: How frustrating is it knowing the Bears weren't particularly explosive offensively and that a few plays could have changed the outcome?
Moore: "That's the NFL, and that's the frustration with it. I thought we battled. It's a really good offense. For our guys to create a couple turnovers was big, to create some short fields there.
"I thought there was some really good play there. We just weren't able to make enough plays to win this football game."
Q: The Saints have lost 23 fumbles since last season, the most in the NFL. Why has protecting the football remained such a persistent problem?
Moore: "Obviously, the disappointing part of it is just the fundamentals of protecting the football.
"The one that happened today was a catch-tuck, and they beat us to it before we could secure the football. They did a better job than us on that down. Obviously, we had the one interception after our own first down."
Q: What did you make of Tyler Shough's performance overall?
Moore: "I think he battled. Obviously, there are going to be things that we're going to have to look at, correct and improve as an offense. Ultimately, 13 points isn't enough to beat these guys."
Q: Do you think Shough has taken a step backward, and has the constant shuffling along the offensive line affected his decision-making?
Moore: "I think ultimately, collectively, we all want to play better football and coach better football. We have to do this thing together.
"Again, Tyler's battling. He gave us an opportunity to get back into that. He got us back down for a field goal opportunity for Charlie to kick that, and then we're down to one possession.
"That game wasn't without opportunities to make some plays. We just didn't get it done."
Q: What happened on Shough's interception?
Moore: "I'll have to look at it again more closely. Obviously, the safety came off. In the scramble phase, we've got to keep running our routes and give ourselves an opportunity so that guy doesn't have a chance to peel back.
"I did not see, based on where I was, where the location of the ball ended up. Obviously, a frustrating one for all of us."
Q: Did Shough need to get rid of the football quicker on the safety?
Moore: "We should be helping the right tackle on that play, and obviously, we just didn't execute it. The edge rusher had the angle."
Q: Was there supposed to be someone helping the right tackle with a chip block?
Moore: "There should be a chipper there, yes."
Q: Was that a missed assignment?
Moore: "No. Jordyn ran the route and didn't do the initial protection element of it. Chip, then run your route."
Q: What did you think about Shough's decision-making on the safety?
Moore: "Obviously, I don't think he's anticipating the edge rusher to be there that quickly. I felt like we'd have some presence there to be able to work through the progression.
"I think if we give ourselves just a touch more time, he's going to have a completion over the ball."
Q: Why did Tyson go approximately 12 consecutive snaps without playing? Was that related to his workload?
Moore: "Just the sequencing of those personnel groups. Again, I've got to do a better job of getting him in there on a few more of those occasions.
"We stayed on the ball a few times and tried to keep certain personnel groups on defense so we could execute some plays. That kind of kept Jordyn off on a few occasions."
Q: Was his absence related to the missed chip block or some form of punishment?
Moore: "No. We had a couple substitutions where we had Bryce and Barry in there for specific plays.
"Once we get into tempo, sometimes we're keeping those guys on the field so we don't allow them to substitute and get to some of their packages."
Q: Were those substitutions predetermined or based on the flow of the game?
Moore: "A lot of it's predetermined."
Q: What went well on Travis Etienne's 46-yard run?
Moore: "Obviously, I'll have to review it from a film perspective. I think being able to capture the edge was an important part, and him being able to get to the edge and make a play was important for us. We needed something like that."
Q: Why wasn't Etienne more involved during the first two offensive possessions?
Moore: "Just the flow of the sequencing there. Again, trying to get completions early based on the hashes and the direction in which we wanted to attack them.
"We probably didn't have as many run opportunities those first two drives, but I think he got in there the rest of the way."
Q: Did you consider kicking a field goal instead of going for it on fourth down late in the game?
Moore: "Yes. We obviously discussed it very briefly. Ultimately, we were going to need a touchdown. We felt like we were down there. It's third-and-two, fourth-and-two. We had an opportunity to get the touchdown at some point.
"It's also an 11-point game at that point, so you're going to have to have a two-point conversion as well. We felt like trying to score there and gather as much information as we could was important."
Q: Did analytics influence that decision?
Q: There appeared to be several issues with offensive substitutions. What happened?
Moore: "There were just some receiver substitutions. I've obviously got to do a better job of making sure we have cleaner communication there. We had to use a couple timeouts."
Q: How frustrating was it to lose timeouts because of a failed challenge and substitution problems?
Moore: "It puts you in a goofy spot at the end of the game because you're not going to have all the timeouts at the end.
"Obviously, we had some situations we've got to do better…

title: Saints Can't Get Out of Their Own Way in Disappointing Loss to Bears
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints ' offensive struggles and inability to protect the football proved costly once again Sunday afternoon.
Despite a strong defensive effort and a late comeback attempt, the Saints couldn't overcome two early turnovers, six sacks and missed scoring opportunities in a frustrating 21-13 loss to the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field.
The loss marks three straight for New Orleans and drops the Saints to 3-7, while Chicago improved to 8-2 with its fifth straight win.
The Saints finished with 307 total yards compared to Chicago's 311, but failed to score a touchdown on their final eight possessions, showcasing the Saints' inability to capitalize on the opportunities given to them, a criticism that head coach Kellen Moore has faced all season.
After a slow start by both teams, things deteriorated for New Orleans. Its second-quarter run game faltered when running back CJ Donaldson fumbled, giving Chicago excellent field position. That allowed the Bears to strike as Caleb Williams with a 3-yard touchdown pass to D'Andre Swift , extending the Bears' lead to 10-0.
Chicago got the ball back after quarterback Tyler Shough threw an interception to rookie safety Dillon Thieneman , and Williams connected with tight end Colston Loveland for a 15-yard strike to give the Bears a commanding 16-0 advantage.
New Orleans did finally show signs of life late in the first half.
Running back Travis Etienne Jr. broke free for a 46-yard run, setting up Shough's 1-yard touchdown pass to Alvin Kamara on fourth-and-goal to cut the deficit to nine.
The Saints defense then got another chance when linebacker Danny Stutsman intercepted Williams after a deflected pass. However, New Orleans’ special teams woes returned midway through the quarter as kicker Charlie Smyth missed a 47-yard field goal.
However, Smyth redeemed himself with a 56-yard field goal as time expired in the first half, cutting Chicago's lead to 16-10.
New Orleans couldn't build on that momentum.
The Bears extended their lead to 19-10 on Santos' third-quarter field goal before their defensive front took control and bullied the Saints' injury-depleted offensive line.
Chicago recorded six sacks, including three from defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons . Montez Sweat delivered one of the game's biggest plays in the fourth quarter, sacking Shough in the end zone for a safety that extended the Bears' advantage to 21-10.
The Saints had another opportunity after Julian Blackmon recovered a Swift fumble, but their ensuing possession stalled on fourth down at Chicago's 10-yard line.
Shough finished 25 of 42 for 222 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Chris Olave led New Orleans with nine receptions for 102 yards, while Devaughn Vele added seven catches for 76 yards.
Smyth connected on a 51-yard field goal with 1:10 remaining, but Chicago recovered the ensuing onside kick to seal the victory.
New Orleans now turns its attention to next Sunday's road matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals , looking to avoid another disappointing result in a season rapidly slipping away.

title: Three Keys to Victory: Can the Saints Upset the Bears?
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints face an uphill battle Sunday when they travel to Soldier Field to take on the Chicago Bears in a matchup between two teams heading in opposite directions.
Coming off another disappointing loss to the Carolina Panthers , the Saints (3-6) are looking to bounce back against a Chicago team (7-2) that has emerged as one of the NFC's top contenders.
However, pulling off an upset won't be easy for head coach Kellen Moore 's squad, especially against a Bears offense averaging nearly 27 points per game and a defense that ranks among the league's best .
For New Orleans to have any chance of leaving Chicago with a victory, it must eliminate the costly mistakes that have plagued it throughout the season while finding a way to slow down Caleb Williams and the Bears' explosive offense.
Here are three keys to victory for the Saints against the Bears.
This is a major necessity for the Saints.
New Orleans has 17 turnovers (tied for 27th in the NFL) and a minus-8 differential (29th). As great as Tyler Shough has been for the Saints, his seven interceptions and four lost fumbles have repeatedly put the Saints in tough spots.
Chicago also has 17 turnovers, including four interceptions from Williams against Tampa Bay. This gives the Saints defense an opportunity, with just nine takeaways (tied for 24th) and none in three games. Forcing turnovers can lead to great opportunities to put points on the board.
However, forcing turnovers requires the offense to capitalize, something New Orleans has struggled with all season.
The Saints have only scored nine first-quarter points through nine games (literally a point per quarter) and have gone scoreless in seven opening quarters. That will not work against a Chicago team averaging nearly 27 points per game. Moore's offense needs faster starts, fewer penalties, and touchdowns instead of field goals.
Do that, and the Saints’ chances of pulling off an upset get a little higher.
The Saints' defense faces a daunting task in slowing down one of the league's most potent offensive units.
Chicago's offense features top-tier production across the board: seventh in scoring (26.8 points per game), seventh in total yards (383.0 per game), and fourth on the ground (142.0 rushing yards per game).
Behind Caleb Williams, who has powered the Bears to four straight wins since returning from a hamstring injury, Chicago has put up 27 points or more in every game of that streak.
Given New Orleans' vulnerability against the pass, keeping Williams from finding a rhythm in the pocket is critical.
The Saints currently rank near the bottom of the league defensively—21st against the pass (231.0 yards per game allowed) and 29th overall (360.8 total yards per game allowed).
Defensive coordinator Brandon Staley needs to dial up pressure to disrupt Williams while keeping him contained inside the pocket to limit playmaking on the run.
Much of that pressure must come from edge rushers Carl Granderson and Chase Young , who have logged a combined 16.5 sacks on the season.
However, pressuring Williams is only part of the equation.
The Saints must also slow down a rushing attack that averages 142 yards per game, fourth-best in the NFL.
Running back D'Andre Swift leads Chicago with 576 rushing yards and 10 touchdowns, while Kyle Monangai averages 5.4 yards per carry with 324 yards and three touchdowns.
That does not bode well for a team ranked 27th in run defense, allowing nearly 130 rushing yards per game.
New Orleans has shown improvement against the run over its past two games, holding Cleveland to 95 yards and Carolina to 97.
Linebacker Kaden Elliss will be particularly important after recording 26 tackles and two sacks over those two contests.
If the Saints can limit Chicago's rushing attack and force Williams into obvious passing situations, they'll have a better opportunity to generate pressure and create turnovers.
Allowing the Bears to establish their running game would make an already difficult matchup even more challenging.
