title: 3 Jets Studs & 3 Duds Stand Out in Win vs. Chargers: Rookies Shine, O-Line Dominates
full_text:
It had been over a month since the last time the Jets won a football game. Their 27-24 victory over the Chargers provided a major breath of relief for head coach Aaron Glenn. The second-year coach has been running out of time this season to show ownership he's deserving of a third year.
A 3-8 record shows there is plenty left to do in that regard. But their victory, in what was one of the most efficient offensive games in franchise history show plenty of studs and duds to talk about.
We're running out of superlatives to describe the impact and play David Bailey has had on the Jets' defense. The second overall pick recorded two sacks on Sunday and even a forced fumble. He's now up to 9.5 sacks and six forced fumbles.
2 sacks today, 9.5 this season for David Bailey 😤 NYJvsLAC on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/CPQkr1Mrc3
Bailey is just the third rookie since the turn of the century to record over 8.5 sacks and six forced fumbles in a season.
A reminder: we're in Week 11.
Bailey is on pace to shatter Javon Kearse's rookie sack record of 14.5. He remains a transcendent talent and a major part of what this team will be over the years.
Some Jets fans are happy the team was able to come away with a win on Sunday. Others are furious that the team has lost out on a chance to get closer to the top overall pick.
Wherever each fan falls on the tanking question, the Jets are unequivocally not tanking. If anything, they continue to play hard for head coach Aaron Glenn and the rest of their staff. Based on that reality, it's a fair bet to assume the team is not going to finish 3-14 on the year. Gang Green will win more games.
People can continue to complain about that, or demand further changes, but the reality is none of that is going to happen yet. Sunday's win was the clearest example of that.
It's been a long road for Sterling Shepard. The former second-round pick has torn his Achilles and ACL in back-to-back years and has been bouncing around practice squads ever since. On Sunday, with the Jets dealing with injuries at the position, he was called in to provide competency.
Two TDs for Sterling Shepard! NYJvsLAC on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/1unKNT1rMh
Shepard caught touchdowns on both of his receptions today to help the Jets solve their red-zone woes. While the Jets have not placed Omar Cooper Jr. on IR with an ankle injury, they should feel confident in the depth of their receiver room.
Shepard is a big reason why. He is deserving of a performance like that to show he still belongs.
The Jets' offense had one of the most efficient days in team history. Their defense, though, has problems that have not been fixed all season. New York gave up 158 yards running to Los Angeles.
The Chargers' run offense came into the game 10th in the league, so it's not like the performance was shocking. Still, the team struggled mightily to control the line of scrimmage on that side of the ball. It will remain an issue so long as the team tries to use four-down linemen as part of their fits.
There were some positive plays on their own, but as a collective problem, the Jets' run defense remains unsolved.
The Jets' run defense was bad, but their own offensive line was superb on Sunday. The Jets ran for 165 yards as a unit for 4.5 yards per carry. Dylan Parham, Josh Myers, and Armand Membou didn't give up a single pressure today either.
It didn't matter that the Chargers needed multiple stops today. They simply couldn't get it because the offensive line dictated the play.
The Jets are going to have to address a lot of needs this offseason—especially at quarterback, linebacker, defensive line, and in their secondary. One group they definitely don't have to worry about, though, is their line.
They remain the focal point for future success.
It was a quiet day for punter Austin McNamara—and that's what all NFL fans will want to see.
The Jets' starting punter never got a chance to do his job, outside of holds on field goals, because they never punted for the second time this century. It's also their first game without a turnover or punt since 2004.
McNamara has had a down year of course, but this is a dud that most fans will be happy to deal with.

title: Sterling Shepard's Big Game Will Likely Force Jets' Hand After Week 11 Win Over Chargers
full_text:
The wide receiver position was one of the Jets' biggest question marks entering Sunday's clash with the Chargers . Not only has the group been inconsistent all season, but New York's WR room was also going to be without Omar Cooper Jr. and Isaiah Williams in Week 11, as the rookie-veteran duo was sidelined by injury .
Cooper and Williams's absence forced the Jets to turn to the practice squad, and they tabbed veteran WR Sterling Shepard as the next man up. That decision proved to be the right one by head coach Aaron Glenn & Co., as Shepard finished Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers with two catches for 24 yards and two touchdowns, marking the first multi-TD game of the ex-Giant's 11-year career.
Two TDs for Sterling Shepard! NYJvsLAC on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/1unKNT1rMh
Considering Shepard had only one catch for three yards in two appearances before Sunday, it's safe to say his big performance was unexpected. That said, it was exactly what the Jets needed out of their WR room, which hasn't been productive outside of Cooper, Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell this season.
As great as it was to see Shepard step up, his big game doesn't come without somewhat of an asterisk. After all, Week 11 was the third time the Jets elevated Shepard from the practice squad, meaning they'll have to sign him to the 53-man roster if they hope to use him in the passing game again.
To add, though, Gang Green must subtract first. Certain Jets who've overstayed their welcome could be cut to make room for Shepard, especially one veteran who hasn't shown much this season.
Assuming Cooper and Williams aren't out for long, it'd benefit the Jets to move on from Tim Patrick if it means making room for Shepard on the 53-man unit.
Knowing Glenn from their time in the Motor City, Patrick joined New York on a one-year contract back in May. Were his best days behind him? Absolutely, but the Jets hoped the former Utah Ute could at least contribute as the fourth- or fifth-best option after tallying 48 catches for 581 receiving yards and six touchdowns in 32 games over the previous two seasons with the Lions and Jaguars.
Patrick's time in Gotham started on the wrong foot, as he opened the 2026 NFL season on injured reserve with a groin injury. He made some decent noise with a two-catch, 26-yard performance in Week 5's win over the Browns, but it was downhill from there. One catch for 15 yards against the Patriots one week later, before stuffing the stat line with zeroes against the Dolphins in Week 7. His playing time absolutely cratered from game to game:
Tim Patrick's offensive snaps
The writing has seemingly been on the wall for Patrick since that stretch. He sat on the sidelines from Weeks 8 to 10 until he finally got a chance in Week 11, with the Jets' WR room needing help. But just like he has all season, Patrick left much to be desired against the Chargers, catching his only target for five receiving yards over 25 offensive snaps.
Sure, Patrick's blocking helped the run game, but that can't be the Jets' sole reason to keep him around—especially when his performance in that area has been a mixed bag this season. His presence as a pass-catcher isn't moving the needle, and it's clear that he doesn't have much chemistry with Smith.
Meanwhile, Shepard now has as many receiving TDs as Cooper, Williams and tight end Mason Taylor this year, as well as only one fewer than Wilson. That doesn't mean that the 33-year-old elder statesman will be a scoring machine down the stretch, but his role as a much-needed red-zone security blanket for Smith could unlock new layers for the Jets' offense.
According to OverTheCap , New York general manager Darren Mougey would create $985,294 in cap savings and $1 million in dead money by cutting Patrick. The savings could be used to sign Shepard for the remainder of the season, as he wouldn't command a big payday despite his two-TD game.
A cut would likely be a blow to Patrick's ego, but he's been around long enough to know how the business side of the NFL works. It's a what-have-you-done-for-me-lately situation, and he hasn't exactly done much.
The Jets can then attempt to re-sign Patrick to the practice squad if they remove him from the 53-man roster. Given how his 2026 campaign has unfolded, there probably won't be much (if any) competition for his services. That way, New York can keep a familiar veteran around in case of emergency, while Patrick wouldn't have to uproot his life midseason.
In the end, other WR-needy teams will see what Shepard did on Sunday and be eager to convince him to join them. The Jets need to avoid that situation by signing him to the 53-man roster as soon as possible, which will likely mean giving Patrick the wake-up call he might desperately need.

title: Ranking Every Jets 2027 Free Agent Based on Their Likelihood of Re-Signing
full_text:
The  Jets have a slew of players who will hit free agency in March .
From starters to benchwarmers, 22 players are hitting free agency , meaning there will be changes in New York this offseason. Some have been integral to the Jets this season, while others are seen as a waste of money.
Here’s a list of every Jets free agent and how likely they are to be in Gotham green and white next season, starting with the likeliest re-signing candidate.
The 30-year-old fullback has been with the Jets since 2024, and it seems likely he would stay. Braelon Allen has broken out, giving the Jets two great running backs. Regardless of how the team looks next year, it would be safe to assume that New York is still a run-first team. Beck would be a crucial retention if that's the case.
Max Mitchell is another player who should jump at a contract if offered. Mitchell has spent his career as a backup offensive tackle for the team, and New York should want to retain that depth. It would be hard to believe any team would want him as a starter, which gives New York the edge over other franchises.
The offensive line is one of the few position groups on the Jets roster that doesn’t need an immediate rehaul. That bodes well for Mitchell. The Jets won’t look much to the draft for O-line depth, leaving Mitchell as a prime candidate to get re-signed. I’d expect the 27-year-old to get a new contract and retain his role with the team.
Austin McNamara has been a New York Jet his whole career. Do not expect that to change when his contract expires after 2026. According to Pro Football Focus , the punter ranked second at his position in 2025 and ranks 15th this season . Those rankings should push the Jets to retain McNamara when his contract runs out.
The defensive lineman is another who would likely re-sign if given the opportunity. Briggs got his shot in New York after a year in Cleveland, and there would be expected loyalty to the team. Briggs is a needed depth piece for a team that has struggled on the interior of the line this year.
Whether New York further addresses the position or not, Briggs would be a likely retention for the team.
Isaiah Williams has carved himself a role in New York. Williams is the de-facto punt returner and has also shown he can slot into a receiver role when needed . New York is where he made his name and he should stay with the team as a restricted free agent.
Unless another team is willing to overpay for his services, it seems like his career will continue as a Jet.
Kene Nwangwu is in a very similar spot as Williams.
The running back has carved out a role as the Jets’ kick returner, and it is hard to believe he would get much market anywhere else. The 28-year-old has signed three consecutive one-year deals with the Jets. What would be a fourth?
Once again, unless another team overpays for the returner, expect Nwangwu to be returning kicks for New York next year.
Jordan Meredith is another o-line depth piece that the Jets should look to retain. While Meredith hasn’t had his best season as a Jet, his 65.0 PFF grade shows that he is serviceable when called on. The offensive lineman can be slotted anywhere on the interior line, which gives New York flexibility if they re-sign him.
Another team may look for his services, but the Jets still have a good chance to retain him.
Dane Belton may be the Jets’ best upcoming free agent. The safety has been one of the bright spots on the 2-8 team, posting a position-high 90.7 run defense grade. Belton has fit in on the Jets and would likely be offered a contract that fits his starting role on the team.
The issue would be who the Jets have as coach next season. If New York is to move on from Aaron Glenn, it would likely bring in a new defensive scheme to the team. If Belton does not fit that, or wants to go somewhere else, he may be on his way out. But the familiarity with the team and his breakout may keep Belton in New York for 2027.
Geno Smith is another player who will be affected by the Aaron Glenn saga. The 36-year-old is on a one-year deal where he has played well enough to keep his starting spot despite New York’s record. The issue is the Jets look likely to search for a rookie QB come the 2027 draft. The question will be whether Smith is retained to act as a bridge quarterback, à la Kirk Cousins and Fernando Mendoza.
Smith was never the long-term answer, as shown by the length of his deal with New York. There is an opportunity, however, for him to sign another similar deal. It will all come down to what New York decides to do at head coach to see if Smith will continue his second tenure as a Jet.
The defensive end has been a fine option on the edge for New York, but the 26-year-old may be looking for a different challenge in 2027. The Jets drafted David Bailey, look like they will keep Will McDonald IV, and may even use one of their first-round picks to draft another end. New York should look to retain Enagbare as a depth piece, but there may be too many cooks in the kitchen for Kingsley to stay.
The big tight end is a toss-up.
He has played his role well for the Jets as mostly a blocking option. Woods has also shown he can catch a pass when called upon. The issue is the tight end has only caught five passes in two years as a Jet. Compared to the 25 he had in one season as a Colt, his Jets’ receiving output is laughable.
If another team is willing to incorporate him into the passing game, Woods’s time as a Jet could be over.
Another toss-up with this one. McCrary-Ball has been a depth piece for New York, only playing 114 snaps during his three-year career. If New York wants to keep him, he probably stays, but they could move on from him easily. The linebacker is replaceable, and it would not be surprising to see him replaced.
Another depth piece linebacker who is out of contract after 2026. Reeder has only played one defensive snap this season. His lack of usage makes it hard to believe that he would remain with the team after this season. Reeder should look for a bigger role, and New York doesn’t seem like the place for that. It would be surprising to see Reeder as a Jet after this season.
There’s a pattern developing in these spots. These are depth pieces who just haven’t seen enough time to garner another contract with the team. Malik McClain has yet to play an offensive snap this season. Between free agency and the draft, he could easily get overtaken on the receiver depth chart, where he already sits near the bottom. The receiver just hasn’t done enough to warrant being re-signed after 2026.
Tim Patrick has actually touched the field, but he hasn’t done much. The 32-year-old’s biggest impact on the team may have been an offensive pass interference against the Patriots in Week 6. The veteran has shown he can play in the league, but his time may be coming to an end. It would be surprising to see New York re-sign the aging receiver who didn’t show much to say he still has it.
David Onyemata falls into the same category as Patrick. An aging veteran whose best days may be behind them.
Onyemata wasn’t terrible to start the season, but the defensive lineman hasn’t played since Week 2. As a 34-year-old on a one-year deal, Onyemata may be trending towards his last years in the NFL. His $10.5 million price tag is too much to bring back for a player who will be 35 next season.
Braiden McGregor is younger than Onyemata but has seen just one more snap than the man who has only played two games in 2026. He won’t be starting anytime soon, and as stated when discussing Enagbare, New York may bolster that position in the draft. McGregor looks like an outside chance to be a Jet in 2027.
Chukwuma Okorafor has been nothing but a backup for New York. The 28-year-old has played just one snap this season, leaving him likely to search for a new home in 2027. He has played the least amount of football in his career during his one year with the Jets.
As he nears his 30s, Okorafor may want a new challenge where he has more of a…

title: What Jets Are Saying About Geno Smith and Week 11 Injury Report vs. Chargers
full_text:
Another week, another lengthy injury report for the New York Jets.
At 2-8, the team is heading to Los Angeles for a Week 11 showdown against the Los Angeles Chargers. The team has dealt with injuries all week to several starters, including quarterback Geno Smith, offensive lineman Dylan Parham, and defensive tackle Harrison Phillips.
Whether it's head coach Aaron Glenn or his assistant staff, the Jets believe confident they'll get most of their starters ready to play.
Let's break down what the team is saying heading into Week 11.
Much has been made whether the Jets should play or sit Smith this week. Some fans wanted him to sit so they would have a better chance of losing. Others want to see their collection of talent on offense look good regardless of the outcome.
In the end, Smith doesn't have an injury designation. He will play in Los Angeles on Sunday.
"He looks solid," Glenn said. "It's very encouraging."
Had Smith not been healthy enough to go, the Jets would have to turn to fourth-round rookie Cade Klubnik. The Clemson product completed 55 percent of his passes in his debut, while also throwing an interception, but the team remains high on his potential.
"You could immediately feel it's not too big for him, he was very poised, made throws, you saw his athleticism," Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich said. "I thought he showed himself well."
Smith gives New York the best chance to win . With the Jets doing everything in their power to keep Glenn as coach, it remains clear they will be rolling with the veteran for the remainder of the year...so long as he's healthy.
When New York took the field in Tennessee to open up the 2026 season, their full collection of weapons appeared to be a group that could make life difficult for opposing defensive coordinators.
Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell, Omar Cooper Jr., Mason Taylor, Kenyon Sadiq, Breece Hall, and Braelon Allen are more than enough to put up points no matter who is quarterback.
There's just one problem: the entire cohort of weapons has seen just two series together. Cooper suffered an ankle injury on the opening drive of the season and left after the first play in last week's loss to Buffalo. Losing Cooper to another ankle injury is just the latest missed opportunity for the organization.
"He's a difference-maker," Reich said. "You could feel it right from the start and it's been a shame he's had the injuries that he's had because I feel his presence on the field, I feel it when we're game planning."
There is hope that a full offseason together will keep the group exciting. However, it's clear the unit missed a lot of opportunities this year due to injuries.
We know the Jets will have Smith on the field. We also know the team will be without two of their quality receivers in Williams and Cooper.
But what about the other cohort of Jets players banged up? The full list of players going into Sunday with the "questionable" label are as follows:
- DT, Harrison Phillips - OL, Dylan Parham - LB, Trevin Wallace - EDGE, Joseph Ossai
The team is not giving up any hope on seeing them all on the field, though.
"We got two days to see how these guys operate," Glenn said. "It is looking promising for all these guys, so feel good about that."
Having Parham healthy will alter how the Jets move offensively. Ossai and Phillips could also help the team on defense against a Chargers offense that wants to run the football . That said, it will be a gametime decision for all of these players.

title: Aaron Glenn's Jets Optimism Falls Short Given the Reality
full_text:
They wouldn't actually do it, would they?
The New York Jets currently sit at 2-8 on the season, and 5-22 under head coach Aaron Glenn. It's a record worse than most other top men across NFL history. The prevailing theory now is when the team will eventually move in, not "if."
Despite the perception, Glenn has remained upbeat both about the team and his prospects as head coach. On Friday, the 54-year-old detailed where he believed the team was improving.
"I think the way that we've operated in our two-minute has improved," Glenn said. "I think the way that we've operated in managing the clock has improved, and I'm really happy about that and I really think that we want to continue to improve in that and that's something that we talk about constantly."
Two minute and clock management....on a 2-8 roster. Glenn's defense isn't exactly glowing at this point.
But with a great relationship with owner Woody Johnson, are Glenn's positive thoughts being taken to heart? Would New York really opt to keep Glenn for a third season despite his poor numbers across the board?
Jets fans have been clear in their distaste for Glenn as coach. Despite his work as a former Pro Bowl player, the fanbase is almost universally clear in its push for a new head coach after the season ends.
Johnson, though, may have a different barometer for Glenn than others.
"I don't believe Woody Johnson's bar for Aaron Glenn is as high as people think it is," ESPN's Rich Cimini said on the Jets Collective Thursday. "Even if he wins like three games and a bunch of guys like all these young players are playing great at the end of the year, that might be enough for Woody."
Fans didn't exactly take Cimini's comments well. Many saw that as the door opening for a Glenn return  to end the year with Johnson looking for any semblance of competence from the team to go in that direction.
But the perception of Johnson potentially keeping Glenn may not be true in reality. The fact of the matter is that the team still has seven games left to play. Three are against teams with below .500 records, including their next two games against the Los Angeles Chargers and Miami Dolphins. A loss to both teams would bump the Jets down to 2-10 and Glenn's personal record to 5-24.
It would drop Glenn's winning percentage to .172—just .05 percentage points better than Rich Kotite.
Any way you slice it, the Jets are expected to end the season not only below .500 for a 11th straight year, but also watch Glenn remain with the second worst winning percentage in team history. No coach received a third year beyond that.
It's true that Johnson wants Glenn to succeed. He was the coach Johnson picked, and has a personal relationship with. More so than his predecessors like Robert Saleh or Adam Gase, Glenn has the ear and trust of Johnson off the field.
But public opinion matters in a situation like this. The eyes of the NFL world will be watching if the Jets' owner is willing to put forth another losing season just so a friend of his gets another chance to fix things with the organization. And if the losing continues, it won't matter what Johnson may want.
He won't have a choice. Glenn will need to be let go, and the Jets must undergo another coaching search again.

title: Jets Continue to Be Sneaky Winners of Colts' Failed Daniel Jones' Experiment
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts are the gift that keeps on giving the whole year for the New York Jets.
When Indianapolis acquired Sauce Gardner in a trade for two first-round picks, the belief from the organization was that the All-Pro cornerback was the missing piece to the organization ending their playoff drought. Since that trade, though, the Colts are just 4-15.
And every move they have made since is a massive win for the Jets. That includes their most recent decision to release quarterback Daniel Jones after not trading him at the NFL Trade Deadline last week.
New York may be 2-8, but its future outlook is far different than that of Indianapolis. They own three first-round picks in the 2027 draft, with two projected to be in the top five as of this current moment.
Indianapolis had a chance this deadline to help themselves in that regard. They traded away All-Pro players like DeForest Buckner and Quenton Nelson. Josh Downs and Keenan Allen were also moved for mid-round selections.
Despite the firesale, the Colts chose to keep running back Jonathan Taylor and Jones on the roster, believing they could still compete with them beyond this season.
The decision to release Jones and roll with former top pick Anthony Richardson as quarterback is a sign the Colts simply did not have a plan for the trade deadline this year. They looked at players with expiring contracts and simply sold them off for a mediocre return. They overvalued other players like Jones and Taylor for no other reason, but they didn't receive the offer they want.
Part of that is due to the team firing general manager Chris Ballard before the deadline. Interim GM Ed Dodds is having to try and prove his worthiness at the top job, while also not hurting long-term assets for the franchise.
But the circus of Jones' release just a week after the deadline so the Colts get nothing for him is an abject failure by the front office.
And the Jets are looking on like that meme of Bill Hader eating popcorn on Saturday Night Live .
New York has had to do nothing but allow the Colts to collapse inward. The acquisition of Gardner gave the Jets two first-round picks that they are using to rebuild their struggling roster. Indianapolis, meanwhile, has no first-round pick to use to rebuild theirs.
The release of Jones is just the latest example of the difference between the two teams as well. New York has had no illusions about their current poor roster, so they got a king's ransom for one of their more talented players . The Colts, meanwhile, hitched their wagon to Jones in the hopes they could build a winner immediately.
And as each week passes by, and both teams continue to lose, it's the Jets who should come out as the better team with both picks expected to be in the top five.

title: 3 Positions the Jets Must Target in Round 1 of the 2027 NFL Draft
full_text:
Barring any unforeseen circumstances, the Jets are going to walk into the 2027 NFL Draft with three first-round picks that will be considered within reach of impact players.
The question becomes which positions and players the team should focus on. It's easy to point to the current 2-8 team and argue they have holes all over the roster, but that is not always the case. In fact, the Jets are better prepared to take the next steps in the rebuild than in any other year before.
The question simply becomes: which area of need should the team focus on? And in that regard, there are three that are more important than all the others.
A team doesn't have three first-round picks in a draft if they don't intend to take a quarterback early. The 2022 Jets are the exception, not the rule.
This time, though, it seems like a foregone conclusion that the team will be focusing on a signal-caller early in the draft, despite past whiffs at the position elsewhere . While there are still decisions that have to be made by many of the quarterbacks in the draft, the safe bet is that three college players will make the jump to the NFL.
Mestemaker is the quarterback with the highest ceiling. He has the athleticism and arm talent of a Josh Allen, which would excite any team. Carr is a more traditional pocket passer who can make all NFL throws. Mensah is a quarterback who has a mix of both Carr and Mestemaker, but may be a bit of a lesser player at each. This isn't to say the Miami quarterback is bad—I firmly expect all three to go into the top 10 of this draft.
And that means New York will come away with one of them.
David Bailey is a rising star in the league, but New York still has major questions at edge rusher. Who they end up selecting will largely be based on who is running the defense in 2027 . If a coordinator wants to run more of a 4-3 scheme, then the Jets would want players who can operate out of the wide nine.
A 3-4 scheme, meanwhile, required edge rushers to be stout against the run as well as the pass. Luckily for New York, the top edge prospects they'll be in line for can handle both. Stewart and Simmons have dominated college football this season. They remain favorites for top-five picks depending on how the draft lines up.
As things stand, the Jets are set to get their future QB and an impact edge defender. That's an excellent haul to rebuild a roster.
It's not just at edge rusher where New York needs major help. Their inability to target an every-down defensive tackle following the Quinnen Williams trade is also a major problem. Luckily for the Jets, many interior defensive linemen are available.
Echoles and Gilliam are two players who could be available when New York makes its third selection in the draft. Both have shown the ability to rush the passer and defend the run at a high clip. It offers New York a chance to solidify the defensive line in a major way very early on draft day.

title: 3 Key Jets vs. Chargers Matchups That Will Decide If New York Tastes Victory in Week 11
full_text:
After extending their losing streak to five games last Sunday, the Jets will look to get back into the win column when they head out west to take on the Chargers at SoFi Stadium. Unlike New York’s last two matchups, which came against two of the AFC’s premier teams, Los Angeles has arguably been the worst team this season.
While the Chargers' defense has been average this season, offensive struggles and mounting injuries have derailed their season. For head coach Aaron Glenn, a win here could go a long way toward cooling his hot seat ; however, a loss against Los Angeles would effectively cement his firing.
If the Jets are going to come away victorious, they must prioritize winning these three key matchups.
While some point to the schematic shift or lack of talent for the Chargers’ offensive struggles, injuries upfront have played a large part. Los Angeles currently has five offensive linemen on injured reserve, four of whom played in the interior.
As a result, the Chargers have relied on two rookies in the middle, along with five-year veteran Cole Strange at right guard. While Logan Taylor has done well in pass protection this season, allowing just two sacks and seven pressures across 212 pass-blocking snaps, the same can’t be said for Slaughter and Strange.
Slaughter has surrendered two sacks and 14 pressures, earning a 60.1 pass-blocking grade, which ranks 22nd among 35 qualifying centers , per Pro Football Focus. Meanwhile, Strange has given up three sacks and 23 pressures. His 37.7 pass-blocking grade ranks 70th among 77 qualifying guards, per PFF.
With Los Angeles vulnerable in the middle, New York must target this area in Sunday’s matchup. While the Jets aren’t among the league’s best at generating pressure, they’ve had some success getting to the backfield this season. Through 10 games, they are tied for 13th in sacks (23) and rank 16th in pressure rate (23.1%).
David Bailey has played a major role in the pass rush, leading the team in sacks (7.5) and quarterback hits (12). While Bailey and Will McDonald IV have been New York’s top pass rushers, the defense hasn’t been able to get much pressure up the middle. Interior defenders account for just three of the team’s 23 sacks, with Jowon Briggs having two of them.
David Bailey had both Patrick Mahomes and Kenneth Walker BEGGING for mercy. Bailey now has 7.5 sacks (T-3rd in NFL) and 5 FF’s (1st in NFL) on his rookie season. The Jets seem to have found their franchise pass rusher in the rookie OLB 😳🔥 pic.twitter.com/Dp0cBc2vzx
For the Jets to increase their chances of winning, they’ll need to exploit the Chargers' weak interior and send pressure up the middle. New York ranks fifth in blitz rate (33.8%), and a more aggressive approach from its linebackers could help take advantage of Los Angeles’ protection woes.
The Jets must use Demario Davis on interior blitzes, as he has already recorded two sacks doing so this season. Jamien Sherwood should also be used in similar situations, as he has the speed and athleticism to get to the quarterback.
This would give the Jets another way to create pressure without relying solely on their edge rushers.
With Geno Smith expected to play Sunday, he’s poised to bounce back against the Chargers. Los Angeles’ secondary has been subpar this season, ranking 23rd in passing yards allowed per game (233.4) and tied for 11th in passing touchdowns allowed (13). Its heavy reliance on zone could also work in Smith’s favor.
According to Sharp Football Analysis, the Chargers rank 23rd in zone rate (23.9%) and are in man coverage just 13.4% of the time. This is an encouraging sign for Smith, as the 14-year veteran has feasted against zone coverage this season, completing 71.3% of his passes for eight yards per attempt.
However, Smith has been criticized for playing too conservatively this season, as he tends to take his time in the pocket while searching for an opening downfield. While that patience has occasionally worked against him, as it’s contributed to his 29 sacks this season (third-most in the NFL), he’s at his best when he has time to read and dissect the defense.
That’s where the Chargers’ reliance on zone coverage could work in his favor. Zone defenses allow Smith to identify soft spots in the secondary and find open receivers. Rather than forcing throws into tight windows, he can use his patience to find receivers in space. Fortunately for Smith, the Jets’ offensive line has done a good job of giving him time, as he ranks ninth in average time to throw (2.93) , per NFL Next Gen Stats.
While the Chargers could certainly look to switch things up against Smith and play more man coverage, their secondary injuries could limit any potential changes. Derwin James is already on the injured reserve, while Rodney Shelley missed Wednesday and Thursday’s practices. Kendall Williamson also missed Thursday’s practice, while Donte Jackson and Isas Waxter were limited participants.
With limited depth in their back end, the Chargers will likely stick to what’s worked for them and try to confuse Smith at the line of scrimmage with blitz disguises and simulated pressure. This could play right into Smith’s strengths, especially if the offensive line can continue to provide him enough time.
When Mike McDaniel became the new offensive coordinator for the Chargers, many thought that he would raise the unit’s play and help elevate Justin Herbert to the upper echelon of quarterbacks. However, Los Angeles’ transition to McDaniel’s offense has done more harm than good.
Herbert has regressed significantly in the new system, consistently making costly mistakes, and the offense has struggled to put up points. The unit hasn’t lived up to expectations and ranks near the bottom in every major statistical category except rushing.
Despite several injuries upfront, the Chargers’ rushing attack has had some success this season, ranking 11th in rushing yards per game (119.6) and tied for 13th in rushing yards per attempt (4.2). Los Angeles is coming off its best rushing performance of the season, thanks to Omarion Hampton, who rushed for 105 of the team’s 160 yards and a touchdown in the team’s Monday night win against the Ravens.
McDaniel finally gave the second-year back from North Carolina the majority of the workload after leaning on a three-back rotation for much of the season. Since that approach led to a win, the Chargers will likely continue to use Hampton as a feature back against the Jets.
New York has notoriously struggled to contain the run this season, ranking 30th in rushing yards allowed per game (135.3), tied for the fourth-most rushing touchdowns allowed, and tied for the third-most rushes of 10+ yards allowed. The unit also hasn’t allowed fewer than 90 rushing yards since Week 2.
Given the Jets' struggles against the run, the team must prioritize holding Hampton in check. He’s a physical, downhill runner who’s also fast for his size, running a 4.46-second 40-yard dash at the NFL Scouting Combine.
Although his numbers don’t back it up this season, he excels at creating extra yards after contact. Hampton averaged 3.95 yards after contact against the Ravens and is tied for 27th in yards after contact per attempt (2.95) , per PFF.
Winning at the point of attack and getting to Hampton before he can build up any momentum will be critical for New York, as slowing Hampton down will force Los Angeles into more passing situations and shut down play-action opportunities.
The Jets have struggled against play-action this season, allowing a 67% completion rate and 8.1 yards per attempt , according to Sharp Football Analysis. With Herbert ranking 12th in play-action dropback rate (26.9%), New York must limit Hampton’s success on the ground and force the Chargers to beat them through the air.
If New York contains Hampton, it’ll significantly increase its chances of winning.

title: Kracz: 5 Biggest Reasons Why Eagles Finally Ended Their Losing Streak in Week 11
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A.  — The locker room music was back, thump, thumping from somewhere. So were the smiles, ear to ear, and the players’ playfulness with each other. This is what winning feels like inside the Eagles’ locker room . It had been more than two months since they experienced this.
It’s nowhere near time to make Super Bowl reservations, especially after the Giants reached six wins on Sunday, to the Eagles’ three, and maybe a win angered draftniks hoping the Eagles could get a top-five pick, but Sunday’s 19-16 win over the Steelers might silence the ‘Fire Sirianni’ crowd. Probably not, but at the very least, it ended a seven-game losing streak that began after their last win on Sept. 20.
“Definitely a good feeling to get that (losing streak) off your shoulders,” kicker Jake Elliott said. “It's something you can build on. Every week we get to a point where we feel really confident about winning a football game, and I think this is a testament to two long weeks of work and looking at ourselves in the mirror and figuring some things out. It's fun to see that come to fruition.”
There are many reasons the Eagles knocked off their cross-state rival. Here are my top five:
Elliott had attempted just eight field goals all year and missed only one. He was 4-for-4 on Sunday, making both attempts beyond 50 yards. He is 4-for-4 on 50-plus field goals this season. He had been just 5-for-13 from that distance over the last two seasons combined.
Both his 50-plus yarders against the Steelers increased the Eagles’ lead to two possessions and came in the third and fourth quarters.
Jake Elliott splits the uprights on a 55-yard field goal. PITvsPHI on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/7ZASF9vxzz
“Haven't had a whole lot of chances this year, so it's always nice to be able to get a few early and kind of get into the rhythm of the game,” Elliott said. “Kind of helps it flow and just knowing what the wind's doing out there. I’m just happy to have a game like that. It feels like it’s been a while since we’ve had a bunch of attempts in a game.”
Playing his third straight game as a starting linebacker, Trotter was superb , making 13 tackles. In his three starts, he has 34 tackles, with three for loss. More starts are coming after Zack Baun was placed on injured reserve on Saturday.
“It's definitely a big opportunity,” he said. “My role has changed, and it’s increased, and I'm just trying to make sure I do my job and do my job out of the 11 guys out there and do what I gotta do to help the team win.”
Trotter played a part, but many others did, too. Pittsburgh's Jaylen Warren was averaging nearly six yards per run this season, but had 28 yards on nine carries. As a team, the Steelers averaged 116.1 yards rushing per game. They had 73 rushing yards on Sunday, and it’s never good when your soon-to-be 43-year-old quarterback, Aaron Rodgers, leads the way with 29 yards on the ground.
“Going into the game, (defensive coordinator) Vic (Fangio) told us to have them (in rushing yards) under less than... what was it?” Jihaad Campbell said, turning to Jonathan Greenard in the locker next to him.
Greenard replied, “I think under 75.”
Campbell, who had seven tackles, responded: “Whatever. It was really about having that mental toughness, that strength, whatever the circumstances were.”
Did T.J. Watt play? The rookie right tackle prevented one of the game’s all-time great sack artists from taking over the game and breathing on Joe Milton. Bell did get called for a hold when he dragged Watt to the ground, but that was better than Watt teeing off on the Eagles’ QB.
The offense still wasn’t much—the Eagles were outgained 255-214 and lost the time of possession by 11 minutes. Still, the Eagles' head coach once again found magic during the bye week, and Sirianni is now 6-0 coming out of a week off.
Some of the things that looked better: more shotgun formations, communication up front, and the offense got to the line quicker.

title: 3 Good, 2 Bad Box Score Surprises After Eagles' Victory vs. Steelers
full_text:
A third-down connection between quarterback Joe Milton and wide receiver DeVonta Smith sealed the deal. The Eagles' losing streak is over. Philadelphia snapped a seven-game skid with a 19-16 win over Pittsburgh in Week 11.
The Steelers are now 0-5 all-time in clashes at Lincoln Financial Field.
Of course, there were peaks and valleys on Sunday. Several Eagles stepped up in front of the home crowd, while a few others fell short of expectations.
Let's dive into the good and the bad box score surprises.
Talk about taking advantage of an opportunity. Linebacker Jeremiah Trotter Jr. has taken on an every-down role lately, as Zack Baun and Jihaad Campbell deal with injuries. Trotter logged a team-high 13 tackles (nine solo) against Pittsburgh. It was his third straight game with double-digit tackles.
It's worth pointing out that it was also Trotter's second straight game with at least two stuffs (tackles at or behind the line of scrimmage). The Clemson product's ferocity in run defense kept the Steelers in long third-down situations. Trotter should remain a leader on defense with Baun on injured reserve.
Philly fans waited with bated breath every time running back Saquon Barkley limped off the field in the three weeks prior to the bye. Week 11 was a different experience. Barkley looked explosive and handled a heavy workload. Backup running back Will Shipley's only carries came in the fourth quarter.
SAQUON HOUSE CALL! pic.twitter.com/e009d6X5H5
Barkley recorded 75 yards and one touchdown on 17 carries (4.4 yards per carry). It was his highest yardage total since Week 3. The veteran's 38-yard sprint to the end zone in the first quarter gave the Eagles their largest lead of the season at 13-0. It was an excellent effort that Philly needs to build on.
The Eagles were not feeling the absence of defensive tackle Jordan Davis in Week 11. That's partly because of Byron Young's performance. The 26-year-old made his presence felt with four tackles and two sacks. It was a major leap forward, considering Young entered with 2.5 sacks in 32 career games.
That's 2️⃣ for BY pic.twitter.com/V6HpQd7KuM
Young never quit during his reps, which helped him get quarterback Aaron Rodgers on the ground. He played 22 of the 71 defensive snaps (31%). Expect that mark to rise with Davis in Jacksonville. More timely sacks down the stretch will be crucial to Young's chances of getting re-signed next offseason.
Makai Lemon was drafted to be a reliable slot option in a wide receiver room filled with deep threats. There have been highlights during his rookie campaign, but his showing in Week 11 was not one of them. Lemon hauled in one of three targets for three yards. Two throws went right through his hands.
Lemon has posted five drops in his last four games. It's a surprising trend, considering he was praised for his sure-handedness at USC. That development cannot continue if the Eagles want to boost their offensive numbers . A matchup against the dismal Dallas defense on Thanksgiving gives Lemon a shot to bounce back.
Milton's first NFL win was far from perfect. He frustrated fans when he stared at his own fumble and overthrew Smith on a deep ball. The most concerning part of Milton's outing was his negligible impact on the ground. Someone with his mobility shouldn't finish with seven yards on five carries.
Milton struggled to escape the pocket, and when he did, a Pittsburgh defender quickly tracked him down. That was a very different result than his 64 rushing yards on nine carries against the Giants. Figuring out how to utilize Milton's legs should be a priority ahead of a duel with the Cowboys.

title: Eagles Week 11 Stock Market: Biggest Takeaways After Sunday's Win Over the Steelers
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — The Eagles finally ended the misery.
After seven consecutive losses, Philadelphia ground out a 19-16 win over Pittsburgh on Sunday at Lincoln Financial Field, snapping the skid and improving to 3-7 with their first victory since Sept. 20.⁠
Joe Milton got his first career win in his second start , going 11-for-21 for 141 yards. Saquon Barkley provided the early spark with a 38-yard touchdown run that helped build a 13-0 first-quarter lead. From there, it was mostly survival mode—the offense managed just over 214 yards total—but Jake Elliott was automatic with four field goals, including bombs from 53 and 55 yards, and the defense sacked Aaron Rodgers five times while keeping Pittsburgh in check most of the afternoon.⁠
Rodgers hit practice-squad call-up Max Hurleman for a late touchdown to cut it to 19-16, but Milton connected with DeVonta Smith on third-and-6 to run out the clock in the waning second.
The Steelers remain winless in Philadelphia since 1965.
It wasn’t pretty, but after two months of nothing, it felt like something. Here's the Week 11 Eagles stock market report: the Bulls and the Bears.
The Steelers arrived having not won in Philadelphia since 1965. That's six-plus decades, but only 11 games between the Keystone State intraconference foes. Whether it's the cheesesteaks or the Schuylkill River, Pittsburgh just can't win in this interstate rivalry, even with the Eagles entering the game on a seven-game skid.
Milton's numbers were pedestrian but his arm strength wasn't.
"Rocket Joe" was really humming in this one, eating up Makai Lemon with a Nolan Ryan fastball and overthrowing DeVonta Smith on a deep shot that traveled about 60 yards in the air. If Milton can ever figure out how to pitch , so to speak, look out. His out patterns are works of art when the accuracy is there, and he won the game with a third-down strike to Smith in the biggest moment.
The Eagles played their first game since trading nose tackle Jordan Davis to Jacksonville. Byron Young and Gabe Hall combined for three sacks, and the run defense didn't suffer at all, with Jeremiah Trotter Jr. showing off his instincts at middle linebacker and Jihaad Campbell playing well in his return.
What a play by Jeremiah Trotter Jr. for the fourth down stop PITvsPHI on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/hrkAdRnrzv
Add in Ty Robinson, and the Eagles' makeshift plan at nose and shade was successful.
Both Braden Mann and Jake Elliott were big parts of the win.
Mann unleashed a 70-yard bomb that was placed to pin the returner on the sideline with near perfection. In four opportunities, Mann finished with a 59.3 gross average, with two punts placed inside the 20. Elliott was responsible for 13 of the Eagles' 19 points, hitting all four field goals and two 50-plus kicks.
The offense generated some explosive plays, including the 38-yard touchdown run by Barkley, and Milton throws of 38 yards and 29 yards to Dallas Goedert and Darius Cooper, respectively. Overall, though, the moribund Steelers offense still outgained the Eagles by a 251 to 214 margin.
Philadelphia's structured offense remains a work in progress, to be kind.
The Eagles' two longest and fastest cornerbacks struggled. Riq Woolen was benched at one point after having some tackling issues, while Kelee Ringo could not track a Rodgers touchdown throw to Max Hurleman that kept Pittsburgh alive late in the fourth quarter.
Eagles defensive line coach Clint Hurtt got into a bit of a dust-up with strength and conditioning coach Fernando Noriega on the sidelines. It was quickly settled, but it shows how frustration can boil over during significant struggles.

title: 7 Eagles Winners & 4 Losers After Sunday's Slump-Snapping Win Over Steelers
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — Lincoln the Eagle showed some fight on his traditional flyover during the National Anthem. The Eagle refused to land well after the song ended, perhaps putting the best pregame ceremony in the NFL in jeopardy of happening again.
Lincoln the eagle is still flying around well after the end of the anthem. Won’t land. They’re doing to coin flip. pic.twitter.com/lvaBBgdrJG
Perhaps inspired by Lincoln’s flight, the Eagles themselves came out soaring, and whattya know, they snapped their seven-game losing streak with an inspired 19-16 win over the visiting Steelers in Week 11.
Pittsburgh is now 0-12 in Philly since last winning a game there in 1965. They are 6-4 and have lost twice. The Eagles’ last win was more than two months ago, when they beat the Titans on Sept. 20. They are now 3-7, with a Thanksgiving trip to Dallas up next.
The Eagles got off to a strong start—thanks, Lincoln—putting up a season-high 13 first-quarter points and holding the Steelers to 35 total yards, 0 passing yards, and one first down in the opening frame.
Joe Milton made his second career start a winning one. He played mistake-free football for a second straight game. He was 11-for-21 for 141 yards. His third-and-six throw to DeVonta Smith that covered six yards sealed the win.
On 3rd & 6, DeVonta Smith comes up clutch. PITvsPHI on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/kx0HtT2tQs
Smith made his return after missing three straight games with a hamstring injury and five-of-nine overall. He ended with five catches for 41 yards.
Now that the losing streak is finally over, let's break down the biggest Eagles winners and losers coming out of Sunday afternoon's victory.
The kicker deserves some love for a solid season that continued with a 4-for-4 day, including a pair of makes beyond 50 yards. His 53-yarder gave the Eagles a 16-6 lead with 8:33 to play in the third quarter. His 55-yarder with 4:9 to go in the fourth quarter made it 19-9. He added makes from 41 and 29.
No Jordan Davis? No problem.
Byron Young had a career-high two sacks, and Gabe Hall, in just his third career game, had a big one in the fourth quarter that led to a three-and-out Steelers possession.
That's 2️⃣ for BY pic.twitter.com/V6HpQd7KuM
The Eagles’ pass rush had five sacks of Aaron Rodgers, one game after putting up six sacks against the Giants. The other two against the Steelers were turned in by Nolan Smith, which was his team-high sixth, and Jonathan Greenard, who has a sack in back-to-back games.
The Eagles' star running back scored a rushing touchdown for the fourth straight game, this one from 38 yards out to make it 13-0 in the first quarter. Looking healthy again, Barkley finished with 75 yards on 17 carries (4.4 yards per carry).
The backup cornerback had an end zone PBU to force the Steelers to make a 25-yard field goal. It was a win for the Eagles’ defense after Pittsburgh marched 77 yards using 17 plays in 8:22, only to settle for three points. Later, Jones made another end zone play to prevent a touchdown and force Pittsburgh to settle for a field goal.
Everywhere that DK Metcalf went, Quinyon Mitchell went with him. So frustrated was the defense Mitchell played on him that Metcalf got tossed from the game with 4:53 to play in the third quarter after his second personal foul penalty.
Status alert: DK Metcalf ejected Sunday. pic.twitter.com/4YZOchHqAC
Metcalf’s final line: one catch for two yards; two penalties for 30 yards.
Jeremiah Trotter, Jr., and Jihaad Campbell made sure the Steelers' running game didn't get going. Trotter ended with 13 tackles. Campbell had seven tackles, one behind Marcus Epps—and a shout-out to the safety here for his sure tackling.
His 70-yard punt pinned the Steelers at their own four. The defense forced a three-and-out and led to good field position; the Eagles cashed in for three points in the third quarter to open a 16-6 lead. There was a point in the game when he had an average of 59 yards. His career high is 53, set four years ago. He finished with a net of 50 against the Steelers.
The kick returner fumbled the opening kickoff of the second half. If not for a strong defensive stand by the defense that limited the Steelers to just a field goal, the damage could have been more severe after Pittsburgh took over at Philly's 24.
Woolen missed tackles on the Steelers’ first scoring drive and may have been benched in favor of Jonathan Jones. Woolen had to return in the second half after Quinyon Mitchell left with a hamstring injury.
The Eagles have five tight ends on the roster, but Dallas Goedert was the only one to make an impact, and even that was minimal, with one catch on one target for 38 yards.
Pressed into action after cornerback Quinyon Mitchell was injured in the third quarter and Jonathan Jones was hurt in the final three minutes of the game, Ringo gave up a third-down TD pass from 20 yards out to pull the Steelers within 19-6 with 1:21 remaining.

title: 5 Eagles Who Will Likely Be Inactive vs. Steelers in Week 11
full_text:
Coming out of their bye week, the Philadelphia Eagles will be looking to snap a seven-game losing streak when they host the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 11.
The bye week afforded the banged-up Eagles some extra time to rest, but they still have a plethora of players dealing with injury issues. Here's a look at five Eagles players who have either already been ruled out of the game against Pittsburgh or are unlikely to be active.
If the Eagles are going to snap their seven-game losing streak, they're going to have to do it without one of their best defensive players. After missing all three practices during the week due to a back injury, star linebacker Zack Baun will be sidelined against the Steelers. It will be the second game of the season that Baun misses. He was also ruled out of Philadelphia's Week 4 loss to the Los Angeles Rams due to a concussion.
The Eagles will miss Baun's production against Pittsburgh. He's leading the Eagles in total tackles on the season with 65. He's also tallied five passes defended, two sacks and one fumble recovery.
The Eagles will likely be getting one starting wide receiver back against the Steelers. DeVonta Smith was a full participant for Philly in practice on Thursday and Friday, and he carries no designation into the game against Pittsburgh, which indicates that he should be good to go. However, another starting receiver will remain sidelined.
Dontayvion Wicks has missed three straight games with an ankle injury, and that number will now stretch to four. Wicks was a limited participant in practice throughout the week, but ultimately he wasn't quite good to go. Perhaps he'll be able to return for Philly's next game against the Dallas Cowboys on Thanksgiving.
In addition to Baun, the Eagles will also likely be without another linebacker in Smael Mondon Jr. Mondon was a full participant in practice on Wednesday, but he suffered an ankle injury and didn't practice at all on Thursday and Friday, which is a pretty good indication that he won't be available to play on Sunday.
Mondon has played 69 percent of all special teams snaps for the Eagles this season, compared to just four percent of all defensive snaps, so he'll be missed more on special teams than he will be defensively.
The Eagles opened the practice window for running back Will Shipley earlier this week, which means that he's trending in the right direction following a stint on IR due to a foot injury. However, it's doubtful that he'll be able to return to in-game action so quickly following an extended stint on the sideline.
He was limited in practice on Wednesday and Thursday and then he didn't practice at all on Friday, which tells you that we shouldn't expect to see him out on the field on Sunday. His return is on the horizon, though.
Joe Milton will get his second straight start at quarterback for the Eagles, and despite dealing with a rib injury all week, it looks like Tanner McKee will be good to go to serve as the backup behind Milton against Pittsburgh.
That could leave Cole Payton as the odd man out, as the Eagles aren't likely to have three active QBs for the game. Payton will likely serve as the emergency third QB for Philly in Week 11.

title: Eagles Seem to Have a Clear Idea of What's Holding Offense Back
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA - The Eagles’ offense has looked lost for stretches of this season, and the diagnosis coming out of the bye week is not complicated, according to the team. It’s communication. Embattled offensive coordinator Sean Mannion has been consistent about it, mentioning the word nearly a dozen times at his post-bye week press conference.
When asked what rose to the top of the recurring issues in the self-scout, Mannion’s answer was direct: “I think just communication really. I think that’s the biggest thing. Making sure we’re razor, razor sharp with our communication.”
That is the through-line. My understanding is that the Eagles are not burning the play clock unnecessarily in Nick Sirianni's mind , nor does the head coach believe the play calls themselves are too wordy in the way some outside analysis has suggested.
The issue is far more granular than that. The staff routinely tags the calls with identifiers for each position group so that everyone is not carrying the entire package in their head at once.
The quarterback still has to process the full picture. A back like Saquon Barkley needs the formation, the protection plan, and his own assignment. Others like the offensive line can be a little more narrow. When any piece of that chain is fuzzy, though, the whole thing slows or breaks.
Mannion described the self-scout as productive precisely because it highlighted both what is working and what keeps showing up as a problem.
“It allowed us to really kind of sharpen our focus in terms of some of the communication things we’ve got to get better at,” the OC said.
The goal is not to invent a new language. It is to make the existing one faster and cleaner so that everyone is on the same page even when the defense presents unscouted looks.
Mannion expanded on the practical side of that. The emphasis is on making the correct call, then streamlining how it is delivered so it is “concise, it’s quick, it’s clear.”
There is room for conversation at the line—Mannion noted that even elite pairings like Peyton Manning and Jeff Saturday had more back-and-forth than the broadcast view always showed—but the default cannot be hesitation or cross-talk. If the huddle call is clear, the alignment is confident. From there, the line-of-scrimmage communication has to be equally sharp. Both layers matter.
The presence of a relatively new center in Drew Kendall and a quarterback still banking live reps in Joe Milton adds another layer to overcome. That’s not Manning and Saturday.
Mannion praised Kendall’s command and intelligence while noting that Milton’s comfort will grow with more actual calls at the line rather than just meeting-room study. That process is normal. What is not sustainable is the current level of inconsistency in getting everyone operating from the same information at the same speed.
The Eagles feel they do not need a radical overhaul.
They need the communication that Mannion identified as the top priority to become the strength it has to be for this offense to function at a high level. Until that happens, the production will continue to lag behind.
As far as what's to blame for the issues, if you take the Eagles' self-reflective deep dive as earnest and honest, that puts the clear impetus on teaching. The new offensive staff hasn't gotten its students up to speed.

title: Examining Eagles' Nose Tackle Options With Jordan Davis Gone
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – Vic Fangio will miss Jordan Davis , perhaps more as a person, but certainly as a player, too. Davis was his nose tackle. The Eagles defensive coordinator doesn’t really have a nose tackle in the truest sense of the word, which is an anchor in the middle that is big, strong, and meaty, like Davis, who is 6-6, 335 pounds.
“Got a little emotional with him when we talked about it after (the trade) happened,” said Fangio. “I've got a lot of players that, over the years, I've remained in touch with and had a good relationship with, some 40 years ago, 30, 20, 10 years ago. He's one of them. So, I'll miss him personally, but he'll do good, and we'll be ready to roll.”
Rolling will be difficult with the Steelers Jaylen Warren and his 5.7 yards per carry coming to town. A good run stuffer would help, but Davis is gone.
So, who will Fangio roll with in the middle of the defense?
Ty Robinson and Byron Young. These are the top two favorites. Their snap counts will rise, and they must show they can handle the job and the increased workload. Robinson is 6-5, 290; Young is 6-3, 290.
“When I first came here, I told you guys I was gonna be a Swiss Army knife,” said Robinson. “All last year I was learning all three positions, so the playbook's the easiest part now. It's just to go out there and execute and try to fill the shoes of Jordan Davis. And those are some big shoes to fill. I know me and BY are gonna be out there handling our business.”
Added Young: “Ty and I are a little bit smaller, but we don't expect there to be any drop-off.”
Gabe Hall. He is 6-6 but lean at 295 pounds. Fangio mentioned him as a possibility, though it feels like a stretch that the nose would suit him. Her made the opening-day roster heading into 2025, played two games, and then was released and added back to the practice squad.
Zion Wilson. He’s an interesting candidate, at 6-3, 320. He was moved to Davis’s locker in a surprising move, at least to him. Wilson said he came back from the bye and went to his locker in the back, where most of the practice squad players dress, only to find his stuff and nameplate gone. He thought he had been cut until someone told him he got moved to Davis’s locker.
To his right is Nolan Smith. Two stalls away to his right is Jalen Carter. On his left is Uar Bernard. Wilson said the team told him they wanted him to “be around the guys.”
By many accounts, Wilson has also had a good two weeks of scout team reps and could be poised for an elevation.
Leki Fotu. Fotu was signed to the practice squad on the same day the Davis trade was announced. He is a seven-year NFL veteran. Most recently, he spent training camp with the Giants this past summer. He is 6-5, 330 pounds, with 4.5 sacks in 66 games played and 26 starts.
“I’m ready to rock,” he said. “This is huge, man. I couldn't be more grateful and blessed to be in this position, so I’m gonna take advantage of the opportunity and go from there.”

title: DeVonta Smith Will Play vs. Steelers, Heating Up Eagles' Race for Leader in Receiving Yards
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – The race is on between DeVonta Smith and Makai Lemon to see who will lead the Eagles in receiving.
Smith will return to the lineup on Sunday when the Pittsburgh Steelers visit for a 1 p.m. kickoff after missing five of nine games this season with a hamstring and three of the previous games before the bye. He has 310 receiving yards in limited action. Lemon has overtaken him and has a two-yard head start with eight games to play. Lemon also has more catches, with 37 to Smith’s 26.
“I feel great,” said Smith earlier in the week, “just continue to go out here this week, get these reps with Joe (Milton), and we just go from there.”
Milton will make his second start at quarterback. He took over the job in Week 9, so Smith has not played with him.
“Joe's a great quarterback,” said Smith. “He's still learning the offense. We're trying to get him up to speed. Being out for a while, I haven't got those reps with him, haven't kind of really been in the huddle with him. So, it’s me trying to learn how he is, how he calls the plays, and things like that. What his thought process is as well.”
Lemon has one game under his belt with Milton. That could be an advantage for the rookie in his quest to lead the team in receiving. Another advantage Lemon could have is that Dontayvion Wicks will miss his fourth straight game with an ankle/foot injury.
With A.J. Brown traded in the offseason, the expectation was that Smith would make it two straight years leading the team in receiving. Last year, he had 1,008 yards, edging Brown, who had 1,003.
In addition to Wicks, linebacker Zack Baun was ruled out for Sunday. Baun suffered a back injury in the Eagles’ pre-bye loss to the Giants.
Jihaad Campbell, who missed the previous two games with a hamstring/quad injury, will line up with Jeremiah Trotter Jr. as the starting linebackers, but depth could be an issue with Smael Mondon listed as doubtful for Sunday with an ankle injury suffered after stepping in for Baun against the Giants and making five tackles in 26 defensive snaps.
Running back Will Shipley, who had his 21-day practice window opened earlier in the week, is still on IR but is listed as questionable. If he plays, the Eagles will have to make a roster move to add him.
The Steelers listed six players as questionable: linebackers Patrick Queen and Nick Herbig, receivers Michael Pitman and Roman Wilson, safety DeShon Elliott, and rookie guard Gennings Dunker.

title: 3 Things Eagles Need From Joe Milton in Week 11 vs. Steelers
full_text:
Eagles quarterback Joe Milton will get his second consecutive start , and the second start of his career, against the Steelers on Sunday.
Milton completed 18 passes for 169 yards against the Giants in Week 9, and he'll look to build on that performance coming out of the bye week against the Steelers. That said, here are three things the Eagles will want to see from Milton in his second start.
With one start already under his belt and an extra week to learn the offense afforded by the bye week, Milton is feeling increased confidence ahead of the game against Pittsburgh.
“What's different for me now? My confidence. Just confidence in knowing this offense and what these coaches and my teammates around me are instilling in me and talking to me about," Milton said.
This increased confidence should translate to increased accuracy for Milton, who completed just 52% of his passes (18 of 34) in his first start. In fairness to Milton, he was consistently under pressure, but he still had his fair share of errant throws he'd like to have back. It would be nice to see improvement in that area. The fact that he'll likely have top receivers DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks back should help.
Milton has garnered nicknames for his arm strength . He recently revealed (h/t Zach Berman) that he prefers "Mr. Rocket" to "Bazooka Joe."
Joe Milton doesn’t like “Bazooka Joe.” He prefers “Mr. Rocket.” “Bazookas only travel so far,” he said. pic.twitter.com/tur5oWbaJU
However, we didn't really get to see too much of that rocket arm in Milton's first start against New York. He averaged just five yards per attempt on his 34 passes during the game, and his longest completion went for just 20 yards. It would be nice to see the Eagles open things up a little bit more in that regard.
That would look like offensive coordinator Sean Mannion dialing up more deep balls to threats like Smith and Makai Lemon. At this point, there's nothing to be gained for the Eagles by remaining conservative. They might as well open things up and let Milton show off that nickname-worthy arm.
The thing that Milton did best in his start against New York was picking up yards with his legs. He actually led the Eagles in rushing in the game with 64 yards on nine carries—an average of 7.1 yards per carry. His ability to take off makes Milton an inherently dangerous quarterback, and he should continue to lean into that skill when the opportunity presents itself.
The goal for Milton moving forward should be to find a nice mix between showing off his arm and using his legs to move the ball downfield.

title: Potential Daniel Jones Flyer Leaves Eagles' Offense With Nothing to Lose (And Everything to Gain)
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — The Eagles’ offensive shift this season has been a disaster .
Through nine games, the Eagles' perennial postseason berth is in hospice at 2-7 and in the midst of a seven-game losing streak, averaging just 16.4 points and 260 total yards per game—numbers that rank near or at the bottom of the league in points, yards, yards per play, and efficiency metrics.
The unit under first-time offensive coordinator Sean Mannion had looked lifeless from a structure standpoint, even when Jalen Hurts was under center , never mind novices like Tanner McKee and current starter Joe Milton.
Hurts is on injured reserve and likely out for the remainder of the season with blood clots in his lungs. The replacements—McKee (three starts, all losses) and Milton (one start: 18-of-34 for 169 yards)—have not provided a meaningful evaluation of Mannion's scheme, the rebuilding offensive line, or the skill-position talent.
Milton gets another start against the Steelers this weekend, but his development isn't going to reveal much about the actual scheme, as his late arrival from the practice squad in Dallas demands scaling things back.
Enter Daniel Jones, whom the Colts waived on Friday after an 11-game stretch that produced a league-worst 13 interceptions, a 65.4 passer rating, and a 3-8 record as a starter.
Per Shane Steichen, we have released QB Daniel Jones. pic.twitter.com/jdGAZqj9ZI
Jones is subject to waivers and would carry only a modest remaining salary this season if claimed, but a somewhat significant injury guarantee for 2027 virtually assures the veteran with 93 career starts will get to the open market and choose his next destination at something near the veteran minimum.
Jones would offer the kind of professional experience the Eagles’ current backups simply do not have and the opportunity to get maybe four to six games of clean evaluation for Mannion’s system.
This is not a call for Jones to be the long-term answer. He has been turnover-prone and inefficient in 2026, still working back from last year’s Achilles injury. But that is precisely why he is useful right now.
The Eagles have not yet seen what this offense looks like with a veteran starter who has navigated full seasons, protections, and complex defenses.
McKee and Milton have been asked to play with almost no runway. Signing Jones would give Mannion, head coach Nick Siriann, and general manager Howie Roseman a better read: Is the scheme fundamentally flawed? Is the offensive line too porous? Are the receivers unable to win at the required rate? Or has the problem been, at least in part, the lack of a quarterback who has actually done this at a high level for an extended stretch?
The Eagles are already out of realistic playoff contention. The second half of the season is an evaluation window, whether they want it to be or not. Using that period with a 29-year-old signal caller who has started nearly 100 games would be far more informative than continuing to cycle through developmental options who have combined for a handful of starts.
If Jones looks competent, it isolates issues elsewhere. If he looks as bad as he did in Indianapolis, the organization learns that the supporting cast and scheme may need even more overhaul than already planned.
From Jones’s perspective, Philadelphia can offer the kind of playing time that could convince another organization to take a flyer on him for the 2027 season. Another fringe benefit is that Jones remains very close to Eagles star running back Saquon Barkley from their days together with the Giants.
The cost would be low to sign Jones, and the information value could be high if the goal is still to figure out what has gone so wrong with the system.
However, if the Eagles have already made that decision and Mannion is essentially coaching out the string, Milton should remain the starter to see if he can develop into a capable backup for future seasons.

title: Steelers’ DK Metcalf Addresses Ejection, Cooper DeJean Incident
full_text:
Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf addressed his ejection in the team's Week 11 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles a day after the incident occurred.
After not speaking with reporters in the Steelers' locker room at Lincoln Financial Field following the contest, Metcalf instead did so back at UPMC Rooney Sports Complex on November 23.
When asked what happened in his interactions with Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean, who was on the receiving end of both of Metcalf's unsportsmanlike conduct penalties in the third quarter that led to his ejection, the latter simply stated, "can't remember."
Metcalf also responded with, "you've gotta ask him," when asked if he felt like DeJean provoked him into those exchanges, as well as stating, "just wish I would've been there for my team," when asked if he wished he handled the situation differently looking back on it.
Additionally, Metcalf answered, "I think you got to ask the people that seemingly do that to me," in response to a question asking why it's been a struggle for him to keep his composure at times throughout his career.
He also denied poking DeJean in the eyes, with Metcalf maintaining that he was telling him to stop pushing him instead.
Metcalf deflected any questions about possible discipline from either the NFL or the Steelers when that topic was broached by stating that those questions should instead be asked to the league or general manager Omar Khan.
A suspension does appear rather likely for the 28-year-old, however, and if one is handed down, it will likely come within the next couple of days ahead of Pittsburgh's Black Friday matinee against the Denver Broncos in Week 12.
The NFL has given out suspensions for poking players in the eyes, with one of the more pertinent examples coming when Denver Broncos cornerback Aqib Talib was suspended for a game in 2015 after doing so to Indianapolis Colts tight end Dwayne Allen.
Should the league's review of the situation prove that Metcalf did in fact poke DeJean in the eye despite the former disputing that narrative, he could ultimately face a similar fate.
It wouldn't be the first time Metcalf was suspended in his two years with the Steelers up to this point, as he missed the team's final two regular season games of the 2025 campaign after an altercation with a Detroit Lions fan at Ford Field.
Because Metcalf doesn't have any guarantees left on the four-year, $132 million contract he signed with Pittsburgh after coming over in a trade from the Seattle Seahawks in March 2025 while also having it reworked this past offseason, his deal essentially can't be voided as a result.
The Steelers do have a few options when it comes to moving on from him, though that decision may not come until the offseason.
If they were to trade or cut him without a post-June 1 designation ahead of next season, the organization would have to take on $35.775 million in dead money for 2027, $23.850 million in 2028 and $11.925 million in 2029. (per Over the Cap ).
Should Metcalf be traded or released with a post-June 1 designation, that dead money hit would lower to $11.925 million in 2027 all the way through the 2029 season on an annual basis.
It remains to be seen how Pittsburgh goes about approaching Metcalf following his ejection against the Eagles, but it's a bit of a precarious spot to be in considering he's still under contract for three more years after this current season.
