title: Mike McCarthy Hints at Changes for Steelers
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers suffered a surprising Week 11 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. Losers of two straight contests, the team is now 6-4 and facing the sobering reality that they might not be the team their earlier 6-2 record indicated.
Following the loss, Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said they have to adjust, while he shouldered blame for the current losing streak.
"You just need a clear vision of the plan for this week and accountability, starting with me," he told reporters postgame. "I start by looking at myself. We'll have a good plan by Friday, but at the end of the day, it's about having systems in place. You need systems that provide answers and adjustments when you hit stretches like this."
McCarthy is certainly right. Adjustments have to be made. But what will they actually look like? After the team's disappointing Week 2 loss to the New England Patriots, McCarthy made the difficult but necessary call to make two changes along the offensive line, and it immediately upgraded the lineup. That also gives some insight into two expected changes the Steelers will make for Week 12, and both could come on the offensive side of the ball.
Back-to-back losses for the Steelers have also come with their running game disappearing. Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle are an incredibly talented pair in the backfield, but the Steelers have lost the ability to run the ball productively. Part of it is the loss of left guard Mason McCormick, and another part of it is playing from behind.
Either way, the Steelers cannot afford to keep going down this road. To get back in the win column and restore their playoff ambitions, the Steelers have to recommit to the run game no matter the cost.
Quarterback Aaron Rodgers made that fact perfectly clear after their latest loss. He shared that while sometimes the game situation dictates what they call, it's no secret that a consistent running game opens up everything else on offense.
"We'd like to run the ball," he said after the game. "That makes everything easier. We're not trying to throw the ball 50 times a game. Some games might dictate some of that stuff, but we've got to run the football and generate explosive runs, and that sets up everything else."
So, what does that actually look like? For starters, 20 carries is not enough. Rodgers was the team's leading rusher against the Eagles, while Dowdle and Warren combined for just 14 carries. That's the second week in a row that they've run the ball less than 15 times.
Moving forward, the Steelers will have to give Warren at least 15 carries and 20 touches, while giving Dowdle 10 to 15 total touches per game.
For the second time this season, Spencer Anderson could lose his starting job along the offensive line. With heart and soul left guard Mason McCormick recovering from a dislocated ankle, the Steelers turned to Anderson.
In his first start at left guard this season, Anderson was the weak link.
With limited options, the Steelers may feel stuck, but they have another option. Rookie lineman Gennings Dunker is ready for action after returning from an MCL sprain, and while he's an imperfect young player, he gives this team a much better chance to get their run game back on track.
After the game, McCarthy stated that everything would be evaluated, but he reiterated that the Steelers need wide receiver DK Metcalf. Even after a disappointing first 10 games and despite being ejected due to an incident with Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean, McCarthy continues to express the organization's commitment to Metcalf.
I don't buy it. They've needed him all season long, and things keep getting worse. He makes too much money to bench, one could argue, but it doesn't matter anymore. Needing a change, DK Metcalf could ride the pine for a week to send a message.

title: Can Steelers Void DK Metcalf's Contract After Ejection?
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA -- The Pittsburgh Steelers didn't have DK Metcalf to finish their Week 11 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles, and there are questions about whether or not he'll be removed from their Week 12 game because of it.
But that's not the biggest question fans have.
Metcalf was ejected in the third quarter of the team's loss to the Philadelphia Eagles after what looked like attempting to poke Cooper DeJean in the eye. The penalty, which was called for taunting, was enough to disqualify him for the remainder of the match; it was not because he had two unsportsmanlike conduct penalties in the game.
He received his first one earlier after getting into a scuffle with DeJean near the Steelers' own goal line.
DK Metcalf has been ejected for unsportsmanlike conduct. Metcalf was ejected after two personal fouls. (📺 CBS) pic.twitter.com/f1OE50Fn6I
It's unknown at this time if Metcalf will be suspended for any further games. Because Metcalf was suspended last season for an altercation with a Detroit Lions fan at Ford Field, though, he may be on a short leash with the NFL when it comes to situations like this.
Because of the situation, fans are curious about Metcalf's contract situation. He and the Steelers have never found the results they were hoping for when Pittsburgh acquired him via trade from the Seattle Seahawks last season, and Metcalf is making over $30 million per year with the team.
The question is if this ejection and a possible suspension would be enough to void any guaranteed money in his remaining contract and allow Pittsburgh to move on from the wide receiver in the offseason. That was the case last year when he was suspended for the Lions fan incident, but the team chose to stick with him moving forward.
That is not the same case as this season. Because Metcalf does not have any more guaranteed money on his contract, the Steelers would not be able to void anything. And since they restructured his deal before the 2026 season, they are still on the hook for the $39 million dead cap they would take on if they were to release him.
Pittsburgh is going to be faced with a difficult decision when it comes to Metcalf this offseason. It's hard to imagine they would release him before the end of the 2026 campaign, as they would take on $35.7 million in dead cap, according to Spotrac.
Come the offseason, though, they may have a different outlook. Metcalf has not played well in the two years he's been with the Steelers and has struggled more this year than last.
You never know if the Steelers feel they've hit the end of the road with their top wide receiver. It doesn't seem to be working and with another in-season incident occurring, Metcalf has become more of a distraction than a benefit to their team.
Maybe the cost is worth starting over.

title: 5 Losers, 2 Winners From Steelers' Embarrassing Loss to Eagles
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers have hit a new low.
After their 38-18 blowout loss to the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football in Week 10, the Steelers' trip to Lincoln Financial Field to face the 2-7 Philadelphia Eagles felt like a perfect get-right spot.
Instead, the Eagles snapped their seven-game losing streak while Pittsburgh lost back-to-back contests for the first time this season and continues to trend downwards at an alarming pace.
With that, here are our winners and losers from the Steelers' 12th-straight loss in Philadelphia.
Metcalf continues to be detrimental to the Steelers.
The 28-year-old's drop issues didn't pop up in this game after they had been a major storyline all season long, as he has the second-most among wide receivers with six (per Pro Football Focus ).
Instead, Metcalf caught just one of his four targets, which was a screen, and finished with two yards before being ejected due to having two unsportsmanlike conduct penalties called against him in the third quarter.
On pace for a career-low 738 yards over 17 games with his antics becoming a real issue alongside his rapidly declining play, Metcalf's four-year, $132 million deal with Pittsburgh continues to look like one of the worst contracts in the NFL.
Rodgers' offensive line didn't do him any favors, as he was sacked five times, and we'll dive into that further a little bit later.
The 42-year-old was far from sharp even without taking into account the rate at which he was pressured, however. He didn't turn the ball over and completed 30 of his 44 passing attempts, but he only racked up 227 yards with a touchdown in the process and was once again largely unsuccessful when he tried to push the ball down the field.
Rodgers has proven to be far too inconsistent throwing the ball while also succumbing to pressure far too often and looking like a shell of his former self. He can manage the game at times, though the Steelers aren't going to get very far if he doesn't turn a corner down the stretch.
Elevated from the practice squad for this game after being activated from the practice squad/injured list earlier in the week, where he had resided since September 19, Hurleman certainly opened some eyes in his regular season debut.
Taking over the return man duties for rookie Kaden Wetjen, who was a healthy inactive, Hurleman posted 32 yards on two kick returns and 36 yards on three punt returns.
That wasn't the most impressive aspect of his performance, though. Taking on a larger role late in the contest, once Metcalf was ejected, Hurleman logged a team-high 61 yards on six receptions to go with a touchdown.
A training camp standout who also received praise from head coach Mike McCarthy and Rodgers in recent weeks , Hurleman might just be here to stay.
In his first start since Week 2, Anderson fell completely flat.
After opening the year as the starter at right guard before being replaced by Brock Hoffman in Week 3, Anderson was placed back into the starting lineup vs. Philadelphia at left guard due to the absence of Mason McCormick, who was placed on the reserve/injured list with an ankle injury he sustained in Week 10 against the Cincinnati Bengals.
Anderson proceeded to allow two sacks against the Eagles (according to Pro Football Focus ), and he was the weakest member of an offensive line that didn't have a banner day across the board.
Watt has begun to trail off after what was a vintage start to the season for the 32-year-old.
The future Hall of Famer's 7.5 sacks on the year was tied for the seventh-most in the NFL coming into the week, but he now has zero over his last two contests following the Steelers' Week 9 bye.
Not only that, but Watt was also held to just one pressure while primarily lining up opposite of rookie right tackle Markel Bell (per PFF ).
That's nowhere near good enough for Watt, and Pittsburgh's defense isn't going to find the same success it had during its four-game win streak if he doesn't bounce back.
Brisker has endured some struggles since signing a one-year, $5.5 million deal with the Steelers as a free agent this past offseason, and they showed up against the Eagles.
The 27-year-old gave up two catches for 40 yards in coverage, and he also missed a tackle ( per PFF ).
Brisker logged a season-low 39 defensive snaps, too, and part of the reasoning behind that decision by Pittsburgh was the fact that DeShon Elliott was back in the lineup after being ruled out against the Bengals in Week 10.
Considering Brisker played 57 (Week 7) and 70 (Week 8) snaps in the prior two contests Elliott appeared in this season, however, perhaps the former is falling a bit out of favor.
Wilson, like most of the Steelers' defense, had a tough day at the office against the Bengals in Week 10.
The 26-year-old was one of the lone bright spots against the Eagles, though, despite posting just three total tackles.
According to PFF , Wilson did not miss a single tackle or give up any yards in coverage, which is just the second time he's done so this season (Week 3 vs. Cincinnati).

title: After Ejection, Could Steelers' DK Metcalf Face Suspension?
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf may have hit rock bottom after his most recent outing. After recording a single reception on four targets, Metcalf's most notable plays were two unsportsmanlike conduct penalties that led to his ejection from the contest.
It was the third time this season that the Steelers watched their highest-paid receiver post fewer than 15 receiving yards in a game and the fourth time he recorded fewer than three receptions.
Now, it's possible Metcalf might face even more discipline after his incident in Week 11. After he attempted to poke the eyes of Philadelphia Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean, Metcalf could face a possible suspension for his actions. Given Metcalf's history and the league's attitude towards this type of action, it feels like a strong bet that the Steelers' top wideout won't play in Week 12.
"The referee told me he (Metcalf) poked the defender in the eye," head coach Mike McCarthy told the media after the game.
"We'll sit down and address everything," he continued. "We need him. We need him in those games, and that's not acceptable to get thrown out of the game as one of the 48 (players active)."
This is the second time since Metcalf joined the Steelers that he has been disciplined for this action.
When the Steelers battled the Green Bay Packers in 2025, Metcalf got into it with Packers linebacker Quay Walker. During the incident, Metcalf didn't quite land it, but he clearly tried to put his fingers inside Walker's visor in a poking motion.
For that incident, the NFL fined Metcalf $12,172.
Metcalf has also been suspended recently for his actions on the field.
During the team's trip to Detroit last season to take on the Detroit Lions, an altercation on the sidelines cost him a pair of games as the regular season came to an end. In response to a jawing Lions fan, Metcalf put his hands on the man before the two were separated.
The action went unnoticed during the game, but the league certainly saw what transpired. In response, he was suspended for two games, forcing him out of the team's final two regular season contests as they tried to make the postseason.
Back in 2015, Denver Broncos cornerback Aqib Talib was suspended for one game after an altercation he had with Indianapolis Colts tight end Dwayne Allen. As the game reached its final moments, the two came together, and Talib eventually poked him in the eye.
The league was not pleased with the incident and suspended him, according to a 2015 ESPN report from Jeff Legwold.
That might be the most comparable situation for Metcalf and the Steelers to gauge their expectations. While it's impossible to predict the NFL's actions ahead of time, they have set a precedent.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers vs. Eagles Takeaways: DK Metcalf Experiment Must End
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA -- The Pittsburgh Steelers' season is closing in on them. After a blowout loss to the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 10, the team laid an egg in Week 11 against the Philadelphia Eagles, and now, things are getting concerning.
A 19-16 loss to Philly moves Pittsburgh to 6-4 on the season, with the Denver Broncos coming up on a short week.
Things need to turn around fast for the Steelers, but their offense is getting worse by the week, and their defense can't keep up.
This team may be headed down a dark road and may now have to do it without one of their highest-paid players.
Max Hurleman needs to learn how to field a kickoff. Right from the jump, you saw the second-year return man look uncomfortable as the deep man and he just never settled in.
He was nervous, you could tell. And whether he just wasn't seeing the ball in the air or was too focused on what was happening in front of him, he couldn't get under the ball and field it successfully on a consistent basis.
This was supposed to be his big opportunity. For the last two weeks, Mike McCarthy and Aaron Rodgers hyped up Hurleman and pushed for him to get a chance to prove himself. This was that chance, and he may have lost it.
Pittsburgh clearly wants more out of their return game after making rookie Kaden Wetjen inactive. But Hurleman was not the answer in this one. It'd be surprising if he got another shot next week against the Denver Broncos.
At the same time, he made a real impact offensively down the stretch. Hurleman finished with a team-leading 61 yards on six receptions, and he scored a 20-yard touchdown on the Steelers' final offensive drive of the game that cut their deficit to three points with 1:21 left in the fourth quarter.
Pittsburgh couldn't stop the Eagles on the ensuing drive, which clinched the win for the latter, but Hurleman's offensive performance was certainly encouraging.
Aaron Rodgers is becoming an issue for the Steelers. Now, you can't bench him, and you aren't going to get better play out of Mason Rudolph, Drew Allar or Will Howard. But you do need to accept that he's not who he once was, and it's very, very evident.
Rodgers misses wide open receivers multiple times a game, and sometimes, it's right in front of him. Roman Wilson had a first down and some on a third down play in the first quarter, and Ben Skowronek may have scored a touchdown on a bootleg to end the opening quarter, being five yards behind the entire defense with his hand up and running with Rodgers in the same direction.
Rodgers decided to tuck it and run for 12 yards. It looked good until you saw the entire play.
Rodgers wasn't playing good football before the offense started to fall off. Now that he's frustrated and doesn't trust his wideouts or offensive line, he's a shell of what he once was.
Without him, it feels like this is the beginning of the end for the Steelers. What was a promising season just a few weeks ago may be collapsing. And Rodgers' farewell tour may not be what he wanted it to be.
The offensive line is starting to struggle again, which brings up a ton of questions, and concerns. Can it be fixed? Probably not. This group just hasn't stayed consistent all season, and without Mason McCormick, Zach Frazier is doing everything he can to try and keep the interior intact.
For now, it brings up questions about how to make the offense work without a good offensive line. It's not easy, but not impossible. McCarthy just needs to put the group in situations where they have an upper-hand. That should mean no huddle and a lot of quick routes.
In the future, it brings up a ton of concerns. Can they find another guard in the offseason? Is Troy Fautanu ever going to make it work? What if Spencer Anderson isn't good enough to start and the team needs to find another option this year to replace him - again?
It's all bad for Pittsburgh's offense, and the o-line. And if they can't fix it, they may not be good for some time.
DK Metcalf's highlight reel in this game would include a two-yard completion on the opening drive when the team needed three yards to get a first down, and a personal foul that moved Pittsburgh back toward the goal line, subtracting four yards from the offense. Then a second personal foul that got him ejected from the ballgame.
DK Metcalf has been ejected in Philly CBS | Paramount+ pic.twitter.com/johlxzOD1J
It's a year to forget for Metcalf, and his poor decision to get into it with Cooper DeJean near the Steelers' own endzone felt like a breaking point. It only got worse when he continued to chirp at Eagles players on the following play after backing his team into a corner when they were down seven points.
Coming into the game, Metcalf was leading all wide receivers with six penalties on the season. He now has eight.
At this point, the best decision the Steelers can make with Metcalf is to bench him. He's not contributing to the offense and is now actively pushing them backward. All around, he's a problem and if it weren't for his starter reputation and $30-plus million contract, he wouldn't be on the field.
The Metcalf experiment is a failure. It's about time to end it.

title: Steelers’ DK Metcalf Ejected During Eagles Game
full_text:
Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf has been ejected from the team's Week 11 game against the Philadelphia Eagles.
With just under five minutes left in the third quarter, Metcalf was called for his second unsportsmanlike conduct penalty of the contest, resulting in his ejection.
On a replay provided by the CBS Sports broadcast of the game, it appeared Metcalf reached up around Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean's face mask and attempted to poke him in the eyes.
Video sure seems to suggest that DK Metcalf poked Cooper DeJean in the eyes to set off the latest confrontation. Certainly possible that could earn him a suspension pic.twitter.com/VJrVPAd4IA https://t.co/sBjj6fPHnv
His prior unsportsmanlike conduct penalty was also against DeJean earlier in the third quarter as the two got into it on what would've been a five-yard run by Jaylen Warren up to Pittsburgh's own nine-yard line had it not been called back due to the penalty by Metcalf.
Metcalf's ejection is yet another stain on his resume in what's been a rough season for the 28-year-old. Prior to leaving the contest vs. Philadelphia, Metcalf had hauled in just one pass for two yards on the day despite being targeted by Aaron Rodgers on four occasions.
With Metcalf out, the Steelers will now rely on Germie Bernard, Roman Wilson, Ben Skowronek and Max Hurleman to hold down the fort at wide receiver to close out a close game against the Eagles.
Metcalf, despite being viewed as Pittsburgh's No. 1 wide receiver, has been a net negative for the team in 2026.
Assuming he plays in all 17 games this season, which may now be in jeopardy if he were to earn a suspension for his actions against the Eagles, Metcalf is on pace for a career-low 738 yards.
Considering he still has three seasons left on a four-year, $132 million deal that he signed with the Steelers after arriving in a trade from the Seattle Seahawks in March 2025 that cost the former their 2025 second-round pick, that's nowhere near good enough just in terms of what he provides on the field without even taking into account some of his antics.
The predicament Pittsburgh finds itself in with Metcalf is that it essentially needs him out there in order for its offense to reach its ceiling. The concern, of course, is that he will continue to not play up to his potential and do more harm than good when he's active.
It remains to be seen if the Steelers consider benching Metcalf or if he is disciplined in the aftermath of his ejection. Perhaps the team could look into parting ways with him in the offseason, but considering they'd take on $35.775 million in dead money by cutting/trading him with a pre-June 1 designation and $11.925 million post-June 1 (per Over the Cap ), doing so may not exactly be simple.

title: Steelers' Alex Highsmith Suffers Injury After Hot Start in Philly
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- Pittsburgh Steelers linebacker Alex Highsmith sustained an injury during the team's Week 11 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles. The veteran EDGE rusher was off to a strong start in the first quarter, forcing a fumble and recording a sack over the first two defensive series.
But after Highsmith helped knock Eagles quarterback Joe Milton down, he hobbled off the field with what appeared to be a left ankle injury. Thankfully, he was able to exit the field under his own power, but he was unable to put his full weight on the injured leg while limping to the sidelines.
With Highsmith out, the Steelers are down another key outside linebacker. Fourth-year linebacker Nick Herbig was previously ruled out for the Week 11 contest, forcing the team to sign K.J. Henry to the active roster.
Shortly after Highsmith exited the contest, the Steelers listed him as questionable to return to the game. Senior Director of Communications for the team, Burt Lauten, shared the latest update on the veteran leader.
"Steelers LB Alex Highsmith sustained an ankle injury and is questionable to return to today's game," he wrote via his official X account.
Highsmith was off to an incredible start in the team's Week 11 contest. During the first series, he nearly created a turnover before the Eagles had the chance to get going. Had the Eagles' offensive lineman not landed on the loose ball, Highsmith would have delivered the ball back to the offense immediately after they turned it over on downs.
Without him, the EDGE rusher group in Pittsburgh is significantly weaker. Outside of regular starter T.J. Watt, the team has to rely on Henry and usual backup EDGE rusher Jack Sawyer.
Sawyer is in his second season in the NFL, and he's still earning more trust and opportunities. With Herbig already out, the team was looking to him to make an impact. In nine games played this season, he's recorded 19 total tackles and one pass defended.
Henry brings very limited NFL experience as well. He's played in a total of 12 NFL contests before this Week 11 game, but the last time he played in a regular season game was during the 2024 campaign with the Dallas Cowboys. Originaly drafted in the fifth-round of the 2023 NFL Draft by the Washington Commanders, he's produced a total of 22 tackles and 2.5 sacks in his career.

title: Steelers' Green Dot LB Active Against Eagles
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers won't be short at inside linebacker against the Philadelphia Eagles.
Patrick Queen was not included amongst the Steelers' inactives for their Week 11 matchup with the Eagles after being deemed questionable to suit up on the team's final injury report of the week with a hand injury.
Queen was a full participant in practice on November 20 after having been limited on November 18 and 19, indicating that he was moving in the right direction when it came to his availability.
Now, the 27-year-old is officially ready to go and will play through a broken thumb that he suffered in Pittsburgh's Week 10 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football.
Queen has yet to miss a contest throughout his seven-year NFL career, and that streak will remain alive while the Steelers look to get back in the win column against an Eagles team that's riding a seven-game losing streak as they return from their bye week.
Queen is in the final season of a three-year, $41 million deal that he signed with Pittsburgh ahead of the 2024 campaign after having spent the first four campaigns of his career with the Baltimore Ravens.
While he had some good spurts here and there, it's fair to say that Queen didn't quite live up to expectations over the first two seasons of his contract with the Steelers.
According to Pro Football Focus, he led the league with 32 missed tackles and also allowed the most yards in coverage of any linebacker with 829 in 2025.
Queen, looking to bounce back in a contract year while adapting to a new defensive scheme under Patrick Graham, came out of the gates slow this season.
From missing a pair of tackles against both the Atlanta Falcons in Week 1 and the Cleveland Browns in Week 4 to giving up 46 yards in coverage vs. the Indianapolis Colts in Week 5 ( per PFF ), Queen's unreliability and inconsistent play in the middle of the defense hurt Pittsburgh early in the year.
In Week 7 against the New Orleans Saints at the Stade de France in Paris, however, he posted 10 tackles and recorded a sack of Tyler Shough on the Saints' final offensive play of the game while also nearly hauling in an interception in the first quarter.
Then, during Week 8 vs. Cleveland, Queen logged a team-high 12 total tackles and 1.5 sacks, the latter of which is a single-game career-high for him.
He took a bit of a step back against the Bengals last week, as did the entire team, but Queen's turnaround has been a sight for sore eyes for the Steelers.
Queen has now posted 1.0 sacks or more in three-straight games, which he had never previously accomplished.
In Eagles quarterback Joe Milton III's first start of his career in a Week 9 loss to the New York Giants, he was sacked seven times, four of which were recorded by inside linebackers Arvell Reese (3.0) and Micah McFadden (1.0).
Given how productive Queen has been at getting after the quarterback recently, perhaps he can follow the blueprint that the Giants laid out and notch yet another sack to raise his streak to four contests in that regard.
The Steelers' inactives include:
QB Drew Allar QB Will Howard (3rd QB) CB Sean Murphy-Bunting RB Eli Heidenreich LB Nick Herbig DE Gabe Rubio KR/PR Kaden Wetjen

title: Steelers Top Draft Priority May Be Changing
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers have a lot of faith in the development of Drew Allar and Will Howard. While they aren't certain either is their next franchise quarterback, they're excited about what they can bring and the progress they continue to make.
Because of it, it's made their top priority in the 2027 NFL Draft a little different.
The Steelers are ready to change course at quarterback. They want to go young after years of trying to make veteran options work, and Allar and Howard are the best bets as to who will get the job in 2027. If they want to bring in a veteran option to provide depth and support, Mason Rudolph will probably be their top choice, if he chooses to take the job.
It's not time to completely rule out quarterback in the first round, but if Mike McCarthy and Omar Khan are ready to roll with their in-house options, there's a clear next top priority for this team.
Wide receiver has been a need in Pittsburgh for some time. After failing to land Brandon Aiyuk, Khan made a move for DK Metcalf from the Seattle Seahawks . He traded for Michael Pittman Jr. the following offseason. Neither has worked out.
Roman Wilson has taken more time than expected to find his footing in the NFL, but may finally be coming into his own. Germie Bernard looks like he has a bright future as a second-round rookie, and it feels like the next move at the position is to shoot even higher with a draft pick.
Names like Nick Marsh and Charlie Becker out of Indiana, Cam Coleman out of Texas, and Reed Harris out of Arizona State all seem to fit what Pittsburgh would be looking for.
Pittsburgh needs an outside option who provides speed as a deep threat and contested-catch ability. This team has craved a bigger wideout who has speed for years, but also needs someone who can be reliable in crucial catch situations.
Essentially, they need an improved DK Metcalf and Pittman Jr. Someone who can shine in big moments and is great at creating separation, making life easier for whoever their quarterback is.
The Steelers are looking for a true WR1. They don't need to walk into Pittsburgh and immediately be a star, but they need to have the potential to be. And it shouldn't take much time to start making an impact within the offense.
Bernard, Wilson and a rookie could be the future of the position. The Steelers will hope so. And if they're ready to roll with one of their young quarterbacks, look for wideout to be their top priority in the 2027 NFL Draft this spring.

title: The Seahawks Only Have One Path to Playoffs After 49ers Big Win
full_text:
Last night, shortly before halftime of the Sunday Night Football game between the Minnesota Vikings and San Francisco 49ers, the NFC West was put on ice.
Ji’Ayir Brown trotted into the endzone after picking off an ill-advised Kirk Cousins pass, and the extra point made it 28-10. My optimism for the Seattle Seahawks, which had been battling to stay alive in recent weeks, was finally extinguished.
The 49ers now lead the NFC West by three games, with seven left to play. Sounds possible to overcome, right? Well, let’s talk it through. If the Seahawks win out and end the season with a 13-4 record, they would need the 49ers to lose three games just to get into a tie. Since the Seahawks play the 49ers this week, that’s one loss taken care of, but are there two more?
They still play the Kansas City Chiefs and New York Giants, so those are the two candidates. They also get the Los Angeles Rams, Los Angeles Chargers, Philadelphia Eagles, and Arizona Cardinals. The 49ers tend to always do well against the Rams, and the Rams are also very injured , so that feels unlikely, and the latter three are among the NFL’s bottom feeders.
So, let’s say the Seahawks go 13-4, and the 49ers do the same after losing to the Seahawks, Chiefs, and Giants. The first tiebreaker is head-to-head, which would be a draw. Then, division record, another draw, both teams at 5-1. Common games, next on the list, would settle nothing, since both teams would be 10-2. Conference record? Both 9-3. Further down the list.
Settling this hypothetical would be strength of victory, combining the winning percentage of the teams each team beat. So we need to see how the season ends for a lot of teams before we know anything for sure, but right now the 49ers have a big leg up. Their beaten opponents are combined for 43-48-1, or .473, and the Seahawks are at 24-39, or .381. Definitive.
So basically, in order to win the division, the Seahawks must win out, have the 49ers lose both of their other toughest remaining games, and then either lose a figurative layup, or have their strength of victory completely collapse. It’s too much to hope for at this point. If the Seahawks are going to defend their title this season, they’ll have to do it as a wild card.
Maybe that’s okay. The Seahawks have been great on the road during Mike Macdonald’s tenure, and often seem like they’re not worse off away from Lumen. I believe the Seahawks are capable of winning in San Francisco, Detroit, Minnesota, Carolina, New York, and (maybe) Chicago. But make no mistake. Last night was the final blow to the divisional hopes.

title: 3 Most Valuable Seahawks Players at the Bye Week
full_text:
I came into the 2026 season with high expectations of the Seattle Seahawks. So far, they’ve fallen short of those expectations. But they remain very much alive in the postseason conversation , and have had some great players driving them to their success. Let’s run down the three who can be most credited after ten games, counting down to one.
Don’t let the absence of plays on the ball fool you. Devon Witherspoon has allowed, depending on which source you use, either 249 or 269 yards in coverage, and zero touchdowns. He’s been whistled for one pass interference penalty on the season. He’s played in all ten games, over 600 snaps, over 350 of them in coverage. It’s his best season yet so far .
Last week saw him unleashed as a pass rusher as well, registering two sacks and another hit on the quarterback. Even with no interceptions and three passes defensed, he’s among the top cornerbacks in football. Put him in the slot, put him outside, even toss him in the box on occasion, he finds a way to come out on top. Worth every penny.
It took awhile for his pass rush production to arrive, but he’s now on pace to top his career best in sacks with 8.5 and pressures with 22. And this is with him continuing to play a non-trivial number of his snaps at nose tackle with Leonard Williams handling a lot of the three-tech business. So you can credit him significantly for Seattle’s run defense.
That run defense, by the way, is allowing a league-best 3.4 yards per carry right now. Their 86.7 rushing yards allowed per game is third best. That’s with Leonard Williams, Drake Thomas, and Uchenna Nwosu missing a couple games each so far. I doubt things are nearly that strong without Murphy’s incredible work in the middle . He’s a clear #2 to me.
This one is so obvious it barely merits discussion. JSN is on pace to break the single season receiving yards record, and will couple it with enough touchdowns to potentially make an argument for greatest wide receiver season ever. He’s got more than quadruple the receiving production of the second leading receiver on the team, and more than everyone combined.
And think about how unstable his situation is to this point. He’s had two different quarterbacks cycle in and out with assorted injuries, one of which has been very shaky. He has a first time offensive coordinator and playcaller, who has looked mostly overwhelmed. Throwing up these numbers in this situation is remarkable, and there’s no doubt he’s the top dog.

title: Toughest to Easiest Remaining Seahawks Games After Week 11
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks (6-4) are fortunately on bye week after an up-and-down first half to the season. The Seahawks are currently No. 8 in the NFC standings thanks to a loaded NFC North Division. Fortunately, with some help, the Seahawks can get back to the top of the NFC West Division thanks to the remaining seven games on their schedule.
​Seattle has seven games that can easily put the team back into playoff contention, at least as a high wildcard team. The Seahawks will have three more divisional games to help decide the NFC West and four winnable non-division games, with some looking more difficult than earlier in the season. Here are the Seahawks’ remaining seven games ranked from most difficult to easiest/shouldn’t lose.
​The Seahawks will come out of a bye week with a rematch against the San Francisco 49ers on the road in Week 12. Despite the four turnovers (including in the end zone for a 49ers touchdown), a bad game from the quarterback and a limited run game, Seattle was close to defeating San Francisco, but lost 32-29 in Week 5. The good news is that Seattle will return some players. The 49ers, however, will have the momentum (pending the Sunday Night Game versus the Minnesota Vikings) and a rowdy home-field advantage.
​Seattle could be favored in the remaining games for the rest of the season. That doesn’t mean they will be easy, especially if the next two toughest games are against the Rams. While the Rams’ home stadium will be tough to play, the first game of the 2026 season will be the most emotional and it will be in primetime. This may be a do-or-die game for both teams in the chase of the NFC Wild Card.
If one or both teams are still in the hunt by the season finale, it will be just as difficult. The reason that it is lower is that one of these teams could be out of the playoff chase and the 49ers might’ve clinched the division by then. This game may come down to bragging rights after a disappointing season for one or both teams. It will remain a tough battle due to their hatred for each other.
​The Jacksonville Jaguars couldn’t get their own way on their way to a 23-28 loss to the New York Giants 23-18 on Sunday. The Giants’ defense has become a respectable unit, but their offense needs more experience. Seattle looks for revenge after the disastrous 29-20 loss to New York in 2024 in Mike Macdonald’s first year as head coach. If Seattle becomes a wild card team, this could be the first of two matchups, with the second being in the postseason.
​Another team the Seahawks could meet in the playoffs as a wild card team could be the Carolina Panthers. The Panthers possess one of the worst defenses in the league and it hasn’t gotten better since firing Ejiro Evero as defensive coordinator a few weeks ago. Carolina is allowing 26.9 points per game through its ten games. This Seahawks team knows how to win in Charlotte after defeating the Panthers 27-10 late last season.
​Speaking of teams the Seahawks know how to beat, Seattle has defeated the Philadelphia Eagles eight consecutive games. The last time they faced each other on the field, quarterback Drew Lock led the Seahawks to a 20-17 home win in 2023. This season, the Eagles have fallen apart with injuries and dysfunction. Philadelphia managed to defeat the Pittsburgh Steelers, but a former Seahawks wide receiver turned Steeler helped the Eagles win. This remains a capable win, but playing in Philadelphia is always tough.
​The Dallas Cowboys are not the easiest team to defeat in the NFL, but this should be the easiest win for the Seahawks for the remainder of the season. Dallas has a high-power offense, but it needs to be with their defense allowing 28.3 points per game. If the Seahawks continue their offensive momentum from Weeks 9 and 10 and come out of Week 12 versus the 49ers, the league’s best wide receiver in Jaxon Smith-Njigba could have a field day against the Cowboys’ defense.

title: 4 Games Seahawks Fans Should Watch During Bye Week
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are enjoying their annual bye week , where they will have a chance to sit back, relax, and watch their NFL counterparts do battle in Week 11.
The Seahawks are 6-4 in the middle of a wild card race in the NFC, and several games this week could impact that race. Here's a look at one game in each television window that the team should keep on the TV screen ... if they aren't watching RedZone.
This is the matchup with arguably the most at stake in the 7-game window. Both teams are currently fighting for playoff spots, as the New Orleans Saints are in the tight NFC South, while the Chicago Bears are one of the teams fighting for a wild card spot in the NFC.
The Bears are also fighting for a division crown, and they will have a chance to compete for first place against the Detroit Lions on Thanksgiving Day. This matchup in the Windy City could set the stage for what the big Turkey Day game has to offer.
The league flexed the game between the Jacksonville Jaguars and New York Giants into the late window in the national TV spot, and it's no surprise, considering both teams are leading their respective divisions going into the matchup.
The Jaguars have been one of the best teams in the league so far this season, with a 7-2 record, and they have won each of their last three games by at least 17 points.
The Giants, meanwhile, are coming off a heartbreaking loss on Thursday Night Football last week to the Washington Commanders but still maintain a multi-game division lead in the NFC East. They are hoping to win their division for the first time since 2011.
This game could go a long way for the Giants if they are able to pull out a win.
Two playoff hopefuls, the San Francisco 49ers and Minnesota Vikings, will take part in the league's Mexico City game for Sunday Night Football. The Vikings are 7-2 and have been one of the league's best teams since starting off 6-0. After dropping two consecutive games, the team traded for quarterback Kirk Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders and turned things around with a big 30-10 victory against the NFC North rival Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field.
The Niners are going into this game leading the NFC West by 2.5 games over the Seahawks and Los Angeles Rams, both of whom are on bye this week. A victory would push them to a three-game lead, while a loss would keep the gap at two games, which would be much more manageable for Seattle to overcome, as they will have a chance to gain a game next week when they visit Levi's Stadium.
Monday Night Football this week pits the Cincinnati Bengals against the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium near the nation's capital. The Bengals hold one of the best records in the league at 7-2, while the Commanders are holding on to faint playoff hopes at 3-5-1.
The Bengals have won each of their last five games and are poised to make a playoff run as the second half of the season gets underway. The Commanders are likely going to have a chance to fight for a division crown, but they need to be able to pick up some wins in these next couple of weeks, as their schedule is rather favorable.
Over the next month, if they can add a victory against the Super Bowl contender Bengals, that could spark some confidence moving forward.

title: Seattle Seahawks Fans Rooting Guide For Week 11
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are off this week , which is going to feel weird for Seahawks fans. They're used to cheering their team on every weekend, so this Sunday might feel a little bare.
That doesn't mean there won't be plenty of games to keep an eye on. With Seattle sitting at 6-4, they find themselves in a tight race for a playoff spot in the NFC. They're currently on the outside looking in with the eighth seed. They have the same record as the Green Bay Packers as well as their NFC West rivals, the Los Angeles Rams, but both teams are on their bye as well.
Seattle won't be able to gain ground on either of them, but they can still benefit from the slate of games this weekend. That said, here's a look at which games the 12's should be watching and who they should root for.
This one might not seem to matter too much since the Arizona Cardinals are just 3-7 and not much of a threat to the Seahawks. Still, they're a divisional rival and they're playing an AFC team in the Kansas City Chiefs. That feels like an easy one for the fan base to figure out. It's always fun to watch a rival lose, especially against a team like the Chiefs who are more than capable of dropping 40 on Arizona.
The NFC North is a division to keep an eye on. The Detroit Lions are the leaders now due to a tiebreaker, but there's a three-way tie with the Lions, Chicago Bears, and Minnesota Vikings all at 7-2. Detroit currently has the No. 2 seed while the Bears and Vikings have two of the three wild card spots. That's why Seattle should be cheering for some losses here so that they remain within striking distance of all three. It will be tough since the Lions are 5-0 at home and the Bucs have been struggling, but we should still be rooting for Tampa Bay in this one.
For the same reasons we should root for the Lions to win, the Bears need to be cheered on as they host the New Orleans Saints. Again, this won't be easy since the Saints are a mess, but anything can happen.
This one is pretty easy as well, even though there might not be a perfect result for Seattle. The San Francisco 49ers are ahead of everyone in the NFC with a record of 8-1. Seattle needs them to take some losses to catch up in the West, so the right thing to do is cheer for the Vikings.
That said, the Vikings could become a problem in the NFC wild card race. They had a two-game losing streak snapped following the return of Kirk Cousins, and he makes them a contender once again. Still, the Seahawks will need them to win this week, then they can root for losses in Minnesota for the remainder of the season.

title: Grading Seahawks' Position Units Through First 10 Games of 2026
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks (6-4) are just a little over halfway through the 2026 NFL season, which means they’re having to take this bye-week development seriously. The Seahawks have seen a lot of good performances this season, but there have been many points where sloppy play and poor decisions held the team back. There have been redeeming moments for many position units on the team. Here are the grades for each position unit for the Seahawks through the first ten games.
​This season has been difficult for the quarterbacks, especially Sam Darnold, who has fallen victim to several injuries and the poor adaptation of offensive coordinator Brian Fleury . Darnold has looked great for most of the game against the Washington Commanders and all of the game against the Kansas City Chiefs. He still has a rough touchdown-to-interception ratio of 10:9. His game back in Week 12 versus the San Francisco 49ers should be an indication of whether he can be a long-term answer for Seattle.
​Backup quarterback Drew Lock, however, has been stellar in his three starts, including two versus the Arizona Cardinals. In four games played, Lock has thrown for 837 yards, seven touchdowns and no interceptions. While many Seahawks fans want Lock as the full-time starter , they need to realize he accomplished this in the two games against Arizona and last week versus the Las Vegas Raiders.
​The Seahawks knew there would be some regression in the running game without running back Kenneth Walker III, but the front office put too much trust in power backs Emanuel Wilson Jr. and George Holani. It didn’t help that rookie Jadarian Price had fumbling issues before being placed on IR. The Seahawks might be finally finding some rhythm and consistency in the run game with veteran Zach Charbonnet and Price back from injuries with a few games under their belt.
​One player, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, is carrying the position group . Through the first ten games of the season, JSN leads the league in receptions (79), receiving yards (1,207), touchdowns (10) and receiving first downs (57). The other three receivers in Cooper Kupp, Rashid Shaheed and Tory Horton, have combined for 50 receptions, 558 yards and four touchdowns. Kupp is well past his prime, but Shaheed and Horton haven’t had breakout games as a pass-catcher this season.
​This season hasn’t been a breakout season for third-year tight end AJ Barner, who has caught 26 receptions for 229 yards and a touchdown. He has been reliable in the jumbo offense, getting first downs under center. He has been more reliable than not when it comes to blocking, but he’s been poorly utilized as a fullback in some games.
Meanwhile, Eric Saubert, Nick Kallerup and fullback Brady Russell have been serviceable as blockers. Finally, Elijah Arroyo has been incredibly disappointing in six games before suffering injuries.
Expectations were high for this Seahawks’ offensive line to be better than last year. Guard Grey Zabel and right tackle Abraham Lucas have heavily regressed. Left tackle Charles Cross and left guard Quenton Nelson are injured. Only right guard Anthony Bradford and center Jalen Sundel are healthy and reliable. The Seahawks have allowed 22 sacks this season and haven’t opened a lot of holes in the running game. The team may make some long-term changes after this season.
​The Dark Side Defense’s pass rush hasn’t been as elite as last season, but the line is still strong. They’re finding ways to put pressure on the quarterback in the last few games. Seattle’s defensive line is a key reason why the defense is eighth in run defense, but allowed the least amount of yards per rush in the league at 3.4 yards. Leonard Williams’ absence will be felt for however long he is out, but Byron Murphy II is playing at an All-Pro level with eight tackles for loss and five sacks.
​Derick Hall and DeMarcus Lawrence have carried the edge rushers unit early in the season. Within the last few games, Uchenna Nwosu and Dante Fowler Jr. have come to life with some key sacks and pressure in the backfield. Meanwhile, Ernest Jones IV and Drake Thomas are tenacious tackling machines defending the run and the passing game. The one concern is their lack of recognition while playing in zone coverage.
​The Seahawks might have one of the most elite secondary, if not the best, the best secondary in the league. Cornerback Devon Witherspoon and nickelback Nick Emmanwori are two of the most efficient and dynamic defenders in the league. The other corners have had great moments. Safety Julian Love is another player that All-Pro consider and Ty Okada remains an underrated weapon. Seattle is second in pass defense this season, just behind the Minnesota Vikings.
​The Seahawks are allowing only 4.3 yards per punt return, with punter Michael Dickson creating bad return moments for the opposing team with his high hang time and his deep kicks. He is another key reason why the Seahawks start the other team’s drives. Jason Myers is having one of his least productive seasons, but he is still 16-of-19 in field goals. He is, however, 3-for-3 on attempts over 50 yards this season.

title: 3 Teams Who Could Hire Seahawks DC Aden Durde After the Season
full_text:
Seattle Seahawks defensive coordinator Aden Durde is a potential head coaching candidate for the 2027 season, especially considering how well his unit has performed since he took over in 2024.
Durde received some interviews last year but ultimately stuck with Seattle, but that may not be the case this time around. Here's a look at three teams that could and should have Durde on their radar to be their next head coach.
The Indianapolis Colts look poised to blow it all up at the end of the season, especially after their 26-3 loss against the Houston Texans on Thursday Night Football which resulted in the team cutting quarterback Daniel Jones.
The Colts surrender 354.8 yards per game, which makes them the seventh-worst defense in the league. Indianapolis would absolutely benefit from hiring a coach like Durde, who has a defense that only allows 236.1 yards per game.
The Chargers were winless going into Monday Night Football in Week 10 against the Baltimore Ravens, but they became the last team in the league to win a football game this season. Their 0-8 start has cranked up the heat on Jim Harbaugh's seat in Los Angeles, and it will likely lead to a parting of ways.
In the offseason, should the Chargers follow through with that, they could look at Durde replacing Harbaugh, especially considering the Chargers have a defense that allows 26.6 points per game, which is tied for fifth most in the league.
The Cowboys are a bit of a wild card, as Brian Schottenheimer's seat is not as hot as the other two teams. However, the Cowboys are 4-6 and have the league's worst defense, giving up almost 400 yards per game and 28.2 points per contest.
Durde also has a connection to the Cowboys as a member of Dan Quinn's defensive staff from 2021-23. He was also an intern with the Cowboys for two seasons in 2014 and 2015, so his relationship with Jerry Jones has lasted longer than a decade.
Perhaps the Cowboys look to fix their defense by bringing in someone like Durde, who is familiar with the organization but will likely bring a fresh perspective that the Cowboys have needed on defense for the last couple of years.

title: 3 Big Seahawks Surprises at the Bye Week
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are enjoying their time off with their bye week , as they sit back and reflect on the past 10 weeks of the season.
Things have not necessarily gone according to plan for the Seahawks, who have already lost more games this year than they did all of last season. Here's a look at the three biggest surprises from the Seahawks through 10 games.
Sam Darnold has been wildly inconsistent for the Seahawks, both in terms of his quality of play and his attendance on the field. Darnold has really only played in 6 of the team's 10 games.
After suffering a glute injury on the first drive against the New England Patriots back in Week 1, he missed Week 2's contest against the Arizona Cardinals but returned in Week 3. He also suffered another injury, this time to his quad and ribs, in Week 8 against the Chicago Bears. That forced him to miss the other game against the Cardinals in Week 9 and the matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 10.
Drew Lock has been remarkable in relief, winning each of his 3 starts and pulling off a comeback against the Patriots on opening night.
While he's been on the field, Darnold has not performed up to par like he did last season. He has completed just over 60 percent of his passes for 1,478 yards, 10 touchdowns, and nine interceptions. The fact that he's averaging more than an interception per game is not a good sign of what's to come. That is something he will have to fix in order for Seattle to be relevant in the Super Bowl contender conversation for the second year in a row.
Part of the reason the Seahawks have not played up to their standard this season is the lack of impact from their rookie class, which has all been affected by injuries this season.
Jadarian Price has missed four games due to a chest injury, while second-round pick Bud Clark was injured in the preseason and is out for the year. Third-round pick Julian Neal has only been available in four games and has played minimal snaps. Meanwhile, fifth-round pick Beau Stephens is a backup offensive lineman.
Simply put, the Seahawks are not getting very much from their rookie class, and it is definitely part of the reason they have not been elite this season. There is hope that Price can improve as the season goes along, as we've seen in the past three games since his return from injury. But the rookie class as a whole has been a massive whiff so far from general manager John Schneider in the front office.
This one has definitely been the most pleasant of the surprises. Jaxon Smith-Njigba was the Offensive Player of the Year last season after gaining 1,793 yards through the air with 10 touchdowns.
Through 10 games, he's matched his touchdown total and is on pace to shatter his total from last year. JSN has over 1,200 receiving yards so far this season, which could make him the first wide receiver in NFL history to surpass 2,000 receiving yards in a single year.
He is looking to surpass his teammate Cooper Kupp, who set the NFL record back in 2021 with 1,947 yards, which was the second-most for a wide receiver in NFL history. He is chasing Calvin Johnson, who recorded 1,964 yards with the Detroit Lions back in 2012.

title: New Seahawks Mock Draft Lands Versatile, Polished EDGE in Round 1
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are clearly a defensive-minded team. We knew that would be the case when they hired Mike Macdonald as their head coach ahead of the 2024 season, and they have not disappointed.
Seattle rode their suffocating defense to a championship this past season and even with their struggles on offense this year , they're still 6-4 and in the NFC playoff race . Knowing they have a strong defense, and an offense that needs work, it would be tempting to suggest an offensive player in the early part of the 2027 NFL draft.
That's not the case, however, in a recent mock draft from FanSided's Cody Williams. In his latest mock, Williams has Seattle adding another player for their front seven as they select Notre Dame's Boubacar Traore at No. 17 overall.
Williams says EDGE makes sense for the Seahawks since they're currently leaning heavy on veterans such as DeMarcus Lawrence and Jarran Reed. Lawrence has already said he plans to retire after the year , which is why adding someone who Williams calls versatile and polished feels logical.
"Edge rusher has made sense for the Seahawks for a while given that they’re relying so heavily on veterans Demarcus Lawrence and Jarran Reed. They need more upside in depth in that department, which is where Boubacar Traore comes into play," Williams said.
"The simplest thing I can say is just watch the BYU game after he went out for Notre Dame and see how the defense changed. He’s so versatile and polished at his craft that he’d be a great fit for Mike Macdonald."
The 6-foot-5, 253-pound Traore suffered a torn ACL during the 2024 season, but was able to come back in 2025 and play well. He had 37 tackles and 6.5 sacks while proving his speed and athleticism off the edge weren't impacted by the injury.
This season, he's looked even better as he has 33 tackles and five sacks through his first 10 games. Traore, who boasts a nasty spin move, will need to improve his run defense to be known as a complete defensive end at the next level. That said, he can be an impact player against the pass from the moment he arrives in the NFL.

title: 49ers'  Biggest Stock Fallers After Vikings Rout
full_text:
While the San Francisco 49ers dominated the Minnesota Vikings and moved to 9-1, there were still some players who saw their stock drop in the win. Which players had tough performances?
This one is not the doing of McKivitz, but he left the game with an injury , and all indications are that he will be out for the season. The injury was gruesome, and the reaction from teammates said it all. This is unfortunate for McKivitz and crushed the 49ers, who are seeing a big drop in talent down to Vederien Lowe. Lowe held things down for a week. We will see if he can continue.
The question with Mike Evans coming back is how much of an impact it would have on Watkins. Watkins played a good bit in the second half because the team was dominating. However, it was clear in the first half that he was now fourth in the pecking order. Keenan Allen and Deebo Samuel led the way in snaps, and Evans took on the role that Watkins was playing. In closer games, Watkins will likely play less.
The good news for Watkins is that Robinson and Cowing have been phased out of the offense. With Evans back, the 49ers reduced what used to be a never-ending rotation of receivers down to just four options. This should make things easier for Brock Purdy and the active pass catchers. However, Robinson is now depth waiting on the bench and Cowing is only a special teams threat.
The thought coming into the game was that San Francisco would lean on the run to take the blitz of Brian Flores out of the picture. However, they went into the half with more passes than rushing attempts. Black had two rushes heading into the fourth quarter. The rookie gets his chances here and there but is not fully involved in the offense quite yet.
The 49ers had a pretty even rotation between their edge rushers throughout the game. It was likely due to the altitude. Still, Williams is struggling to beat out Keion White for snaps, and Romello Height provides similar pass-rush threat right now. The 49ers need to get Williams to a point where he is clearly better than White and the team is pushing White into more of a depth role.

title: 49ers' 5 Biggest Winners From Vikings Rout
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers dominated the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City to move to 9-1 on the season. Which 49ers players were the biggest winners from the Week 11 dominance?
If Brock Purdy did not have a strong MVP case before Week 11, he surely is one of the top frontrunners now. Even when the Detroit Lions and Buffalo Bills beat the Minnesota Vikings, they leaned on the running game and took pressure off of their passer. The 49ers came out firing on the best pass defense in the NFL. Purdy had three touchdowns and, more importantly, no turnovers and a sack. It was dominant.
Every time Evans takes the field, he dominates. He put up 100 yards and was a force in the 49ers win. The issue for the 49ers will be keeping him healthy. Still, they are arguably the best offense in the NFL without Evans. With him, they appear unstoppable. What is the line between keeping him fresh and also giving him enough work to stay engaged down the stretch?
Kittle started the game with two catches for two touchdowns. He hauled in all three of his targets. Adding in his blocking, Kittle was everything the 49ers need. His versatile skill set forces the Vikings to be honest, and it negates their blitz. He is an underrated reason for the schematic advantage.
Minnesota was hanging around, and then Brown recorded a pick-six that slammed the door shut. The interception was huge, not only for the 49ers to take the score to 28-10. It was huge to keep Brown on the field. He has been third in the three-man safety rotation between himself, Malik Mustapha and  Marques Sigle. Brown showed in Week 11 that he is not going to be the odd man out any time soon.
Green had been playing his best football until an injury a couple of weeks. That, combined with the Dallas Cowboys' wide receivers, had his stock trending down coming into the game. Green gave up a couple of catches but was relentless in getting the ball carrier down. The 49ers can move into Week 12 trusting their cornerbacks. They could not say that at this time last week. That is a pretty notable win.

title: 49ers' Grades After 35-10 Win Over the Vikings: Kyle Shanahan Exposes Brian Flores
full_text:
MEXICO CITY -- The 49ers just beat the Minnesota Vikings 35-10 . Here are the 49ers' grades for this performance.
I knew Brock Purdy was good, but I had no idea he was this good. He might be the best player in the league right now. He certainly is the front-runner to win the MVP Award after making this Vikings defense look remedial. Purdy never was confused or rattled against a defense that confuses and rattles almost every quarterback. It's amazing how much Purdy has improved since he first became the starting quarterback, considering he was good right away. If the 49ers fall short of winning the Super Bowl this season, Purdy won't be the reason. He's a championship-caliber quarterback.
The Vikings held the 49ers to just 3.6 yards per carry because they loaded the line of scrimmage and dared the 49ers to pass. This was a bad strategy.
Mike Evans played, which means the 49ers offense was close to unstoppable. He is what this offense has been missing for years. He didn't even practice this week; plus, he took the past five weeks off, and he still finished this game with 6 catches for 109 yards and a one-handed touchdown catch. If he can stay healthy for the playoffs, the 49ers will win the NFC and probably the Super Bowl. But Evans wasn't the only wide receiver who played well. Keenan Allen had three catches for 38 yards. He's an upgrade over Jauan Jennings, who had 3 catches for 20 yards as a member of the Vikings today.
George Kittle caught just three passes, but two of them were touchdowns, plus he drew a defensive holding penalty that extended a touchdown drive. He's one of the greatest tight ends ever, but we already knew that.
Colton McKivitz left the game with a gruesome broken ankle -- his season is over. This injury could hurt the 49ers in the future. Tonight, it didn't hurt them at all. Backup right tackle Vederian Lowe was good, as was the rest of the offensive line. They had no problem picking up the Vikings' blitzes.
Nick Bosa seemed motivated after playing so poorly last week and offending some Mexicans with his comments during the week about their excessive cheering. The Mexican crowd booed him relentlessly, but he took the jeers with a good spirit and actually played well. Instead of letting the offensive tackle push him past the quarterback, Bosa actually used a counter spin move to bring him back in the play. This was wonderful to see. Unfortunately for him, he still didn't register a sack, because he's not nearly the player he once was, but he did hit Kirk Cousins twice. And the rest of the defensive line did a good job defending the run.
Dre Greenlaw didn't play, and the 49ers didn't miss him at all. That's because Raheem Morris used a five-man defensive line that kept Fred Warner unblocked. This made it very difficult for the Vikings to run the ball. As a result, the 49ers put the game into Kirk Cousins' hands, and he folded under pressure, as he usually does.
They were the stars of the defense. They covered so well that they gave the 49ers' modest pass rush a chance to make an impact. Renardo Green was outstanding, and Deommodore Lenoir bounced back from the worst game of his career to strip the ball from Justin Jefferson and recover it. This play saved a potential touchdown. And then Ji'Ayir Brown put the game away with a pick-six on the first drive of the third quarter. It's almost like they own Kirk Cousins, whom they picked off three times just two weeks ago when he was on the Raiders.
They were flawless. Eddie Pineiro made all of his kicks, and Jacob Cowing had a long punt return that was called back because of a penalty. If the special teams become a strength, the 49ers will have no weaknesses.
Raheem Morris made the Vikings one-dimensional by using a five-man front on first down, which effectively shut down Minnesota's run game. A one-dimensional offense led by Kirk Cousins has no chance against the 49ers. Brilliant game plan by Morris.
Kyle Shanahan's game plan against Brian Flores was even better. Coming into this game, a Shanahan offense never had scored more than 17 points in a game against a Flores' defense. The last time they faced each other, Purdy got sacked six times and seemes completeley overwhelmed. In this game, Shanahan didn't let Purdy get overwhelmed. That's because Shanahan made sure the offense snapped the ball quickly at the line of scrimmage, which prevented the Vikings from walking their defenders up to the line of scrimmage and disguising which ones will rush. And then, Shanahan called lots of quick passes which Flores' defense was not equipped to cover. Shanahan made Flores seem like a gimmick coach, considering Flores never adjusted or found anything that worked.
When the 49ers play and coach like they did today, they're clearly the best team in the NFC. And when their defense forces turnovers, they're unstoppable.

title: 6 Instant Takeaways From 49ers' Win Over Vikings: Welcome Back, Mike Evans
full_text:
MEXICO CITY -- What a statement win for the San Francisco 49ers in primetime.
They throttled the Minnesota Vikings at the Estadio Banorte in Mexico City, 35-10. Let's dive into the six instant takeaways from their stellar Week 11 win.
Mike Evans reminded everyone that he is the difference-maker for the 49ers' offense. Practically every catch he made was for a first down.
He made plays left and right, but his most impressive one came in the second quarter with roughly two minutes left in the first half. Brock Purdy lobbed him a perfectly placed pass.
Evans reeled in a one-handed catch and secured it in the corner of the end zone. His impact cannot be overstated. He is a significant reason the 49ers can win the Super Bowl this year.
With around six minutes left in the first half, Colton McKivitz suffered a devastating ankle injury that required him to be carted off the field.
Given how gruesome the injury looked, it's safe to say that his 2026 season is over. It's brutal for McKivitz, as he was putting together the best season of his career.
His loss will hurt the 49ers significantly. He's only allowed a 3.6% pressure rate and no sacks, per Sumer Sports. The downgrade from McKivitz to Vederian Lowe will be derailing at times.
The MVP leader entering Week 11 was undeniably Joe Burrow, but after the performance that Purdy had tonight, he's taken the MVP lead. There's no question about it.
All he needed to do tonight was play well in a win against the Vikings. But not only did he play well in a win – he was terrific. Quarterbacks have played poorly against the vaunted Vikings' defense this year.
Purdy lit them up like no other quarterback has this year. He made light work of Flores' constant blitzing, making them look pedestrian. Without a doubt, Purdy separated himself from Burrow as the MVP.
The last two times the 49ers played the Vikings, they got mauled by the Vikings' defense. Defensive coordinator Brian Flores always got the better of Kyle Shanahan and Purdy.
The 49ers had never scored more than 17 points in their last two games against them. That all changed tonight. The 49ers put up 21 points on offense by halftime.
Flores tried going with a blitz-heavy plan as always, and it failed him for once. Shanahan outwitted Flores tonight, which shows just how brilliant he has been this year.
After beating down the Vikings, it's safe to say that the NFC will run through Santa Clara. The Vikings were the 49ers' biggest threat to attaining the No. 1 seed.
But now that the Vikings' defense was dismantled and their offense muzzled, the 49ers proved they're the top dog in the conference. They have a clear shot at clinching the No. 1 seed.
Everyone should fully expect them to do it. I doubt they will lose more than two games the rest of the season. They're the most well-rounded team in the NFC, and it's not even close. They have all the momentum in the world and show no signs of slowing down.
I've been to three Super Bowls. The energy for those games was awesome. However, all three of them pale in comparison to the atmosphere at Estadio Banorte. It was riveting.
You can feel the electric ambience flowing. It's a special stadium that was perfect for the prime-time occasion tonight. I can only imagine how incredible it was during the World Cup.

title: Kyle Shanahan Explains What Makes Mac Jones So Popular With His 49ers Teammates
full_text:
San Francisco 49ers quarterback Mac Jones is arguably the biggest personality on the roster.
He's unapologetically himself, and that's one of his biggest strengths. He has a more extravagant, outgoing personality that's infectious and brings nothing but positive vibes.
A recent clip of Jones particularly enjoying the team walkout ahead of the previous game offered another glimpse into his personality.
Obviously, these moments are designed to motivate players and get everyone hyped up, but Jones' enthusiasm stood out and reminded everyone of his infectious personality.
Kyle Shanahan has also highlighted the positive impact that personality has on the locker room. It seems the 49ers are more than happy to let that side of Jones shine through, and that's ultimately a good thing.
"It was awesome," Shanahan said . "But that's how we see Mac like that every day. If you just saw it once, you'd be like, 'Who's this corny white dude?' But you don't at all, because he is like that all the time.
"He is always upbeat. He's always having fun. He's always dancing with the guys. He's just doing whatever, and there really hasn't been a day that Mac hasn't been like that, which is extremely unique.
"I think anyone who, whatever it is, if you're authentically yourself at all times, especially when it's an upbeat, fun self, everyone respects that, everyone enjoys that, and that's why he's one of the most liked guys on our team."
Jones' more unserious side also offers a glimpse into the team's culture. When players feel comfortable being themselves, it allows the group to develop an even stronger connection. There are numerous personalities within the locker room, and Shanahan's openness towards that shows his ability to manage people.
His standards for football are obviously the highest, but he also understands that building a successful team takes more than demanding performances on the field. Giving players the freedom to express themselves can be just as important in creating a positive environment.
This should provide all the more reason for Jones to stay in San Francisco at the end of this season. He seems content as backup, he loves the culture, and if called upon, he has already proven he's capable of playing backup to Brock Purdy should he miss game time.
The 49ers and Jones partnership finally happened, and both sides would be foolish to end their affiliation heading into this year's free agency.

title: Kyle Shanahan Urges 49ers to Ignore the External Noise Ahead of Vikings Clash
full_text:
Despite the oddity of the scoreline against the Dallas Cowboys, San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan reminds his players to focus on improving.
The 49ers won 46-40 against the Cowboys last week, a scoreline so rare that it had never happened before, but the game showed positives and negatives.
If anything, it showed the key areas to improve. Scoring 46 points provides many positives, but conceding 40 points is ultimately a poor return, especially against their biggest historic rival outside their own division.
In a recent interview with NBC Sports Bay Area , Shanahan provided more insight into his culture, something that's always incredibly intriguing to listen too. Given the complexity of the result, he shed light on how he forced a reaction from the players heading into the Mexico City game on Sunday.
“Let’s not sensationalize anything. Let’s not hype someone up cause they have a few catches this game. Let’s not hype an offense or defense up because they did really bad on the scoreboard," said Shanahan.
"Let’s watch the tape and see how it is. That was one of the best offensive stats I’ve been a part of. Definitely wasn’t close to one of our top games, but our numbers showed that way.
"So everyone is gonna treat you like you guys have arrived and it’s your best game ever. That wasn’t even close to our best game ever….
"On defense, I don’t think it was one of their worst games ever. I don’t think they played great, but they played pretty good for three quarters and then they kinda fell apart and broke down.
"So don’t sit there and act like everything is melting and you’re just completely falling apart. Let’s look at the film. Let’s see what happened. Let’s see where we can get better. Let’s fix that.”
In a way, the mentality sounds boring, but it's the correct one to have. Over-sensationalising leads to complacency, and the 49ers are still lacking in many areas, but the answer is to keep growing and finding ways to improve.
There is little value in getting carried away by individual performances or allowing one disappointing result to define the bigger picture. Maintaining perspective is essential throughout a long season, particularly for a team with ambitions of competing for a championship.
These snippets into the 49ers' way of doing things are always interesting, especially when they offer a glimpse into Shanahan's expectations and the standards he wants everyone to maintain.

title: Why the 49ers will Lose to the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City
full_text:
The 49ers will lose to the Vikings Sunday Night in Mexico City, but not for the reason you might think.
Most people picking the Vikings to win expect the 49ers' defensse to struggle, considering it gave up 40 points to the Cowboys last week and 29 points to the Falcons a few weeks ago.
I don't expect the 49ers' defense to struggle. They get to face Kirk Cousins, a decidedly mediocre quarterback whom they just intercepted three times two weeks ago when he was on the Raiders. The 49ers also don't have to face the Vikings' No. 2 wide receiver, Jordan Addison, because he's out.
The only player the 49ers' defense really has to worry about is Justin Jefferson, who's great, but I doubt he'll score three touchdowns by himself without Addison on the field.
The reason the 49ers will lose this game is their offense. It's the best offense in the league, but it's going to struggle on Sunday.
That's because the Vikings have the best defense in the league, and their defensive coordinator, Brian Flores, has ownage over Shanahan. A Shanahan-coached team never has scored more than 17 points in a game against a Flores-coached team.
Chris Simms, Shanahan's best friend, thinks Shanahan will struggle on Sunday.
"I don't think Shanahan is going to be able to get in his bag," Simms said on NBC Sports . "I don't. One of the things I know with Kyle and what he has said about Brian Flores in the past is, 'I've come to terms with the fact that half the game is going to be sh---y, and I'm hoping the other half of the game we can make some big plays.
"I think you'll see some inconsistencies from the 49ers. You might see one drive where they go three plays, 70 yards and score a touchdown, then they go three-and-out four drives in a row. I think that's the game you'll see."
This game will come down to the chess match between Shanahan and Flores, and Shanahan hasn't shown that he can win that contest. He likes to use condensed formations -- wide receivers lined up extremely close to the tight end and offensive linemen -- which invite defensive players to line up close to the quarterback and blitz.
Brock Purdy is elite at beating blitzes with quick passes if he knows where the blitzes are coming from. Unfortunately for Purdy, he and Shanahan don't do a good job of anticipating Flores' blitzes -- the condensed formations make it difficult to decipher pre-snap who is and isn't blitzing -- and Shanahan doesn't give Purdy the power to reset protections at the line of scrimmage, which is a big reason Purdy got sacked six times when the 49ers faced the Vikings in 2024. It's also why the 49ers gave up 9 unblocked rushers to the Chiefs in the Super Bowl.
The proper adjustment would be to spread out the Vikings' defense in one-by-three formations that provide the threat of quick screen passes to Deebo Samuel on the perimeter, but I don't expect Shanahan to make this adjustment. He won't abandon his scheme even when it's the reason the 49ers will lose.
