title: Why the 49ers Have a Massive Advantage Over the Vikings
full_text:
Kyle Shanahan and Brock Purdy have never beaten the Minnesota Vikings together. They're like their NFC Kansas City Chiefs.
They have struggled against the Vikings, and defensive coordinator Brian Flores is the reason for that. He has the San Francisco 49ers' number.
To make matters worse, his defense this season is better than the previous two times he's faced the 49ers. It could be a long night in Mexico City for the 49ers.
However, they have a better chance of having the last laugh this time, and it's thanks to their massive advantage that they have over the Vikings.
That massive advantage is the acclimation to elevation. The 49ers have been practicing in Colorado Springs all week. It sits 6,035 feet above sea level, which is roughly 1,300 feet lower than Mexico City.
While it's not a perfect match, the fact that the 49ers have closely replicated the conditions in Mexico City for their war with the Vikings gives them the advantage.
They won't gas out as much or as early in the game as the Vikings will, which will help the 49ers get off to a fast start. They're already feeling the difference after being there since Monday.
"I know everyone makes a big deal about it and sometimes it is, but I'm less out of breath right now walking here than I was on Wednesday I think when I talked to you guys," Kyle Shanahan said. "Then I couldn't read the whole injury report, so everybody gets better each day but you can definitely still feel it. We'll be better after today, a little bit better tomorrow, but still when you get to Mexico City and it's 2,000 feet higher, we'll still feel it then too but it definitely won't be as bad."
Shanahan is underselling how crucial it was to acclimate to the elevation this week. It's just like when they went to Australia a week before playing the Los Angeles Rams in the season opener.
It turns all of the disadvantages that would typically derail a team into a massive advantage. It helped them in Week 1, and it will certainly help them in Week 11 against the Vikings.
In a way, playing the Vikings in Mexico City was an awesome setup as opposed to Santa Clara. The 49ers need all the help they can get to defeat the Vikings with playoff seeding on the line.

title: The Buccaneers' 2026 Season Isn't Dead Yet
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have dropped to 3-7 on the year following their 10-point loss to the Detroit Lions at Ford Field.
The Bucs made the game close for the majority of the contest before falling behind late and securing a touchdown to make it a 10-point game, but they ultimately weren't able to do enough through the full 60 minutes of the game to come away with a much-needed victory.
It was a gut punch for the team as they look to find some sort of rhythm to try and come back to take over the NFC South and make the playoffs.
However, even with the loss to the Lions, Tampa Bay isn't quite dead in the water just yet.
Following the Bucs' loss to the Lions, they currently have a 36% chance of making the playoffs, according to The Athletic . However, they have an important matchup on Monday Night Football in Week 12 against the Carolina Panthers that could have a major impact on their chances of reaching the postseason.
With a win and sweep of the Panthers on primetime, the Bucs' playoff chances would climb back up to 49%, but if they drop that game, their chances fall drastically to 10% — making it a must-win game.
The Panthers just narrowly avoided a loss to the Baltimore Ravens at home, but with the win, they extended their lead over the Bucs in the division to two games.
Fortunately for Tampa Bay, they seem to have the Panthers figured out this season, as they whalloped them 43-13 in Carolina in their first matchup back in Week 7 after a tremendous game from Bucky Irving and the running attack. So, they should have confidence that they can come out and do much of the same.
If the Bucs can come away with a victory to close the gap on the Panthers, their schedule lines up for them to continue increasing their odds of making the postseason with games against the Atlanta Falcons, Los Angeles Chargers, Baltimore Ravens, New Orleans Saints and Los Angeles Rams, who have a combined record of 17-34 (.333 winning percentage).
The Bucs are straddling the line at the midway point of the season and will need a strong finish to the season if they hope to salvage it. It won't be easy, as every team is pushing for its own goals to end the season, and the Bucs might have some issues with key players being hurt on the defensive side of the ball.
However, they find themselves still in the thick of things, and if they are able to overcome the injuries and the deficiencies on offense, they can make some noise down the home stretch and into the playoffs.

title: Overreactions From Buccaneers' Week 11 Loss to Lions
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers dropped yet another game on Sunday, losing to the Detroit Lions on the road. That's their seventh loss of the year, and it puts them at 3-7 on the season.
Miraculously, the Bucs are two games out of the NFC South and have a chance to narrow the gap next Monday against the Carolina Panthers. But does that even matter any more with the game we just watched?
As always, we have no qualms overreacting to Week 11. Here are three of our overreactions after Tampa Bay's loss to the Lions:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers trusted Baker Mayfield this offseason by giving him a three-year extension worth $55 million a year. They did this in hopes that he would return to the quarterback we saw in 2024 and the first half of 2025, as opposed to the quarterback we saw in the back half of 2025.
So far, all of his faults have remained, and they're very present. Mayfield struggles presnap to identify blitz patterns, and it has gotten him sacked on more than one occasion. When he drops back, he holds on to the ball far, far too long, and that also creates sacks — he was strip sacked on the first play of the game, and he finished the game with a staggering 36.4% pressure-to-sack ratio.
Per PFF, Baker Mayfield was under pressure on just 25 percent of his dropbacks - 11 dropbacks under pressure. He managed to throw the ball - just release the football from his hand - on only 4 of those dropbacks. 1 completion. Took 4 sacks for a pressure to sack rate of 36.4%
He didn't make any bad decisions with the football on Sunday as he has in the past, but we've seen that recently, too. And at his age — and with is tendency to play through injuries — this is likely who he is at this point.
All of those flaws will not get better at this point in his career. He may succeed with a better coordinator and better wideouts, but Baker Mayfield will always have these problems, and they will continue to lose the Bucs games in the future.
The Bucs have tolerated these problems, and they seem to be okay tolerating them more after extending him. But how long will that last?
If Bucky Irving isn't firing, this offense is moving nowhere.
Irving had exactly 100 yards from scrimmage on Sunday, but he generated explosives to get the ball downfield and he scored a touchdown for Tampa Bay as well to keep them in the game. He's an elite running back who can do it all, but if he's shut down, Tampa Bay has quite literally nothing else.
There are no receivers to dominate the game, nor can Mayfield play well enough to elevate the rest of the team. Teams will begin to hone in on Irving far more than they already have — he is the nexus of the entire paltry offense, and if that nexus is destroyed, Tampa Bay simply has nothing to offer.
The Bucs have to find a way to be more varied offensively. Irving has been carrying the team on his back, and he cannot do that every week.
There has been, and remains, talk about the NFC South. The Bucs are two games back from the Carolina Panthers as it stands, and if they beat the Panthers on Monday Night Football next week, they'll be just one game back and have a shot at the playoffs.
It wouldn't really matter if they made it, though. This offense is so anemic that any visitor in the first round would trample this team, and changes would almost certainly be made in the offseason. The Bucs would limp to the postseason at best, and everyone would know the resulting outcome.
Change will come in Tampa Bay, whether or not they make the playoffs. The iteration of the Buccaneers must die for a new, better team to be born, and that's abundantly clear now after Sunday's loss.

title: Grading Each Position Group in Buccaneers' Frustrating Lions Loss
full_text:
It's another week and another loss for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in a very forgettable 2026 season. The Bucs simply looked outmatched in this matchup against a very legitimate Super Bowl contender in the Detroit Lions, and they fell flat coming out of the bye week.
Let's go over how each position group did with the weekly grades.
I don't think that it's crazy to say this was Baker Mayfield's best game of the season. Mayfield finished with 20 completions for 187 yards, two touchdowns and zero interceptions. However, there were still some moments when Mayfield held on to the ball for a bit too long.
Bucky Irving had an overall solid game, finishing with 18 carries for 68 yards and a touchdown as well as three catches for 32 yards. Kenny Gainwell also did some good work with four runs for 16 yards, as well as four receptions for 43 yards.
This group was hard-carried by Ted Hurst III, who finished with five receptions for 56 yards and two touchdowns. Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin Jr. finished with five receptions for 31 yards combined. This group continues to be one of the biggest disappointments this season.
This group took a massive step back in blocking this week and still didn't add anything to the passing attack. Cade Otton, Payne Durham and Bauer Sharp struggled with a solid group of Lions linebackers in this game.
This group did a little bit better later in the game, but it was a very rough start. A Luke Goedeke holding penalty wiped out an 80-yard Bucky Irving touchdown run and Mayfield was sacked four times in this game, and that was without Aiden Hutchinson for the Lions' front.
Frustrations boiled over in this group as both Vita Vea and A'Shawn Robinson got multiple penalties throughout the game. They did a better job than most at containing Jahmyr Gibbs, but Jared Goff had a pretty clean jersey, only getting sacked once by David Walker.
While Josiah Trotter and Alex Anzalone were solid at making tackles in this matchup, they did struggle in coverage, giving up multiple plays to tight ends and check downs in the middle of the field.
Zyon McCollum was great throughout the game, as was Jacob Parrish before he left the game with a back injury. Benjamin Morrison came in relief and was really bad until he left with a hamstring injury of his own. Kevin Knowles II filled in after Morrison left with an injury and did a pretty solid job.
The Bucs still need a new punter, as this might have been Riley Dixon's worst game of the season. A positive is that Chase McLaughlin made all of his kicks.

title: The Good, Bad and Ugly From Buccaneers' 31-21 Loss to Lions
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers showed some glimpses on Sunday, but simply couldn't maintain the offensive pace required to hang with a team like the Detroit Lions. When it was all said and done, the Bucs lost 30-21, and although the final score is all that matters, this one did feel much closer than the final score indicates.
We saw some positive things from the Bucs, but to no one's surprise, the bad and the ugly will outweigh the good as we look back at what transpired in this game between the Buccaneers and Lions.
Despite his length, speed, and athletic ability, Ted Hurst has seemingly dropped a lot more balls than he's caught. That trend continued early in this game, but in the second quarter, the talented young wideout finally did his job and caught a beautiful 23-yard TD pass from Baker Mayfield.
Baker Mayfield finds Ted Hurst III for a 23-yard TD just before halftime! 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/XKCshSxJnv
On the Buccaneers' final drive with a victory no longer in sight, Hurst registered a couple more catches, including a five-yard TD reception to cap it off. Hurst finished the game with five catches for 56 yards and 2 TDs.
The Bucs' offense has been anemic this year, and they desperately need someone in the WR room to step up. It was nice to see Hurst finally provide a bit of a spark in this one, but it would be even nicer to see him do so more often.
If the Buccaneers had just a league-average offense, it's safe to say they would be one of the better teams in the league. That's how good the Bucs' defense has been this season.
Even though the Lions did put up 31 points by the time this game was over, I thought Todd Bowles' group performed extremely well despite missing several key players in the secondary. Although the Lions did score on a couple of explosive plays in the passing game, the Bucs did a solid job stifling Jahmyr Gibbs prior to garbage time, which is an impressive feat considering that he is one of the league's most dynamic offensive weapons at any position.
The Bucs' defense did what they needed to do, which was hold an explosive offense at bay just enough to give their offense a chance to go win them the game. Unfortunately, like we've seen so many times already this season, the offense couldn't hold up its end of the bargain.
Despite being kept at bay in the first half, Bucky Irving came out firing in the second half and refused to be denied on numerous occasions. Although he didn't crack the 100-yard plateau because an 80-yard TD run was called back, he was tough, elusive and relentless running the football, and he was without a doubt the team's most dynamic offensive player.
I think I have found my new favorite NFL celebration thanks to Bucky Irving and Vita Vea: pic.twitter.com/PDLxsxgeG0
Buccaneers' standout cornerback Jacob Parrish was injured in the first half and ruled out for the remainder of the game with a back injury.
It was a brutal blow for the Buccaneers, who were already without starting safety Antoine Winfield Jr., and desperately needed Parrish in the lineup to help slow down the potent receiving trio of Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams and Sam LaPorta.
When Jacob Parrish left early in the game, Benjamin Morrison was thrust into a big-time spot at outside corner opposite Zyon McCollum. Unsurprisingly, the Lions immediately targeted the second-year corner in coverage and he gave up multiple TD receptions, including one to Amon-Ra St. Brown and another 57-yard TD to Jameson Williams in the third quarter.
The TD surrendered to St. Brown seemed like more of a failure on the back end of the defense, but the Williams TD was simply a matter of Morrison not being able to hang with one of the league's fastest wideouts.
Benjamin Morrison, per @NextGenStats 19 coverage snaps 6 targets 5 receptions allowed 131 yards allowed 2 touchdowns allowed https://t.co/Fi4VY0YtR3
To make matters worse, Morrison left the game with a hamstring injury in the third quarter, continuing what has become a consistent trend throughout his NFL career while further cementing his status as an injury-prone NFL draft bust.
Coming into this game, the Buccaneers had 13 straight losses when trailing or tied entering the fourth quarter of games, which was the longest streak in the NFL. Unfortunately, the longest streak in the NFL is now 14 and still held by the Buccaneers because, once again, they were unable to put together a fourth quarter comeback.
After a very slow first half, Bucky Irving busted free for an 80-yard TD run early in the third quarter that would have given the Buccaneers their first lead of the game. However, instead of 80 yards and six points on the scoreboard, the Buccaneers actually lost yards because Luke Goedeke was called for a holding penalty and ended up having to punt the ball away from deep in their own territory.
Not only was Goedeke's penalty a critical error because of the result on the scoreboard — Detroit scored a TD just a few plays later — but it also killed all of the momentum that the Buccaneers' offense had established. Had Irving's TD run stood, it would have been the second consecutive drive resulting in a touchdown for Tampa Bay.
Bucky Irving got absolutely obliterated by Brian Branch partway through the third quarter. Irving dropped the ball, but more importantly, couldn't get up off the turf after the vicious tackle from the Lions' hard-hitting safety.
This is football, and many injuries are unavoidable, but that was not the case on this particular play. I think everyone in the stadium aside from Mayfield could see Branch closing in on Irving before he received the ball.
Thankfully, Irving is tough as nails and came back into the game just a few plays later. Still, though, Mayfield needs to improve on his anticipation when throwing the football, and this play could be used as an example of that. The Bucs cannot afford to lose their most dynamic offensive weapon, and Mayfield needs to do his part to ensure that doesn't happen.

title: Winners and Losers From Buccaneers' Week 11 Loss to Lions
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers couldn't get it done on Sunday, falling to 3-7 after losing to the Detroit Lions 31-21.
The Bucs defense once again played admirably, but the offense could not do enough to keep them in the game. Tampa Bay's leading receiver was running back Kenny Gainwell, and quarterback Baker Mayfield once again had a tough game under center.
Here are our winners and losers from the tough loss on the road:
Josiah Trotter was all over the field on Sunday.
He had 14 combined tackles on the day, and he was able to help keep Detroit's running game at bay for a good portion of the contest. He was erroneously called for a facemask, which unfortunately stood despite a replay revealing that Trotter grabbed hold of the collar and not the facemask.
Trotter was expected to step in and immediately contribute at linebacker, and so far, he's done very well in that respect throughout the whole year.
Ted Hurst started off his day with some drops, but he made up for it in the back half of the contest.
Hurst caught two touchdowns on Sunday, the first at the beginning of the game in the back corner of the end zone and the last with just eight seconds left in the front corner of the end zone. The latter catch may not have actually mattered, but it was a good confidence boost for Hurst — and after being benched against the Chicago Bears in Week 9, he needed it.
As always, Irving remains the best player on Tampa Bay's offense.
Irving broke one massive touchdown that got called back for holding, but he still managed to net multiple explosive runs afterward. He also got in the end zone as the third quarter ended, leading an offensive drive largely by himself before scoring to put the Bucs within three, 17-14.
Irving took a bit to get going in this game. But he can do it all as a running back, and he proved it on Sunday with his play in the back half.
Starting cornerback Jacob Parrish left the game very early with a back injury, and once that happened, the Lions' offense took advantage by targeting his replacement.
Benjamin Morrison came in for Parrish, and he was picked on right away. He gave up quite a few catches to the likes of Jameson Williams and Amon-Ra St. Brown, and both of them caught a touchdown over Morrison over the course of the game.
Morrison has played good football at times this year, but that wasn't the case when the Bucs really needed him on Sunday in Parrish's absence.
The Bucs offense has played a familiar tune week in and week out so far this season, and Robinson has largely been to blame for it.
The Bucs' passing offense has a lot of trouble stretching the field and getting the football between the hashes. The run game wasn't working well the whole game, and Robinson largely failed to adjust it during the matchup. Finally, play calls were getting in late all game, and it made the entire offensive operation a struggle — the Lions' defense could tee off on Tampa Bay while they didn't have a lot of time to make pre-snap adjustments.
This Bucs offense continues to flounder, and Robinson isn't finding ways to fix it like he should be.
Quarterback Baker Mayfield remains unable to elevate this Buccaneers offense, and while the team has problems overall in that area, he isn't helping.
Outside of a nice dime to Ted Hurst, Mayfield struggled to move the ball down the field in a meaningful way. A good chunk of his passing yards on Sunday were YAC yards after screens and dump-offs behind the line, and he continues to hold on to the football and get punished for it — a strip sack started the game off, and he found himself sacked multiple other times throughout the game because of this too.
Mayfield continues to play middling football at best in Tampa Bay, and it's hurting the offense.

title: Buccaneers Starter Suffers Injury and Leaves Game Against Lions
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have been staying in games because of how well their defense has been playing this year, especially with how porous the offense has been.
That defense will continue to be needed against the Detroit Lions and for the rest of the season, but there is now a pause for concern as one of their top players on that side of the ball has been ruled out of the game with a back injury.
Jacob Parrish has been downgraded to OUT for the remainder of today's game. https://t.co/FQ3wcXzH6J
Parrish has been a stalwart for the Bucs' secondary alongside Zyon McCollum, leading the league with 14 pass breakups. He has continuously been a force to reckon with when targeted, locking down opposing teams' second option.
With Parrish out for the game, Tampa Bay will turn to fellow second-year cornerback Benjamin Morrison to try to help contain the likes of Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams.
Once Parrish went out of the game with his injury, Jared Goff and the Lions realized that they could attack Morrison, who has been in coverage on a large chunk play to Williams and a touchdown to St. Brown.
With Morrison in, the Bucs' defense has had some communication and positioning issues, so the hope is that he is able to get on the same page as everyone else for the remainder of the contest.
The hope is that Parrish's back injury is not too severe to keep him out for multiple games now that we are in the back half of the season. But if he is, the Bucs seem confident in running Morrison out there as his replacement.
Morrison hasn't seen a ton of action since entering the league, mostly due to injury problems, but when he has seen action, he has played fairly well.
The sticking point will be whether Morrison can hold up when it comes to staying healthy himself. If Parrish is set to miss any amount of time and Morrison goes down, then the Bucs will have a big problem on their hands, as they are fairly thin when it comes to cornerback depth.

title: New Details About Baker Mayfield's Injury Revealed Ahead of Buccaneers-Lions
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are set to face off against the Detroit Lions in Week 11 in what should be a hard matchup. Unfortunately for them, their quarterback is also fighting through an injury.
Quarterback Baker Mayfield suffered a foot injury against the Chicago Bears in Week 9. He was reportedly in doubt to play against the Bears, but after practicing on Thursday and Friday, it seems as if he will indeed start despite the injury.
The exact specifics of Mayfield's injury weren't known — until now. An NFL insider revealed those specifics on Saturday, and Mayfield's injury is among the more painful an athlete can suffer.
NFL insider Tom Pelissero revealed that Mayfield is dealing with a plantar fascia injury. It's the connective tissue at the bottom of the foot that extends from the heel to the toes.
Baker Mayfield is dealing with a painful plantar fascia injury – the latest challenge in a season full of them for the Bucs and their franchise QB. More in The Sweep Insider Notebook: https://t.co/NCQdLURx1t pic.twitter.com/lwV2rAiZ4x
The injury is notably a very painful one. Per Pelissero, Mayfield will have to wear a special orthotic and new cleats to help manage the injury as he starts against the Lions on Sunday.
It isn't the first time the Bucs have had a player dealing with this injury in recent memory. Right tackle Luke Goedeke suffered a plantar fascia injury last season when he tore it in Week 2. He missed six games and spent seven weeks on injured reserve, returning to action that November.
It's unknown if Mayfield tore his plantar fascia or merely strained it. It is almost certainly not as severe as Goedeke's injury, but either way, Mayfield won't miss a game because of it, and he'll be back on the field just two weeks after suffering the injury against the Bears.
Mayfield is also dealing with a dislocated thumb he suffered in Week 3 against the Minnesota Vikings. He's still recovering from that injury, too, so he'll be pretty banged up heading into this matchup.
The Bucs will face the Lions at 1 p.m. on Sunday. It will be a tough task already, but with Mayfield playing through multiple injuries, it might get even harder.

title: Our Buccaneers vs. Lions Score Predictions Are In
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have a tough game ahead of them on Sunday. They're well-rested off their bye week, but they're set to face off against a strong 7-2 Detroit Lions team on the road in what could be the toughest remaining game on the schedule.
The Bucs themselves are 3-6, but despite that, they remain one game back from the NFC South lead. The defense has been elite and the run game has been stout, but the passing offense has been a big problem for Tampa Bay — and it may not get much better, as quarterback Baker Mayfield is set to play this game while dealing with a painful plantar fascia injury.
As always, we've rounded up our staff to lock in our picks for Sunday's game. Can the Bucs pull off the upset? Or will they fall to 3-7?
It's getting to the point for the Bucs that they must win, or their season could be over. And things don't get easier this week as they take on the Lions.
The Lions own one of the NFL's elite offenses and will test the Bucs' top-rated defense. It's unlikely they'll replicate their turnover margin as they did against the Bears, but they can most definitely slow Detroit down.
While the defense won't be too much of a worry, the problems will once again come on the offensive side of the ball for Tampa Bay.
The Lions' defense has stepped it up in recent weeks, and even without Aidan Hutchinson, they should be able to stymie the offense enough. I expect this one to be a low-scoring affair at Ford Field, with the Lions coming away with a close home victory to drop the Bucs to 3-7 on the year.
Baker Mayfield is once again on the mend from an injury. Yes, the Lions have injuries of their own with Aiden Hutchinson and Jack Campbell, but I don’t know if a hobbled Baker Mayfield or a healthy Jalon Daniels will be able to get the job done.
As much as I believe that the Buccaneers' defense is for real, I also believe the offense is not.
Detroit, on the other hand, has one of the most dynamic offenses in the entire league. Beyond just the litany of weapons he has at his disposal, Jared Goff has been extremely effective playing against Bowles' blitz-heavy defenses over the past several years.
For the Bucs to win, they'll need to get pressure with four to avoid sending extra guys to disrupt Goff in the pocket. The problem is, even if they do that and manage to generate turnovers like they have been so far this year on defense, the Bucs will need Baker Mayfield to look like a competent NFL QB on offense to win this football game. Sadly, I'm not sure if that version of Mayfield even exists anymore.
Another battle for Todd Bowles against a high-scoring offense in Detroit. I’m excited to watch that, but the next thing I’m most intrigued about is the Bucs’ offensive passing attack.
That has to improve, or Tampa Bay isn’t making the playoffs — It’s quite simple for me on that. Hopefully the bye week helped, but I’m very cautious about picking the Buccaneers.
The Bucs have a few things going for them, but this is a passing league, and unfortunately, they don't have the passing offense to hang with good teams — much less an elite one like the Lions.
The defense will likely hold the Detroit Lions' dynamic offense in check, but the passing offense won't be enough, and it could be even worse than usual with Mayfield's injury. I think the Bucs defense will keep them in it, but it won't be enough to win against a team that could end up winning the brutal NFC North this season.
Once again, our staff isn't picking Tampa Bay whatsoever. Our staff unanimously picked the Bears two weeks ago, and we've unanimously picked the Lions here.
It's any given Sunday in the NFL, so the Bucs are always in it. But they'll have to convince us that they can beat good teams, and so far, they simply haven't.

title: Buccaneers-Lions Game Features Massive Swing for Playoff Chances
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are sitting at a paltry 3-6 record after their Week 10 bye. In most NFL divisions, that would be the end of the road for any playoff-hopeful team. Thankfully for the Bucs, they don't play in most NFL divisions.
The Bucs play in the NFC South, where the Carolina Panthers lead the division with a 4-5 record. The Bucs are very much in the race, and a division win would mean making the playoffs and hosting a playoff game.
The Bucs are going to have to win quite a few games outside of their four remaining division games to make that happen, though, and that includes their Week 11 game this Sunday against the Detroit Lions. The Lions are 7-2 and present a tough challenge, so it would be an upset if the Bucs could pull it off.
If they do, though? Their playoff chances will increase dramatically.
Per The Athletic's Playoff Simulator , the Bucs have a 47% chance of making the playoffs. They're second in the division behind the Panthers, but despite that, they still have the highest playoff odds in the NFC South.
A win over the Lions would put that percentage much higher, though. Beating Detroit shoots Tampa Bay's number up 11 percentage points to 58%, as they'd go into their crucial Week 12 game against the Panthers either one game behind or tied for the lead. A loss would plummet them down seven percentage points to 40%.
The Lions have some significant stake in this game too, however. They currently have a 74% chance to make the playoffs in a division with all four teams winning six or more games — if they beat the Bucs, that number shoots up eight percentage points to 82%, while a loss brings it down 12 percentage points to 62%.
Even if the Bucs lose, though, hope is not lost. They'll play the division-leading Panthers in Week 12 on Monday Night Football, and even with a loss against the Lions, they'd still have a 53% chance to make the playoffs. Win two in a row, though? Tampa Bay would be looking at a 73% chance.
The Bucs will do their best to get that win on Sunday in Detroit at 1 p.m., but it won't be easy.

title: Buccaneers' Todd Bowles Gets Put on the Spot About Bruce Arians
full_text:
Bruce Arians handed the keys to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' head coaching position over to Todd Bowles after he retired in 2022, and the two have maintained their close friendship ever since.
Arians had a short stint in a front office role with the Bucs since his retirement, but in a recent interview with NFL insider Jordan Schultz, he relayed that he is itching to get back into coaching in 2027.
Arians expressed that he doesn't want to join a team in any capacity other than as the head coach, so it will be interesting to see if he garners any interest once the coaching carousel begins.
When speaking with the media following practice, Bowles gave his thoughts on whether his predecessor could still coach despite being 74 years old.
"I talk to Bruce [Arians], but we don't talk about coaching," Bowles exclaimed . "Tom Moore made Bruce look like a college student. So, you can still coach at that age, and Tom's probably a younger heart more than anybody. And so, it doesn't surprise me. Bruce can do whatever he wants to do."
It was a funny little quip from Bowles comparing the former Bucs' offensive assistant Tom Moore to Arians.
Moore coached in some capacity until the age of 88 years old, which means that Arians has some 14 years to catch him.
With all that said, it's hard to imagine that Bowles isn't right in stating that Arians can do whatever he puts his mind to.
Arians had retired before unretiring and joining the Bucs in 2019 to try and win his first Super Bowl.
If he does in fact return to coaching, he likely will only accept an offer where he can foresee himself having ultimate control while also having high thoughts on how the roster is stacked up to potentially go out and contend for his second Lombardi Trophy.
But will Arians return to coach the Bucs if Bowles is relieved of his duties at the end of the season? It's highly doubtful.
Arians handed the keys to Bowles after winning a Super Bowl, so taking over following him could likely create a rift between the two, especially if there were to be behind-the-scenes talks.
On top of that, this Bucs' roster probably doesn't move Arians enough to come back and coach.

title: Robert Saleh Rips Titans Defense and Threatens Job Losses After Cowboys Disaster
full_text:
It's apparently "no more Mr. Nice Guy" in Nashville today. Robert Saleh took the podium for his day-after press conference following yesterday's 51-30 loss to the Dallas Cowboys, and for perhaps the first time this season, didn't show an ounce of restraint.
Saleh called the Titans' performance "disgusting" and "embarrassing" after the game on Sunday. Clearly, his frustrations didn't subside with a night to sleep on them. The head coach said today that Tennessee's defense didn't "reciprocate" the offense's success moving the ball.
What's more, when asked for positives regarding his defense, Saleh didn't hold back: "I'm not going to try and sugar-coat things ... It's been dog ----." Saleh went as far as to openly call jobs into question, adding of both players and coaches that those who get better will stay.
Those that don't? Well, they won't. Saleh also alluded to the hard conversations going on behind the scenes right now for Tennessee, though as expected, he won't reveal those details. This sounds like a dumpster fire, and on the field, it is.
But there's something refreshing about Saleh threatening to burn this thing to the ground. Saleh, alongside general manager Mike Borgonzi, are initiating the sort of purification process that this franchise has needed for years.
The Titans have allowed 45 points per game in the month of November. If that doesn't beg for a reset, I'm not sure what does. Saleh's own unit is broken, and the offense that Borgonzi has built through the draft isn't being allowed to fully flourish as a result.
Thankfully, the first step has already been taken. The Titans made some difficult trades and acquired the draft capital to see them through for the next two years. Borgonzi, coming off an inarguably solid draft that saw Carnell Tate and Anthony Hill Jr. join the ranks, appears equipped to keep building.
But Tennessee must fully tear down what is broken to build something sturdier in the same spot. Saleh's first year behind the wheel has been marred by the miscues of Brian Callahan before him, and Callahan's short-lived era was marred by Mike Vrabel's bitter end.
The cycle has to stop, and the slate must be wiped completely clean, at some point. That's why Saleh's comments should be a breath of fresh air for Titans fans. He's publicly furious at the brand of football this team is playing; finally, the usual "coach speak" has been entirely dropped.
Expect a flurry of moves across the board this offseason if things don't improve for Tennessee before the end of the year. At 1-9, I'm not sure what the next seven games could bring that will satisfy Saleh. If embarrassment is what it takes to spark change, then Tennessee must temporarily embrace it.
Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. A longtime sports fanatic and recent baby blue jersey aficionado.

title: Titans Mill: Debating Whether or Not Cam Ward Has Turned the Page, or if He Still Has More to Prove
full_text:
Today's Titans Mill is all about Tennessee's most important player. After a loss like yesterday's, you can only look at what's to come for a 1-9 team like the Titans. What's to come in Nashville hinges entirely on the state of Cam Ward's progression. Every game is his to prove.
Just how much has Ward proved up to now? Tennessee has seven games left in this season, but Ward's recent hot streak has taken QBs out of the conversation on draft boards for the Titans; is the discussion about QB1 in the long run already over?
The short answer is yes, for now. The long answer is a little more complicated
Ward, after catching fire in Week 8 against the Cincinnati Bengals, has since thrown six touchdowns to one interception. The sophomore passer has surpassed 200 passing yards in each of his last three contests, and even broke 300 yards in Week 10 vs. the Jacksonville Jaguars.
He's on one, to put it blunty. His recent stretch culminated in a ridiculous, late-fourth-quarter touchdown that has amassed almost four million views on X. The cross-body deep ball came in garbage time, but it immediately emerged as a viral highlight.
A career isn't made by a highlight, nor a starting job secured. But Ward has silenced any doubts about his role this season, and most likely going into next year.
He's got the keys, barring a complete breakdown.
That's the catch here. Tennessee's draft capital is so vast this year and next that nothing is really off the table; general manager Mike Borgonzi will have the tools to build whatever kind of roster he chooses in the aftermath of the team's recent trades.
Ward looks fully the part of a franchise passer right now, but it was barely more than a month ago that Robert Saleh was being asked about the possibility of benching him. A turnaround only takes a few games, and the Titans have plenty more for momentum to be charted in either direction.
Losing 51-30 to the Dallas Cowboys is likely to cloud all positivity for most teams; for Ward to come out of that mess with any semblance of hope is a great sign of the player he's becoming. Fans should believe he's turned the page, but the debate isn't over until Tennessee starts winning games.
That means we won't know for sure, unfortunately, until next season. That's the way of the road with a rebuild that goes as deep as the Titans' does.

title: Cowboys Exposed Titans' Talent Problem, and the Obvious Solution is at Least 1 Season Away
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans losing 51-30 to the Dallas Cowboys came as a mild surprise. Nothing about the way the game went down, play-to-play, wasn't all that shocking. Cam Ward and the offense slowly came on, scoring 23+ in their fifth straight game - the first time Tennessee has done that since 2021.
Robert Saleh's defense, on the other hand, continued their recent miserable stretch by allowing 40+ points for the third straight game. The defense is the main topic at hand in this post-game autopsy of sorts; therein is this team's current, overarching problem.
Tennessee simply doesn't have the talent to contend with your average competitive team, specifically on defense. That's the bad news.
This problem is at its worst when guys are missing time; CB Cor'Dale Flott (who has had his own issues) leaving in Week 11 with a neck injury meant reserve Micah Robinson had to step up in his place against a free-firing Cowboys offense.
Jeffery Simmons being traded resulted in waiver-wire add DT Jonah Laulu and DT Timmy Horne, who was cut and re-added for Laulu, getting quality minutes in his place. The Titans marched into AT&T Stadium with second-string guys, in some cases at best, and got slammed.
Saleh, both due to nagging injuries and deadline trades, just doesn't have a group that can consistently battle with the best of them... or really even those in the middle of the pack. The good news, however?
This problem is likely to fix itself in time.
Trading Simmons, as well as S Amani Hooker, cut Saleh's defense off at the knees. Tennessee's offense is the opposite; that unit is thriving, even after being forced to start high-upside guys across the board after Wan'Dale Robinson was sent to IR.
The few pieces that are working in Saleh's defense are more aligned with a younger, yet proven vision for this roster. Anthony Hill Jr. has developed into a resident starter in his first season, and leads the Titans in tackles. He's earned his heavy-handed role.
Hill's fellow LB, Cedric Gray, just worked his way back into a starting role in Week 11 alongside the rookie. Gray had his first interception the week prior, helping tip him over the edge into the leading role he had last season.
It's not necessarily about age, as both Robinson and Horne fit the youthful demographic. Rather, it's about well-selected talent that specifically thrives in Saleh's system. With two first and second-round picks this year, Tennessee has a golden opportunity to right the ship in year two.
The only catch is, that means enduring the between-stages product that's taking the field right now. It will get better eventually, Titans fans, but don't count on it anytime soon.

title: Titans' Kryptonite vs. Cowboys: How Inability to Play a Complete Game Caused Fourth Straight Defeat
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans fell to 1-9 following another lifeless defensive performance, losing to the Dallas Cowboys 51-30. This was truly an atrocious performance by the Titans' defense specifically. It honestly felt like the Cowboys were destined to score a touchdown every time they touched the ball, and that’s practically what they did.
Cowboys RB Javonte Williams routinely gashed them seemingly every time he touched the ball, finishing with 91 total yards and one touchdown, while RB KaVontae Turpin added 41 yards and another score on just two carries.
Meanwhile, the electric trio of QB Dak Prescott, WR CeeDee Lamb and WR George Pickens tore this depleted secondary apart with ease. Dallas’ two star receivers combined for 18 catches, 234 yards, and two touchdowns. As for Prescott, he completed 85 percent of his passes for 325 yards and four touchdowns.
If there was ever a game where this team felt the absence of DT Jeffery Simmons and S Amani Hooker, it was this one. This Titans defense has been forced to depend on the likes of DB Isaiah Oliver, DL Nazir Stackhouse, DT Tommy Horne, and DL Jonah Laulu.
Respectfully, those aren’t the type of names you can realistically compete with, especially when playing an explosive offense like Dallas’
If there’s any sign of optimism going forward, it’s the fact that the Titans offense is at least showing signs of life. They’re still a young unit that undoubtedly needs more talent, but they at least show a collective fight as a unit.
QB Cam Ward and WR Carnell Tate continue to develop into an intriguing young tandem that will only get better the more they play together.
RB Tony Pollard is a consistent running back that a lot of contending teams clearly valued enough to try to trade for. He’s single-handedly given this team a balanced ground game that’s helped Ward grow over the last few weeks.
This offense has the pieces to at least compete with anybody on any given Sunday. But right now, it feels like the Titans are fighting a losing, never-ending battle offensively. No matter what they do, it probably won’t be enough to overcome the type of defensive ineptitude the Titans are currently displaying.
The Titans could score 45 and the defense would respond by giving up 50. The Titans obviously need a complete overhaul defensively, but unfortunately for everyone who watches this team, it won’t be coming until the spring at the earliest.
Shaun is a longtime Titans fan who has years of experience in the field. He missed being on the team beat, and is here to change that. He also writes scripts for EA Sports' Madden games, where fans may have heard his work.

title: 5 Titans Quick Hits After Loss to Cowboys: Cam Ward Makes Recent History, While Defense Collapses
full_text:
Not good, Nashville, not good. The Tennessee Titans have fallen to 1-9 in one of their worst losses of the season, as the Dallas Cowboys ran away with today's game to a grating final tune of 51-30.
The offense is still scoring, and keeping relative pace as far as their own achievements go. But on the whole, this is a broken Titans team desperate for a perfect offseason. Those 2027 first-round picks can't come soon enough.
But until then, here are five quick hits for Titans fans to brood about from today's defeat. They're not all horrible, believe it or not.
Yes, the Titans lost, and that comes down to not scoring as many points as the other team. But as we pointed out at halftime, with a defense like this, what can be expected of Tennessee's offense?
Positive strides are being made. Today, Cam Ward led his unit to an impressive bit of recent history. The Titans just made their streak of scoring at least 23 or more five straight games, per Easton Freeze. Ward has largely answered questions surrounding his incoming third year.
Ward would finish the day with 248 yards (his third straight game with 200+) and two touchdowns on 21/30 passing. His one touchdown was a career-long 59-yard score to Carnell Tate. That was a weird play, but we'll take it regardless.
Again, Tate had a 59-yard score today due to a heads-up play that saw him stand back up after a catch and run for a free score. His return after two weeks off with a shoulder injury was properly exciting.
But an early-game drop for Tate (on a wide open slant, no less) continued to point out his ball-securityt issues. The Titans' WR1 has three fumbles in his rookie year, with two of those lost to opposing teams. This is something he'll have to clean up on his rise to elite status.
On the defensive side of the ball, things couldn't be going worse for Tennessee. The Titans allowed the Cowboys to score on all six of their first six drives in this game before forcing a field goal... which Dallas made. The Cowboys' 51 points speak for themselves.
Robert Saleh's continued adjustments just aren't taking hold on a unit that looks beyond help. The Titans have now allowed 40+ points in three straight games for the second time in franchise history, and the first since 2004.
Historically bad, if you will.
It doesn't help that the secondary, which has been the Titans' weakest defensive unit pretty much all year, is suffering numerous injuries.
S Tony Adams barely played today due to an illness. CB Cor'Dale Flott left in the first half with a neck injury. S Amani Hooker was traded right before the deadline. Obviously Hooker wasn't injured, but his absence continues to be felt on defense.
Not only is this group not at full strength, but they're not particularly strong even when they are. Saleh may need to wipe the slate clean in the secondary if the Titans want a chance to improve down the road.
Finally, in more negative news, the Titans' offensive line allowed five sacks today. Sure, LG Peter Skoronski and RG Fernando Carmona Jr. remain out (LT Dan Moore Jr. also exited today with a knee injury), but this bunch had done a solid job up to Week 11 in performing well despite injuries.
Everything fell apart against Dallas. Ward was stripped in the fourth quarter for a sack-fumble. Prior to today, Tennessee hadn't allowed any more than four sacks in a contest; that high game in Week 5's 26-3 blowout loss to the Houston Texans.
It's a miracle that the Titans' offense put up as many points as they did with pieces falling apart almost everywhere else. A miserable game, with a handful of equally miserable quick takeaways.
Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. A longtime sports fanatic and recent baby blue jersey aficionado.

title: Titans Halftime vs. Cowboys: Tennessee Can't Win With a Defense This Bad... But Who is to Blame?
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans' offense doesn't look the same as they have been in the past two weeks right now. Tennessee has a meager nine points (all via Joey Slye) at halftime against the Dallas Cowboys, failing to score a touchdown or make any real mark on the road in Texas.
Dallas, on the other hand, are scoring at will. The Cowboys put up 27 points in the first half alone, led by 182 passing yards and two scores through the air for QB Dak Prescott. WR CeeDee Lamb has already chalked up 103 yards through the air and a touchdown of his own.  The Cowboys scored on their first four drives today for the first time since 2022.
Put plainly: The Titans are being run out of the stadium. Clearly, the staff's efforts to simplify the defense aren't working; to be clear, nothing is working. Robert Saleh's own unit is this team's greatest weakness, and it's only getting worse week after week.
To be fair, that's what happens when you trade two pieces like S Amani Hooker and DT Jeffery Simmons right before the deadline. Those are promising moves for the Titans a year or two from now, but it's left the current roster with virtually no defensive resilience or consistency.
The team's current struggles are the unfortunate result of fair moves made by the front office. The blame only goes as far as the players on the field, for now.
Naturally, people may be quick to point fingers at a defense-first head coach whose specialty looks like the worst aspect of his team. However, it's hard to pin these issues on Coach Saleh. He's made adjustments, and the players brought in over the offseason are faring better than the holdovers.
Save for the secondary, which again today looks like a total loss. The Titans need a reset there.
But Saleh was brought in and took hold of a sort of limbo for this franchise. Brian Callahan had a shot at a fresh rebuild prior to Saleh, and he failed to deliver during his short tenure. Saleh's overall record (likely about to move to 1-9) is obviously poor, but next year will be his first real shot at an overhaul.
This isn't to say that Saleh is on the fast-track to success; rather, the coach can't be judged based on a roster that was between phases when he was hired. The Titans don't have the personnel to compete with Dallas right now.
We're not counting out a second-half miracle, but no team is winning with a defense this bad. Terry McCormick pointed out on X that, dating back to last week, the Titans have given up 54 points on nine straight drives without forcing a punt. The only fix appears to be waiting it out... which Titans fans are unfortunately used to by now.

title: Titans’ Inactives vs. Cowboys: Carnell Tate’s Return is All That Matters for Breakout-Ready Offense
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans will look to capture their second victory of the 2026 NFL season on Sunday, as head coach Robert Saleh's squad will take on the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium.
Though Tennessee is 1-8 and currently possesses the No. 1 overall pick in April's draft, the team has shown tremendous progress over the last few weeks, especially the offense. After a rough start to the year, the unit has finally started to find a groove, and quarterback Cam Ward is also making much-needed progress in his development.
Brian Daboll's offense will eye another productive outing in Week 11 against the Cowboys, and luckily for them, the group is getting its No. 1 receiver back.
The Titans released their list of inactives ahead of Sunday's contest in Dallas, and rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate was not among those listed. Tate has missed the last two games with a shoulder injury, but seems ready to return.
In seven games this season, Tate has posted 34 receptions for 413 yards and one touchdown, including a 145-yard day against the Baltimore Ravens in Week 4. His comeback should only mean this offense ticks further up than they already have in the past two productive weeks.
Here's the full list of inactives for Tennessee, including rookie running back Nick Singleton as a healthy scratch:
. @Titans inactives vs Cowboys: RB Nick Singleton LB Mohamoud Diabate CB Jaylon Jones DT Jackie Marshall OT Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson
When the Titans selected Singleton in the fifth round of April's draft, many expected him to make an impact in his rookie season and eventually establish himself as the clear-cut replacement for Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears, who are both set to hit free agency in the spring. However, that hasn't been the case so far this year.
Singleton has tallied just 12 yards on seven carries, and hasn't been given many opportunities to flash his skill set. Even with Spears landing on injured reserve this week, the coaching staff isn't handing Singleton a more featured role. Instead, Tennessee elevated veteran Michael Carter to serve as Pollard's backup for Sunday's game.
We'll see how Carter plays in Week 11 and whether he truly is a better, more reliable backup running back option than Singleton. Regardless of performance, it's a bit deflating that the Titans seem to have little faith in their young back who came out of training camp and the preseason with a lot of hype surrounding him.

title: Game Day vs. Cowboys: 2 Players Titans Have No Excuse Not to Feed on Offense
full_text:
Carnell Tate's expected return marks the comeback of the Tennessee Titans' best receiver. But don't be fooled, Titans fans; Week 11 is not a return to form for Brian Daboll's bunch. With Wan'Dale Robinson and Tyjae Spears on IR, both the pass-catching core and backfield have to pivot.
Tennessee's 1-8 record allows, if not necessitates, backup options to get some time in the spotlight. The Titans should be trial-running their young players right now before drafting a whole new batch of them with their litany of picks in 2027.
That's why we've got two must-feed players on offense this game-day morning. These are guys that, given the aforementioned injuries, should absolutely be getting touches against the Dallas Cowboys.
The excuses have run out on Nick Singleton more than anyone else on the roster. Tennessee's fifth-round rookie back has seven touches on the entire season; with Spears on IR, there's no reason the Titans shouldn't be playing Singleton behind Tony Pollard.
Earlier this year, it was a "not ready" issue with Singleton. But with no real opportunities since Week 4, how will we know when the rookie is ready? Better yet, on a 1-8 team, why does it matter? The Titans have the draft assets to overhaul the backfield if need be. Why not play the rook now?
Michael Carter, the veteran who has been playing over Singleton when Spears is absent, was elevated to the roster upon Spears' move to IR. That means Titans fans should prepare for the worst, but hope for the best, with the former Penn State stud against Dallas.
As far as the passing game is concerned, second-year WR Chimere Dike should continue to see an uptick in targets and production.
Dike stepped into the limelight back in Week 8, when Tate missed his first game. The former came down with five receptions and his first touchdown of the season. He added two more catches for 16 yards last week.
This is a playmaker who has already achieved Pro-Bowl status on special teams; he's proven his elite ability on that front. Per Adam Koffler, Dike played 71% of his snaps from the slot last season. He thrives where Ayomanor doesn't, and should be first in line to soak up Robinson's snaps.
With Tate and Ayomanor on the outside, and Dike seeing more work in the slot, we'd be looking at a Titans offense fully embracing the long-term future of this team. Let's hope the staff embraces that, and Dike takes his anticipated leap this afternoon.

title: 3 Matchups That Will Decide Titans Duel vs. Cowboys: All Eyes on Carnell Tate in Likely Return
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans are entering their Week 11 duel with the Dallas Cowboys in a sort of limbo. Robert Saleh's team currently holds the first overall pick in 2027, but naturally, Saleh's own clock on the sideline turns much faster than almost anyone else in the organization.
Fans are still looking out for improvement. Weeks 8 and 10 saw the Titans' offense take a leap while the defense fell behind, with Tennessee trading a few franchise cornerstones in the middle of that stretch. No big deal.
Heading into tomorrow's game, I expect three matchups will decide the Titans' road battle. Saleh needs a win (in more ways than one), but these picks go beyond his individual status. Let's jump in.
In his likely return tomorrow, Titans' WR1 Carnell Tate couldn't have drawn a bigger matchup. The Cowboys have one of the worst overall defenses in the NFL, but on the frontlines in the secondary is CB Joey Porter Jr. Tate outplaying Porter could uncork this Tennessee offense.
With Wan'Dale Robinson headed to IR, Tate is essentially the only remaining preseason starter in the rotation. It's probably better that Elic Ayomanor and Chimere Dike are starting instead of Robinson and Calvin Ridley, but all the same, the group is depleted.
With CB DaRon Bland placed on IR, Dallas is already a step behind in this matchup. The Titans need Tate to make a statement in his return, and help lead this offense to yet another net-positive showing.
Tennessee's secondary has been miserable over the past two weeks, and really this season as a whole, save for the now-traded Amani Hooker picking Joe Burrow off three times in Week 8. So miserable, in fact, that I'm instead anchoring the defensive matchup to Tennessee's d-line.
If any group has the remaining pieces to elevate the Titans' defense into a competitive state, it's that one. DT John Franklin-Myers and off-the-edge duo Jacob Martin and Jermaine Johnson have inherited a mess sans Jeffery Simmons. They'll be facing a fringe-top 10 OL in Dallas, per PFF.
It's not a favorable duel for the Titans' d-line, but Robert Saleh desperately needs his veterans to pull through and generate some pressure so that the Cowboys don't do what the Bengals and Jaguars did to Tennessee. That is, throw the ball virtually wherever they please.
A little bit of pressure goes a long way, and any path that Tennessee can take to make things easier on their secondary should be promptly taken.
Lastly, we've got a matchup on the sidelines. OC Brian Daboll will be coaching against the Cowboys' newly-dubbed defensive play-caller Mike Pettine. Christian Parker remains the DC in Dallas, but the duties often tied to the position have been shifted to the more experienced Pettine.
Daboll should be taking advantage of this change by pressing the main thing that has worked for Tennessee; the no-huddle offense. In Week 10, Tennessee ran an astonishing 49.1% of their plays in the no-huddle. The Green Bay Packers were second to that, all the way down at 24.1%.
Play fast, keep Dallas on their feet, and play to Cam Ward's strengths. That formula has led to two solid offensive showings in the past two weeks, even given both were losses, and could lead to even greater results as the Cowboys' defense adjusts to their internal movement.
This is a matchup Daboll should win, but then again, his play-calling track record this season has been far from flawless. We'll see which way the tide turns tomorrow.

title: RB Tyjae Spears Hitting IR May End His Run With Titans, Lighting the Fuse for Nick Singleton
full_text:
Tony Pollard tracking for a career-best season with the Tennessee Titans this season has shadowed a blemish right behind him in the backfield. Tyjae Spears was supposed to really come on this season - he entered it healthy, and seemingly prepared to take over for Pollard at some point.
Not only has the opposite been true, but after practicing in full just yesterday, Tyjae Spears has been sent to IR just one day before Tennessee's Week 11 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys. Michael Carter has been elevated from the practice squad as a result.
It's a lingering knee issue being cited for Spears, which will now force him to miss at least four games. The Titans only have eight more games on the schedule this year. Up to now, Spears has missed just two games, but he's basically been nonexistent for Tennessee after Week 1.
His former split-snap share with Pollard has disintegrated; what remains is a pass-catching back picking up the scraps of a guy four years his elder. Not only should Titans fans expect little to nothing of Spears if he comes back, but this could actually be the premature end of his time in Nashville.
When he has seen the field this season, Spears' 22 carries have gone for just 94 yards and no touchdown. He has no score through the air either, where 16 receptions yielded just 75 yards for the back up to now.
It's not just his current struggles that signal the end, either. Spears will be a free agent this coming offseason, alongside Pollard. You have to think that the Titans bring back the latter between the two, and that's if Tennessee doesn't use one of their many draft picks on an RB and let them both walk.
The path back to a relevant role with Tennessee is simply as thin and unrealistic as it has ever been for Spears. This was the year that he was supposed to come into his own as a primary playmaker in a young, budding offense. The experiment is over. Spears looks like an outlier.
As for where the Titans go without Spears, the obvious answer should be more touches for rookie back Nick Singleton. Pollard will continue to helm RB1 duties, but Tennessee won't get any forward momentum from backing him up with two or three carries for Carter every game.
Pollard coming back next season isn't surefire, and even if he does, the guy is going on 30 years old. Singleton was a fifth-round draft pick who has seen seven carries across four appearances. He was shaking off some rookie frost early in the year, which could fairly lead to less playing time, but Singleton hasn't been given an extended chance since Week 4. That's unfair.
It also doesn't make sense. With Spears' time in Tennessee almost certainly winding down, it's time for the Titans to ramp Singleton up from here on out to determine exactly what he's capable of. The backfield can't be this team's next long-term issue.
Preventing that starts with hugging the cactus and allowing your rookie to make some mistakes on a 1-8 team without putting him in the dog house as a result. Week 11 will be a big tell for the Titans' plans at RB either way.

title: 10 Commanders Quotes on Stopping Joe Burrow and Keeping NFC East Hopes Alive
full_text:
The Washington Commanders beat the Giants 24–21 with a touchdown drive between two late defensive stops. Dan Quinn liked the finish. He also wants to know whether his team can do it again. The Bengals have scored at least 30 points in five straight games , and Washington is still working through its problems in pass coverage . Offensive coordinator David Blough said his group has not reached its standard, either. Monday night gives both sides another chance to show where they stand. From Quinn’s review of the Giants game through Saturday’s final practice, these 10 quotes tell the story of Washington’s week before facing Cincinnati.
Question: If Hartman can bring people from his life onto The Bachelor, would he bring anyone from the Commanders? “I’d bring the whole team if I could. I think maybe, I know towards the end you get to do, like, a home or they kind of meet the family thing. I think maybe I’ll just bring the whole team because that is my family right now. They probably know me the best in the world. So I think that would be a good barometer for her and myself to kind of see what I’m about and what she’s about.”
Question: Is there anything about Ja’Marr Chase’s game that Williams would like to bring into his own? “Definitely. I think one of the things that really makes him special is his ability just to make guys miss and run through tackles after the catch. But this year I’ve actually had the opportunity to watch, like, a lot of the top guys that we’ve gone against. So I always, you know, watch them from the sideline and see what they’re doing on the field in person.”
Question: Burrow likes to step up through the B gaps when he escapes pressure. How can Washington take that away? “As a defensive line, we have to cage the quarterback. So when we do have pressure, make sure there’s no holes or leaky gaps that he can run through and gain 15 yards plus.”
Question: In the 2024 Bengals game , how did Daniels decide to throw to Terry McLaurin in single coverage with a free rusher coming at him? “I think it was more so like I’m going to throw the ball to Terry and whatever happens, I got to pick myself up, somebody else pick me up off the ground. You know, at that moment, but it was worth it.”
Question: Why is Burrow so good against the blitz ? “He knows where the hot is. He can see it. Like I said, elite processing. He sees the hot and he’s right now to it. And those guys are great run after catch. So he just gets the ball in their hands quick and then lets them go and make plays. When you got two dudes like that on the outside and you got a running back like [Chase] Brown and you got a tight end, you just want to get the ball to those guys’ hands and let them be playmakers like they are.” Brown entered Week 11 leading all NFL running backs with 47 receptions , giving Burrow a reliable outlet underneath when teams bring pressure.
Question: What did Quinn like about Washington’s no-huddle sequence against the Giants, and why did the offense wait until the fourth quarter to use it again? “We did make that decision just to, one, have that as part of the game plan. To say, this would be something we think that we wanted to get to, to move quickly. And so we’ll have that available in the games moving forward when we want to choose to use it. But I do think it’s a weapon worth doing. Sometimes it’s even by a personnel group, just to stay in this group to get going. And so having, I don’t know how to say this, more guys, just I felt like the last couple weeks, we found a better rhythm of people not in and out. And so I think that plays into it too, to stay in this group and get them going for a while.”
Question: What techniques must Washington’s cornerbacks keep in mind against Cincinnati’s receivers? “Where’s his split? What leverage am I playing? And then when I have my leverage, I have to own my leverage. ... And then you gotta be tight enough to contest the catch. You gotta compete. That’s gonna be huge. ... But we can’t make it a seven-on-seven pitch and catch all over the field and can’t have that. We gotta be tighter in coverage.”
Question: How has Washington’s defense helped the offense during games? “I think for our players specifically, they feel the confidence of that. You feel like our defense is running off after a sack or a turnover and you’re like, ‘Man, these guys, if we score seven tonight, if we score 10 tonight, we score 13 or 14, whatever it may be, we got a chance to win this game.’ But, at the same point, we wanna live up to our standard of execution and things like that. And we really haven’t reached it as an offensive unit yet. So it’s being able to run the ball efficiently; it’s being able to be explosive in the passing game. We have done a good job taking care of the football, but we gotta be better on third down. And then I think when we can kind of piece a full game together, it’ll really help our defense out as well.” Entering Week 11, Washington’s offense ranked 30th on third down, and Cincinnati’s 30th-ranked third-down defense gives Blough’s unit an opening to extend drives and address its red-zone issues .
Question: Does Cosmi see a path for Washington to go on a run after the Giants win? “For sure. I mean, I think we could compete with anybody coming down this pipe. So we got to keep stacking them and getting wins and putting wins in the win column. From that standpoint, the division is very much accessible to us. So we just got to win ball games here. It’s that simple. Execute and we got a shot for sure.”
Question: How much did the Giants win change Washington’s opportunities in the second half of the season? “You take advantage of an opportunity. And when you miss them, there’s regret. And when you take advantage of them, I think it does provide something of proof to say, ‘This is how you can operate and do that.’ And so the proof is in, can you do it again? Can you do it again? And so that’s the response with the group. And that’s what I’m looking for.”

title: Jonathan Allen Returns to Washington on MNF. Does He Hold a Grudge?
full_text:
Jonathan Allen never thought he'd wear another jersey after being drafted 17th overall in 2017 by the team located literally in his backyard. But that's precisely what happened: last December, he played them for the first time on the opposing side as a traveling Washington Commanders team lost 31-0 to the Minnesota Vikings. Monday night , he'll make his first trip back home to play the team he grew up cheering for, as a member of the Cincinnati Bengals. Allen recorded 42 sacks in 108 starts across eight seasons — good enough to rank 10th in franchise history, but he was part of a bad era of football in D.C. — one that led him to tell reporters on more than one occasion that he'd had enough . On Wednesday’s Up & Adams , he said, “Obviously, it’s going to be emotional come game time.”
Allen tore a pectoral muscle in 2024 and missed nine games. He returned for Washington’s final two regular-season games and its NFC Championship Game run. In 2025, Commanders GM Adam Peters was asked about Allen at the combine; Peters said the club wanted to “do right by Jon.” Washington released Allen on March 7 after no trade materialized , saving the team $16.5 million against the salary cap. In Thursday’s Bengals locker-room interview , Allen said, “I’ll be lying if I say there wasn’t any hard feelings.” Asked whether he holds the decision against Washington, he answered, "Is it something I hold against them? No." “But one thing I can always say is I always give that city my all, gave that team my all, and when fans come out to watch us play, they knew that 93 was gonna show up and give everything he had," Allen said. "At the end of the day, the things that I did wrong, I apologize and move on.”
Will have more later, but #Bengals DT Jonathan Allen talked for 12 minutes today about going back to Washington, where he played his first 8 seasons. Emphasized his love for the city, the fans and his teammates but admitted some hard feelings for the organization. pic.twitter.com/QvDcaCUr0a
Through nine Bengals games, Allen has four sacks and nine quarterback hits. He enters Monday with 49.5 career sacks, putting his 50th within reach against the team that drafted him. Cincinnati defensive coordinator Al Golden said, “Maybe he’s rejuvenated because he’s kind of gone back to his roots.” Allen’s fourth sack came last Sunday against Aaron Rodgers on third down, forcing Pittsburgh to settle for a field goal. He got there using a move Jim Tomsula taught him in 2017 , when Tomsula was Washington’s defensive line coach. Golden has been impressed with Allen against the run, too, saying he’s given Cincinnati more than it expected there. Sam Cosmi got plenty of work against Allen in Washington practices and faced him again when Allen was with Minnesota. Cosmi said Thursday they used to talk about meeting in a game, and he expects some chirping when they do it again Monday. Washington’s offensive line will also have to account for Dexter Lawrence II, who has five sacks, and Boye Mafe, who has 6.5 off the edge. Washington can't double-team them all, so somebody is always going to be one-on-one with a blocker. Allen said he’s looking forward to seeing some of the people who helped him in Washington, including longtime strength coach Chad Engelhart. He called Jayden Daniels “the complete package” this week, while noting Cincinnati has to keep him from running and bring consistent pressure. That puts the spotlight squarely on Cosmi, who knows his old teammate as well as anyone — and will spend Monday night trying to keep Allen from hitting career sack No. 50 at his quarterback’s expense. title: Commanders-Bengals Final Injury Report: Lucas Patrick Named Starter, Backfield Still Unsettled
full_text:
The Washington Commanders released their final Week 11 injury report on Saturday afternoon. The biggest news is that Jacory “Bill” Croskey-Merritt (groin), Lucas Patrick (concussion), Amik Robertson (ankle), and Rachaad White (heel) are all questionable. Three pieces of vital information are still to be determined, as Robertson was injured on the final sequence Friday, didn't practice Saturday, and while the team did not rule him out, they're going to wait to decide. Commanders head coach Dan Quinn named Patrick the starting center for Monday's game despite his game designation, and Rachaad White's heel is something to watch. Bill was a full participant in practice all three days this week, but remains on injured reserve , meaning the team will have to activate him before Monday's game. Quinn didn't leave much to the imagination: "He had a really good week, so we’ll finish up the last part of the process tonight and tomorrow," Quinn said Saturday. Running back Rachaad White was added to the report Friday , and then didn't practice at all Saturday with an injured heel that Quinn believes White can still play through, and he held him out of practice to relieve soreness. Austin Ekeler stands to get a boost in carries if White can't play. Patrick cleared concussion protocol and fully practiced all three days, but still has a game designation of questionable despite Quinn saying he'll be the starting center against Cincy, which is a bit of double talk. Oddly enough, Nick Allegretti was also in practice all week and has no game designation after his best professional game at center last weekend . If Robertson can’t go, Quinn said Washington would use a combination of Rasul Douglas, Mike Sainristil and Fabian Moreau, with Sainristil and Moreau among the options inside against Joe Burrow and Cincinnati’s receivers . Treylon Burks returned to full practice Saturday after missing Friday with his foot injury. He has no game designation. Quan Martin (shoulder) also finished the week as a full participant after two limited days. Jayden Daniels (left elbow), John Bates (shoulder), Chig Okonkwo (back), Tyler Owens (ankle), Andrew Wylie (hip), Colson Yankoff (knee), Allegretti (chest), and Deatrich Wise Jr. (rest) also have no game designation.

Cincinnati ruled out starting right guard Dalton Risner (knees), while left guard Dylan Fairchild (oblique) is questionable. The Bengals also placed linebacker Oren Burks (groin) on injured reserve Saturday . Dax Hill (illness), Kyle Dugger (quad), Swayze Bozeman (forearm) and Brian Parker II (knee) are questionable; Jalen Davis (hamstring) and Andrei Iosivas (thumb) are doubtful. Bozeman, Parker, Davis and Iosivas remain on injured reserve and would need to be activated before they can play.

title: Commanders Face the NFL’s Busiest Pass-Catching Running Back in Week 11
full_text:
Cincinnati Bengals running back Chase Brown currently leads all NFL running backs with 47 receptions heading into Monday night's game against the Washington Commanders . The Bengals also have one of the league's best wide receiver duos, with Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . Brown ranks third on the Bengals in receptions, behind Chase and Higgins. His 47 catches have produced 246 yards and two touchdowns, an average of 5.2 yards per reception. He also leads Cincinnati with 441 rushing yards. Washington has to account for him whether Burrow hands him the ball or drops back to pass. After Sunday's game against the Steelers, Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow said , “When people devote too many resources to stopping the guys on the outside, Chase can beat you in a lot of different ways.” Brown caught eight passes for 39 yards and two touchdowns against Pittsburgh. While the two touchdown catches were only two and four yards, he helped finish drives without needing a large receiving-yardage total.
Touch. Down. Chase. Brown. #PITvsCIN on NBC pic.twitter.com/IlxU0qC4pR
That puts a lot on Sonny Styles and Frankie Luvu. They have to see Brown coming out of the backfield while keeping track of the routes crossing in front of them. Commanders defensive coordinator Daronte Jones singled out Brown’s ability to make one cut and take a play the distance. He wants Washington taking good angles and getting help to the ball, so one missed tackle does not turn a short gain into a big one. With Chase and Higgins drawing help downfield, Washington’s underneath defenders have to find Brown quickly and keep a short catch from becoming a bigger gain. A four-yard catch on first-and-10 leaves Cincinnati at second-and-6. Give him those same four yards on third-and-3, and Burrow gets a fresh set of downs. Inside the 5, there may be no time for a second defender to clean up a missed tackle. When Burrow goes to Brown underneath Monday night, watch where the Commanders get him down.
